_about: The landlord forms in the NOHM app, state by state: a copy of the server catalog (nohm-backend src/modules/legal-forms, stateView of every state). Refresh it from there with tools/seo/export-legal-forms.md; never edit it by hand.

forms.label: 7-business-day notice to pay rent or the lease ends
forms.explain: States the rent and late fees owed; if they aren’t paid within 7 business days after the tenant receives it, the lease ends.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid when due (Alabama has no grace period).
notes: Rent is payable without demand when the lease says. Alabama sets no grace period: you may deliver this once rent is unpaid when due.

The seven business days run from when the tenant receives it, not when you send it, and no Alabama law presumes a mailed notice was received (Ala. Code § 35-9A-144(e)). Hand it over and keep proof; NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

The Act doesn’t define “business day”. NOHM skips Saturdays, Sundays and state and federal holidays (Ala. Code § 1-3-8), which can only make the date later. In Baldwin and Mobile Counties, Mardi Gras is also a holiday: if the count crosses it, add a day.
A tenant can cure a breach no more than twice in any 12 months unless you agree in writing (Ala. Code § 35-9A-421(d)).
Accepting rent knowing of the default waives your right to end the lease for it, unless you agree otherwise after the breach (Ala. Code § 35-9A-424).
Keep a copy and your proof of delivery: you attach them to the court’s default-judgment affidavit (Form C-25B).
Alabama has no separate demand for possession: if the rent isn’t paid, the lease ends on the date in this notice and you can file Form C-59.

forms.label: 7-business-day notice to remedy a lease violation
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong; if it isn’t remedied within 7 business days after they receive it, the lease ends.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease, or a duty that affects health and safety.
notes: Use it for a material noncompliance with the lease, or a noncompliance with the tenant’s duties (Ala. Code § 35-9A-301) that materially affects health and safety. Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do.

Some breaches can’t be cured and end the lease on a 7-day notice instead (Ala. Code § 35-9A-421(d)): illegal drugs, illegal firearm use, criminal assault on the premises, or a repeat within 6 months of a breach already cured. An intentional misrepresentation on the application can’t be cured either (§ 35-9A-421(a)). NOHM doesn’t draw that notice; ask a lawyer.
A tenant can cure a breach no more than twice in any 12 months unless you agree in writing (Ala. Code § 35-9A-421(d)).
A tenant who refuses you lawful access can be served this notice (Ala. Code § 35-9A-442(a)).

The seven business days run from when the tenant receives it, not when you send it, and no Alabama law presumes a mailed notice was received (Ala. Code § 35-9A-144(e)). Hand it over and keep proof; NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

The Act doesn’t define “business day”. NOHM skips Saturdays, Sundays and state and federal holidays (Ala. Code § 1-3-8), which can only make the date later. In Baldwin and Mobile Counties, Mardi Gras is also a holiday: if the count crosses it, add a day.
Some county court pages say 14 days for other violations; the statute says seven business days.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a rental date at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out; Alabama needs no reason.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice instead (Ala. Code § 35-9A-441(a)). A lease with a fixed term ends on its own; no notice is needed.

Alabama has no separate demand for possession: if the tenant stays after the date, file Form C-59 (Ala. Code § 35-9A-441(c)). If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, you may also recover up to three months’ rent or your actual damages, whichever is greater, and reasonable attorney’s fees.
Alabama has no statewide just-cause rule, but you can’t end a tenancy to retaliate against a tenant (Ala. Code § 35-9A-501).
NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it, for delivery time.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Forms C-59, C-25B)
forms.explain: What to write on the court’s Statement of Claim for eviction (Form C-59), filled in from the lease, with the steps and deadlines that follow.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Alabama evictions are filed on the court’s own Form C-59, not a complaint you write. Print it from the court’s site and copy NOHM’s values onto it.

An individual landlord can file without a lawyer. A company (an LLC or a corporation) needs an Alabama attorney: a court held a complaint filed for a company by a non-lawyer void (Ex parte Williams, 89 So. 3d 135 (Ala. Civ. App. 2011), read from a summary NOHM couldn’t check against the official reporter).
Filing and service fees are set by each county; Montgomery County’s page lists $350 plus service fees per defendant, and asks you to bring a copy of the notice (a court web page, not law).
Don’t accept rent after the lease terminates: the default form asks you to swear you haven’t.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Alabama doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: signed by both of you, it is your record of the home’s condition when the deposit comes back.

Before the tenancy starts, give the tenant in writing the name and business address of the manager and of the owner or the owner’s agent for notices (Ala. Code § 35-9A-202(a)): NOHM’s disclosure form does it.
Give the tenant any rules and regulations when they sign, or when you adopt them; otherwise they can’t be enforced (Ala. Code § 35-9A-302(b)(6)).
For a home built before 1978, give the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet (42 U.S.C. § 4852d).

forms.label: Disclosure of manager and owner
forms.explain: Tells the tenant in writing who manages the home and who receives notices and legal papers for the owner.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, and again whenever it changes.
notes: Required at or before the start of the tenancy (Ala. Code § 35-9A-202(a)). Keep it current (§ 35-9A-202(b)).
If it isn’t given, the person who signed the lease for the landlord becomes the landlord’s agent for service of process and for notices and demands (Ala. Code § 35-9A-202(c)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: Give at least 2 days’ notice and enter only at reasonable times (Ala. Code § 35-9A-303(c)). Posting a note on the tenant’s main entry door, with the time and purpose, is a permitted way to give it.

A general notice or schedule given apart from the lease, more than 2 days ahead, covers repairs, maintenance, pest control and health or safety service; the tenant may also agree to less notice (§ 35-9A-303(d)). A tenant’s repair request is consent to enter to make it (§ 35-9A-303(e)).

In an emergency you may enter without consent (§ 35-9A-303(b)). Showing the home in its last 4 months without consent needs a separate general notice the tenant signed, and only with the prospective tenant or buyer.
Abusing access can cost you an injunction, termination or actual damages (Ala. Code § 35-9A-442(b)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Alabama statute sets the notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date: a month-to-month can only be changed by ending it on 30 days’ notice to a rental date (Ala. Code § 35-9A-441(b)), so that is the safe minimum.
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Alabama has no rent cap, and cities and counties can’t control rents (Ala. Code § 11-80-8.1(b)).
You can’t raise rent to retaliate against a tenant who complained to a code agency or to you, or joined a tenants’ union (Ala. Code § 35-9A-501(a)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 60 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Mail it within 60 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant gives back possession (Ala. Code § 35-9A-201(b)–(c)). First-class mail to the address the tenant gave in writing is enough (§ 35-9A-201(e)).
No forwarding address? Mail it first class to the tenant’s last known address, or if none, to the premises (§ 35-9A-201(d)).
Deduct only accrued rent and damage from the tenant’s breach of their duties, each on its own line.
Miss the 60 days and you owe the tenant double the original deposit (§ 35-9A-201(f)).
A deposit or check the tenant doesn’t claim within 90 days is forfeited (§ 35-9A-201(d)).
The deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent, except for pets, changes to the premises or added liability risk (§ 35-9A-201(a)). No interest or separate account is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Alabama doesn’t require this notice. Property left in the unit more than 14 days after the tenancy terminates may be disposed of (Ala. Code § 35-9A-423(d)); NOHM counts the 14 days from this notice, which is never earlier.
A unit is also considered abandoned if its electric service has been off for seven days in a row (§ 35-9A-423(e)).
Alabama abolished distress for rent: you can’t hold the tenant’s things for unpaid rent (Ala. Code § 35-9A-425).
Photograph the property before you move or dispose of it.

forms.label: 7-day notice to quit for unpaid rent
forms.explain: Gives the tenant 7 days to pay the rent in full, or the tenancy ends; goes with the court’s MED-600 sheet.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid when due (Alaska has no grace period).
notes: Give the tenant the court’s MED-600 information sheet with this notice: it is required with every notice to quit, and the eviction complaint asks you to confirm you gave it (Administrative Bulletin 98 ¶ 3(a)). Without it the judge may continue the hearing up to 2 days. Print it from public.courts.alaska.gov/web/forms/docs/med-600.pdf.
Mailed by registered or certified mail, the law adds 3 days to the period (AS 09.45.090(c)); NOHM counts them.
The law requires the date and time the tenancy ends (AS 09.45.105); NOHM states 11:59 p.m. on the last day.

Only one written notice is needed for any one default. You may accept a partial payment and extend the date for the eviction (AS 34.03.220(b)); otherwise accepting rent knowing of the default can waive your right to end the tenancy for it (AS 34.03.240).
Rent paid in advance: you can’t file until the prepaid period runs out (AS 09.45.130).

For a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a federal housing program, the CARES Act requires 30 days’ notice to vacate for nonpayment, and the court requires form CIV-731 with every complaint.
NOHM’s calendar doesn’t know Seward’s Day (last Monday in March) or Alaska Day (October 18): if the last day falls on one, move it a day later (AS 44.12.010).

forms.label: 10-day notice to quit for a lease violation
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong and how to fix it within 10 days, or the tenancy ends; goes with the MED-600 sheet.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease, or a duty that affects health and safety.
notes: Describe both the violation and exactly what the tenant must do to fix it: the law requires both (AS 09.45.105(1)(A)–(B)).

Give the tenant the court’s MED-600 information sheet with this notice: it is required with every notice to quit, and the eviction complaint asks you to confirm you gave it (Administrative Bulletin 98 ¶ 3(a)). Without it the judge may continue the hearing up to 2 days. Print it from public.courts.alaska.gov/web/forms/docs/med-600.pdf.
Mailed by registered or certified mail, the law adds 3 days to the period (AS 09.45.090(c)); NOHM counts them.
The law requires the date and time the tenancy ends (AS 09.45.105); NOHM states 11:59 p.m. on the last day.

If substantially the same breach recurs within 6 months of one you gave notice of, the lease can end on 5 days’ notice with no chance to fix it (AS 34.03.220(a)(2); court form CIV-727’s “No Remedy” box).

Shorter notices apply to deliberate damage over $400 and to illegal activity (24 hours to 5 days, court forms CIV-728 and CIV-729), and to utilities shut off for the tenant’s nonpayment (5 days, CIV-726). A tenant who refuses lawful access can be given 10 days’ notice (AS 34.03.300(a)). NOHM doesn’t draw those; the court’s forms are free.
NOHM’s calendar doesn’t know Seward’s Day (last Monday in March) or Alaska Day (October 18): if the last day falls on one, move it a day later (AS 44.12.010).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a rental due date at least 30 days out; goes with the MED-600 sheet.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out; Alaska needs no reason.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy needs 14 days’ written notice instead, and only while rent is current (AS 34.03.290(a)).

Give the tenant the court’s MED-600 information sheet with this notice: it is required with every notice to quit, and the eviction complaint asks you to confirm you gave it (Administrative Bulletin 98 ¶ 3(a)). Without it the judge may continue the hearing up to 2 days. Print it from public.courts.alaska.gov/web/forms/docs/med-600.pdf.
Mailed by registered or certified mail, the law adds 3 days to the period (AS 09.45.090(c)); NOHM counts them.
The law requires the date and time the tenancy ends (AS 09.45.105); NOHM states 11:59 p.m. on the last day.

Alaska has no statewide just-cause rule, but you can’t end a tenancy to retaliate against a tenant (AS 34.03.310). For some of the reasons the retaliation law allows, the tenant gets the longer of 30 days or the lease’s notice period (AS 09.45.090(a)(2)(D)).
A lease with a fixed term that has run out still needs a notice to quit before you can file (AS 34.03.290(c); AS 09.45.100(a)): use NOHM’s notice to quit for a holdover.

forms.label: Notice to quit (holdover)
forms.explain: The notice to quit Alaska requires before filing when a tenant stays after the lease ended.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Alaska requires a notice to quit before you can file to evict, even when a lease term has simply run out (AS 09.45.100(a); AS 34.03.290(c)).
The law sets no number of days for it; NOHM fills in 7. If you mail it, the law adds 3 days for mail (AS 09.45.090(c)): give at least 10.
Serve it in hand, leave it at the premises if the tenant is absent, or send it by registered or certified mail (AS 09.45.100(c)), with the court’s MED-600 sheet (Administrative Bulletin 98 ¶ 3(a)).
The law requires the date and time the tenant must leave (AS 09.45.105); NOHM states 11:59 p.m. on the date.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (CIV-730, CIV-731, CIV-732, CIV-105)
forms.explain: What to write on the court’s Complaint for Forcible Entry and Detainer and the papers filed with it, filled in from the lease, with the steps and deadlines that follow.
forms.when: The notice to quit ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Use the court’s own complaint, CIV-730: a complaint you write must still carry the court form’s notice about dismissal word for word (Civil Rule 85(a)(1)). NOHM fills in what to write on it.

An individual owner can file without a lawyer. A corporation, a property manager, or anyone acting under a power of attorney must have an attorney sign the complaint (court booklet CIV-720; AS 22.20.040). The booklet doesn’t name LLCs; treat one like a corporation.
Bring the original notice to quit, your record of serving it, and the lease.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Alaska lets you require a premises condition statement (and a contents inventory for a furnished home) in the lease, by reference or as an attachment; signed by both of you, it becomes part of the rental agreement (AS 34.03.020(e)).

Give the tenant in writing, at or before the start: who manages the home and who receives notices for the owner (AS 34.03.080; NOHM’s disclosure form), and the terms on which you may keep any of the deposit (AS 34.03.070(c)).
The lease must require the tenant to tell you of an absence of more than 7 days (AS 34.03.150). Post the rules prominently on the premises (AS 34.03.130(a)).
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors must be working (AS 34.03.100(a)(7)). For a home built before 1978, give the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Disclosure of manager and owner
forms.explain: Tells the tenant in writing who manages the home and who receives notices and legal papers for the owner.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, and again whenever it changes.
notes: Required at or before the start of the tenancy, and kept current (AS 34.03.080(a)–(b)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ notice, enter only at reasonable times, and with the tenant’s consent (AS 34.03.140(c)).

You may enter to inspect, make repairs or improvements, supply services, remove your own property not covered by the lease, or show the home to buyers, lenders, tenants, workers or contractors (AS 34.03.140(a)). In an emergency you may enter without consent (§ 34.03.140(b)); also during an absence of more than 7 days (§ 34.03.230(b)).
Abusing access, or refusing it, has remedies under AS 34.03.300.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Alaska statute sets the notice for a rent increase. The Department of Law’s handbook says to give at least 30 days in a month-to-month, effective on a rental due date; NOHM does the same (official guidance, not statute).
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Alaska has no rent cap. You can’t raise rent to retaliate against a tenant, though an increase for higher costs or improvements may be allowed (AS 34.03.310).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 14 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back (30 days if you deduct for damage, or no proper notice was given).
notes: Mail it within 14 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant gives back possession, if the tenancy was ended by a proper notice. You have 30 days if you deduct for damage, or if the tenant didn’t give proper notice (AS 34.03.070(g)).
Don’t know the tenant’s mailing address but know how to reach them? Make a reasonable effort to deliver it (AS 34.03.070(g)).
Wilfully failing to return it or itemize it can cost up to twice the amount withheld (AS 34.03.070(d)).

The deposit and prepaid rent can’t exceed two months’ rent unless the rent is over $2,000 a month; a pet deposit up to one month’s rent is accounted for separately (AS 34.03.070(a), (h)). Keep deposits in a trust account where practicable (§ 34.03.070(c)). No interest is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Give at least 15 days after you deliver or mail it (AS 34.03.260(a)). Mark in the list which items you’ll sell at public sale and which you’ll destroy or dispose of: the law asks the notice to say.

Store the property in a place of safekeeping with reasonable care. You may charge storage: on the premises, no more than its fair rental value; in commercial storage, the actual charge (AS 34.03.260(b)).
If the tenant answers in writing within the time, they get 15 more days to remove it, and pay the storage (AS 34.03.260(c)).
A public sale follows the execution-sale procedure of AS 09.35.140, which NOHM didn’t read: ask the court or a lawyer before you sell.
Violating this section deliberately or negligently can cost actual damages and as much again (AS 34.03.260(d)).

forms.label: 5-day notice to pay rent
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid and that the lease will end by a court filing if it isn’t paid within 5 days after they receive it.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid when due (Arizona has no grace period).
notes: Arizona has no grace period by statute: you may give this once rent is unpaid when due.

You don’t have to accept a partial payment. If you do, you keep the right to proceed only if the tenant agrees in a contemporaneous writing to its terms, with the date the balance is due; otherwise accepting rent knowing of the default waives your right to terminate for it (A.R.S. § 33-1371). Housing assistance payments aren’t partial payments.

Hand it to the tenant, or send it by registered or certified mail; mailed, NOHM counts the 5 days the law allows for it to arrive (A.R.S. § 33-1313(B)). Posting it on the door or mailing it first class is not a way the law allows.
A last day that falls on a Sunday or a legal holiday moves to the next day (A.R.S. § 1-243(A)); NOHM also moves it off a Saturday, which is only later.
The court dismisses an eviction if the notice doesn’t meet the statute or wasn’t properly served (Rules of Procedure for Eviction Actions, Rule 13(a)(2), read from an unofficial copy).

forms.label: 10-day notice to remedy a lease violation
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong; if it isn’t remedied within 10 days after they receive it, the lease ends.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease.
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the law requires the notice to specify it.

A noncompliance with the tenant’s duties (A.R.S. § 33-1341) that materially affects health and safety has a 5-day notice instead. A breach that is both material and irreparable (a weapon discharged, a serious crime, threats, or serious damage, among others) allows a notice of immediate termination. NOHM doesn’t draw those; ask a lawyer.

Some breaches can’t be cured: material falsification of the application (occupants, pets, income, Social Security number, employment, criminal or eviction history), and a second noncompliance of the same or a similar nature during the lease, which allows a special detainer action 10 days after a written notice saying so (A.R.S. § 33-1368(A)).
The tenant is responsible for guests’ lease violations they could reasonably foresee (A.R.S. § 33-1368(F)).
A last day that falls on a Sunday or a legal holiday moves to the next day (A.R.S. § 1-243(A)); NOHM also moves it off a Saturday, which is only later.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at the end of a rental period at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out; Arizona needs no reason.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy needs 10 days’ written notice instead (A.R.S. § 33-1375(A)).
Arizona has no just-cause rule, but you can’t end a tenancy to retaliate against a tenant (A.R.S. § 33-1381).

If the tenant stays after the date, you may file a special detainer action; a willful holdover not in good faith can cost the tenant up to two months’ rent or twice your actual damages, whichever is greater (A.R.S. § 33-1375(C)).

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: A tenant who stays after the lease term ends, or after receiving a written demand for possession, is in forcible detainer (A.R.S. § 12-1173(A)(1)). The demand isn’t strictly required after a month-to-month notice, but it’s the safe step when a fixed term simply runs out.
Arizona sets no waiting period for it; NOHM fills in 5 days. If you mail it, allow 5 days for it to arrive (A.R.S. § 33-1313(B)).

forms.label: Eviction complaint (special detainer), verified
forms.explain: The eviction filing: the complaint, sworn before a notary, with the facts Arizona’s statute and eviction rules ask for.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Arizona lets you write your own complaint: no court may require its form, and one that meets the statute is enough (A.R.S. § 12-1175(D)). The courts’ generic complaint (AOCLJEA2F) is accepted too.
Sign the verification in front of a notary: the complaint must be under oath (A.R.S. § 12-1175(A)). Attach the notice and your proof of delivering it as Exhibit A.
File it in the justice court for the precinct where the rental is, or in superior court. Justice courts hear claims up to $10,000 (the courts’ self-service page).

The court issues the summons the day you file, setting the trial 3 to 6 days later; it must be served at least 2 days before (A.R.S. § 33-1377(B)). Serve the courts’ Residential Eviction Information Sheet (AOCLJEA3F) with the summons and complaint.

If personal service is attempted and fails, posting the summons on the main entrance within a day of issuance and mailing it certified the same day counts as received 3 days after mailing (A.R.S. § 33-1377(B)).
No writ of restitution until 5 calendar days after judgment (A.R.S. § 12-1178(C)). Either side may appeal within 5 days (§ 12-1179). No bond is needed to file.
After the judgment is paid in full, file a satisfaction of judgment in the justice court within 40 days (A.R.S. § 22-247(A), from September 12, 2026).

Who may appear: the owner, an LLC’s member or manager, or an Arizona attorney; a property manager can’t represent the owner (Rules of Procedure for Eviction Actions, Rule 11(b)(1), and a Maricopa County Justice Courts handout, neither read from an official copy).

The heading “YOU ARE BEING SUED TO BE EVICTED”, the subsidized-housing statement and, for unpaid rent, serving the lease’s rent terms and six months of the ledger come from the Rules of Procedure for Eviction Actions, Rule 5, read from an unofficial copy (amended September 12, 2026).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Required: on move-in, give the tenant a signed copy of the lease, a move-in form for listing existing damage, and written notice that they may be present at the move-out inspection (A.R.S. § 33-1321(C)). This form does the last two.

Before the tenancy starts, give the tenant in writing who manages the home and who receives notices for the owner, and tell them the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act is on the Department of Housing’s website (A.R.S. § 33-1322(A)–(B)): NOHM’s disclosure form does it.
State in writing the purpose of any nonrefundable fee or deposit; one not called nonrefundable is refundable (A.R.S. § 33-1321(B)).
Give bedbug educational materials to new tenants, except in a single-family home (A.R.S. § 33-1319). With a pool, give the Department of Health Services’ pool safety notice (A.R.S. § 36-1681(E)).

If foreclosure has begun, the lease must say so in the statute’s words (A.R.S. § 33-1331). Utility billing by submeter or ratio must be disclosed (A.R.S. § 33-1314.01). The property must be registered with the county assessor (A.R.S. § 33-1902). For a home built before 1978, give the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Disclosure of manager and owner
forms.explain: Tells the tenant in writing who manages the home and who receives notices for the owner, and where to read Arizona’s landlord and tenant law.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, and again whenever it changes.
notes: Required at or before the start of the tenancy; keep it current, and give it again when the tenant asks (A.R.S. § 33-1322(A)–(C)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: Give at least 2 days’ notice and enter only at reasonable times (A.R.S. § 33-1343(D)).
A tenant’s request for service or maintenance is permission to enter for it, and waives a separate notice (§ 33-1343(B)). In an emergency you may enter without consent (§ 33-1343(C)).
Abusing access can cost you actual damages of at least one month’s rent (A.R.S. § 33-1376).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Arizona statute sets the notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date: a month-to-month can only be changed by ending it on 30 days’ notice to a rental date (A.R.S. § 33-1375(B)), so that is the safe minimum.
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Arizona has no rent cap, and cities and towns can’t control rents (A.R.S. § 33-1329(A)).
Adding submetered or ratio utility billing mid-tenancy needs at least 90 days’ notice (A.R.S. § 33-1314.01(G)). No retaliatory increases (A.R.S. § 33-1381).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 14 business days after the tenancy ends, you get the home back, and the tenant asks for it.
notes: Within 14 days, not counting Saturdays, Sundays or legal holidays, after the tenancy ends, the tenant gives back possession, and the tenant asks for it, give the itemized list of deductions and the amount due (A.R.S. § 33-1321(D)).
Mail it first class to the tenant’s last known place of residence unless they arranged otherwise in writing. If the tenant doesn’t dispute it within 60 days after mailing, the list is final.
Wrongfully keeping deposit money can cost twice the amount withheld (A.R.S. § 33-1321(E)).
The deposit can’t be more than one and one-half months’ rent. A fee or deposit not stated in writing as nonrefundable is refundable (A.R.S. § 33-1321(A)–(B)). No interest is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Use it after you retake an abandoned unit, or after a writ of restitution, when the tenant’s things remain (A.R.S. §§ 33-1370(D), 33-1368(E)). Send it by certified mail AND post it (§ 33-1370(A)).

Before retaking an abandoned unit, send the tenant a notice of abandonment by certified mail and post it on the door for 5 days (A.R.S. § 33-1370(A)–(B)). NOHM doesn’t draw that notice. If the tenant returned the keys and left things behind, you may remove them at once (§ 33-1370(I)).

Hold the property 14 calendar days after you retake possession; then sell it or donate it to a qualified charity, and keep records for 12 months (A.R.S. § 33-1370(F)–(G)). A tenant who gives written notice of intent to reclaim has 5 days to do so (§ 33-1370(H)).
Perishables, plants and contaminated items may be disposed of; animals go to a shelter (A.R.S. § 33-1370(E)).

forms.label: 3-day notice to quit (rent not paid)
forms.explain: Ends the tenancy for unpaid rent and demands the home back in 3 days.
forms.when: Rent is more than 5 days late.
notes: Rent must be more than 5 days late before you serve this (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-701(b)): serve it no sooner than the 6th day after the due date.
Arkansas’s notice to quit is a demand to leave, not to pay. You may still accept full payment, but taking rent after the notice can waive it; ask a lawyer before you do.
Hand it to the tenant, or mail it certified or registered (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-303(b)); NOHM adds 3 business days if you mail it.
Don’t use the criminal “failure to vacate” law (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-16-101) without a lawyer.

forms.label: 14-day notice of noncompliance
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what they did wrong: fix it in 14 days, or the lease ends.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term (other than rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the law requires the notice to specify it.
If the tenant fixes it in time, the lease goes on. If not, it ends on the date in the notice, and you can demand possession and file for unlawful detainer.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a date at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice instead (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-704(a)).
Ending on the day before rent is due is the cleanest choice, though Arkansas doesn’t require it.
If the tenant stays after the date, you may bring an action for possession (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-704(c)).

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing for unlawful detainer.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Arkansas sets no waiting period for this demand. NOHM fills in 3 days; give more if you like.
Hand it to the tenant or mail it certified, and keep proof: the court will ask how you demanded possession.
If the tenant stays after the date, file the complaint for unlawful detainer.

forms.label: Complaint for unlawful detainer
forms.explain: The eviction filing: the complaint, your sworn affidavit, and the Notice of Intention to Issue Writ of Possession for the clerk.
forms.when: The notice or demand ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: File the complaint and the affidavit with the clerk of the district or circuit court in the county where the rental is. The clerk issues the summons and the Notice of Intention (the last page); the sheriff or a process server serves them on each tenant.

The tenant has 5 days after service, not counting Sundays and legal holidays, to file a written objection. If they don’t, the court orders the writ of possession. If they do, get a hearing date and send the Notice of Hearing.
No bond is needed for an eviction under Arkansas’s landlord-tenant act (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-701(c)(1)).
An individual landlord can file for themselves. A company (an LLC or a corporation) generally must be represented by a lawyer in court.
Sign the affidavit in front of a notary.
Bring the lease, the notice and your proof of serving it, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Notice of hearing
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when and where the court will hear your claim for possession.
forms.when: The tenant filed a written objection and the court gave you a hearing date.
notes: Get the date, time and place from the court first.
Send it by certified mail, postage prepaid, to the tenant or to their lawyer of record, and keep the receipt (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-60-307(c)).
At the hearing you show the court why you are entitled to possession; the tenant can answer it.

forms.label: Move-in defect form (Healthy Homes Act)
forms.explain: The Healthy Homes Act’s form for the tenant to list defects in water, power, plumbing, roof and heat or air.
forms.when: Give it when the tenant gets possession; they have 2 business days to return it.
notes: Hand it to the tenant when possession is available to them. If they sign it without noting a defect and take possession, or don’t return it within 2 business days, that defect generally isn’t held against you (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-502(c)).
It applies to leases entered into or renewed after November 1, 2021.
Fix what they note. A tenant whose rent is current can end the lease if a defect they gave you written notice of isn’t fixed within 30 days (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-502(d)).
Keep the signed form with the lease.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Arkansas law sets no advance notice for entry; your lease may. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
A tenant may not unreasonably refuse you entry for these reasons (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-17-602(a)). Come at reasonable times.
In an emergency you may need to go in right away; tell the tenant as soon as you can.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Arkansas statute sets the notice for a rent increase. The Attorney General advises at least one rental period; NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date.
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Arkansas has no rent cap, and cities and counties can’t control rents.
You can’t raise rent to retaliate against a victim of domestic abuse (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-16-112).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 60 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Mail this and any refund first class to the tenant’s last known address within 60 days after the tenancy ends and they give back possession; that counts as returning it (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-16-305(b)).
Deduct only unpaid rent and damage from the tenant’s breaking the lease, each on its own line.
If the letter comes back and you can’t find the tenant after a reasonable effort, the money becomes yours 180 days after you mailed it.
Keeping a deposit wrongfully can cost up to twice the amount kept, plus costs and attorney’s fees.

The deposit law doesn’t apply if you, your family and your companies own 5 or fewer units and manage them yourselves; it does if you pay someone to manage them (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-16-303). Itemizing is still the safe practice.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the lease ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Arkansas doesn’t require this notice; property left when a lease ends is considered abandoned (Ark. Code Ann. § 18-16-108(a)). Giving one heads off disputes.
Use it only after the lease has ended, by its term, a notice, or the court’s writ, and the tenant has left: never while they still have possession.
Photograph the property before you move or dispose of it.

forms.label: 3-day notice to pay rent or quit
forms.explain: Demands the rent due within 3 court days, or the home back, and elects to forfeit the lease.
forms.when: Rent is past due (California has no grace period by statute).
notes: Serve it any time within one year after the rent was due (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 1161(2)). If someone else lives there as a subtenant, serve them too.

Under PAYMENT give the name, phone number and address of the person to pay, and the usual days and hours they take payment in person; or a bank account within five miles of the rental; or an electronic transfer already set up (§ 1161(2)).
A new owner or manager who hasn’t given the tenant the owner and manager disclosures (Cal. Civ. Code § 1962) can’t serve this notice for rent that came due before they did.
You can’t charge the tenant a fee for serving, posting or delivering this notice (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 1161(6)).

Whether the law adds days when a copy is mailed with substituted or posted service is unsettled; NOHM adds 5 days when a copy is mailed (as Code Civ. Proc. § 1013 does for papers mailed in a case), which only makes the date later.

Cities and counties with rent control or just-cause ordinances (Los Angeles, San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, San Jose, Santa Monica and others) may require more words, a copy to a rent board, or a different notice. NOHM doesn’t cover local ordinances.

forms.label: 3-day notice to perform covenant or quit
forms.explain: Requires the tenant to fix a lease violation within 3 court days, or give the home back.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term that can still be performed.
notes: Name the covenant and exactly what the tenant must do to perform it.
Under the Tenant Protection Act, a curable violation needs this notice first; if it isn’t cured in time, a 3-day notice to quit without a chance to cure may follow (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(c)).

Some breaches can’t be cured: assigning or subletting against the lease, committing waste, a nuisance, or using the premises for an unlawful purpose. They allow a 3-day notice to quit (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 1161(4)), which NOHM doesn’t draw.
You can’t charge the tenant a fee for serving, posting or delivering this notice (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 1161(6)).

Whether the law adds days when a copy is mailed with substituted or posted service is unsettled; NOHM adds 5 days when a copy is mailed (as Code Civ. Proc. § 1013 does for papers mailed in a case), which only makes the date later.

Cities and counties with rent control or just-cause ordinances (Los Angeles, San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, San Jose, Santa Monica and others) may require more words, a copy to a rent board, or a different notice. NOHM doesn’t cover local ordinances.

forms.label: 30- or 60-day notice to end a tenancy
forms.explain: Ends a periodic tenancy: 60 days if a tenant has lived there a year or more, 30 if less, with just cause after 12 months.
forms.when: You want to end a month-to-month; check the Tenant Protection Act and local rules first.
notes: The notice is 60 days if any tenant has lived there a year or more, 30 days if less (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.1(b)–(c)); 30 days also for a qualifying sale to a buyer who will live there (§ 1946.1(d)). The date doesn’t have to end a rental period.

After 12 months (24 for a tenant joined by new adults), the Tenant Protection Act applies unless the home is exempt: the notice must state the just cause, and a no-fault cause (owner move-in, withdrawal from the market, a government order, demolition or substantial remodel) needs one month’s rent paid within 15 days, or waived, and the notice must say so. A notice that doesn’t strictly comply is void (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(a), (b), (d)).

A single-family home or condo owned by individuals (not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member) is exempt only if the lease gave the tenant the statute’s exemption notice (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(e)(8)).
California has no separate demand for possession: after this notice runs, or a fixed-term lease ends, you file the unlawful detainer (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 1161(1), (5)).
For a property with a federally backed mortgage or in a federal housing program, the CARES Act requires 30 days’ notice for nonpayment.
You can’t charge for serving the notice (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.1(i)).

Cities and counties with rent control or just-cause ordinances (Los Angeles, San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley, San Jose, Santa Monica and others) may require more words, a copy to a rent board, or a different notice. NOHM doesn’t cover local ordinances.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (UD-100, SUM-130, CM-010)
forms.explain: What to write on the Judicial Council’s unlawful detainer complaint, summons and cover sheet, filled in from the lease, with the steps and deadlines that follow.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Use the Judicial Council’s forms: the summons (SUM-130) and cover sheet (CM-010) are mandatory, and the complaint form (UD-100) asks every question the statute does. NOHM fills in what to write on them.
Don’t use UD-101 (Plaintiff’s Mandatory Cover Sheet): the COVID-19 law it rests on is no longer in the code. Ask the clerk if your court still lists it.
An individual landlord can file without a lawyer. A company generally must appear through an attorney (case law NOHM didn’t read), and verifies the complaint on a different form.
Cities with rent control or just-cause ordinances add steps; UD-100 asks about them (item 17). NOHM doesn’t cover local ordinances.
Filing fees vary with the amount claimed; ask the clerk.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: California doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice, signed by both of you. Photos are required: for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, photograph the unit immediately before, or at the start of, the tenancy (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(g)(1)).
In the lease, give the name, phone and address of each manager and of the owner or agent for notices and service, and who, where and how rent is paid (Cal. Civ. Code § 1962).

Unless the home is exempt, the lease (or a signed notice) must carry the Tenant Protection Act notice in the statute’s words, in at least 12-point type (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2(f)(3)). A single-family home or condo exempt under § 1946.2(e)(8) must have the statute’s exemption notice in the lease instead. Put these in the lease itself.

Other required notices: Megan’s Law database notice (Civ. Code § 2079.10a), flood hazard (Gov. Code § 8589.45), bed bugs (Civ. Code § 1954.603), known mold (Health & Safety Code § 26147), pest control service (Civ. Code § 1940.8), a pending demolition permit (§ 1940.6), former ordnance nearby (§ 1940.7), shared utility meters (§ 1940.9), the offer of positive rent reporting (§ 1954.07), and a working stove and refrigerator for leases from January 1, 2026 (§ 1941.1). For a home built before 1978, the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give it in writing, with the date, approximate time and purpose; enter only during normal business hours (Cal. Civ. Code § 1954(b), (d)(1)).

Hand it to the tenant, leave it with someone of suitable age at the home, or leave it on, near or under the usual entry door where they’ll find it: 24 hours is presumed reasonable. If you mail it, mail it at least 6 days ahead.

To show the home to a buyer, notice can be oral if you told the tenant in writing within the last 120 days that it’s for sale (§ 1954(d)(2)). No notice is needed in an emergency, if the tenant agrees at the time, or after they’ve abandoned it (§ 1954(e)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: An increase of 10% or less needs at least 30 days’ notice; more than 10% (counted against the lowest rent in the past 12 months) needs at least 90 days (Cal. Civ. Code § 827(b)(2)–(3)). Mailed, add 5 days (Code Civ. Proc. § 1013).

For a home the Tenant Protection Act covers, the increase over any 12 months can’t exceed 5% plus the regional cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower, of the lowest rent in the past 12 months, in no more than two steps (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12(a)). NOHM stops anything over 10%; check the lower figure for your region.

Exempt from the cap: housing first occupied within the last 15 years, an owner-occupied duplex, and a single-family home or condo owned by individuals whose lease has the exemption notice (§ 1947.12(d)).
City rent control (Los Angeles, San Francisco, Oakland and others) may allow less; NOHM doesn’t cover it. No retaliatory increases (Cal. Civ. Code § 1942.5).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 21 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Send it, with any refund, no later than 21 days after the tenant vacates (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(h)(1)).

If the deposit or rent was paid electronically, return the refund electronically to the account the tenant names, unless you agree otherwise; tell the tenant of that right near the end of the tenancy. For several adult tenants, one check payable to all of them unless they all agree otherwise.

Attach receipts, invoices and photos for each repair or cleaning deduction; for your own work, the time spent and the hourly rate. Not needed if the deductions total $125 or less (§ 1950.5(h)(2)–(4)).
Take photos after the tenant leaves, before and after repairs and cleaning (§ 1950.5(g)(2)). Before the tenancy ends, offer the tenant an initial inspection (§ 1950.5(f)).

Keeping a deposit in bad faith can cost up to twice the deposit plus actual damages (§ 1950.5(m)). Since July 1, 2024, a deposit is capped at one month’s rent (two for a small landlord with no more than two properties and four units). Nothing may be “nonrefundable.” Some cities may require interest on deposits (NOHM didn’t check local law).

forms.label: Notice of right to reclaim abandoned property
forms.explain: The statute’s own notice to a former tenant: what they left, where to claim it, and the date after which it may be disposed of.
forms.when: After the tenant vacated and left things behind.
notes: This is the form Cal. Civ. Code § 1984(a) sets out, word for word.

The last day to claim must be at least 15 days after you hand it over, or 18 days after you mail it (Cal. Civ. Code § 1983(b)). Mail it first class to the tenant’s last known address, and if you mail it, send one copy to the vacated premises too; you may also email it if the tenant gave you an email (§ 1983(c)).
Property worth $700 or more is sold at a public sale after publication in a newspaper; under $700 you may keep, sell or destroy it (Cal. Civ. Code § 1988). Store it with reasonable care meanwhile.

Property that belongs to someone other than the tenant takes a different notice (Cal. Civ. Code § 1985). After a writ of possession, the rules in Code Civ. Proc. § 1174(f)–(i) apply. NOHM doesn’t draw those.

forms.label: 10-day demand to pay rent or move
forms.explain: Demands the rent due within 10 days, or the home back, with the mediation and repayment-plan statements the law requires.
forms.when: Rent is past due (no grace period for the demand; late fees wait 7 days).
notes: NOHM gives 10 days, the residential notice. Only 5 days apply to an “exempt residential agreement” (a single-family home whose landlord owns five or fewer and whose lease says the 10-day notice doesn’t apply), and 3 days to employer-provided housing (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-104). A property with a federally backed mortgage or in a federal housing program needs 30 days under the CARES Act (court form JDF 99 A).

You must accept the tenant’s full payment of everything lawfully due under this demand, plus rent that has since come due, at any time until the judge enters judgment for possession (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-115(4)).

If the tenant gives you documentation that domestic violence, stalking or sexual misconduct caused the missed rent (a police report, a protection order, a signed self-attestation, or a letter from a qualified third party), offer a repayment plan within 3 business days: payments of at least $25 a month, no more than 9 months, no fees or interest (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-104(4)(e)).
The law requires the date and time to deliver up the premises (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-106(1)); NOHM states 11:59 p.m. on the last day.
Write it in English, Spanish, or the tenant’s primary language if you know or should know it’s another (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-106(3)). The court posts JDF 99 A in many languages.

If the tenant has told you they are a victim-survivor of domestic violence, stalking or sexual misconduct, make every reasonable effort to serve them in person; after three failed tries, post it AND send it by certified mail or a courier with proof of delivery (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-108(2)).
A late fee may be charged only after rent is 7 days late, up to $50 or 5% of the past-due rent, whichever is greater, and only if the lease sets it (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-105(1)).
NOHM’s calendar doesn’t know Frances Xavier Cabrini Day (the first Monday in October, a Colorado legal holiday): if the last day falls on it, move it a day later.

forms.label: 10-day demand to comply with the lease or move
forms.explain: Describes the violation and requires the tenant to comply within 10 days, or give the home back.
forms.when: The tenant broke a material term of the lease.
notes: Describe the violation specifically: the law requires it (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-106(1)). For conduct that disturbed others or a nuisance, describe the conduct and demand that it stop (§ 13-40-104(1)(j)).

NOHM gives 10 days, the residential notice. Only 5 days apply to an “exempt residential agreement” (a single-family home whose landlord owns five or fewer and whose lease says the 10-day notice doesn’t apply), and 3 days to employer-provided housing (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-104). A property with a federally backed mortgage or in a federal housing program needs 30 days under the CARES Act (court form JDF 99 A).

A second violation of the same condition after this demand allows a notice ending the tenancy in 10 days with no chance to cure (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-104(1)(e.5); court form JDF 99 B). A substantial violation (a violent or drug felony, endangering people or property) allows 3 days (§ 13-40-107.5). NOHM doesn’t draw those; the court’s forms are free.
A documented victim-survivor isn’t in unlawful detention if domestic violence, stalking or sexual misconduct caused or contributed to the violation (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-104(4)).
The law requires the date and time to deliver up the premises (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-106(1)); NOHM states 11:59 p.m. on the last day.
Write it in English, Spanish, or the tenant’s primary language if you know or should know it’s another (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-106(3)). The court posts JDF 99 A in many languages.

If the tenant has told you they are a victim-survivor of domestic violence, stalking or sexual misconduct, make every reasonable effort to serve them in person; after three failed tries, post it AND send it by certified mail or a courier with proof of delivery (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-108(2)).
NOHM’s calendar doesn’t know Frances Xavier Cabrini Day (the first Monday in October, a Colorado legal holiday): if the last day falls on it, move it a day later.

forms.label: Notice to end a tenancy (21 to 91 days)
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy at the end of a period: 21 days for a month-to-month the just-cause law doesn’t cover; 90 days and a stated cause once it does.
forms.when: You want a tenancy to end; after 12 months you need a cause the law allows.
notes: For a tenancy the just-cause law doesn’t cover (the tenant there less than 12 months, an owner-occupied home of up to three units, and others in Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-1302): the notice must expire at the end of the period, served at least 21 days before for a month-to-month, 28 for a tenancy of six months to a year, 91 for a year or longer, and 3 for week-to-week (§ 13-40-107(2)). Court form JDF 99 B.

For a covered tenancy, end it only for a cause the statute allows. A no-fault cause (demolition or conversion, substantial repairs, the landlord or family moving in, a sale, refusal to sign a reasonable new lease, a history of late rent) needs at least 90 days’ notice ending with the lease term and a statement of the legal and factual basis (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-1303(3), (5)(b)). Court form JDF 99 C. NOHM gives 91 days once the tenant has been there 12 months.
A notice that doesn’t meet the just-cause law is a defense, and the case is dismissed (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-1306). A rent increase meant to get around it is barred (§ 38-12-1307).
Colorado’s court forms use no further demand after this notice: if the tenant stays, the eviction rests on it (court forms JDF 99 B and 99 C). Whether a court wants another demand is unsettled.

If the tenant has told you they are a victim-survivor of domestic violence, stalking or sexual misconduct, make every reasonable effort to serve them in person; after three failed tries, post it AND send it by certified mail or a courier with proof of delivery (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-108(2)).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (JDF 101, JDF 102)
forms.explain: What to write on Colorado’s standard eviction complaint and affidavit and the summons, filled in from the lease, with the steps and deadlines that follow.
forms.when: The demand or notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Colorado’s statute names the court’s standard complaint and affidavit (JDF 101) for a residential eviction; a different form must meet every requirement (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-110(1)(a), (f)). NOHM fills in what to write on JDF 101.

An individual landlord can file without a lawyer. A closely held company (three or fewer owners) may appear through an officer if $15,000 or less is at issue and the officer shows the court their authority; otherwise a lawyer is required (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-1-127(2)).
If the tenant consents, tell the court they are a victim-survivor (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-110(3.5)). Court records stay suppressed until the court orders possession (§ 13-40-110.5).
Bring the lease, the notice and your proof of serving it, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Colorado doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: a deposit can’t be kept for damage that existed before the tenancy (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-103(1)(a)), and a signed checklist shows what did.
Give the tenant a copy of the signed lease within 7 days, electronically unless they ask for paper; name yourself or your agent and an address in it (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-801(1)–(2)).
Unless you own five or fewer single-family homes and no more than five units, the lease must say that Colo. Rev. Stat. § 24-34-502(1) prohibits source-of-income discrimination (§ 38-12-801(2.5)).
Before the lease is signed, give the radon disclosure (NOHM’s form) and get it acknowledged (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-803). For a home built before 1978, the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Radon disclosure
forms.explain: The statute’s radon warning, with what you know of the home’s radon tests, for the tenant to acknowledge.
forms.when: Before the tenant signs the lease.
notes: Give it before the lease is signed, with the warning in bold, any radon test results, records and mitigation you know of, and the state health department’s radon brochure; get the tenant’s signed acknowledgment (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-803(2)).
If you don’t, the tenant may be able to void the lease; that right doesn’t apply to leases of one year or less entered on or after January 1, 2026 (§ 38-12-803(3)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Colorado has no general statute on notice of entry; your lease decides. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.

To fix a condition that makes the home unlivable, give written notice at least 24 hours ahead with the date and time and how long you expect to be there, unless the condition threatens life, health or safety or serious damage right away; the tenant may reasonably decline a time and propose another (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-503(6)).

To inspect or treat for bed bugs, give reasonable written or electronic notice at least 48 hours ahead, unless the lease sets another minimum or the tenant waives it (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-1004(1)(a)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 60 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Without a written lease, a rent increase needs at least 60 days’ written notice (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-701(2)(a)). With one, the lease decides; NOHM asks for 60 days either way.
Rent can go up only once in any 12 months of the tenant’s occupancy, whatever the lease (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-702).

Colorado has no rent cap, and cities and counties can’t control rents (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-301). An increase to retaliate, or to get around the just-cause law, is barred (§§ 38-12-509, 38-12-1307).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Return it, with the written statement of the exact reasons for anything kept, within 30 days after the lease ends or the tenant surrenders the home, whichever is later, unless the lease sets a longer time of up to 60 days (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-103(1)(a), as HB 25-1249 rewrote it from January 1, 2026).
If the tenant asked in writing, send the photos, inspection reports, receipts, invoices or estimates for each amount kept within 14 days of the request (§ 38-12-103(8)).

Carpet replacement or repainting the whole unit only for substantial damage that can’t be repaired; carpet over 10 years old can’t count (§ 38-12-103(11)). A walk-through before move-out on either side’s request (§ 38-12-103(1.5)).

Keeping it wrongfully, after the tenant’s 7-day demand, can cost three times the amount plus attorney’s fees (§ 38-12-103(3)). The deposit can’t be more than two months’ rent (§ 38-12-102.5); a pet deposit no more than $300 (§ 38-12-106). No interest is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Colorado gives a landlord a lien on a tenant’s household goods left on the premises for unpaid rent, except pets, small kitchen appliances, utensils, beds, bedding, clothing, records and personal effects (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-20-102(3)).

Property is presumed abandoned once the owner hasn’t contacted you for at least 30 days. At least 15 days before you sell or dispose of it, send this notice by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, signed by the addressee only; keep a copy for a year, and if it comes back unclaimed, publish the notice once in a newspaper in the county (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-20-116).
Property removed while a writ of restitution is executed: you have no duty to store it (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-40-122(3)).

When a tenant dies, you may take possession without court once the personal representative surrenders it, or 30 days after the death if rent is unpaid or the property is substantially removed (Colo. Rev. Stat. § 38-12-801(3.5), leases from September 1, 2025).

forms.label: Notice to quit for nonpayment (3 full days, JD-HM-7)
forms.explain: Connecticut’s notice to quit for unpaid rent, in the statute’s words, served by a state marshal.
forms.when: Rent is still unpaid 9 days after it was due (from the 10th day; 5 days later if your online payment system blocked it).
notes: Wait out the grace period first: rent unpaid 9 days after it was due (4 days for a week-to-week tenancy). For rent due on the 1st, the notice can be served on the 10th at the earliest (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-15a(a)).

If your online rent payment system kept the tenant from paying, the grace period is 5 days longer for that month, and you can’t serve a nonpayment notice to quit until it ends (Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 47a-15a(a), 47a-23(a)(1)(D)).

For a month-to-month or week-to-week tenancy, the notice ends the rental agreement for the month or week in which it is delivered, even if it is delivered in the month after the unpaid one (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(d)).

The tenant can’t cure by paying after it’s served. After a judgment for nonpayment, a tenant who deposits the full arrearage with the clerk within 5 days may ask for a stay of up to 3 months (Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 47a-37, 47a-39).
The last statement on the notice is the one Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(e) allows: payments you take after the quit date are for use and occupancy only, so taking them doesn’t undo the notice.

This is Connecticut’s notice to quit in the words Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(b) sets. The Judicial Branch’s own form, JD-HM-7 (Notice to Quit (End) Possession), says the same; the court accepts either.

Since October 1, 2025 only a proper officer can serve it: give it to a state marshal, who serves an attested copy on every adult tenant and occupant and completes the return of service. Mail and hand delivery by you are not allowed.
Name every lessee and occupant. An occupant whose name you don’t know can be named “John Doe” or “Jane Doe” (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(b)).
Attach the Judicial Branch’s Right to Counsel (CT-RTC) notice (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-75(f)(2)): jud.ct.gov, linked from form JD-HM-7.

Three full days: neither the day it is served nor the quit date counts, and the tenant has until midnight of the quit date. Weekends count, and it may be served on any day of the week (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(c)).
Write the town where you sign it beside the date: the statute’s form asks for the date and place of signing.
Connecticut has no separate demand for possession: this notice to quit is the notice the court needs before a summary process case.
Tenants who are 62 or older or have a disability, living in a building or complex of 5 or more units, can be evicted only for a reason Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23c lists.

forms.label: 15-day pretermination notice (lease violation)
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong and that the lease ends in at least 15 days unless a fixable breach is fixed.
forms.when: The tenant broke the lease or a rule (not rent, and not a serious nuisance).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do, and the lease term, rule or § 47a-11 duty it breaks: the law requires the notice to specify the acts or omissions (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-15).
The 15 days run from when the tenant receives it. The statute sets no way to deliver it; a state marshal gives you proof of the day. NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.
Only a breach that can be fixed by repairs or by paying damages can be cured. If the tenant fixes it in time, the lease goes on.

If it isn’t fixed, the rental agreement ends on the date in this notice. You must then have a state marshal serve a notice to quit (JD-HM-7), at least 3 full days, before you file (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(a)(1)(C)).
If substantially the same act or omission happens again within 6 months, you can go straight to a notice to quit (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-15).

Skip this notice and serve a notice to quit directly for nonpayment, for a serious nuisance (bodily harm or a threat of it, substantial and wilful destruction, an immediate and serious danger to safety, or prostitution or illegal drug sales on the premises), or for letting back in a household member evicted for drug sales (Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 47a-15, 47a-11(h)).
Tenants who are 62 or older or have a disability, in a building or complex of 5 or more units, can be evicted only for a reason Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23c lists; material noncompliance is one.

forms.label: Notice to quit for lapse of time (3 full days, JD-HM-7)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month (or a lease that ran out) with Connecticut’s notice to quit, served by a state marshal.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, or a lease has ended; the quit date ends a rental period.
notes: Connecticut has no 30-day notice for a month-to-month: the notice to quit for lapse of time gives at least 3 full days, and the quit date may not come before the end of the tenant’s rental period. NOHM picks the last day of a rental period at least 3 full days out; you may give more.
A tenancy without a fixed term is month to month, or week to week if rent is paid weekly (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-3b).
If a written lease expressly waives the notice to quit when it ends by lapse of time, the notice isn’t needed (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-25).
A tenant protected by Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23c (62 or older, or with a disability, in a building or complex of 5 or more units) can’t be evicted for lapse of time at all.
A federally backed property (CARES Act) needs a 30-day notice to vacate; the court asks for the CARES Act Affidavit of Compliance (JD-HM-41) before judgment.

This is Connecticut’s notice to quit in the words Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(b) sets. The Judicial Branch’s own form, JD-HM-7 (Notice to Quit (End) Possession), says the same; the court accepts either.

Since October 1, 2025 only a proper officer can serve it: give it to a state marshal, who serves an attested copy on every adult tenant and occupant and completes the return of service. Mail and hand delivery by you are not allowed.
Name every lessee and occupant. An occupant whose name you don’t know can be named “John Doe” or “Jane Doe” (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(b)).
Attach the Judicial Branch’s Right to Counsel (CT-RTC) notice (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-75(f)(2)): jud.ct.gov, linked from form JD-HM-7.

Three full days: neither the day it is served nor the quit date counts, and the tenant has until midnight of the quit date. Weekends count, and it may be served on any day of the week (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23(c)).
Write the town where you sign it beside the date: the statute’s form asks for the date and place of signing.
Connecticut has no separate demand for possession: this notice to quit is the notice the court needs before a summary process case.
Tenants who are 62 or older or have a disability, living in a building or complex of 5 or more units, can be evicted only for a reason Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23c lists.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (JD-HM-32, JD-HM-8, JD-HM-20)
forms.explain: What to put on the Judicial Branch’s summary process forms, where to get them, and the deadlines after you file.
forms.when: The quit date in the notice to quit has passed and the tenant is still there.
notes: Connecticut’s eviction is “summary process” in the Superior Court: the Housing Session where there is one, otherwise the judicial district court. You choose where the tenant lives or where the premises are (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-23a(b)).
Use the Judicial Branch’s forms: the summons (JD-HM-32) and the complaint for nonpayment (JD-HM-8) or lapse of time (JD-HM-20). This worksheet tells you what goes on them.
There is no court complaint form for a lease violation or a nuisance: that complaint is drafted by hand (Practice Book § 10-29). Ask a lawyer.
A state marshal serves the summons and complaint. If you represent yourself, the clerk signs your summons.

A company (an LLC or a corporation) should appear through a lawyer: Connecticut courts generally require it (NOHM couldn’t confirm the rule’s text). If there is more than one plaintiff, all may have to sign and appear.
The Judicial Branch’s guide, A Landlord’s Guide to Eviction (JDP-HM-14), walks through each form.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: For a lease entered into on or after January 1, 2024, you must offer the tenant a walk-through before they move in. If they ask for one, use the Department of Housing’s Pre-Occupancy Walk-Through Checklist, and both sign duplicate copies; a condition noted on it can’t be charged against the security deposit (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7c). The checklist is on the Department of Housing’s mandatory forms page.
This checklist is a record of its own; it doesn’t replace the Department’s checklist when the tenant asks for the walk-through.

From April 1, 2026, every written lease must have the Department of Housing’s Rental Terms Summary Form, completed, as its first page; otherwise a civil penalty of one month’s rent (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7d(c)).
Before or at the start of the tenancy, give the tenant in writing the name and address of the manager and of the person who receives notices and service (§ 47a-6(a)).
In a building or complex of 5 or more units, give the Department of Housing’s notice to protected tenants (Form AM-011) at the start of every tenancy and every renewal (§ 47a-23c(e)).
Within 30 days of receiving a security deposit, tell the tenant in writing the amount and the escrow bank’s name and address (§ 47a-21(h)(4)(A)): use the escrow notice.

Other papers: whether the unit or a unit next to it you own has bed bugs (§ 47a-7a(c)); the fire sprinkler statement in 12-point bold where one is required (§ 47a-3f); a receipt for every cash payment, and the ledger on request (§ 47a-3a); the federal lead-paint disclosure for a home built before 1978.
A security deposit can’t be more than two months’ rent, or one month’s for a tenant 62 or older (§ 47a-21(b)).

forms.label: Security deposit escrow notice
forms.explain: Tells the tenant how much deposit you hold and the bank holding it in escrow.
forms.when: Within 30 days after you receive a security deposit.
notes: Put the whole deposit in an escrow account at a financial institution in Connecticut right away (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(h)(1)), and send this within 30 days of receiving it.
The deposit earns interest at no less than the deposit index the Banking Commissioner sets each year, paid on each anniversary of the tenancy or credited toward rent (§ 47a-21(i)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Connecticut asks for “reasonable” notice, written or oral, and entry at reasonable times; it sets no hours. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.

Without the tenant’s consent you may enter only in an emergency, during a long absence (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-16a), with a court order, or after the tenant abandoned or surrendered the unit (§ 47a-16(d)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 31 days before the new rent starts.
notes: A rent increase takes effect only after written notice at least 45 days ahead; for a tenancy of a month or less, notice as long as one full term (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4e). For a month-to-month NOHM asks for 31 days, the longest month. For a lease longer than a month, give 45.
A tenant who doesn’t answer the notice hasn’t agreed to the increase. You can’t raise the rent during a lease’s term unless it allows it.

No statewide cap. A tenant protected by § 47a-23c (62 or older, or with a disability, in 5 or more units) may be charged only a fair and equitable increase, which they can challenge before the town’s fair rent commission (§ 47a-23c(c)).
No increase within 6 months after a tenant’s good-faith code or fair rent complaint, repair request, or union activity (§ 47a-20).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 21 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Send the deposit and accrued interest, less damages, with this statement, within 21 days after the tenancy ends or 15 days after the tenant gives you a forwarding address in writing, whichever is later (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(d)(2)).

You may deduct unpaid rent or utility charges owed to you, damage beyond the tenant’s duties under § 47a-11, and the reasonable cost of a lock change the tenant didn’t pay; not a condition noted on the move-in walk-through checklist (§§ 47a-21(a), 47a-7c).
Include interest at no less than the deposit index for each year, except for any month the tenant was more than 10 days late with rent, unless you charged a late fee for it (§ 47a-21(i)).
Missing the deadline costs twice the deposit; missing only the interest, $10 or twice the interest, whichever is more (§ 47a-21(d)(2)).

forms.label: Notice of belief of abandonment
forms.explain: Tells an occupant who seems to have left for good that you will reenter, and how long their belongings will be kept.
forms.when: The occupant left without notice: most belongings gone, and rent unpaid over two months or they said they won’t return.
notes: Abandonment means the occupant left without notice and doesn’t intend to return: they removed substantially all their belongings, and either haven’t paid rent for more than two months or said they won’t be back (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-11b).
Send it to each occupant’s last-known address both by regular mail and by certified mail, return receipt requested. It must give your phone number and mailing address.

If they don’t contact you within 10 days of receiving it, you may reenter without a notice to quit or a court case. Inventory what’s left, remove it, and keep it at least 30 days after the notice; then you may dispose of it as you see fit (§ 47a-11b(c)–(d)).

Not for after an eviction: then the state marshal moves belongings to the town’s storage (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-42). If the sole occupant died, § 47a-11d’s different notice and Probate Court steps apply; ask a lawyer.

forms.label: 7-day notice to pay rent
forms.explain: Demands the past-due rent within 7 days, or the landlord may file to end the rental agreement.
forms.when: Rent is past due and the 5-day late-fee window has passed (8 days if you keep no payment office in the county).
notes: Wait until the late-fee grace period has passed: 5 days after the due date, or 8 if you keep no office in the county where rent can be paid (25 Del. C. §§ 5501(d), 5502(a)).
The 7 days count from the day after it’s given or sent; mailing adds nothing. If the 7th day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the period runs to the next business day (25 Del. C. § 5112).

You may not refuse rent paid by or for the tenant; you may limit payment to the methods the lease allows (25 Del. C. § 5502(c)). If all rent due is paid after you file, you may not go on with the case (§ 5502(d)).
Attach the Courts’ Right to Representation notice (25 Del. C. § 5606): courts.delaware.gov/forms/download.aspx?id=224598.
Email and text messages are not valid ways to give notice in Delaware. Keep the return receipt or the certificate of mailing (PS Form 3817): either is evidence of service (25 Del. C. § 5113(b)).

forms.label: 7-day notice to remedy a breach
forms.explain: Names the rule or lease term broken and gives the tenant 7 days to remedy it.
forms.when: The tenant broke a material rule or covenant of the lease (not late rent).
notes: Name the rule or lease term the tenant broke, and what they did: the notice must substantially specify it (25 Del. C. § 5513(a)(1)).
A breach you can fix yourself (cleaning, a repair, a replacement): you may do it and bill the tenant the actual reasonable cost, due as additional rent on receipt (§ 5513(a)(2)).

A breach that is also a material breach of a code, ordinance or statute lets you terminate and file (§ 5513(a)(3)). One that causes or threatens irreparable harm to a person or property lets you terminate at once on notice and file, without the 7 days (§ 5513(b)).
