Late rent isn’t a breach under this section: use the 7-day notice to pay rent.
A landlord renting 3 or fewer rooms in their own home has its own rules (25 Del. C. § 5512).
Attach the Courts’ Right to Representation notice (25 Del. C. § 5606): courts.delaware.gov/forms/download.aspx?id=224598.
Email and text messages are not valid ways to give notice in Delaware. Keep the return receipt or the certificate of mailing (PS Form 3817): either is evidence of service (25 Del. C. § 5113(b)).

forms.label: 60-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month 60 days after the 1st of the month following the day the tenant gets it.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, or not to renew a lease (60 days before it ends).
notes: Sixty days, counted from the 1st of the month after the tenant actually gets it (25 Del. C. § 5106(d)). NOHM adds 3 days for a notice you mail.

A lease with a fixed term also needs 60 days’ written notice before it ends, and the notice must say the agreement terminates on its expiration date (§ 5106(c)). Without it, a lease of a year or more becomes month-to-month (§ 5108(a)).

Delaware has no separate demand for possession: once this notice runs out, a tenant who stays is holding over, and you can file for summary possession (25 Del. C. § 5702(1)). Holdover damages can reach double the monthly rent, prorated by the day (§ 5515(b)).
Delaware sets no separate notice for a week-to-week tenancy; a tenancy with no stated term is month-to-month (§ 5106(b)).

The Right to Representation notice is required with this notice when the tenancy can be ended only for good cause (§ 5602(b)(1)); the Courts’ notice says to attach it to every termination notice, so NOHM lists it.
Attach the Courts’ Right to Representation notice (25 Del. C. § 5606): courts.delaware.gov/forms/download.aspx?id=224598.
Email and text messages are not valid ways to give notice in Delaware. Keep the return receipt or the certificate of mailing (PS Form 3817): either is evidence of service (25 Del. C. § 5113(b)).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (J.P. Civil Form No. 1, CF83A)
forms.explain: What to put on the Justice of the Peace Court’s complaint for summary possession, where to get the forms, and the deadlines after you file.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid, remedied the breach, or left.
notes: File in the Justice of the Peace Court that hears civil cases in the county where the rental is (25 Del. C. § 5701), on J.P. Civil Form No. 1, checking “Summary Possession (LLT) – Residential Unit”.
Attach a copy of the notice you served: the complaint must have it as an exhibit (§ 5707(4)).
A corporation, LLC or other entity filing without a lawyer must file Form 50, Certificate of Representation (Supreme Court Rule 57).

Every case goes to mediation first (eviction diversion). File the Landlord’s Affidavit of Participation in Eviction Diversion Program (CF83A) at least 5 days before the hearing, with a copy to the tenant.

In a rent case the tenant can redeem the tenancy by paying everything the court sets, with costs and fees, at any time before the writ is executed, unless they had 2 nonpayment judgments in the past 18 months (§ 5716A). The court gives its effective date as September 1, 2026; NOHM couldn’t confirm that date from the session law.
The court also names a breakdown-of-amounts form (CF13LT) and a right-of-redemption motion (CF20RR); NOHM hasn’t read them.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Delaware doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It’s good practice: it is your evidence of damage beyond normal wear and tear when the deposit comes back.

Give the tenant the Attorney General’s Summary of the Delaware Residential Landlord-Tenant Code at the start of the tenancy; without it, the tenant may plead ignorance of the law (25 Del. C. § 5118). The current edition is on the Attorney General’s site.
Give the Right to Representation notice at lease signing, and at the first renewal (25 Del. C. § 5606).
Every written lease must prominently disclose the names and usual business addresses of the owners or their resident agents (§ 5105(a)); give the tenant a free copy of the signed lease (§ 5105(b)).

Hold the deposit in a security deposit account at a federally insured bank with an office in Delaware, and tell the tenant where it is (§ 5514(b)). The deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent for a lease of a year or more, unless the unit is furnished (§ 5514(a)).

Before renting, inspect for bed bugs and tell the tenant if a unit next door is infested or being treated (§ 5317). A tenant-employee gets the written disclosure § 5123(b) describes. Give a receipt for rent paid in cash (§ 5501(e)).

Coming: the Rights and Responsibilities Guide (§ 5124, by June 10, 2027 at the latest) and Delaware’s lead-safe certificate disclosures (§§ 5406–5407, by March 1, 2028). Today, the federal lead-paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: At least 48 hours’ notice, and enter only between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m.; choose a time window inside those hours (25 Del. C. § 5509(b)).
No notice is needed for repairs the tenant asked for, or in an emergency. For showing the unit to prospective tenants or buyers, the tenant may waive the 48 hours in a signed addendum.
Don’t abuse the right of entry or use it to harass the tenant.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 60 days before the new rent starts.
notes: To renew with a new rent, give at least 60 days’ written notice before the rental agreement expires, saying the new rent and the date it takes effect (25 Del. C. § 5107(a)).
Applying the 60 days to a month-to-month is the common and the safe reading; the statute speaks of a rental agreement’s expiration and doesn’t name month-to-month tenancies. NOHM couldn’t confirm it.

The tenant is deemed to accept unless they give notice of termination at least 45 days before the last day of the term; a tenant who rejects the renewal has given notice to end the tenancy (§ 5107(b)–(c)).
No statewide cap. An increase within 90 days after a tenant’s protected complaint is presumed retaliatory (§ 5516(c)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 20 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 20 days after the rental agreement ends, send the itemized list of damages with the estimated cost of repair of each, and pay the difference; if you don’t, you’ve acknowledged no damages are due (25 Del. C. § 5514(e)–(f)).

You may keep: damage beyond normal wear and tear, or that painting and ordinary cleaning can’t correct; unpaid rent and late charges, including rent for an early termination or abandonment; and reasonable costs of re-renting after an early termination (§ 5514(c)).

Send it to the forwarding address the tenant gave you in writing, or to the rental unit; if they gave none, you aren’t liable for double damages, but they may claim the deposit for a year (§ 5514(h)).
Wrongful withholding costs double the amount withheld (§ 5514(g)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Delaware has no procedure for belongings a tenant leaves without a court case: property is handled after a judgment for summary possession.
At the writ, you may remove and store what’s left for 7 days at the tenant’s expense; then it’s abandoned (25 Del. C. § 5715(e)). The writ itself carries the court’s notice to the tenant.
After a judgment for a tenant who abandoned the unit, if there’s no appeal you may remove and store the items; seven days after the appeal period ends they’re abandoned (25 Del. C. § 5507(e)).
Photograph the property before you move or dispose of it.

forms.label: 30-day notice of past due rent (intent to file)
forms.explain: The statute’s notice of the rent owed, with a ledger: pay in full and stay, or the landlord may file.
forms.when: At least $600 in rent is past due.
notes: D.C. Law 26-80 (eff. Dec. 31, 2025) cut the wait before filing to 10 days, but the words the statute prescribes for this notice still say “within 30 days of this notice”, and so does the regulation (14 DCMR 4300.6–4300.7). NOHM uses the longer, safer 30 days: don’t file before the 31st day after service.
Don’t serve it unless the tenant owes at least $600 in rent; you can’t file for less (D.C. Code §§ 42-3505.01(a-1)(1), 16-1501(b)).

Deliver it both ways: by certified mail (or a tracked delivery service), return receipt requested, AND by hand delivery to the unit or posting on the front door. If you post it, take a photograph with a readable timestamp: the court will ask for it (§ 42-3505.01(a-1)(3)). NOHM counts from the later delivery, adding 3 days for the mail.
Attach the ledger of charges and payments for the months behind.
The tenant can stay by paying the full balance, and, once a case is filed, by paying it in full before the eviction (redemption).

D.C. notices must be served in English and Spanish, and also in the tenant’s primary language if you know (or should know) it is another language D.C. law covers (14 DCMR 4300.22; D.C. Code § 42-3206). NOHM prints English: serve a Spanish translation with it.
To file, you’ll also need a valid rental registration or claim of exemption and a current basic business license for rental housing (D.C. Code § 16-1501(c)).
A corporation or partnership (treat an LLC the same) can’t appear in the Landlord and Tenant Branch without a lawyer who is a member of the D.C. Bar (L&T Rule 9(b)).

forms.label: 30-day notice to correct or vacate
forms.explain: States the violation, the lease provision or regulation, and what to do to correct it within 30 days.
forms.when: The tenant is violating a substantial lease obligation (not rent) within the last 6 months.
notes: Describe the violation in enough detail for the tenant to understand it, name the lease provision or Housing Regulation that creates the obligation, and say exactly what the tenant must do to correct it (14 DCMR 4301.4).
Only a substantial obligation in a valid lease or in the Housing Regulations counts, never the rent (14 DCMR 4301.2). You can’t serve this notice for a violation more than 6 months old (4301.3).

Fill in the Rental Accommodations Division’s address and phone (dhcd.dc.gov) and the Office of Human Rights’ contact information (ohr.dc.gov) on the lines in the statements: the regulation requires both (4301.4(d), 4301.6(b)).
Within 5 business days after serving it, file a copy with the Rent Administrator, with a certification of how the tenant was served (14 DCMR 4300.8).

Serve it in person; if the tenant has left the District or can’t be found, on a person over 16 living there; or, after at least two tries at different times of day, by posting it (with a timestamped photograph) and mailing it first-class within 3 calendar days (14 DCMR 4300.25–4300.26). NOHM adds 3 days for the mail.
A violent or dangerous crime has its own 10-day notice to vacate, and an illegal act a court has found has a 30-day notice to vacate (D.C. Code § 42-3505.01(c)). Ask a lawyer before using either.

D.C. notices must be served in English and Spanish, and also in the tenant’s primary language if you know (or should know) it is another language D.C. law covers (14 DCMR 4300.22; D.C. Code § 42-3206). NOHM prints English: serve a Spanish translation with it.
A corporation or partnership (treat an LLC the same) can’t appear in the Landlord and Tenant Branch without a lawyer who is a member of the D.C. Bar (L&T Rule 9(b)).

forms.label: Notice to vacate (only for a cause D.C. law lists)
forms.explain: D.C. doesn’t let a landlord end a tenancy because the lease is over; possession is recovered only for a cause the law lists.
forms.when: Only for a listed cause, such as the owner’s own use; ask a lawyer first.
notes: Don’t use this to end a tenancy because a lease is over: in D.C. that isn’t a ground for eviction.

The causes the law allows include an illegal act a court has found (30 days), the owner’s own use (90 days), a sale to a buyer for their own use (90 days, after the tenant’s purchase rights), substantial rehabilitation (120 days), and demolition or ending housing use (180 days), each with its own conditions (D.C. Code § 42-3505.01(c)–(i)). Ask a lawyer first.
There’s no separate demand for possession in D.C.

D.C. notices must be served in English and Spanish, and also in the tenant’s primary language if you know (or should know) it is another language D.C. law covers (14 DCMR 4300.22; D.C. Code § 42-3206). NOHM prints English: serve a Spanish translation with it.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Forms 1A, 1B, 1C, 1S)
forms.explain: What to put on the Superior Court’s mandatory complaint forms, where to get them, and the deadlines after you file.
forms.when: The notice’s 30 days have run and the tenant hasn’t paid or corrected the violation.
notes: A complaint for possession must be filed on the court’s Form 1A, 1B or 1C, verified under oath before a notary, with a prepared Form 1S (L&T Rule 3(a)). The clerk won’t take a homemade complaint.
A corporation or partnership can’t appear in the Landlord and Tenant Branch without a member of the D.C. Bar (L&T Rule 9(b)); the rule doesn’t name LLCs, so treat an LLC the same.

You can’t file a rent case for less than $600, or any case without a valid rental registration or claim of exemption and a current basic business license for rental housing (D.C. Code § 16-1501(b)–(c)).
NOHM counts the notice’s 30 days before filing: the statute now says 10 for a rent case, but the notice’s prescribed words and the regulation still say 30.
The court’s Supplement for rent cases dates from 2022 and still lists pandemic-era items; ask the clerk which it still requires.
The rule on serving the summons (L&T Rule 4) was amended in 2026 to follow the RENTAL Act; NOHM couldn’t read the order. Check with the clerk.

forms.label: Final notice of the eviction date (21 days)
forms.explain: The notice D.C. requires at least 21 days before the eviction: the date, the warning about belongings, and the phone numbers.
forms.when: The court issued the writ and the Marshals gave you an eviction date.
notes: Deliver it at least 21 days before the eviction date, all three ways: by phone or electronic message (email or text), by first-class mail to the rental unit, and by posting it conspicuously at the unit (D.C. Code § 42-3505.01a(b)(1)). Without it, the court may stop the eviction (§ 42-3505.01a(g)).
Fill in the phone numbers of the U.S. Marshals Service and the Landlord and Tenant Branch.
Serve it in Spanish too, with the tenant’s primary language if it is another one D.C. law covers.
On the eviction day you must also post and mail the day-of-eviction notice, with the text of § 42-3505.01a(c)–(d); NOHM doesn’t have that text.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: D.C. doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It’s good practice: it is your evidence of damage beyond ordinary wear and tear when the deposit comes back.

When a prospective tenant applies, give the Rent Administrator’s disclosure form with its documents: the rent, rent-control status, registration, business license, code violations, the deposit and its interest, any indoor mold in the past 3 years not professionally remediated, the Office of the Tenant Advocate’s Tenant Bill of Rights, and the voter registration packet (D.C. Code § 42-3502.22(b)). Tell each tenant where the full disclosure file is kept.
At the start of every tenancy, give a copy of 14 DCMR chapter 3 (the landlord-tenant housing regulations) and §§ 101 and 106 of chapter 1 (14 DCMR 300.1).

State the security deposit terms in the lease or the receipt (14 DCMR 308.6). The deposit can be no more than the first full month’s rent, charged once, held in an interest-bearing escrow account at a D.C. financial institution (308.2–308.3).
A late fee is allowed only if the written lease states its maximum (D.C. Code § 42-3505.31(b)).

For rent-controlled units, the notice of the maximum increase for elderly and disabled tenants (§ 42-3502.08). For a new building exempt from the tenant’s purchase rights, the exemption notice before the lease (§ 42-3404.02b(d)).
Lead: the federal disclosure for homes built before 1978; D.C. adds its own lead disclosures, which NOHM hasn’t confirmed.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: Written notice at least 48 hours ahead, unless the tenant agrees in writing to less. Enter between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., not on a Sunday or federal holiday, unless the tenant agrees to another time (D.C. Code § 42-3505.51).
Email or text counts as written notice; if the tenant doesn’t acknowledge it in writing, give a paper notice.
In an emergency you may enter without notice.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 61 days before the new rent starts.
notes: An increase takes effect only on the first rent day more than 60 calendar days after the notice is given (D.C. Code § 42-3509.04(b)): NOHM requires 61 days.

For a rent-controlled unit the increase must also meet § 42-3502.08: the unit registered, licensed and in substantial compliance with the housing code; no more than once in 12 months; and for an occupied unit no more than the adjustment of general applicability plus 2%, and never over 10%. The notice must give the current and new rent, the utilities, a summary of the tenant’s rights and a list of help sources.
No increase during a lease that fixes the rent. Whether the 60 days reach rent-control-exempt units isn’t settled in the text; NOHM applies them to every unit.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends, either return the deposit and interest, or tell the tenant in writing, personally or by certified mail, what you’ll withhold; then refund the balance with this itemized statement within 30 days of that notice (14 DCMR 309.1–309.2). Sending this statement with the refund within 45 days does both.

Since August 14, 2026 the notice of unpaid amounts must include photographs or other documentation, a statement of the tenant’s right to dispute, and your contact information; the tenant has 30 days to dispute and you 10 days to answer (D.C. Code § 42-3502.17(e)). Ask the tenant for a forwarding mail or email address when the tenancy ends. Email is allowed for this notice.
No deduction for ordinary wear and tear, including breakage or malfunction from age (§ 42-3502.17(c)). Unpaid invoiced late fees may be deducted (§ 42-3505.31(d)).
Interest at the statement savings rate for each six-month period is due on a tenancy of 12 months or more (14 DCMR 311). Enclose the list of rates.
Missing the deadline makes the tenant prima facie entitled to the whole deposit; bad faith costs triple (14 DCMR 309.3, 309.5).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Only after an eviction carried out by the U.S. Marshals. D.C. has no procedure for belongings of a tenant who leaves without one, and a landlord may not remove a tenant’s property except as § 42-3505.01a allows.

Store it with reasonable care, give at least 16 hours of access between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. over no more than 2 days, and charge nothing for it. After 7 days (not counting Sundays and federal holidays) it is abandoned: remove or dispose of it, never by putting it outdoors except at a licensed disposal facility or receptacle (D.C. Code § 42-3505.01a).
NOHM fills in the date 7 days after the eviction, not counting Sundays and federal holidays.

forms.label: 3-day notice to pay rent or deliver possession
forms.explain: The statute’s 3-day notice: pay the rent or give back the premises, weekends and legal holidays not counted.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Florida sets no grace period; your lease may).
notes: The statute’s form is printed word for word. Your name, address and phone number must appear on it (they print as the landlord’s, and under your signature).
Florida sets no grace period: serve it any time after rent is late, unless your lease gives the tenant longer.
Only court-observed legal holidays are skipped by law; NOHM skips every federal holiday and a few more, so its date is never early.

Accepting the full past-due rent, knowing of the default, waives this nonpayment. If you accept partial rent after serving it, you must give a receipt with the date, amount and the new balance due before you file, put the partial rent in the court registry when you file, or serve a new 3-day notice for the new amount (Fla. Stat. § 83.56(5)(a)).
No separate demand for possession is needed: if the rent isn’t paid by the date, the rental agreement can be terminated and you may file for possession in county court.

Deliver it by mail, by handing the tenant a true copy, by leaving a copy at the residence if the tenant is absent, or by e-mail if you both signed the § 83.505 e-mail addendum (an e-mail is delivered when sent unless it bounces; keep a copy and proof of sending). NOHM adds 5 days when it’s mailed. A lease can’t waive these notices (Fla. Stat. § 83.56(4)).

forms.label: 7-day notice to cure
forms.explain: The statute’s 7-day notice: fix the noncompliance, or the lease is terminated.
forms.when: The tenant broke the lease in a way they can fix (pets, guests, parking, cleanliness).
notes: For a noncompliance the tenant can fix: for example unauthorized pets, guests or vehicles, unauthorized parking, or not keeping the premises clean and sanitary (Fla. Stat. § 83.56(2)(b)). Describe it after “You are hereby notified that”.
If the same or similar conduct happens again within 12 months, you may file without another notice.

Some violations get no chance to cure: intentional destruction, damage or misuse of property, fraudulent entry of a dwelling (from October 1, 2026), or a repeated or continuing unreasonable disturbance, or a similar violation within 12 months of a written warning. Use the 7-day notice to vacate (no cure) for those (Fla. Stat. § 83.56(2)(a)).
Accepting rent knowing of the noncompliance waives your right to terminate for it, though not for a continuing one (§ 83.56(5)(a)).

Deliver it by mail, by handing the tenant a true copy, by leaving a copy at the residence if the tenant is absent, or by e-mail if you both signed the § 83.505 e-mail addendum (an e-mail is delivered when sent unless it bounces; keep a copy and proof of sending). NOHM adds 5 days when it’s mailed. A lease can’t waive these notices (Fla. Stat. § 83.56(4)).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month at the end of a monthly period, at least 30 days after the tenant gets it.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: For a month-to-month: not less than 30 days before the end of a monthly period (Fla. Stat. § 83.57(3)). The other periodic tenancies differ: week to week 7 days before the end of a weekly period, quarter to quarter 30 days, year to year 60 days before the end of the annual period (§ 83.57(1), (2), (4)).
A fixed-term lease ends on its date. A lease may require notice of nonrenewal only if it requires it of both of you, between 30 and 60 days (§ 83.575(1)).

No separate demand for possession is needed: a tenant who stays after the tenancy ends without your permission is holding over, and you may file for possession and ask for double rent for the holdover (Fla. Stat. § 83.58).
Local governments can’t add their own notice rules: the state law preempts them (§ 83.425).

Deliver it by mail, by handing the tenant a true copy, by leaving a copy at the residence if the tenant is absent, or by e-mail if you both signed the § 83.505 e-mail addendum (an e-mail is delivered when sent unless it bounces; keep a copy and proof of sending). NOHM adds 5 days when it’s mailed. A lease can’t waive these notices (Fla. Stat. § 83.56(4)).

forms.label: 7-day notice of termination (no chance to cure)
forms.explain: The statute’s notice that the lease is terminated now, with 7 days to vacate, for a violation the tenant can’t cure.
forms.when: Intentional damage, fraudulent entry, a repeated unreasonable disturbance, or a repeat within 12 months of a written warning.
notes: For noncompliance the tenant shouldn’t be given a chance to cure: destruction, damage or misuse of your or other tenants’ property by intentional act; fraudulent entry of a dwelling unit under § 817.537(2) (from October 1, 2026, whether or not criminal charges were brought); a subsequent or continued unreasonable disturbance; or a similar violation within 12 months of a written warning (Fla. Stat. § 83.56(2)(a)).
The words are the statute’s own form. Say exactly what happened after “This action is taken because”.
The 7 days run from delivery. NOHM adds 5 days if you mail it.
For a violation the tenant can fix, use the 7-day notice to cure instead.
Accepting rent knowing of the noncompliance waives your right to terminate for it (§ 83.56(5)(a)).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Forms 5, 5a, 6, 7)
forms.explain: What to put on the Florida Supreme Court–approved eviction forms, where to get them, and the deadlines after you file.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid, cured, or left.
notes: File in the county court of the county where the rental is (Fla. Stat. § 83.59(2)), on the Florida Supreme Court–approved forms from The Florida Bar. The Bar warns the forms aren’t guaranteed to track every change in the law: Form 1 still cites the 2007 statute and lacks the 2025 e-mail option.
Attach the lease as Exhibit A and the notice you served as Exhibit B.

Only you or your lawyer can act after filing: an agent who isn’t a lawyer may file the complaint and nothing more (§ 83.59(2)). A company (an LLC or a corporation) generally needs a Florida lawyer in court (NOHM couldn’t confirm the case law).
To collect past-due rent as well as possession, use Form 5a and the damages summons (Form 8); a money judgment needs personal service on the tenant.
There is no approved form for a holdover after a tenancy ended by notice or by its term; the complaint describes the unit and the facts that entitle you to it (§§ 83.58, 83.59(2)). Ask a lawyer.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Florida doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It’s good practice: it is your evidence for a claim on the deposit.
At or before the start of the tenancy, give the tenant in writing your name and address, or those of the person authorized to receive notices (Fla. Stat. § 83.50).

If you rent 5 or more units: within 30 days of receiving the deposit (or in the lease), tell the tenant where it is held, whether interest is paid, and give the capitalized disclosure Fla. Stat. § 83.49(2) prescribes word for word. NOHM doesn’t print that disclosure: copy it from the statute.

For a lease of a year or longer, give the flood disclosure in the form Fla. Stat. § 83.512 prescribes, as a separate document, at or before signing (since October 1, 2025). NOHM doesn’t print it: copy it from the statute.
Give the radon statement on a document signed at or before the lease (Fla. Stat. § 404.056(5)): use NOHM’s radon gas disclosure, or put the statement in the lease.

Optional statutory papers: the e-mail notice addendum (§ 83.505), the fee-in-lieu-of-deposit disclosures (§ 83.491), the abandoned-property legend in the lease (§ 83.67(5)). A lease that requires notice of nonrenewal must require it of both sides, 30 to 60 days (§ 83.575). The federal lead-paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.

forms.label: Radon gas disclosure
forms.explain: The radon statement Florida requires on a document signed at or before the rental agreement, in the statute’s words.
forms.when: At or before signing the lease.
notes: Florida requires this statement on at least one document signed at or before the rental agreement; it may be in the lease itself (Fla. Stat. § 404.056(5)).
Not needed for a transient stay of 45 days or less.
Have every adult tenant sign it, and keep it with the lease.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: For repairs: at least 24 hours’ notice, and enter between 7:30 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. (Fla. Stat. § 83.53(2)).

For other purposes (an inspection, a showing, agreed services) enter with the tenant’s consent, in an emergency, when the tenant unreasonably withholds consent, or when the tenant has been away for half a rental period, unless the rent is current and the tenant told you of the absence (Fla. Stat. § 83.53).
Don’t abuse the right of access or use it to harass the tenant.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Florida has no statute on notice of a rent increase. During a fixed-term lease the rent changes only as the lease allows. For a month-to-month, NOHM asks for 30 days, the notice that ends a monthly tenancy (Fla. Stat. § 83.57(3)), and starts the new rent on a due date: NOHM’s practice, not a statute.
No rent control: local governments can’t regulate tenancies (§ 83.425).
You can’t raise rent to retaliate against a tenant’s good-faith complaint (§ 83.64).

forms.label: Notice of intention to claim on the deposit
forms.explain: The statute’s notice of what you’ll deduct from the deposit, and why, giving the tenant 15 days to object.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the rental agreement ends, if you’ll keep any of the deposit.
notes: Within 30 days after the rental agreement ends, send this by certified mail to the tenant’s last known mailing address, or by e-mail under § 83.505. Miss it and you lose the right to claim against the deposit (Fla. Stat. § 83.49(3)(a)).
If you won’t claim anything, don’t send this: return the whole deposit, with any interest owed, within 15 days.
The tenant has 15 days after receiving it to object in writing. If they don’t, deduct the claim and send the balance within 30 days of the date of this notice (§ 83.49(3)(b)).
Add interest only if the deposit was in an interest-bearing account or under a surety bond (§ 83.49(1)).
A tenant who left without 7 days’ written notice, by certified mail or in person, with a forwarding address, relieves you of the notice requirement, but doesn’t forfeit the deposit (§ 83.49(5)).
The statute’s form is printed word for word; your address for objections is the one you give as yours.

forms.label: Notice of right to reclaim abandoned property
forms.explain: The statute’s notice to a former tenant of the property left behind, where to claim it, and by when.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: After the tenancy ends and the tenant has left, by eviction or otherwise, send this to the former tenant (and a similar notice to anyone you believe owns any of the property) personally or by first-class mail to the last known address and any other address you know (Fla. Stat. § 715.104).
The date to claim it must be at least 10 days after you hand it over, or at least 15 days after you mail it.

Store the property with reasonable care, on the premises or in a safe place (§ 715.107). If it’s worth $500 or more and isn’t claimed, it’s sold at a public sale after advertising once a week for two weeks; the balance goes to the county (§ 715.109). Under $500 you may keep, sell or destroy it.
If your lease carries the legend of Fla. Stat. § 83.67(5), you need not follow this procedure after the tenant surrenders or abandons the unit, or after the last tenant dies.
When the sheriff executes a writ of possession, you may remove property found on the premises to or near the property line instead (§ 83.62(2)).

forms.label: 3-business-day notice to vacate or pay
forms.explain: Demands all past-due rent, late fees, utilities and other charges within 3 business days, or the premises.
forms.when: Rent is past due, on a lease made or renewed on or after July 1, 2024.
notes: This notice is for leases made or renewed on or after July 1, 2024. For an older lease never renewed, use a demand for possession instead (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a)).
Georgia doesn’t define “business day” for this notice. NOHM skips Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, the reading that never gives too few days.
Georgia sets no grace period or late-fee cap: your lease does.

Once the case is served, the tenant can end it by paying all the rent claimed plus the cost of the dispossessory warrant within 7 days; you must accept that only once in any 12 months (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-52).
Post it in a sealed envelope on the door AND send it by every other way your lease says notices go (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(d)). Both are required for leases made or renewed on or after July 1, 2024.

If the tenant doesn’t pay or leave, you make a dispossessory affidavit under oath, before a magistrate, the court’s clerk or a notary, in the magistrate court of the county where the property is (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a), (c)).

forms.label: Demand for possession (lease violation)
forms.explain: Georgia has no notice to cure: where the lease ends the tenancy for a violation, you demand possession.
forms.when: The tenant broke the lease, and the lease says that ends the tenancy (after any cure period it gives).
notes: Georgia has no statutory notice to cure a lease violation, and no waiting period: your lease decides whether a violation ends the tenancy, and whether the tenant gets time to fix it first. If the lease gives a cure period, give it before you serve this.
Name the lease term that was broken, what happened, and the lease clause that ends the tenancy for it.
The statute sets no time to leave; NOHM lets you pick the date.
Public housing: the demand may go with the federal termination notice, in a separate writing (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(b)).
Post it in a sealed envelope on the door AND send it by every other way your lease says notices go (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(d)). Both are required for leases made or renewed on or after July 1, 2024.

If the tenant doesn’t pay or leave, you make a dispossessory affidavit under oath, before a magistrate, the court’s clerk or a notary, in the magistrate court of the county where the property is (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a), (c)).

forms.label: 60-day notice to end a tenancy at will
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy with no fixed term on 60 days’ notice.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month (a tenancy at will) to end, no fault needed.
notes: A tenancy with no fixed term (month-to-month included) is a tenancy at will: the landlord must give 60 days’ notice to end it, the tenant 30 (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-7). The date doesn’t have to end a rental period.
The statute doesn’t say how to deliver it. Hand it over or mail it certified and keep proof; NOHM adds 3 days for the mail.
A fixed-term lease ends on its own date with no notice required by statute.

A tenant who stays after the date is holding over: give a demand for possession (sealed envelope on the door and the lease’s method) before you file the dispossessory affidavit (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a), (d)).
You can’t end a tenancy to retaliate within 3 months after a tenant’s protected act (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-24).

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Georgia requires a demand for possession before you file a dispossessory affidavit, when a tenant holds over after the term, is a tenant at will or at sufferance, or (on a lease made before July 1, 2024 and not renewed) hasn’t paid rent (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a)).
The statute sets no waiting period: if the tenant refuses, you may file at once. NOHM fills in 3 days; give more if you like.
Post it in a sealed envelope on the door AND send it by every way your lease says notices go (§ 44-7-50(d)).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (MAG 30-02, MAG 30-08)
forms.explain: What to put on the magistrate court’s dispossessory affidavit, where to get the forms, and the deadlines after you file.
forms.when: The notice or demand ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid or left.
notes: File the dispossessory affidavit in the magistrate court of the county where the property is (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(a)), on the Council of Magistrate Court Judges’ statewide form, MAG 30-02. Most counties take it through their e-filing portal; counties brand the form.
You swear to the affidavit before a magistrate, the court’s clerk or deputy clerk, or a notary (§ 44-7-50(a), (c)).

A company (an LLC or a corporation) may be represented in magistrate court by a full-time employee or officer it designates on MAG 11-02 (the form cites O.C.G.A. § 15-10-43(i) and Uniform Magistrate Court Rule 31; NOHM read the form, not the rule). In superior or state court, use a lawyer.
Don’t cut off the tenant’s heat, cooling, light or water while the case is pending (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-14.1).
From January 1, 2027, a court may restrict public access to dispossessory records in some cases (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-50(e), SB 406).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Before the tenant pays the security deposit; both of you sign it.
notes: Before the tenant pays a security deposit, give them a comprehensive list of any existing damage. They may inspect the premises; you both sign it, or they dissent in writing; they keep it permanently (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-33(a), (c)).

Within 3 business days after the tenant moves out, inspect and make a list of any damage; the tenant may inspect within 5 business days (§ 44-7-33(b)). Without both lists you can’t keep any of the deposit (§ 44-7-35).

A natural person who, with spouse and minor children, owns 10 or fewer rental units and manages them without a paid manager is exempt from the lists and the escrow rule (§ 44-7-36). The lists are still good practice.
Give in writing, at or before the start of the tenancy, the names and addresses of the owner of record (or an agent for notices) and of the manager (§ 44-7-3).
If the living space flooded 3 or more times in the 5 years before the lease, tell the tenant in writing before signing (§ 44-7-20).

Tell the tenant in writing where the deposit is held in escrow (§ 44-7-31): use the escrow notice. The deposit can’t be more than two months’ rent on a lease made or renewed on or after July 1, 2024 (§ 44-7-30.1).

An owner out of state renting a single-family home or duplex must hire a Georgia-licensed broker, with someone in the state for tenants to deal with (§ 44-7-25). The federal lead-paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.

forms.label: Security deposit escrow notice
forms.explain: Tells the tenant in writing where the security deposit is held.
forms.when: When you take the security deposit.
notes: Keep the deposit in an escrow account used only for deposits, at a bank or lending institution regulated by Georgia or the United States, and tell the tenant in writing where it is (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-31).
Georgia also allows a surety bond instead (§ 44-7-32); NOHM hasn’t read that section.
Exempt: a natural person who, with spouse and minor children, owns 10 or fewer rental units and manages them without a paid manager (§ 44-7-36).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No Georgia statute sets notice, hours or reasons for a landlord’s entry; your lease does. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours’ notice and daytime hours.
In an emergency you may need to go in right away; tell the tenant as soon as you can.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 60 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Georgia statute sets notice for a rent increase; during a fixed-term lease the rent changes only as the lease allows. A tenancy at will (a month-to-month) can be ended only on 60 days’ notice (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-7), so NOHM gives 60 days to change its rent: NOHM’s practice, not a statute.
No statewide cap. Georgia bars local rent control (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-19; NOHM didn’t re-read it).
No rent increase within 3 months after a tenant’s protected act (§ 44-7-24).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after you get possession back, return the deposit, or send this written statement of the exact reasons for keeping any of it, by first-class mail to the tenant’s last known address (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-34).

You may keep: unpaid rent or late fees, rent lost to the tenant’s abandoning the premises, unpaid utilities and pet fees, the cost of repairs or cleaning the tenant contracted for, and actual damages beyond ordinary wear and tear (after mitigating).
Make the move-out list of damage within 3 business days after the tenant leaves; the tenant may inspect it within 5 business days (§ 44-7-33(b)).
If a refund comes back and you can’t find the tenant, it becomes yours 90 days after you mailed it.

Keeping it improperly costs three times the amount withheld plus attorney’s fees, and failing to follow the rules forfeits your right to keep any of it (§ 44-7-35). The 30-day rule applies even to an exempt small landlord (§ 44-7-36).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Georgia sets no notice, storage or sale procedure: once the writ of possession is executed, the tenant’s property is regarded as abandoned (O.C.G.A. § 44-7-55(c)). Holding it, and this notice, are NOHM’s courtesy, not the law’s.
For a tenant who left without an eviction, Georgia has no statute on their belongings; ask a lawyer before you dispose of anything.
Photograph the property before you move or dispose of it.

forms.label: 10-calendar-day notice for failure to pay rent
forms.explain: Demands the rent due within 10 calendar days of receipt, or the rental agreement ends; a copy goes to a mediation center.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Hawaii has no grace period).
notes: Since February 5, 2026, the notice must carry everything HRS § 521-68(b) lists, the warning in bold. NOHM prints each; write each tenant’s phone, and email and mailing address if you have them, and the mediation center’s name in the blanks.

Give a copy to a state-funded mediation center the same day, and keep proof: the court complaint must include the center’s verification, or your statement of how you sent it (HRS § 521-68(c)–(d)). On O‘ahu: The Mediation Center of the Pacific, (808) 521-6767, Landlordtenant@mediatehawaii.org, 1301 Young Street, 2nd Floor, Honolulu 96814. Each island’s form names its own center.
Post it on the unit (received that day) or mail it (received 2 business days after the postmark). The court’s complaint asks which of the two you used, so NOHM offers only those.

If mediation is scheduled within the 10 days and the tenant takes part, you can’t file until 20 calendar days after they received the notice, unless they don’t attend or cancel. If they schedule it, you must take part.
The mediation parts apply from February 5, 2026 through February 4, 2028; the 10 calendar days stay after that.
HRS § 1-29 moves a last day that is a Sunday or a holiday; NOHM also moves a Saturday, so the date is never early.
The Judiciary’s fillable form (RG-AC-508) is the courts’ version of this notice. Tenancies under the Maui wildfire proclamations have a separate 15-day notice (HRS § 521-84): ask a lawyer.

forms.label: 10-day notice of a rule violation
forms.explain: Names the rule broken, in the statute’s form: if it continues after the date, the rental agreement can end.
forms.when: The tenant broke a house rule they were told about when they signed.
notes: This is the form HRS § 521-72(a) sets out, for a rule you adopted under HRS § 521-52 and brought to the tenant’s attention when they entered the rental agreement. Name the rule and how it was broken.
For failing to keep the unit clean and safe or follow housing laws (HRS § 521-51), use the 10-day notice of noncompliance in the forms list.
No time to remedy is required when the breach causes or threatens damage to a person, or violates HRS § 521-51(1) or (6): ask a lawyer about ending the agreement without one.
If the breach continues or recurs after the date, you may bring a summary proceeding for possession within 30 days after that (HRS § 521-72(b)).
The law names no way to serve it: hand it to the tenant, or mail it (NOHM adds 2 business days).

forms.label: 45-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on any day at least 45 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: Any day at least 45 days out; it needn’t end a rental period (HRS § 521-71(a)).

Demolition, conversion to a condominium, or conversion to transient vacation rental use needs 120 days’ notice (§ 521-71(c)). A tenancy shorter than month-to-month: 10 days (§ 521-71(d)). A fixed-term lease ends on its date.

No demand for possession is needed after the tenancy ends. If the tenant stays, file for summary possession within the first 60 days of the holdover, or a month-to-month tenancy at the old rent begins; you may recover up to twice the monthly rent, prorated daily, for each day they stay (HRS § 521-71(e)).
A notice given to evade the 45-day rent-increase rule is void (§ 521-71(f)), and you can’t terminate to retaliate (HRS § 521-74).
The law names no way to serve it; hand it to the tenant and keep proof.

forms.label: 10-day notice of noncompliance (tenant’s duties)
forms.explain: Tells the tenant how they’re failing a duty under HRS § 521-51 and gives at least 10 days from receipt to fix it.
forms.when: The tenant isn’t keeping the unit clean and safe, is damaging it, or breaks a housing law.
notes: For a material noncompliance with the tenant’s duties in HRS § 521-51. After the time to remedy, you may end the agreement and sue for possession only if the noncompliance is with § 521-51(1), building and housing laws materially affecting health and safety; otherwise, fix it and bill the tenant, and the bill is rent due with the next rent (HRS § 521-69(a)).
No time to remedy is required when the noncompliance causes or threatens irremediable damage to a person or property: ask a lawyer.
Give at least 10 days after the tenant receives it. If you can’t serve the tenant, you may post it in a conspicuous place on the unit (§ 521-69(a)). Mailed, allow a few days for delivery.
For a broken house rule, use the 10-day rule-violation notice instead (HRS § 521-72).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Act 278 Complaint, 1DC08, 1DC50 Summons)
forms.explain: Hawaii’s district courts use the Judiciary’s summary possession forms: this lists them, fills in what to write on the complaint from the lease, and sets out the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid or left.
notes: The form numbers are the First Circuit’s (O‘ahu). The other circuits have their own versions (2DC on Maui, 3DC on Hawai‘i Island, 5DC on Kaua‘i, from search results; not opened): get yours from your island’s landlord forms page.
A company (an LLC or corporation) must be represented by a lawyer licensed in Hawaii; an individual landlord may represent themselves.
Nonpayment: attach the 10-day notice and the mediation center’s verification of receiving it (or your affirmation of how you sent it), and say where mediation stands (HRS § 521-68(d)).
If rent is disputed, either side can ask the court to order the tenant to pay it into court as it comes due; if the tenant doesn’t, you get judgment for possession (HRS § 666-21).
The Judiciary’s Act 278 landlord information sheet and FAQ explain the mediation rules.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Required: before the tenant first moves in, inventory the home and its furnishings and appliances in writing; you and each tenant sign duplicate copies, and each tenant gets one (HRS § 521-42(a)).
Without it, the home at move-out is presumed to be in the condition it was in at move-in (§ 521-42(a)), which makes damage hard to charge to the deposit.
Give the owner and manager disclosure, with your general excise tax number, at or before the start: it’s the next form.
If you live off the island where the unit is, name an agent who lives on that island in the written rental agreement (HRS § 521-43(f)).
Give the tenant a copy of the lease, a written receipt for rent when it’s paid (for a check, when the tenant asks), and your rules when they sign (HRS §§ 521-43(d)–(e), 521-52(a)).
At the start you may collect only the first month’s rent and the security deposit (HRS § 521-44(b)).
Built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Owner and manager disclosure
forms.explain: The written disclosure Hawaii requires at the start: who manages the home, who accepts rent, notices and legal papers for the owner, and your general excise tax number.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, and again when any of it changes.
notes: Required in writing at or before the start of the tenancy, and kept current (HRS § 521-43(a)). If you don’t, the person who signs the rental agreement for you becomes your agent (§ 521-43(b)); not fixing it within 10 days of the tenant’s demand can cost $100 and fees (§ 521-67).
Landlords must give all tenants their general excise tax number, for the low-income tax credit (§ 521-43(h)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: At least two days’ notice, and only during reasonable hours (HRS § 521-53(b)); in an emergency, or where it’s impracticable, you may enter sooner.

Don’t use entry to harass the tenant. Otherwise you may enter only by court order, if the tenant appears to have abandoned the unit, or while they’re away as reasonably necessary (§§ 521-53(c), 521-70(b)).
Repeated unreasonable entry lets the tenant end the agreement, and can bring an injunction and a fine (HRS § 521-73).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 45 days before the new rent starts.
notes: A month-to-month rent can’t go up without written notice given 45 consecutive days before the increase takes effect (HRS § 521-21(d)); a tenancy shorter than month-to-month needs 15 days (§ 521-21(e)).
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Hawaii has no statewide rent cap. You can’t raise rent to retaliate (HRS § 521-74), and a termination notice meant to evade this rule is void (§ 521-71(f)).
A late charge can’t be more than 8 per cent of the rent due (§ 521-21(f)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 14 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 14 days after the rental agreement ends, return the deposit, or notify the tenant in writing of what you keep and why, with written evidence of the costs: estimates, invoices or receipts (HRS § 521-44(c)). Miss it and you can’t keep any of it.
Mailed to an address the tenant gave you, with proof of mailing, postmarked before midnight of the 14th day, it is presumed on time.
A tenant who wrongfully quit (gone 20 or more days without notice or rent) isn’t owed this notice, and you may keep the whole deposit (§ 521-44(c)–(d)).
The deposit can’t exceed one month’s rent, plus a pet deposit of up to one month’s rent for a tenant with a pet (never for an assistance animal) (§ 521-44(b)).
Wrongful, wilful retention can cost three times the amount kept (§ 521-44(h)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Applies when the tenant has wrongfully quit, or left under a notice to quit or at the end of the term, and abandoned property you determine in good faith to be of value (HRS § 521-56(a)). Property of no value you may dispose of (§ 521-56(c)).

Before you sell or donate it, mail this notice to the tenant’s forwarding address, an address they gave for notices, or their previous known address. You may sell it only after advertising the sale in a daily paper in the circuit for at least three consecutive days, or donate it to a charity; not until 15 days after mailing.
You may also store it at the tenant’s expense. Hold sale proceeds, after rent and costs, in trust for the tenant for 30 days (§ 521-56(b)).

forms.label: 3-day notice to pay rent or vacate
forms.explain: Demands the rent due: pay it in 3 days, or hand back the home.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Idaho has no grace period), within a year of the due date.
notes: State the rent now due only, with no other fees or charges such as damage (Idaho courts’ instructions). The notice may demand payment or possession, not both.
Serve it any time within one year after the rent was due (Idaho Code § 6-303(2)). Serve any subtenant living there too.
Fees are recoverable only because the notice says attorney fees shall be awarded to the prevailing party (Idaho Code § 6-324); NOHM’s says so.
Where a copy is mailed, NOHM gives 3 more days: whether the court rule’s 3 days for mail reaches this notice isn’t settled.
The Idaho courts’ form for this notice is CAO UD 1; whoever serves it can use CAO UD 2, the Affidavit of Service, which you file with the complaint.
At trial you must show it was served at least 4 days before you filed (Idaho courts’ instructions).

forms.label: 3-day notice to perform or quit
forms.explain: Tells the tenant to do what the lease requires in 3 days, or hand back the home.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term other than paying rent.
notes: Describe the condition or covenant broken and what the tenant must do.

A breach that can’t afterward be performed needs no notice to perform (Idaho Code § 6-303(3)). Assigning, subletting or committing waste against the lease ends it, and needs only a 3-day notice to quit (§ 6-303(4)). Drug activity on the premises is its own ground (§ 6-303(5)). Ask a lawyer for those.
A lease-violation case isn’t on the expedited track: the tenant has 21 days to answer the complaint (I.R.C.P. 12(a)), and the Idaho courts’ eviction forms don’t cover it.
The prevailing party is entitled to attorney fees (Idaho Code § 6-324).

forms.label: One-month notice to end a tenancy at will
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month or other tenancy at will on a date at least one month and 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, or won’t renew a lease, no fault needed.
notes: Idaho requires at least one month (Idaho Code § 55-208(1)) and, for a residential lease, at least 30 days (§ 55-304(2)). A month can be 28 days, or 31, so NOHM counts 31 days, which meets both every month. Any day: it needn’t end a rental period.
A fixed-term lease you won’t renew needs the same 30 days’ written notice before it ends (§ 55-304(2)). After the term ends, no further demand is needed before you file (§ 6-303(1)).
This notice is the only notice before court: Idaho needs no separate demand for possession. After the date passes, and not before, you may go to court (§ 55-209).
The statute says to serve it “in the manner prescribed by the code of civil procedure”; NOHM reads that as the § 6-304 methods.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (CAO UD 1-1, 1-2, 2-1, 8-1, 10-1)
forms.explain: Idaho’s courts use the Court Assistance Office’s statewide eviction forms: this lists them, fills in what to write on the complaint from the lease, and sets out the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The 3-day notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid or left.
notes: The Court Assistance Office forms are for eviction for unpaid rent (the expedited track). They can’t be used for another lease violation or a holdover: that complaint must be written to the facts and verified (Idaho Code § 6-318), and the tenant has 21 days to answer. Use a lawyer for it.

The owner must be the plaintiff and sign the complaint. A property manager or other agent can’t represent the owner unless they’re an Idaho lawyer (CAO instructions). A company (an LLC or corporation) generally must appear through a lawyer (from a case summary; not confirmed in the case itself).
Asking for damages as well as possession takes the case off the expedited schedule (Idaho Code § 6-311E).
The filing fee shown by the Court Assistance Office is $166; issuing the writ is $2.
Bring the lease, the notice and its affidavit of service, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Idaho doesn’t require a move-in checklist; the Attorney General’s manual includes a sample, and a signed record helps with the deposit. Verifying the smoke detectors at the start is required (Idaho Code § 6-320(a)(6)), and this form records it.
List every fee in the written rental agreement: a fee not in it needs 30 days’ written notice (Idaho Code § 55-305(2)).
Write the deposit’s contingencies into the lease: only they can be deducted (Idaho Code § 6-321(1)).
Built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No Idaho statute sets notice before entry; your lease should. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
If the lease is silent, the Attorney General advises telling the tenant why you need to enter and agreeing on a reasonable time.
In an emergency involving life or property you may need to go in right away; tell the tenant as soon as you can.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: A residential landlord must give written notice of a rent increase at least 30 days before it takes effect (Idaho Code § 55-304(2)).
A new or changed fee not in the written rental agreement also needs 30 days’ written notice (Idaho Code § 55-305(2)).
Idaho has no rent cap, and cities and counties can’t regulate rent, fees or deposits (Idaho Code § 55-306).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 21 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Refund the deposit within 21 days after the tenant surrenders the home, or the time the lease fixes, never more than 30 days (Idaho Code § 6-321(2)).
Any refund less than the full deposit needs this signed, itemized statement, with a detailed list of what was spent from it.
Deduct only for the contingencies the deposit arrangement names, never normal wear and tear (§ 6-321(1)).
A third-party manager must keep deposits in a separate account at a federally insured institution (§ 6-321(4)).
A tenant can sue for a deposit not returned as the law requires, after 3 days’ written notice; damages can be trebled, and the prevailing party gets attorney fees (Idaho Code §§ 6-320, 6-317, 6-324).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: No Idaho statute covers property left after a tenant moves out on their own; this letter isn’t a statutory notice. NOHM fills in 14 days to hold it.

For property of value, the Attorney General advises filing an eviction complaint and asking the court for an order allowing its removal, and permission to sell it to cover costs or back rent. Idaho gives landlords no lien on it unless the lease does.

forms.label: 5-day notice to pay rent
forms.explain: Demands the rent owed: pay it in full within 5 days, or the lease is terminated.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Illinois has no grace period).
notes: The Illinois Supreme Court’s Notice of Termination for Unpaid Rent (ATJ 3502.3) is the courts’ version of this notice; NOHM’s carries the statute’s required words, the FULL PAYMENT sentence printed prominently (735 ILCS 5/9-209).
Demand rent only. From January 1, 2027, you can’t charge a fee for an eviction notice (765 ILCS 705/35(c)(4)).
If the tenant pays the full amount within the period, the lease goes on. A partial payment doesn’t stop the notice unless you agree in writing to continue the lease.
Mailed certified or registered: the period starts when it’s delivered, so NOHM adds 3 days. Post it only if no one is living there.
Whoever serves it fills out the Supreme Court’s Affidavit of Service of a Demand or Notice (ATJ 3507.3); you attach it to the eviction complaint.
If it isn’t paid, file the eviction the day after the period ends; no further notice or demand is needed (735 ILCS 5/9-209).
Chicago, suburban Cook County and other cities may require more.

forms.label: 10-day notice of termination (lease violation)
forms.explain: Ends the lease for a default in its terms and tells the tenant to leave in 10 days.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term other than paying rent.
notes: This is the form of notice 735 ILCS 5/9-210 sets out. Describe the default so it reads in the sentence “in consequence of your default in ___ of the premises”, for example “keeping a dog, against the lease’s no-pets clause,”.

Illinois gives no right to cure. If your lease or a local ordinance (Chicago’s, for one) gives the tenant one, the notice must say so and give at least 10 days to fix it; ask a lawyer, or use the Supreme Court’s form (ATJ 3503.3), which has a box for it.
You or your agent must sign it (735 ILCS 5/9-210). Whoever serves it fills out the Affidavit of Service of a Demand or Notice (ATJ 3507.3).
Using the premises for a felony or Class A misdemeanor lets you void the lease; the tenant then has 5 days after a written notice to vacate (735 ILCS 5/9-120). Ask a lawyer.
Watch for defenses: domestic or sexual violence (735 ILCS 5/9-106.2), immigration status (§ 9-106.3), and retaliation (765 ILCS 721).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at the end of a rental period at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A tenancy for any term under a year other than week-to-week ends on 30 days’ written notice (735 ILCS 5/9-207(b)). The Illinois courts’ instructions start the period at the beginning of the next rental month, so NOHM ends it on the last day of a rental period at least 30 days out.
Week-to-week: 7 days (§ 9-207(a)). Year-to-year: 60 days before the end of the year (§ 9-205).

No further demand is needed before you file once this notice ends the tenancy (735 ILCS 5/9-208), and none when a fixed-term lease runs out (§ 9-213), so NOHM has no separate demand for possession in Illinois.
To claim double rent from a tenant who wilfully holds over, you need a written demand for possession (735 ILCS 5/9-202): ask a lawyer.

Local law may require more. From the Illinois courts’ instructions (the ordinances weren’t re-read): Chicago, 60 days if the tenant has lived there more than 6 months but less than 3 years, 120 days for more than 3 years; suburban Cook County, 60 days before a lease you won’t renew ends.
You can’t refuse to renew to retaliate against a tenant (765 ILCS 721/5).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (ATJ 3508.4, 3510.4, 3507.3, Eviction Order 3601.7)
forms.explain: Illinois courts use the Supreme Court’s statewide eviction forms: this lists them, fills in what to write on the complaint from the lease, and sets out the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Print the forms from the Illinois courts’ approved eviction forms page and copy the values from this worksheet. Every Illinois court must accept them, and the judge uses the statewide Eviction Order (735 ILCS 5/9-109.6).
If a corporation or LLC owns the property, it must hire a lawyer; a property manager can’t file for the owner (Illinois courts’ instructions).
Don’t name a minor as a defendant: the whole case is dismissed and sealed, and naming one willfully can cost $1,000 (735 ILCS 5/9-106(b)–(d)).
Attorney’s fees can be asked for only if the lease provides for them, local law allows them, and a licensed attorney represents you (the complaint form).
Cook County cases start in the Early Resolution Program, and Chicago and suburban Cook County add their own rules.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Illinois doesn’t require a move-in checklist; a signed record of the condition helps when you itemize damage from the deposit (765 ILCS 710/1).

Since January 1, 2026, attach the Illinois Department of Human Rights’ Summary of Rights for Safer Homes as the first page of every written lease and renewal, and have each tenant sign the acknowledgment on each page (765 ILCS 752/20).
Give the radon disclosure and the flood disclosure: they’re the next two forms.
A written lease must say that using the premises for a felony or Class A misdemeanor lets you void the lease (735 ILCS 5/9-120(a)).
From January 1, 2027, every non-optional fee must be on the first page of the lease, with whether utilities are included in the rent, and many fees are banned (765 ILCS 705/35).
Charging for master-metered utilities needs the allocation formula in writing first (765 ILCS 740/5).
Built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Radon disclosure
forms.explain: The Disclosure of Information on Radon Hazards to Tenants, in the words Illinois law sets out.
forms.when: With the lease application or before the lease is signed, with IEMA’s “Radon Guide for Tenants”.
notes: Give it, with the Illinois Emergency Management Agency’s pamphlet “Radon Guide for Tenants” and copies of any records or reports showing a radon hazard in the unit, at the tenant’s application or before the lease is signed (420 ILCS 46/26(a)).
It applies to leases entered on or after January 1, 2024, and not to units on the third story or higher above ground (420 ILCS 46/20, 46/26(g)).
Initial each line that applies, by hand; the tenant does the same, and both of you sign.
You can’t deduct radon testing or mitigation from the deposit (420 ILCS 46/30(c)).

forms.label: Flood disclosure
forms.explain: Whether the home is in a FEMA flood zone and has flooded, in the form Illinois law sets out.
forms.when: Before the lease or a renewal is signed; put it in the lease too.
notes: Since January 1, 2025, tell the tenant in writing, before they sign, whether the home is in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area and, as far as you know, whether and how often it has flooded; for a garden, basement or first-floor unit, its flooding in the last 10 years (765 ILCS 705/25(b)–(c)).
The same disclosure must be in the written lease or renewal, signed by both of you (765 ILCS 705/25).
If you don’t, the tenant may end the lease within 30 days, with a refund within 15 days, and recover damages (705/25(e)).
Search FEMA’s flood map by address before you answer.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Illinois has no statewide law on notice before entry; your lease decides. NOHM suggests at least 48 hours.
Local ordinances may set it: Chicago, Evanston, Oak Park and suburban Cook County require 2 days, Urbana 24 hours (from secondary sources; the ordinances weren’t re-read).
In an emergency you may need to go in right away; tell the tenant as soon as you can.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Illinois statute sets the notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date; ending a month-to-month itself takes 30 days’ notice (735 ILCS 5/9-207(b)).
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Illinois has no rent cap, and local governments can’t control rents (50 ILCS 825/5).
You can’t raise rent to retaliate against a tenant (765 ILCS 721/5); doing so can cost two months’ rent or twice the damages.
Chicago may require more notice (from secondary sources; not re-read).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: To keep any of the deposit for damage, give this statement, with paid receipts or copies, within 30 days after the tenant moves out or their right of possession ends, whichever is later (765 ILCS 710/1(a)). Without it, return the whole deposit within 45 days after they move out.
Deliver it in person, by postmarked mail to their last known address, or by email to a verified address they gave you.

If you give estimates, send the paid receipts within 30 days after the statement. If you did the work yourself, you may include the reasonable cost of your labor. With no receipts, attach the cost list and your verified statement of why you can’t produce them (710/1(b)).
Where the lease sets a cost for cleaning or repairing a component, refer to that amount and attach that part of the lease.
With 25 or more units in a building or complex, interest is owed on deposits held more than 6 months (765 ILCS 715): enter it on the form.
Refusing in bad faith can cost twice the deposit, with costs and attorney’s fees (710/1(c)). You can’t deduct radon testing or mitigation (420 ILCS 46/30(c)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Illinois has no statewide law for property a tenant leaves behind; this letter isn’t a statutory notice. NOHM fills in 14 days to hold it.
After an eviction order, ask the sheriff’s office about removing personal property from the unit.
Chicago’s ordinance has its own rules. Ask a lawyer before you dispose of anything of value.

forms.label: 10-day notice to pay rent or vacate
forms.explain: Tells the tenant to pay the rent due within 10 days of getting it, or move out.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Indiana has no grace period).
notes: This is the form of notice Ind. Code § 32-31-1-7 sets out. If the tenant pays the rent in full before the notice period ends, the lease isn’t terminated (§ 32-31-1-6).
Your lease can set a different period (§ 32-31-1-6(1)).

Indiana provides no mail service for this notice: hand it to the tenant; if they can’t be found, to a person living there, explaining what it says; if no one is there, fix it to a conspicuous part of the premises (§ 32-31-1-9).
Some tenancies need no notice (§ 32-31-1-8), but the courts advise giving one when in doubt; NOHM always does.

Demand rent only; late fees only if the written lease provides for them (Indiana Small Claims Manual). If you’ve accepted late rent before, first tell the tenant in writing that late payment will be treated as a breach.
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Notice of noncompliance (lease violation)
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what they’re doing wrong and gives them a reasonable time to fix it.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term or a tenant duty (not rent).
notes: Indiana has no statute for a notice to end a lease for a breach other than rent: your lease decides (its forfeiture clause). Pick the date yourself; at least 10 days is a fair time to fix most breaches.

This notice is also the notice Ind. Code § 32-31-7-7(b) requires before you sue a tenant for not meeting their duties (following codes, keeping the unit clean, not damaging it, following reasonable rules, keeping smoke detectors working), with a reasonable time to fix it.

Waste, a crime by a tenant or guest affecting others’ health or safety, or materially false information on the application: you can ask the court for an emergency possessory order, heard within 3 business days (Ind. Code § 32-31-6). Ask a lawyer.
Unpaid rent isn’t a violation for this notice: use the 10-day notice to pay rent or vacate.

forms.label: One-month notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at the end of a rental period at least a month out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A tenancy at will ends on one month’s written notice delivered to the tenant (Ind. Code § 32-31-1-1), and a periodic tenancy of 3 months or less on notice equal to the interval between periods (§ 32-31-1-4). The statute doesn’t say the date must end a rental period, but that is how the interval reads; NOHM ends it on the last day of one. A month can be 28 to 31 days and the courts’ manual says at least 30, so NOHM counts 31.
Week-to-week: 7 days (§ 32-31-1-4). Year-to-year: 3 months before the year ends, in the statute’s own form (§§ 32-31-1-3, 32-31-1-5).
A fixed-term lease ends on its date, and no notice is needed (§ 32-31-1-8); nor is a separate demand for possession after this notice runs.
Not renewing a lease at the end of its term isn’t retaliation (Ind. Code § 32-31-8.5-5(b)(1)).
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (CCA-EV-0321-8001)
forms.explain: Indiana’s statewide small claims eviction form: this names it, fills in what to write on it from the lease, and sets out the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: The Small Claims Complaint and Clerk’s Notice of Claim for Possession, Rent Due and Damages is approved statewide by the Indiana Supreme Court’s Coalition for Court Access; some counties (Marion, for one) use their own. Ask the clerk which to file.

In small claims a company may be represented by counsel, its owner, or a designated full-time employee with the certificate and affidavit Small Claims Rule 8(C) requires. A building manager can’t sue in their own name: the landlord must bring it.

Waste, a crime by a tenant or guest affecting others’ safety, or lies on the application: an emergency possessory order is a separate, faster petition (Ind. Code § 32-31-6). Unpaid rent isn’t a ground for it.
Bring the lease, the notice and how you served it, and the rent ledger.
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: When you deliver the unit, the tenant must acknowledge in writing that it has a functional smoke detector (Ind. Code § 32-31-5-7(a)); this form records it. The room-by-room checklist isn’t required, but the Small Claims Manual advises a walk-through and photos.
Give the owner and manager disclosure at or before the start: it’s the next form.
If the lowest floor, basement included, is at or below the 100-year flood elevation, say clearly in the rental agreement that the structure is in a flood plain (Ind. Code § 32-31-1-21(b)).
Built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Owner and manager disclosure
forms.explain: The written disclosure Indiana requires at the start: who in Indiana manages the home, and who accepts notices and legal papers for the owner.
forms.when: At or before the start of the rental agreement.
notes: Required in writing at or before the start of the rental agreement (Ind. Code § 32-31-3-18(a)). Both people must live in Indiana; the agent must be reasonably accessible to the tenant.
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Indiana requires reasonable written or oral notice and entry at reasonable times, but sets no number of hours (Ind. Code § 32-31-5-6(g)). NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.

In an emergency that threatens the occupants’ safety or your property you may enter without notice; without consent, only by court order or if the tenant abandoned or surrendered the unit (§ 32-31-5-6(f)).
Don’t use entry to harass the tenant. It applies to rental agreements entered into or renewed after June 30, 1999.
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
