forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Unless a written rental agreement provides otherwise, give at least 30 days’ written notice before modifying the rental agreement, a rent increase included (Ind. Code § 32-31-5-4).
Indiana has no rent cap, and local governments can’t regulate rents (Ind. Code § 32-31-1-20(b)).
Raising rent to what comparable rentals charge isn’t retaliation (Ind. Code § 32-31-8.5-5(b)(2)).
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Mail the itemized list of damages, with a check or money order for the rest of the deposit, within 45 days after the tenancy ends and you get possession back (Ind. Code §§ 32-31-3-12(a), 32-31-3-14).
You’re not liable until the tenant gives you, in writing, a mailing address to send it to.

List the estimated cost of repair for each damaged item. Deduct only damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, rent owed (and rent for leaving early), and utility or sewer charges you paid for the tenant (§ 32-31-3-13).
Miss it and you’ve agreed no damages are due: the whole deposit must be returned, and you can owe the amount withheld plus attorney’s fees (§§ 32-31-3-15, -16).
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: Notice of order to remove property left behind
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the court ordered their property removed, and where it will be stored: personally served before you move it.
forms.when: The court awarded you possession and ordered the tenant’s property removed.
notes: Property a reasonable person would conclude the tenant left when they vacated and surrendered possession is abandoned, and you aren’t liable for it (Ind. Code § 32-31-4-2(a)–(b)); a lease can’t define abandonment differently.

Otherwise, ask the court that awarded you possession for an order allowing removal of the tenant’s property (§ 32-31-4-2(d)). You may deliver it to a warehouse or a court-approved storage facility only after this notice, of the order and of the facility’s identity and location, is personally served on the tenant at their last known address (§ 32-31-4-3(a)). Attach a copy of the order.
Exempt property (§ 32-31-4-1: among it medical items, tools of the trade, a week’s clothing, blankets and children’s school items) must be released without payment (§ 32-31-4-3(b)).
The storage facility may sell property not claimed within 45 days after the tenant receives this notice (§ 32-31-4-5, as amended in 2025).
Never take or keep a tenant’s property to make them pay (Ind. Code § 32-31-5-5(a)).
Read from an unofficial copy of the Indiana Code current to 2024 (the official site couldn’t be opened), checked against the 2025 and 2026 session laws.

forms.label: 3-day notice of nonpayment of rent
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid and the rental agreement ends unless they pay within 3 days.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid when due (Iowa has no grace period).
notes: Iowa has no grace period: rent is payable without demand when due, so you can serve this the day after (Iowa Code § 562A.9(3)).
Serve it one of the three ways Iowa Code § 562A.29A(1) allows. Simply handing it over without a signed, dated acknowledgment from a resident 18 or older is not one of them.

Posted and mailed: post it on the main entrance door, write the posting date on it, and mail it both regular and certified. Service is complete 4 days after mailing (§ 562A.29A(2)); NOHM adds those days.
If the rent isn’t paid in the 3 days, you can file for forcible entry and detainer without a separate notice to quit (Iowa Code § 648.3(1)).
Late fees are capped (Iowa Code § 562A.9(4)) and aren’t part of this notice.
Accepting rent knowing of the default can waive your right to terminate for it (Iowa Code § 562A.30(1)).
A tenant who gave you 7 days’ written notice before rent was due and fixed a repair you were required to make, costing up to a month’s rent, has a defense (Iowa Code § 562A.27(4)).
Iowa moves a last day that is a Sunday to Monday (Iowa Code § 4.1(34)); NOHM also moves a Saturday or a holiday, so the date is never early.

forms.label: 7-day notice of noncompliance
forms.explain: Specifies the breach: remedy it in 7 days, or the rental agreement terminates.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease, or a duty that affects health and safety.
notes: For a material breach of the lease, or of a tenant duty in Iowa Code § 562A.17 that materially affects health and safety. Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do.

If substantially the same breach recurs within 6 months, you can end the agreement on at least 7 days’ written notice specifying the breach and the termination date, with no chance to remedy (Iowa Code § 562A.27(1)).
A clear and present danger (assault or threats, illegal firearm use, controlled substances) has its own 3-day notice with no cure (Iowa Code § 562A.27A): it’s in the forms list.
After the agreement terminates, serve a 3-day notice to quit before you file (Iowa Code § 648.3(1)): it’s in the forms list.
If the tenant fails to maintain the unit, you may instead give 7 days’ written notice to remedy, then fix it and bill the cost with the next rent (Iowa Code § 562A.28).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a rental date at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A month-to-month tenancy ends on a periodic rental date, with at least 30 days’ written notice (Iowa Code § 562A.34(2)); NOHM ends it on the last day of a rental period.
Week-to-week: 10 days’ notice (§ 562A.34(1)). A term longer than month-to-month that renews: 30 days before the end of the term (§ 562A.34(3)).
If the tenant stays after the date, serve a 3-day notice to quit before you file (Iowa Code § 648.3(1)): it’s in the forms list.
You can’t end a tenancy to retaliate against a tenant (Iowa Code § 562A.36).

forms.label: 3-day notice: clear and present danger
forms.explain: Ends the tenancy, with no chance to cure, for activity that is a clear and present danger, and tells the tenant to quit in 3 days.
forms.when: A tenant or someone there assaulted or threatened someone, used a firearm illegally, or had illegal drugs.
notes: A clear and present danger includes physical assault or threats of it, illegal use or threatened use of a firearm, and possession of a controlled substance (Iowa Code § 562A.27A(2)); lawfully storing a firearm is not one.
State the specific activity. The notice must set out subsection 3 of the statute word for word; NOHM prints it.
Serve it one of the three ways Iowa Code § 562A.29A(1) allows; posted and mailed, service is complete 4 days after mailing, so give 4 more days.

After the 3 days you may file for forcible entry and detainer without another notice. If the tenant gives you written proof, before you file, that they took one of the measures in subsection 3 against someone else who caused the danger, this route isn’t open against them.
Ask a lawyer before you use it: it ends the tenancy without a chance to cure.

forms.label: 3-day notice to quit
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Iowa requires this 3-day notice to quit before you file for forcible entry and detainer, on every ground except unpaid rent after the 3-day rent notice (Iowa Code § 648.3(1)).

Serve it one of the three ways Iowa Code § 648.3(2) allows: personal service, a resident 18 or older signing and dating an acknowledgment, or posting on the main entrance door (with the posting date) and mailing by both regular and certified mail. Mailed, service is complete 4 days after mailing (§ 648.3(3)): give 4 more days.
File within 30 days after the cause of action accrues: thirty days’ peaceable possession with your knowledge bars the case (Iowa Code § 648.18).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Small Claims Forms 3.6 and 3.1)
forms.explain: Iowa’s clerk takes only the Supreme Court’s forms: this lists them, fills in what to write on each from the lease, and sets out the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Iowa’s standard small claims forms are the only forms a small claims case may use (Iowa Code § 631.15): print them from the Iowa courts’ site and copy the values from this worksheet.

An individual, partnership or company may bring the case; a company may be represented by an officer or employee, and an employee or a property manager may bring it for owners who are individuals (Iowa Code § 631.14). Appear in person at the hearing unless a lawyer appears for you.
Bring the lease, the notice and your proof of serving it, and the rent ledger to the hearing.
The filing fee is $115 for fees paid on and after July 1, 2026 (Iowa Code § 631.6(1)(a)).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Iowa doesn’t require a move-in checklist, but deductions are measured against the unit’s condition at the start of the tenancy (Iowa Code § 562A.12(3)(a)(2)): a signed record is good practice.
Before the lease is signed, fully explain utility rates, charges and services the tenant doesn’t pay the utility directly for (Iowa Code § 562A.13(4)).
Give the owner and manager disclosure, and say whether the property is on the federal Superfund (CERCLIS) list, in writing before the tenancy starts (Iowa Code § 562A.13(1), (6)): it’s the next form.
Built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.
Late fees in the lease must stay within Iowa’s caps (Iowa Code § 562A.9(4)), and some lease terms are prohibited (Iowa Code § 562A.11).

forms.label: Owner and manager disclosure
forms.explain: The written disclosure Iowa requires before the tenancy starts: who manages the home, who accepts notices and legal papers for the owner, and whether it’s a Superfund site.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, and again when any of it changes.
notes: Required at or before the start of the tenancy, and kept current (Iowa Code § 562A.13(1)–(2)). If you don’t, the person who signs the rental agreement for you becomes your agent for service and for performing the landlord’s obligations (§ 562A.13(3)).
Check whether the property is listed in the EPA’s Superfund information system (CERCLIS) before you answer.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ notice and enter only at reasonable times (Iowa Code § 562A.19(3)). In an emergency you may enter without consent (§ 562A.19(2)).

Don’t use entry to harass the tenant. Other than this, you may enter only by court order, while the tenant is away more than 14 days as reasonably necessary, or after they abandon or surrender the unit (§§ 562A.19(4), 562A.29).
Give it any way Iowa Code § 562A.8 allows: in hand, by regular and certified mail, posted, or any way it actually reaches the tenant.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Each tenant must be notified in writing at least 30 days before the increase takes effect, and not before the end of the lease term or any renewal (Iowa Code § 562A.13(5)).
Iowa has no rent cap, and cities may not limit rents (Iowa Code § 364.3(9)).
You can’t raise rent to retaliate against a tenant (Iowa Code § 562A.36).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you receive the tenant’s mailing address or delivery instructions, return the deposit or give this statement (Iowa Code § 562A.12(3)). Miss it and you lose the right to keep any of it (§ 562A.12(4)).

Deduct only unpaid rent and other money due under the lease, restoring the unit to its move-in condition (not ordinary wear and tear), and costs of getting possession from a tenant who didn’t leave in good faith. Name the damage where you keep money for it. The burden of proof is yours.
Interest earned during the first five years of a tenancy is yours; after that it belongs to the tenant: enter it on the form.
If the tenant gives no address within one year after the tenancy ends, the deposit becomes yours (§ 562A.12(4)).

The deposit can’t exceed two months’ rent, and must be held in a federally insured account, not mixed with your own money (§ 562A.12(1)–(2)). Keeping it in bad faith can cost up to twice the monthly rent on top of actual damages (§ 562A.12(7)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Iowa Code chapter 562A has no procedure for property a tenant leaves behind, and landlords can’t hold it for rent (distraint is abolished, § 562A.31(2)). This letter isn’t a statutory notice.
NOHM fills in 14 days to hold it; no statute sets a period. Ask a lawyer before you dispose of anything of value.
Mobile homes and manufactured-home communities follow their own law (Iowa Code ch. 555B, § 562B.27).

forms.label: 10-day notice of nonpayment and notice to quit
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid and that the lease ends if it isn’t paid in 10 days; it is also the notice to leave the premises.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Kansas has no grace period).
notes: Kansas has two rules for unpaid rent. The Residential Landlord and Tenant Act gives the tenant 3 days to pay (K.S.A. 58-2564(b)); an older law that was never repealed gives a tenant for three months or longer 10 days’ notice to quit (K.S.A. 58-2507). No Kansas court has said which one controls, so NOHM gives 10 days, the longer and safer period. Ten days also meets the 3-day rule.
Rent is due without demand on the day the lease sets; Kansas has no grace period (K.S.A. 58-2545(c)). You can serve this the day after rent is unpaid.

If you mail it, the law allows two more days from the date of mailing (K.S.A. 58-2564(b); 61-3803); NOHM adds them. The 10th day moves to the next business day if it falls on a weekend or legal holiday (K.S.A. 60-206(a)).

Deliver it in hand, or leave it with someone over 12 who lives there; post it on the home only if no such person is there; or mail it to the tenant at the home (K.S.A. 61-3803). Keep proof of how and when.

Taking late rent without reservation waives your right to end the lease for that late payment (K.S.A. 58-2566). If you take a partial payment, say in writing that you accept it with reservation of your rights.
This notice is also the notice to leave the premises every Kansas eviction lawsuit needs (K.S.A. 61-3803): if the rent stays unpaid past the date, you can file without another notice.

forms.label: 14-day notice to remedy a breach (30 days to terminate)
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong: fix it in 14 days, or the lease ends at least 30 days after they get the notice.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease (other than rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the statute requires the notice to specify the acts and omissions that are the breach. It must be a material breach of the rental agreement, or of the tenant’s duties that materially affects health and safety (K.S.A. 58-2564(a); 58-2555).
Tell the tenant they can fix it: leaving out the right to remedy can cost you the rent after they leave (Fenn v. Windsor at Kingsborough, 226 Kan. 653).

If the same or a similar breach happens again after the 14 days, the law lets you end the agreement on 30 days’ notice after receipt with no chance to remedy it (K.S.A. 58-2564(a)). NOHM’s notice always offers the 14 days; giving more than the law requires is allowed.
A tenant who refuses you lawful access can be given this notice too (K.S.A. 58-2571(a)).
You can’t evict a tenant on the basis of, or as a direct result of, their being a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking or stalking (K.S.A. 58-25,137).

The statute doesn’t say how to deliver this notice; NOHM uses the ways K.S.A. 61-3803 allows for the notice to leave, which this notice also is. Deliver it in hand, or leave it with someone over 12 who lives there; post it on the home only if no such person is there; or mail it to the tenant at the home (K.S.A. 61-3803). Keep proof of how and when. The 14 and 30 days run from receipt: NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a rent-paying date at least 30 days after the tenant gets it.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: The tenancy must end on a rent-paying date at least 30 days after the tenant receives the notice (K.S.A. 58-2570(b)); NOHM ends it with the rental period that closes the day before. NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.
A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice instead (K.S.A. 58-2570(a)). A tenant in the military with orders needs to give you only 15 days.

A lease for a definite term ends on its own date with no notice. If the tenant stays, give the notice to leave the premises (NOHM’s demand for possession) at least 3 days before you file (K.S.A. 61-3803). This notice is that notice for a month-to-month: no second one is needed.
A tenant who holds over willfully and not in good faith can owe up to 1½ months’ rent or 1½ times your actual damages, whichever is greater (K.S.A. 58-2570(c)).
You can’t end a tenancy to retaliate against a tenant’s good-faith complaint to a code agency or to you, or for joining a tenants’ union (K.S.A. 58-2572).
If you ask the tenant to sign a move-out paper with terms not in the lease, it must carry the warning K.S.A. 58-2570(e) sets, in at least 10-point bold type.

Deliver it in hand, or leave it with someone over 12 who lives there; post it on the home only if no such person is there; or mail it to the tenant at the home (K.S.A. 61-3803). Keep proof of how and when.

forms.label: Notice to leave the premises (3 days)
forms.explain: The written notice to leave every Kansas eviction lawsuit needs, delivered at least 3 days before you file.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Every Kansas eviction lawsuit needs a written notice to leave the premises delivered at least 3 days before you file (K.S.A. 61-3803). The 3 days are three 24-hour periods from the hour it is delivered or posted, weekends and holidays included; if you mail it, allow 2 more days from the date of mailing.

NOHM’s rent, lease-violation and month-to-month notices already include this notice. Use this one when a lease for a fixed term ran out, or when the notice that ended the tenancy didn’t tell the tenant to leave.
Hand it to the tenant, or leave it with someone over 12 who lives there; post it only if no such person is there; or mail it to the tenant at the home. Keep proof of how and when.
If the tenant is still there after the date, file the petition for eviction: see NOHM’s filing worksheet.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Kansas Judicial Council forms)
forms.explain: Everything the Kansas Judicial Council’s eviction forms ask for, filled in from the lease, with where to get each form and the steps and deadlines after filing.
forms.when: The lease has ended or been terminated, the notice to leave has run, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Kansas’s courts use the Kansas Judicial Council’s statewide eviction forms. Fill those in from this worksheet; this worksheet isn’t filed.

The Judicial Council’s site couldn’t be opened while NOHM researched it, so the form titles and dates come from its listing, and the values here follow what the statute requires a petition to say (K.S.A. 61-3804). Check each form for anything else it asks.

An individual landlord may file for themselves. A business (an LLC or a corporation) generally must file through a licensed attorney: the Shawnee County District Court says so in writing, and Kansas follows the common-law rule outside small claims. NOHM couldn’t confirm a statewide rule; ask the clerk.
Bring the lease, the notice and your proof of how it was delivered, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Joint move-in inventory
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition and the furnishings and appliances, made together with the tenant and signed by both.
forms.when: Within 5 days after the tenant moves in: walk through it together, both sign two copies, and give the tenant one.
notes: Kansas requires it: within 5 days after the tenant moves in or gets possession, you (or your representative) and the tenant inventory the home together, write down its condition and any furnishings or appliances, both sign two copies, and the tenant keeps one (K.S.A. 58-2548).

Required in writing at or before the start of the tenancy: the name and address of the manager and of the owner or the owner’s agent for legal papers and notices (K.S.A. 58-2551). Use NOHM’s owner and manager disclosure.
A deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent for an unfurnished home, 1½ months’ for a furnished one, plus up to ½ month’s for a pet (K.S.A. 58-2550(a)).
A lease can’t make the tenant waive their rights, confess judgment, pay your attorney’s fees, or excuse you from liability (K.S.A. 58-2547).
Kansas requires no mold, flood, bed bug or smoke detector disclosure. A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Disclosure of manager and owner
forms.explain: Tells the tenant in writing who manages the home and who receives legal papers and notices for the owner.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, and again whenever it changes.
notes: Required in writing at or before the start of the tenancy (K.S.A. 58-2551(a)), and kept current (§ 58-2551(b)).
Anyone who fails to give it becomes your agent for service of process and for receiving notices and demands (K.S.A. 58-2551(c)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Kansas requires reasonable notice and entry at reasonable hours, but sets no number of hours (K.S.A. 58-2557(a)). NOHM suggests at least 24 hours; your lease may say more.

In an extreme hazard involving the potential loss of life or severe property damage you may enter without the tenant’s consent (K.S.A. 58-2557(b)). If the tenant is away more than 30 days, you may enter at times reasonably necessary (§ 58-2565(b)).
Don’t abuse the right of access or use it to harass the tenant (K.S.A. 58-2557(c)); the tenant may end the lease or recover damages (§ 58-2571).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Kansas statute sets the notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date: a month-to-month can’t be ended on less (K.S.A. 58-2570(b)), so the tenant has the same time to decide.
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
No rent cap, and cities and counties can’t control rents (K.S.A. 12-16,120).

You can’t raise rent to retaliate against a tenant’s good-faith complaint to a code agency or to you, or for joining a tenants’ union; an increase from a good-faith rise in your costs is allowed (K.S.A. 58-2572).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 14 days after you work out the deductions, and no later than 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Deduct only accrued rent and the damage from the tenant’s failure to follow the lease or their duties under K.S.A. 58-2555, each itemized in writing (K.S.A. 58-2550(b)).

Return the balance within 14 days after you work out the deductions, and never more than 30 days after the tenancy ends, you get the home back and the tenant asks for it. If the tenant doesn’t ask within 30 days after the tenancy ends, mail what’s due to their last known address (K.S.A. 58-2550(b)).
Keeping a deposit wrongfully lets the tenant recover what was due plus damages of 1½ times the amount wrongfully withheld (K.S.A. 58-2550(c)).

No interest or separate account is required. The deposit cap is one month’s rent unfurnished, 1½ months’ furnished, plus ½ month’s for a pet (K.S.A. 58-2550(a)). The tenant can’t use it as the last month’s rent unless the lease allows it (§ 58-2550(d)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Use it once the tenant has abandoned or surrendered the home, or after the writ of restitution is executed (K.S.A. 58-2565(d)). You may presume abandonment when the tenant is 10 days behind on rent and has removed a substantial part of their belongings, unless they told you otherwise (§ 58-2565(b)).

Store the property at the tenant’s expense. Publish this notice once in a newspaper of general circulation in the county at least 15 days before the sale, and mail a copy to the tenant’s last known address within 7 days after publishing. Sell or dispose of it no sooner than 30 days after you took possession of it (K.S.A. 58-2565(d)). NOHM fills in 30 days from this notice, which meets both.
The notice must state the tenant’s name, a brief description of the property and the approximate date of the sale (K.S.A. 58-2565(d)).

Apply the proceeds first to your costs of taking, storing, noticing and selling the property, then to what the tenant owes; you may keep the balance, except as to a secured creditor who gave you notice (K.S.A. 58-2565(e)).
Make reasonable efforts to rent the home again (K.S.A. 58-2565(c)).

forms.label: 7-day notice of nonpayment and intent to terminate
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid and the lease ends if it isn’t paid within 7 days of getting the notice.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Kentucky has no grace period).
notes: These rules apply where the city or county adopted the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (KRS 383.500). There is no official list; advocates list Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville. Ask your city or county.

Outside those areas no statute sets a notice to pay rent: the lease decides. The court’s complaint form (AOC-216) still asks the date you gave written notice to vacate, so serve this notice anyway; NOHM never gives less than 7 days.

Rent is due without demand when the lease says; Kentucky has no grace period (KRS 383.565(2)). The 7th day moves to the next business day if it falls on a weekend or legal holiday (KRS 446.030(1)(a)).
Taking rent while knowing of the default waives your right to end the lease for it, unless you both agree otherwise after the default (KRS 383.675).
Hand it to the tenant, or send it by registered or certified mail (KRS 383.560(3)(c)); regular mail and posting aren’t ways the Act allows. NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

forms.label: 15-day notice of breach and termination
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong; the lease ends on the date in it, at least 15 days out, unless they fix it first.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease (other than rent).
notes: These rules apply where the city or county adopted the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (KRS 383.500). There is no official list; advocates list Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville. Ask your city or county.

The statute sets the termination date at least 14 days after receipt, and also says the agreement ends if the breach isn’t remedied in 15 days (KRS 383.660(1)). NOHM uses 15 days, which meets both, and lets the tenant remedy it up to that date.
Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the notice must specify the acts and omissions that are the breach.

If substantially the same act or omission recurs within 6 months, the Act lets you end the agreement on at least 14 days’ written notice specifying the breach and the date, with no chance to remedy it (KRS 383.660(1)). NOHM’s notice always offers the remedy; giving more than the law requires is allowed.
A tenant who refuses you lawful access can be given this notice too (KRS 383.700(1)).
A notice to vacate substantially based on acts that violated a tenant’s protective order, or led to one, is a defense to eviction (KRS 383.300(3)(b)).
Outside the Act’s areas no statute sets this notice: the lease decides. The complaint form (AOC-216) has an “Other violation of lease” box and asks the date of your written notice to vacate.
Hand it to the tenant, or send it by registered or certified mail (KRS 383.560(3)(c)); regular mail and posting aren’t ways the Act allows. NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a rental date at least 30 days after the tenant gets it.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: These rules apply where the city or county adopted the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (KRS 383.500). There is no official list; advocates list Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville. Ask your city or county.

Outside those areas a tenancy at will ends on one month’s written notice requiring the tenant to remove (KRS 383.195). NOHM’s 30 days ending a rental period is at least a month in nearly every case; if the date it gives is before the same day next month, pick the next period end.

A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice (KRS 383.695(1)). A tenancy that began when a written lease ended needs 10 days’ written notice, and none if the tenant fails to pay rent within 10 days after it is due (KRS 383.695(3)).
If the tenant stays willfully and not in good faith, you may recover up to 3 months’ rent or three times your actual damages, whichever is greater, and reasonable attorney’s fees (KRS 383.695(4)).
You can’t end a tenancy in retaliation (KRS 383.705): a tenant’s complaint within the year before can make the court presume it was.
A lease for a fixed term ends on its own date; for a tenant who stays, use NOHM’s notice to vacate before you file.
Hand it to the tenant, or send it by registered or certified mail (KRS 383.560(3)(c)); regular mail and posting aren’t ways the Act allows. NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Kentucky sets no period for this notice, but the court’s complaint form (AOC-216) asks the date you gave the tenant written notice to vacate: give one before you file. NOHM fills in 7 days.
NOHM’s rent, breach and month-to-month notices are written notices to vacate too. Use this one when a lease for a fixed term ran out, or a tenancy ended another way.

Outside the Act’s areas, after a lease of less than a year ends you may recover possession without demand or notice if you file within 30 days after it ends; if you don’t, you can’t file until 60 days after it ended. For a lease of a year or more it is 90 days, then one year (KRS 383.160). The notice is good practice either way.
Hand it to the tenant or send it by registered or certified mail, and keep proof.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (AOC-216, AOC-215, AOC-220)
forms.explain: Everything the forcible detainer complaint (AOC-216) asks for, filled in from the lease, with where to get each court form and the steps and deadlines after filing.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Kentucky’s District Courts use the AOC’s forcible detainer forms. File AOC-216 filled in from this worksheet; this worksheet isn’t filed.
AOC-216 is sworn: sign it in front of the clerk or a notary. It certifies you are the owner or the attorney.

A business (an LLC or a corporation) must have an attorney file the complaint: Kentucky’s Court of Appeals has held one filed by a non-lawyer, a property manager included, is void. NOHM read only summaries of those cases.
Under the Act a notice by mail counts when it is mailed by registered or certified mail (KRS 383.560(3)(c)); NOHM counts from the date you enter.

forms.label: Move-in damage listing
forms.explain: The list of damage already in the home, with what each would cost to repair, signed by you and the tenant before the deposit is paid.
forms.when: Before the tenant pays the deposit: list the damage and its estimated repair cost, let them inspect, and both sign.
notes: Required where the Act applies: give the tenant this listing of existing damage, with the estimated cost of repairing each, before they pay the deposit; let them inspect; both sign (KRS 383.580(2)). Without it, and the move-out listing, you may not keep any of the deposit (§ 383.580(4)). This is a rule of the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, which applies only where the city or county adopted it (KRS 383.500): Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville, by advocates’ lists (there is no official one). Ask your city or county.
Outside the Act’s areas it isn’t required; it is still good practice.

Also required under the Act, in writing at or before the start of the tenancy: who manages the home and who receives legal papers for the owner (KRS 383.585), and where the separate deposit account is, with its number (§ 383.580(1)). Use NOHM’s two disclosures.

Statewide: a lease can’t penalize a tenant for calling the police or emergency help (KRS 383.302). Under the Act a lease can’t make the tenant waive their rights, confess judgment, pay your attorney’s fees, or excuse you from liability (KRS 383.570).
A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Disclosure of manager and owner
forms.explain: Tells the tenant in writing who manages the home and who receives legal papers and notices for the owner.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, and again whenever it changes.
notes: Required in writing at or before the start of the tenancy, and kept current (KRS 383.585(1)–(2)). This is a rule of the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, which applies only where the city or county adopted it (KRS 383.500): Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville, by advocates’ lists (there is no official one). Ask your city or county.
Anyone who fails to give it becomes your agent for service of process and for receiving notices and demands (KRS 383.585(3)).

forms.label: Notice of security deposit account
forms.explain: Tells the tenant where the separate account holding their deposit is, and its number.
forms.when: When you take a security deposit, before the tenant moves in.
notes: Required where the Act applies: keep every deposit in an account used only for deposits, at a bank or other lending institution regulated by Kentucky or a federal agency, and tell the tenant where the account is and its number (KRS 383.580(1)). This is a rule of the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, which applies only where the city or county adopted it (KRS 383.500): Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville, by advocates’ lists (there is no official one). Ask your city or county.
Without the separate account, and the move-in and move-out damage listings, you may not keep any part of the deposit (KRS 383.580(4)).
Kentucky caps no deposit and requires no interest on it.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: Give at least 2 days’ notice and enter only at reasonable times, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable (KRS 383.615(2)–(3)). This is a rule of the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, which applies only where the city or county adopted it (KRS 383.500): Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville, by advocates’ lists (there is no official one). Ask your city or county.
Outside the Act’s areas no statute sets entry notice: your lease decides. NOHM uses 2 days anyway.
Don’t abuse the right of access or use it to harass the tenant (KRS 383.615(3)). If the tenant is away more than 7 days, you may enter at times reasonably necessary (§ 383.670(2)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Kentucky statute sets the notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date: under the Act a month-to-month can’t be ended on less (KRS 383.695(2)), and elsewhere on less than a month (§ 383.195).
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
No statewide rent cap; local governments can’t control rents on private property (KRS 65.875).
Under the Act you can’t raise rent to retaliate against a tenant (KRS 383.705).

forms.label: Move-out damage listing and deposit statement
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: When the tenant moves out: inspect, list the damage with its estimated repair cost, and both sign.
notes: Required where the Act applies: when the tenant leaves, inspect the home and list any damage you’ll charge against the deposit, with the estimated cost of repairing it; the tenant may inspect, and you both sign. A tenant who disagrees lists the items they dissent from and signs that (KRS 383.580(3)). This is a rule of the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, which applies only where the city or county adopted it (KRS 383.500): Louisville/Jefferson County, Lexington/Fayette County, Oldham and Pulaski Counties, and cities including Covington, Newport, Florence, Bellevue, Dayton, Georgetown, Shelbyville and Barbourville, by advocates’ lists (there is no official one). Ask your city or county.
Without this listing, the move-in listing and the separate account, you may not keep any of the deposit (KRS 383.580(4)). The tenant can sue only over the items they dissented from (§ 383.580(5)).

Kentucky sets no deadline to return it. If a refund is due, send notice of the amount to the tenant’s last known address; if they don’t respond within 60 days, you may take it from the account and keep it (KRS 383.580(7)). If they left without paying the last month’s rent and don’t ask for the deposit, you may apply it to the debt after 30 days (§ 383.580(6)).
Outside the Act’s areas no statute governs deposits: the lease does. This statement is still good practice.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: No Kentucky statute covers a tenant’s belongings left behind. NOHM suggests holding them at least 14 days after this notice; the date is yours to set.
Use it only after the tenancy has ended and the tenant has left: never while they still have possession. Photograph the property before you move it.
The squatter law that lets an owner move an unlawful occupant’s belongings to the property line doesn’t apply to tenants or former tenants (KRS 383.290).

forms.label: 5-day notice to vacate (rent not paid)
forms.explain: After you dissolve the lease for unpaid rent, tells the lessee to leave within 5 days of delivery.
forms.when: Rent is past due and you have ended the lease (Louisiana has no grace period).
notes: Louisiana gives no statutory time to pay: when rent isn’t paid when due, the lessor may dissolve the lease (La. Civ. Code art. 2704) and then send this notice. If you’d rather give the lessee a chance to pay first, the Civil Code allows a notice to perform within a reasonable time, with a warning that the lease will otherwise be dissolved (art. 2015); NOHM’s notice doesn’t do that.
Rent is due at the beginning of each period unless the lease says otherwise (La. Civ. Code art. 2703); there is no grace period.

The 5 days leave out legal holidays because the period is under 7 days (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 5059(C)). Whether Saturdays are legal holidays (La. R.S. 1:55) wasn’t confirmed, so NOHM skips Saturdays and Sundays too: the longer, safer count.

Many Louisiana leases contain the lessee’s written waiver of the notice to vacate. If yours does, you may file the rule to show cause as soon as the lessee’s right of occupancy ends (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4701).

Hand it to the lessee and keep proof of delivery. You may attach it to a door of the home only if the home is abandoned or closed, or you don’t know where the lessee is (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4703). The Code names no mail delivery, so NOHM doesn’t offer it.

Under an oral lease, a written demand for the rent that gives the correct amount makes the lessee liable for your attorney fees if it isn’t paid within 20 days after delivery (La. R.S. 9:3259). It can go by certified mail, by hand, or tacked on the door.

forms.label: 5-day notice to vacate (lease broken)
forms.explain: After you dissolve the lease for a failure to perform it, tells the lessee to leave within 5 days of delivery.
forms.when: The lessee broke the lease (other than rent) and you have ended it.
notes: A lessee must pay the rent, use the home as a prudent administrator for its purpose, and return it as delivered except for normal wear and tear (La. Civ. Code art. 2683). When a party fails to perform, the other may dissolve the lease (art. 2719).

A lease can’t be dissolved when the lessee has rendered a substantial part of the performance and the part not rendered doesn’t substantially impair your interest (La. Civ. Code art. 2014). For a smaller breach, a notice to perform within a reasonable time, warning that the lease will otherwise be dissolved, is the safer first step (art. 2015).

In a building of 6 or more units (other than an owner-occupied building of 10 or fewer), you may not give a notice to vacate because domestic abuse occurred on the premises and the victim is a lessee or a member of the lessee’s household (La. R.S. 9:3261.1).

The 5 days leave out legal holidays because the period is under 7 days (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 5059(C)). Whether Saturdays are legal holidays (La. R.S. 1:55) wasn’t confirmed, so NOHM skips Saturdays and Sundays too: the longer, safer count.

Many Louisiana leases contain the lessee’s written waiver of the notice to vacate. If yours does, you may file the rule to show cause as soon as the lessee’s right of occupancy ends (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4701).

Hand it to the lessee and keep proof of delivery. You may attach it to a door of the home only if the home is abandoned or closed, or you don’t know where the lessee is (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4703). The Code names no mail delivery, so NOHM doesn’t offer it.

forms.label: 10-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month lease at the end of a month, given at least 10 calendar days before; it is also the notice to vacate.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month lessee out, no fault needed.
notes: A month-to-month lease ends by written notice given at least 10 calendar days before the end of the month (La. Civ. Code arts. 2728(2), 2729). The notice ends the lease at the end of that month; one given late ends it at the end of the next month for which it is timely.

Other terms: a lease by periods longer than a month needs 30 calendar days before the period ends; by the week, 5 calendar days (La. Civ. Code art. 2728). A lease with no agreed term is month to month (art. 2680).
This notice is also the notice to vacate (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4701): when the month ends you may file the rule to show cause without another one.

A lease with a fixed term ends on its own date without notice (La. Civ. Code art. 2720), but you still need a notice to vacate (NOHM’s, given up to 30 days before the term ends) unless the lease waives it (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4701). If the lessee stays a week after the term without your objection, the lease is reconducted month to month (La. Civ. Code arts. 2721, 2723).
No just-cause rule or rent control: a lessor’s rights can be limited only by state law (La. R.S. 9:3258).

Hand it to the lessee and keep proof of delivery. You may attach it to a door of the home only if the home is abandoned or closed, or you don’t know where the lessee is (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4703). The Code names no mail delivery, so NOHM doesn’t offer it.

forms.label: Notice to vacate (5 days)
forms.explain: The written notice to vacate a lessee must get before an eviction, when the lease ran out or ended another way.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Louisiana requires a written notice to vacate before every eviction, including when a fixed-term lease simply runs out, unless the lease waives it in writing (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4701). It must allow at least 5 days from delivery; NOHM doesn’t count Saturdays, Sundays or legal holidays (art. 5059), the safer reading.

For a fixed term you may give it up to 30 days before the term ends (art. 4701). Give it before the lessee has stayed a week past the term without your objection: that reconducts the lease month to month (La. Civ. Code art. 2721).

NOHM’s 5-day rent and lease-violation notices, and its month-to-month termination, are notices to vacate already. Use this one for a lease that ran out, or for an occupant who isn’t a lessee (5 days, art. 4702).
Hand it to the lessee and keep proof of delivery. Attach it to a door of the home only if the home is abandoned or closed, or you don’t know where the lessee is (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4703).

forms.label: 20-day written demand for rent (oral lease)
forms.explain: Demands the past-due rent in writing; under an oral lease, if it isn’t paid in 20 days the lessee owes your attorney fees for collecting it.
forms.when: Rent is past due under an oral lease.
notes: For oral leases only (La. R.S. 9:3259(C)). If the lessee doesn’t pay within 20 days after delivery of a written demand that correctly sets out the rent due and owing, they are liable for reasonable attorney fees for collecting it once you win a judgment on it (§ 9:3259(A)).
Get the amount right: list only the rent that has become due and delinquent.
Deliver it by certified mail to the lessee’s last known address, by hand, or by tacking it on the door of the leased premises (La. R.S. 9:3259(B)).
This demand is about money. To get the home back, the lessor dissolves the lease and gives the 5-day notice to vacate.

forms.label: Petition for eviction (rule to show cause)
forms.explain: The eviction filing: your petition stating the grounds, and the order for the judge to sign that cites the lessee to show cause why they should not deliver possession.
forms.when: The notice to vacate ran out (or the lease waives it) and the lessee hasn’t left.
notes: File it in the court for the home’s location: a justice of the peace court hears evictions of residential tenants whatever the rent, and so do city and parish courts; the district court can too (La. Code Civ. Proc. arts. 4912(A)(1), 4844). Ask the clerk which court your address goes to, and its fee.

Louisiana has no statewide eviction forms; some courts have their own, and if yours does, use it with these facts. In a justice of the peace court no written pleading is required, and you may state the claim orally (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4917(A)).

The judge signs the order and fixes the day: no earlier than the third day after the rule is served (art. 4732(A)). The sheriff, constable or marshal serves it; a justice of the peace court may serve by certified mail; if the home is abandoned or closed or the lessee can’t be found, it may be attached to a door (art. 4703).

If the lessee doesn’t answer or appear, or you prove your case, the court renders the judgment of eviction immediately, effective for at least 90 days (art. 4732(B)). If they don’t leave within 24 hours, the court issues the warrant for possession (art. 4733). Their appeal stops it only if they answered under oath with an affirmative defense and filed the appeal and bond within 24 hours (art. 4735).
The rule is for possession. Whether rent can be claimed in the same filing wasn’t confirmed, so the petition reserves it (art. 4705): sue for it separately.
No verification or bond is required of you. Whether a company may appear without a lawyer wasn’t confirmed: ask the court.
Bring the lease, the notice to vacate and your proof of delivering it, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Louisiana doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: you may keep the deposit only to remedy the lessee’s default or unreasonable wear (La. R.S. 9:3251(A)), and the lessee must return the home as it was delivered, except for normal wear and tear (La. Civ. Code art. 2683(3)). This form records its condition.
Louisiana requires no move-in disclosure by statute. A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

Lease terms to know: a waiver of the notice to vacate must be written in the lease (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4701); a waiver of the warranty against vices or defects has limits (La. Civ. Code art. 2699); and in covered buildings a lease can’t limit or penalize calling the police or emergency help (La. R.S. 9:3261.1).
No cap on the deposit, and no interest or separate account is required.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No Louisiana statute sets notice or hours for a lessor’s entry; your lease may. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours, as a courtesy.

The Civil Code still limits you: during the lease you may not make alterations to the home (La. Civ. Code art. 2690); you may make a repair that can’t wait until the lease ends, even if it inconveniences the lessee (art. 2693); and you warrant the lessee’s peaceful possession (art. 2700).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Louisiana statute sets the notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date.

A month-to-month lease can be ended only by written notice 10 calendar days before the month ends (La. Civ. Code art. 2728), so a lessee who won’t accept the new rent can be given that notice. During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it.
No rent cap, and parishes and cities can’t limit a lessor’s rights (La. R.S. 9:3258).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within one month after the lease ends.
notes: Return the deposit within one month after the lease ends, less what is reasonably necessary to remedy the lessee’s default or unreasonable wear to the home, with an itemized statement of what you kept and why (La. R.S. 9:3251(A)).

Since Act 63 of 2026 the itemized statement may follow up to 15 days after that month; when the change took effect wasn’t confirmed, and the refund itself is still due within the month, so NOHM sends both within the month.
Send it to the forwarding address the lessee must give you when the lease ends (La. R.S. 9:3251(A)).

Willfully failing to return it costs the amount wrongly kept plus $300 or twice that amount, whichever is greater; not paying within 30 days after the lessee’s written demand counts as willful (La. R.S. 9:3252(A)).
The one-month rule doesn’t apply when the lessee abandons the home without the notice required, or before the lease ends (La. R.S. 9:3251(C)). No cap on the deposit, and no interest is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: No Louisiana statute covers a lessee’s belongings left behind. NOHM suggests holding them at least 14 days after this notice; the date is yours to set.

After the notice to vacate, you may take possession of a home you reasonably believe the lessee abandoned (keys returned, furnishings removed, no one living there) without going to court (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4731(B)); in a parish under a federal disaster declaration, not for 30 days after it.
With a warrant for possession, the officer clears the home of any property in it (La. Code Civ. Proc. art. 4734).
Your privilege on the lessee’s movables for the rent is enforced by a court seizure, not by keeping them yourself (La. Civ. Code arts. 2707, 2710).
Photograph the property before you move it.

forms.label: 7-day notice to quit (rent 7 days or more in arrears)
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy at will in 7 days for rent 7 days or more in arrears, unless the tenant pays it all first; form CV-256 goes with it.
forms.when: Rent is 7 days or more in arrears.
notes: Serve it only once the tenant is 7 days or more in arrears (14 M.R.S. § 6002(1)(C)), and state the amount 7 or more days in arrears as of the date of the notice. An unintentional clerical error in the amount doesn’t invalidate it (§ 6002(2)(B)).

If the tenant pays the full rent due before the notice expires, the notice is void. After it expires, paying all arrears, the rent due to date and your filing and service fees before the writ issues reinstates the tenancy. Payment or a written assurance of payment through general assistance counts as cash (14 M.R.S. § 6002(1)).

Attach form CV-256 from the Judicial Branch website (courts.maine.gov) to the notice: the law requires it with every notice to terminate (14 M.R.S. § 6001(7)). You don’t write anything on it. Serve it again with the summons and complaint.

Try at least 3 times, in good faith, to hand it to the tenant before you mail it first class and leave it at the home (14 M.R.S. § 6002). A notice served by a sheriff, constable or other authorized server can be proved by their return (§ 6001(8)). Maine adds no days for mailing; NOHM adds 3.
A written lease: serve the notice the lease requires; where the lease says nothing about ending it, this notice applies (14 M.R.S. § 6001(1-B)).
A late fee may be charged only after rent is 15 days late, up to 4% of a month’s rent, and only if you told the tenant in writing at the start (14 M.R.S. § 6028). Collect it separately.
No separate demand is needed: once this notice expires, you may file for forcible entry and detainer (14 M.R.S. § 6002).

forms.label: 7-day notice to quit for cause
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy at will in 7 days for a ground the statute lists, such as substantial damage, a nuisance or violence; form CV-256 goes with it.
forms.when: The tenant did one of the things 14 M.R.S. § 6002(1) lists.
notes: The 7-day notice is only for the grounds 14 M.R.S. § 6002(1) lists, which you must be able to show by affirmative proof: the tenant, their family or an invitee caused substantial damage they haven’t repaired; caused or permitted a nuisance, made the unit unfit for human habitation, or violated the law regarding the tenancy; the tenant is a perpetrator of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking against another tenant; the tenant or a guest committed or threatened violence or sexual assault against another tenant, a guest, you or your employee or agent; or the occupant isn’t authorized. A tenant who changes the lock and won’t give you a key can also be given 7 days (§ 6025(3)).
Name the specific ground in the details: the notice must state it (14 M.R.S. § 6002(2)).
For any other breach of a tenancy at will, use the 30-day notice. A 30-day and a 7-day notice may be combined in one notice (14 M.R.S. § 6002).
A victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking may not be evicted for an incident of it at the premises treated as a nuisance, damage or lease violation (14 M.R.S. § 6001(6)).
No separate demand is needed: once this notice expires, you may file for forcible entry and detainer (14 M.R.S. § 6002).

Attach form CV-256 from the Judicial Branch website (courts.maine.gov) to the notice: the law requires it with every notice to terminate (14 M.R.S. § 6001(7)). You don’t write anything on it. Serve it again with the summons and complaint.

Try at least 3 times, in good faith, to hand it to the tenant before you mail it first class and leave it at the home (14 M.R.S. § 6002). A notice served by a sheriff, constable or other authorized server can be proved by their return (§ 6001(8)). Maine adds no days for mailing; NOHM adds 3.
A written lease: serve the notice the lease requires; where the lease says nothing about ending it, this notice applies (14 M.R.S. § 6001(1-B)).

forms.label: 30-day notice to quit (tenancy at will)
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy at will on at least 30 days’ written notice, no reason needed; form CV-256 goes with it.
forms.when: You want a tenant at will out, no fault needed.
notes: At least 30 days; the date needn’t end a rental period. If the tenant has paid rent through a later date, the notice must expire on or after that date (14 M.R.S. § 6002).
The tenant may waive the 30 days in writing, but only at the time the notice is given. Money you receive after giving the notice doesn’t undo it until a writ of possession issues (§ 6002).

No separate demand is needed: when the notice expires, the tenant is liable to forcible entry and detainer without further notice, unless they paid, after the notice, rent that accrued after the tenancy ended (14 M.R.S. § 6002).

A written lease that has ended: you may file without notice within 7 days after it ends (14 M.R.S. § 6001(1)). After that, NOHM treats the tenant as a tenant at will and gives this 30-day notice, the safer reading.
Within 6 months after a tenant takes one of the actions 14 M.R.S. § 6001(3) protects, an eviction is presumed retaliatory, unless it is for a § 6002(1) ground or a lease violation.

Attach form CV-256 from the Judicial Branch website (courts.maine.gov) to the notice: the law requires it with every notice to terminate (14 M.R.S. § 6001(7)). You don’t write anything on it. Serve it again with the summons and complaint.

Try at least 3 times, in good faith, to hand it to the tenant before you mail it first class and leave it at the home (14 M.R.S. § 6002). A notice served by a sheriff, constable or other authorized server can be proved by their return (§ 6001(8)). Maine adds no days for mailing; NOHM adds 3.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (CV-007, CV-034, CV-256)
forms.explain: Everything the Judicial Branch’s complaint for forcible entry and detainer asks for, filled in from the lease, with where to get each form and the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The notice to quit expired and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Maine’s District Courts use the Judicial Branch’s forms. Fill in the complaint (CV-007) from this worksheet; this worksheet isn’t filed.
Attach form CV-256 to the summons and complaint, as you did to the notice to quit (14 M.R.S. § 6004(2)).
Bring the lease, the notice to quit with its CV-256, your proof of service, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Maine doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: you can’t deduct normal wear and tear from the deposit (14 M.R.S. § 6033(1)), and this form records the home’s condition.

Before the tenant signs or pays a deposit, Maine requires: the radon notice in the form the Department of Health and Human Services prescribes, with the date and result of the latest test (§ 6030-D); written notice of the smoking policy, with the tenant’s written acknowledgment (§ 6030-E; NOHM’s smoking policy disclosure); the energy efficiency disclosure statement, signed by you both, where the tenant pays for energy (§ 6030-C); and the total price disclosure, signed by you both, where there are recurring fees (§ 6030-J).

At the start of the tenancy: written notice that a late fee of up to 4% of a month’s rent may be charged, if you’ll charge one (§ 6028(3)); and whether an adjacent unit is infested with or being treated for bedbugs (§ 6021-A).
Give a written receipt for every cash rent or deposit payment (§ 6022). The deposit can’t be more than 2 months’ rent (§ 6032). A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Smoking policy disclosure
forms.explain: Tells the tenant in writing whether smoking is prohibited, allowed, or allowed only in some areas, and records their acknowledgment.
forms.when: Before the tenant signs the lease or pays a deposit.
notes: Required: before a tenant enters into a lease or pays a deposit, tell them in writing whether smoking is prohibited on the property, allowed on all of it, or allowed only in limited areas (and which), and get their written acknowledgment (14 M.R.S. § 6030-E). It can be in the lease instead.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give reasonable notice and enter only at reasonable times; 24 hours is presumed reasonable (14 M.R.S. § 6025(2)). The tenant can’t waive this (§ 6025(4)).

You may enter to inspect, make necessary or agreed repairs, decorations, alterations or improvements, supply services, or show the home to buyers, mortgagees, tenants, workers or contractors (§ 6025(1)). For bedbugs, the notice must give the reasons for and scope of the access (§ 6021-A).

Entering without it can cost the greater of actual damages or $250, plus attorney’s fees after a contested hearing (§ 6025(3)). An emergency, including an animal whose welfare is at risk, allows entry without 24 hours’ notice.
A tenant who changes the lock and won’t give you a key can be given a 7-day notice to quit (§ 6025(3)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 45 days before the new rent starts; 75 days for an increase of 10% or more.
notes: Rent, or a mandatory recurring fee, may be increased only on at least 45 days’ written notice; 75 days’ for an increase of 10% or more, counting every increase in the last 12 months (14 M.R.S. § 6015). A waiver of the notice is void. Fill in the rent of 12 months ago if it changed since.
The 75-day rule doesn’t apply to deed-restricted affordable housing or a rent subsidy program’s housing.
No increase while the home violates the warranty of habitability, unless the tenant caused it (14 M.R.S. § 6016).
During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it. Maine has no statewide cap, and doesn’t stop cities from adding rent rules: Portland has its own.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 21 days after a tenancy at will ends and you get the home back; under a written lease, the time it states, up to 30 days.
notes: Return the deposit, or this written statement itemizing why you kept any of it with the rest of the deposit, within 21 days after a tenancy at will ends or the home is surrendered and accepted, whichever is later; under a written lease, within the time it states, up to 30 days (14 M.R.S. § 6033(2)). Mailing it to the tenant’s last known address complies.

No deduction for normal wear and tear (§ 6033(1)). Missing the deadline forfeits your right to keep any of it (§ 6033(3)); wrongful retention costs double the amount, plus fees, after the tenant gives 7 days’ notice of a suit (§ 6034).
Keep the deposit in a bank account, apart from your own money and beyond your creditors’ reach; on request, tell the tenant the bank and the account number (§ 6038).
The deposit rules don’t apply to a unit in a building of 5 units or fewer where you live in one (§ 6037).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Use it after the tenant has vacated, or after a judgment for you. Mail it first class with proof of mailing (a certificate of mailing) to the tenant’s last known address, with an itemized list of the items and containers of items (14 M.R.S. § 6013(2)(B)).
If the tenant still lives there, the notice goes to the rental unit, and can’t give less than 7 days after mailing or 48 hours after the writ is served, whichever is longer (§ 6013(2)(A)).

Claimed within 7 days: release it without asking for payment, and keep it at least 14 days after the notice. Not claimed: you may make its release depend on paying the arrears, damages and storage, sell it for a reasonable fair market price and apply the proceeds (any balance goes to the Treasurer of State), or dispose of property with no reasonable fair market value (§ 6013(3)–(5)).
The tenant may waive this in writing at or after vacating (§ 6013(6)).

forms.label: 10-day notice of intent to file (DC-CV-115)
forms.explain: The Judiciary’s required notice that you’ll file for unpaid rent if it isn’t paid within 10 days; served with form DC-CV-115.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Maryland has no grace period).
notes: The law requires this notice to be in a form created by the Maryland Judiciary: DC-CV-115 (RP § 8-401(c)(2)). Fill in DC-CV-115 with these amounts and dates and serve it with NOHM’s notice, which carries its words and works out the deadline. Get it at https://www.mdcourts.gov/sites/default/files/court-forms/dccv115.pdf.

Notice occurs when it is sent by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing, affixed to the door, or, if the tenant chose it, sent by e-mail, text or tenant portal with proof of transmission (RP § 8-401(c)(2)). A lease can’t require the tenant to accept it electronically (§ 8-208(d)(9)).

Wait the full 10 days before you file. A Sunday or legal holiday at the end moves the last day to the next day (Gen. Prov. § 1-302); NOHM moves a Saturday too, to be safe. Your complaint (DC-CV-082) must state the date you gave this notice (§ 8-401(c)(3)).
Rent can be demanded once it is unpaid when due; Maryland has no grace period (RP § 8-401(a)).

After a judgment the tenant may still redeem the home by paying all past-due amounts the court found, with court costs and fees, before the eviction is carried out, unless they had three judgments for unpaid rent in the 12 months before (RP § 8-401(h)).
Baltimore City, Montgomery County, Prince George’s County and Takoma Park have their own rules that may add to these; check yours.

forms.label: 30-day notice of breach of lease
forms.explain: Tells a tenant under a lease for a stated term that they are in breach and you want the home back, 30 days before you can file.
forms.when: The tenant breached a lease that lets you repossess for a breach.
notes: Only for a lease for a stated term that lets you repossess the home if the tenant breaches it (RP § 8-402.1(a)). For a month-to-month, end it with the 60-day notice instead.

If the breach shows a clear and imminent danger of the tenant, or someone there with the tenant’s consent, doing serious harm to themselves, other tenants, you, your property or representatives, or anyone else on the property, the law allows 14 days’ notice. NOHM’s notice gives 30.
The court will order possession only if it finds the breach was substantial and warrants an eviction (RP § 8-402.1(b)(1)).
Taking payment after this notice isn’t a waiver of it, unless you agree to that in writing (RP § 8-402.1(d)(1)).

Maryland’s law doesn’t say how to deliver this notice. Hand it to the tenant, or mail it first class with a certificate of mailing (NOHM adds 3 days), and keep a copy: the court’s complaint form asks for the date and has you attach it.
Baltimore City, Montgomery County, Prince George’s County and Takoma Park have their own rules that may add to these; check yours.

forms.label: 60-day notice to end a tenancy
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month, or a lease at the end of its term, on 60 days’ written notice before it expires.
forms.when: You want the tenant out when the month or the lease ends, no fault needed.
notes: A month-to-month, or a written lease for a stated term of more than a week, needs 60 days’ written notice before the tenancy expires; a fixed lease doesn’t end on its own (RP § 8-402(c)(2)(i)). A tenancy from year to year needs 90 days before the year ends; week to week, 7 days with a written lease, 21 without.
No separate demand is needed: if the tenant stays, this notice is the one the holdover complaint (DC-CV-080) asks for and has you attach (RP § 8-402(b)).
Taking rent after the notice isn’t a waiver of it, unless you agree to that in writing (RP § 8-402(c)(5)). A lease can’t set a shorter notice (§ 8-208(d)(5)).
A holdover tenant owes your actual damages, at least the rent for the time held over (RP § 8-402(a)).

Maryland’s law doesn’t say how to deliver this notice. Hand it to the tenant, or mail it first class with a certificate of mailing (NOHM adds 3 days), and keep a copy: the court’s complaint form asks for the date and has you attach it.
Baltimore City, Montgomery County, Prince George’s County and Takoma Park have their own rules that may add to these; check yours.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (DC-CV-115, DC-CV-082, DC-CV-080, DC-CV-085)
forms.explain: Everything the Maryland Judiciary’s notice and complaint forms ask for, filled in from the lease, with where to get each form and the steps and deadlines to the eviction.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid or left.
notes: Maryland’s District Court uses the Judiciary’s forms: DC-CV-115 before a rent case, then DC-CV-082 (the court requires its carbonless multi-part form, from any District Court location), DC-CV-080 or DC-CV-085. Fill them in from this worksheet; this worksheet isn’t filed.
Each complaint is affirmed under the penalties of perjury: check every amount against the ledger.
A rental license is required in some counties and cities; where it is, the complaint must give it (Real Prop. § 8-406).

In a failure-to-pay-rent case anyone may represent you (Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 10-206(b)(1)). In a holdover or breach case a business may need a lawyer; the Judiciary says only that some entities must have one, and NOHM couldn’t confirm the rule. Ask the clerk.
Baltimore City, Montgomery County, Prince George’s County and Takoma Park have their own rules that may add to these.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: The tenant may ask, by certified mail within 15 days after moving in, for a joint inspection and a written list of existing damage (Real Prop. § 8-203.1(a)(1)). Doing it at move-in, with this form, meets that.

The lease must include the deposit receipt with the tenant’s rights under the deposit law (Real Prop. § 8-203.1(a)) and a copy of the current Maryland Tenants’ Bill of Rights from the Department of Housing and Community Development (§ 8-208(c)(4)), and must state the home’s condition and who is responsible for heat, gas, electricity, water and repairs (§ 8-208(c)). A landlord who offers 5 or more units must use a written lease (§ 8-208(a)).
Give the State’s mold pamphlet when the lease is signed, and ask the tenant to sign that they received it (Real Prop. § 8-220(b)).
A lead “affected property” must be registered with the Department of the Environment and have a current inspection certificate at each change of tenant (Env. § 6-811).
The deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent (Real Prop. § 8-203(b)); at move-in you may ask for no more than the deposit and the first month’s rent (§ 8-208(d)(11)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give written notice at least 24 hours ahead with the date, the approximate time and the specific purpose, and enter only 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday through Saturday, unless the tenant agrees in writing to another time or to shorter notice (Real Prop. § 8-221).

Deliver it by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing (only if it will arrive at least 24 hours ahead), by affixing it to the door, or electronically if the tenant chose that, with proof of transmission (§ 8-221(c)).
In an emergency you may enter without it. A tenant who reports a code violation must let you in within 24 hours to fix it (§ 8-221(f)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 60 days before the new rent starts on a month-to-month; 90 days on a lease of more than a month.
notes: Give written notice before any rent increase: at least 60 days for a tenancy of more than a week up to a month (month to month), 90 days for a lease term of more than a month; 7 days for a week-to-week with a written lease, 21 without (Real Prop. § 8-209).

Send it by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing, or, if the tenant chose it, by e-mail, text or tenant portal with proof of transmission. A lease application can’t require the tenant to choose electronic notice (§ 8-209).
Not needed if you’ve already given notice to end the tenancy (§ 8-402(c)). No statewide cap; Montgomery County, Prince George’s County and Takoma Park have their own rent stabilization laws.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends, return the deposit with its interest, less damages rightfully withheld, and send this list of damages with the cost of each by first-class mail to the tenant’s last known address (Real Prop. § 8-203(e), (g)).

Interest is owed on a deposit of $50 or more held 6 months or more, for each full month, at the greater of the 1-year Treasury rate on the first business day of each year or 1.5% a year. The Department of Housing and Community Development posts the rates and a calculator you may rely on (§ 8-203(e), (m)–(n)).

Deduct only unpaid rent, damage from a breach of the lease, and damage beyond ordinary wear and tear (§ 8-203(f)). Attach the invoices or receipts, or an estimate followed by the final invoice and any refund within 30 days after the repair (§ 8-203(j)–(k)).

No list in time, or a move-out inspection the tenant asked for and didn’t get, forfeits your right to keep any of it for damages; withholding it without a reasonable basis can cost up to 3 times the amount withheld plus attorney’s fees (§ 8-203(e)(4), (f), (g)(2)).
A tenant who was evicted or abandoned the home must ask for it by first-class mail within 45 days; you then have 45 days (§ 8-203(h)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: No statewide statute covers a tenant’s belongings left behind; your county or city may have rules. NOHM suggests holding them at least 14 days after this notice; the date is yours to set.

A lease can’t let you take the tenant’s belongings unless the lease has ended and the tenant abandoned them without formal legal process (Real Prop. § 8-208(d)(6)). Taking possession any way but a warrant the sheriff executes, or the tenant’s abandonment or surrender, is unlawful (§ 8-216).
When a warrant is executed, the sheriff removes the tenant’s belongings; the final notice of pending eviction warns the tenant they could lose what they leave (Real Prop. §§ 8-401(f), 8-407).
Use it only after the tenant has left: never while they still have possession. Photograph the property before you move it.

forms.label: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
forms.explain: Ends the tenancy 14 days after the tenant gets it unless the rent is paid; goes with the state’s required form.
forms.when: Rent is due and unpaid (Massachusetts has no grace period).
notes: Attach the state’s “Form to Accompany Residential Notice to Quit” (M.G.L. c. 186, § 31), with the part on any repayment agreement filled in. The court won’t accept your summons and complaint without proof you delivered it. Get the current PDF at mass.gov/notice-to-quit-accompanying-form: NOHM couldn’t open that page to check its version.

A tenant at will who hasn’t had a nonpayment notice to quit in the last 12 months can stop the termination by paying the full rent due within 10 days after getting this notice. A tenant under a written lease can pay all rent due, with interest and costs, up to the day the answer is due. NOHM’s notice gives 14 days to pay; if the tenant pays in that time, the tenancy goes on.
Massachusetts sets no grace period before this notice: serve it once rent is due and unpaid.

Massachusetts law doesn’t say how to serve a notice to quit: it runs from when the tenant receives it, and you must prove that. A constable’s or sheriff’s return is the usual proof; NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.
