If the 14th day is a weekend or holiday, NOHM moves the date to the next business day. Massachusetts moves a tenant’s payment deadline that falls on a Sunday or legal holiday to the next business day (M.G.L. c. 4, § 9).
If the tenant shows the court a pending application for emergency rental assistance, the court must pause the case until it is decided (M.G.L. c. 239, § 15).

forms.label: Notice to quit for breach of the lease
forms.explain: Ends a written lease for a breach, on the notice and terms the lease itself sets.
forms.when: The tenant broke a term of a written lease that lets you end it.
notes: Massachusetts has no statutory notice for a lease violation: your written lease decides. Use the notice period, and any chance to fix the breach, that the lease’s termination clause gives, and set the date to match.
A tenant at will (no written lease) can’t be ended for a breach this way. Use the notice to quit for a tenancy at will (M.G.L. c. 186, § 12).
Using the premises for illegal drugs, prostitution, illegal gaming, illegal weapons or explosives lets you void the lease, with no time to cure (M.G.L. c. 139, § 19).

A termination notice, other than for rent, within 6 months after the tenant reported a code violation, joined a tenants’ union or used another legal right is presumed to be a reprisal (M.G.L. c. 186, § 18).

Massachusetts law doesn’t say how to serve a notice to quit: it runs from when the tenant receives it, and you must prove that. A constable’s or sheriff’s return is the usual proof; NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

forms.label: Notice to quit a tenancy at will (a rental period, at least 30 days)
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy at will on the last day of a rental period, at least 30 days after the tenant gets it.
forms.when: You want to end a tenancy at will (month to month), no fault needed.
notes: For monthly rent the notice is a full rental period, and at least 30 days, from when the tenant receives it; for weekly rent, 30 days. If rent is payable every three months or less often, it is three months (M.G.L. c. 186, § 12).

The statute doesn’t say the date must end a rental period; Massachusetts practice (from court decisions NOHM didn’t check) is that it should. NOHM ends it on the last day of a rental period, which satisfies both readings.
Massachusetts has no separate demand for possession: this notice is the demand. A written lease that ran out on its own date needs no notice before summary process (M.G.L. c. 239, § 1).
You may offer a new tenancy on different terms, such as a new rent, in this notice without affecting it (M.G.L. c. 186, § 12).

You can’t file until that same period has passed after the tenant receives the notice (M.G.L. c. 186, § 13). A court may stay a no-fault eviction up to 6 months, or 12 if the tenant is disabled or 60 or older (M.G.L. c. 239, § 9).
A notice within 6 months after the tenant used a legal right is presumed to be a reprisal (M.G.L. c. 186, § 18).

Massachusetts law doesn’t say how to serve a notice to quit: it runs from when the tenant receives it, and you must prove that. A constable’s or sheriff’s return is the usual proof; NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Summary Process Summons and Complaint, TC0030)
forms.explain: What to write on the Trial Court’s summary process forms, what goes with them, and the steps and deadlines after you file.
forms.when: The notice to quit has run, or the lease has ended, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Massachusetts courts take summary process on their own Summary Process Summons and Complaint, which you get from the clerk (reported: only a sample is online; NOHM couldn’t open mass.gov). NOHM doesn’t write a complaint for you; this sheet tells you what to put on the court’s.

The timing is set by the Uniform Summary Process Rules, which NOHM could read only in search excerpts: serve the summons and complaint no later than the 7th day and no earlier than the 30th day before the entry day; entry days are Mondays; the answer is due the Monday after entry; the case is listed for the second Thursday after entry. Courts now also hold a first court event (mediation) under standing orders. Check the current rules with the clerk.
A constable or sheriff usually serves the summons and complaint.
TC0030 is the Trial Court’s e-form; NOHM couldn’t read its text.
A company (LLC or corporation) must appear through a Massachusetts lawyer (from case law as reported; NOHM didn’t read it).
Before a default, the court will ask for a Servicemembers Civil Relief Act affidavit (federal law).
The Superior Court also hears summary process, usually only where damages over $25,000 are likely (M.G.L. c. 239, § 2).

forms.label: Notice of satisfaction of judgment
forms.explain: Tells the court that a judgment or agreement in a case only for unpaid rent has been paid, as the law requires.
forms.when: Within 14 days after a nonpayment judgment or agreement is paid.
notes: The law requires it only in a case solely for nonpayment of rent: file it with the court that entered the judgment or agreement, not more than 14 days after it is paid (M.G.L. c. 239, § 16(k)).
If the clerk has a form of their own for it, use theirs. Send the tenant a copy.

forms.label: Statement of condition (move-in)
forms.explain: The signed statement of the home’s condition, with the notice the law requires, that goes with a security deposit.
forms.when: Give it at move-in; the tenant has 15 days to return it.
notes: Required when you take a security deposit: give it when you receive the deposit or within 10 days after the tenancy starts, whichever is later, signed by you or your agent (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(2)(c)).
List all damage existing in the premises, including any code violation certified by a board of health or building official or found by a court.
If the tenant returns a separate signed list of damage, within 15 days give them a copy with your signed agreement, or a clear statement of disagreement, attached.

You can’t deduct from the deposit for damage on this statement or the tenant’s list (§ 15B(4)). Keep a record of damage and repairs for each unit, open to the tenant, until 2 years after the tenancy ends (§ 15B(2)(d)).

Other papers Massachusetts requires: a signed deposit receipt when you take the deposit, and a bank receipt within 30 days (NOHM has both); a receipt for last month’s rent, saying the tenant is owed 5% interest on it (or the lower rate the bank paid) and should give you a forwarding address (§ 15B(2)(a)); a statement of interest each year (§ 15B(3)(b)); a copy of the signed lease within 30 days (§ 15D); the lead law notification, the latest lead inspection report or letter of compliance, and the tenant certification, before the tenancy starts (c. 111, § 197A; NOHM didn’t check the Department of Public Health’s form titles); the federal lead disclosure for homes built before 1978; your name and contact posted, and the Department of Public Health’s notice of occupants’ rights (105 CMR 410.400); and your fire insurance details within 15 days if the tenant asks (§ 21).
Up front you may take only the first month’s rent, the last month’s rent, a deposit of no more than one month’s rent, and the cost of a new lock and key (§ 15B(1)(b)).

forms.label: Security deposit receipt
forms.explain: The signed receipt Massachusetts requires when you take a security deposit.
forms.when: When the tenant pays the deposit.
notes: Give it when you take the deposit, signed by whoever received it (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(2)(b)).
Put the deposit in a separate, interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank, and give the bank receipt within 30 days (§ 15B(3)(a)). Give the statement of condition too (§ 15B(2)(c)).
The deposit can be no more than the first month’s rent (§ 15B(1)(b)).

forms.label: Security deposit bank receipt
forms.explain: Tells the tenant where the deposit is held: the bank and its location, the amount and the account number.
forms.when: Within 30 days after you receive the deposit.
notes: Give it within 30 days after you receive the deposit. If you don’t, the tenant is entitled to the deposit back right away (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(3)(a)).
The account must be separate and interest-bearing, in a bank located in Massachusetts, and out of reach of your creditors.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Massachusetts sets no advance notice for entry; your lease may. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
Enter only for the purposes the statute lists: to inspect, make repairs or show the home; under a court order; if it appears abandoned; or, near the end of the tenancy, to check for damage.
Entering for other reasons, or too often, can breach the tenant’s quiet enjoyment, with damages of at least three months’ rent (M.G.L. c. 186, § 14).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Massachusetts sets no notice for a rent increase. For a tenant at will, a new rent is a new tenancy: give at least what a notice to quit would need, a full rental period and at least 30 days, starting on a rent day (M.G.L. c. 186, § 12 lets a notice to quit offer the new terms). NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date.
During a lease, change the rent only as the lease allows.
Massachusetts has no rent cap, and cities and towns can’t control rents (M.G.L. c. 40P).
A rent increase within 6 months after the tenant used a legal right is presumed to be a reprisal (M.G.L. c. 186, § 18).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, return the deposit with its interest, less only what the law allows, and give this list, signed under the pains and penalties of perjury, with the estimates, bills, invoices or receipts for each repair (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(4)).
You can’t deduct for damage listed on the statement of condition or on the tenant’s own list at move-in.
Interest is 5% a year, or the lower rate the bank paid (§ 15B(3)(b)).

Miss a step (the separate bank account, this sworn list within 30 days, the return within 30 days) and you lose the right to keep any of it; some failures cost three times the deposit, plus interest, costs and attorney’s fees (§ 15B(6), (7)).
The deposit can be no more than the first month’s rent (§ 15B(1)(b)). Vacation rentals of 100 days or less are exempt (§ 15B(9)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Massachusetts has no statute for property a tenant leaves after moving out on their own. NOHM fills in 30 days to pick it up; it isn’t a statutory period. Store it safely, and photograph it before you move it.
After an eviction, don’t use this: the sheriff or constable stores the tenant’s belongings with a licensed public warehouser (M.G.L. c. 239, § 4).
Within 3 days after you know, or should know, the tenant has left, check the home for animals left behind and notify an animal control or police officer right away (M.G.L. c. 186, § 30).

forms.label: 7-day demand for possession (rent not paid)
forms.explain: Demands the rent owed: pay it, or move, within 7 days of service.
forms.when: Rent is due and unpaid (Michigan has no grace period).
notes: This demand has what Michigan requires (MCL 600.5716): the premises, the reason, the time to act, the amount due, dated and signed by you, your attorney or your agent. The courts’ own form is DC 100a; either may be used.

Serve it any time rent is due and unpaid: Michigan sets no grace period. Hand it to the tenant; give it on the premises to a household member of suitable age, asking them to pass it on; mail it first class; or send it electronically if the tenant agreed in writing. Posting it on the door is not a way Michigan allows.
Mail counts as served on the next mail-delivery day; NOHM counts the next business day, which can be a day later than the law’s.
Keep a copy that shows when and how you served it: it goes with your complaint (DC 102a).
Mobile home park tenants need just cause and the courts’ form DC 100d.
If the tenant pays the judgment and the costs within the time the judgment gives, no order of eviction issues (MCL 600.5744(7)).

forms.label: 7-day demand for possession (damage or health hazard)
forms.explain: Demands the tenant repair serious damage or remove a health hazard they caused, or move, within 7 days.
forms.when: The tenant caused serious, continuing damage or a health hazard.
notes: Use this only for serious, continuing damage or a health hazard the tenant caused, and file within 90 days after you discovered it (MCL 600.5714(1)(d)). The courts’ form is DC 100b.
Michigan has no general notice to fix other lease violations. For another breach, end the lease under its own termination clause (MCL 600.5714(1)(c)(i)) and serve the courts’ notice to quit, DC 100c.

Two other grounds have their own court forms: illegal drugs on the premises, with a lease clause and a police report, 24 hours (DC 100e; MCL 600.5714(1)(b)); a tenant, household member or guest who caused or threatened physical injury, with the police notified, a 7-day notice to quit (DC 100c; MCL 600.5714(1)(e)).
If, within 90 days before you file, the tenant tried to enforce their rights or complained to a government agency, the court may presume the case is retaliation (MCL 600.5720).

forms.label: Notice to quit (1 month, month-to-month)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a date at least one month out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: One month’s notice ends a month-to-month tenancy; for weekly rent, a week’s notice is enough (MCL 554.134(1)). The date doesn’t have to be the end of a rental period.
A year-to-year tenancy ends one year after the notice is served (MCL 554.134(3)).

Michigan has no separate demand for possession: once this notice ends the tenancy, or a lease runs out on its own date, you can file without another demand (MCL 600.5714(1)(c)). The courts’ form for this notice is DC 100c.
Public housing and mobile home park tenants need just cause (MCL 600.5714(2), (3)).
If, within 90 days before you file, the tenant tried to enforce their rights or complained to a government agency, the court may presume the case is retaliation (MCL 600.5720).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (DC 102a, DC 102b, DC 102c, DC 104, DC 105, DC 107)
forms.explain: Which of the courts’ landlord-tenant forms to use, what to write on them, and the steps and deadlines after you file.
forms.when: The demand or notice to quit has run, or the lease has expired, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Michigan’s district courts use the State Court Administrative Office’s landlord-tenant forms. NOHM doesn’t write a complaint for you; this sheet tells you which form to use and what to put on it.
Mailing is a required part of serving the summons in Michigan (MCR 4.201(D)); NOHM didn’t read the whole rule, so follow the court’s instructions for it.
A company (LLC or corporation) or a property manager needs a lawyer in district court, as several courts tell landlords (not confirmed in a statute or court rule by NOHM).
Either side may demand a jury (form MC 22). The tenant’s answer form is DC 111c.
If you mailed the demand, NOHM counts it served on the next business day; mail is delivered on Saturdays, so the law’s date can be a day or two sooner.

forms.label: Inventory checklist (move-in)
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in; the tenant has 7 days to return it.
notes: Give the tenant two blank copies at move-in, listing every item you own in the unit; the tenant returns one within 7 days after taking possession (MCL 554.608). Use the same checklist at move-out, as the termination checklist.

Other papers Michigan requires: the security deposit notice within 14 days after the tenant takes possession (NOHM has it; MCL 554.603); in the lease, your name and address for notices and the Truth in Renting notice (MCL 554.634); the statement on release from a lease for domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, in the lease or given at signing (MCL 554.601b); if the lease allows more than one way to pay rent, at least one without a fee (MCL 554.633(1)(o)); and the federal lead disclosure for homes built before 1978.
The deposit can be no more than 1½ months’ rent (MCL 554.602).

forms.label: Security deposit notice (within 14 days)
forms.explain: Tells the tenant where to send you notices, who holds the deposit, and that they must give a forwarding address within 4 days after moving out.
forms.when: Within 14 days after the tenant takes possession.
notes: Give it no later than 14 days after the tenant takes possession: without it you may not require a security deposit (MCL 554.603).
Keep the deposit in a regulated financial institution; to use the money, you must first file a cash or surety bond with the Secretary of State (MCL 554.604).
The deposit can be no more than 1½ months’ rent (MCL 554.602).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Michigan has no statute on entry or notice before it; your lease decides. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
Entering to make needed repairs or inspect is allowed only as the law provides; anything more can be unlawful interference with the tenant’s possession (MCL 600.2918(3)(b)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Michigan sets no notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date. For a month-to-month, the safest way is to end the tenancy with a notice to quit and offer a new one at the new rent.
During a lease, change the rent only as the lease allows.
Michigan has no rent cap, and local governments can’t control rents (MCL 123.411).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Mail it within 30 days after the tenancy ends, with a check or money order for any balance. Since September 21, 2026, you may instead send the balance by direct deposit or electronic transfer within 10 days after mailing the notice (MCL 554.609(3)).
Miss the 30 days and you agree that no damages are due: return the whole deposit right away (MCL 554.610).
If the tenant disputes it, you must sue within 45 days after the tenancy ends to keep the amount in dispute, unless an exception applies; failing that costs double the amount kept (MCL 554.613).
If the tenant didn’t give a forwarding address within 4 days after moving out, you don’t have to send this, as long as your deposit notice told them so (MCL 554.603).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Michigan has no statute for this notice. NOHM fills in 30 days to pick things up; it isn’t a statutory period.

Use it only once you have possession lawfully. After a court’s order of eviction, the officer decides what is abandoned and removes it (MCL 600.5744(1)–(2)). Without one, you may retake a unit only if you believe in good faith the tenant abandoned it, after diligent inquiry you have reason to believe they don’t intend to return, and current rent is unpaid (MCL 600.2918(3)(c)).
Taking or keeping a tenant’s belongings otherwise is unlawful interference: $200 or actual damages for each time, three times that for forcible removal (MCL 600.2918).

forms.label: 14-day notice of possible eviction (rent not paid)
forms.explain: The notice Minnesota requires before an eviction for unpaid rent or charges: the amounts, who to pay, and 14 days to pay or move.
forms.when: Rent or another charge under the lease is due and unpaid (no grace period by statute).
notes: Under Payment, give the name and address of the person authorized to receive rent and fees for you: the law requires it.

Date the notice the day you deliver or mail it: the 14 days run from delivery or mailing, and the notice tells the tenant they run “from the date of this notice”. Mail counts from the day you mail it, so NOHM adds no days.
Some cities (Minneapolis and St. Paul among them) require a longer notice; follow the longer one.
Attach a copy of this notice to your eviction complaint: without it the court must dismiss the case and expunge it (Minn. Stat. § 504B.321, subd. 1(d)).
After you file, the tenant can still pay what’s owed, with interest, costs and a $5 attorney’s fee, until possession is delivered (§ 504B.291).
If your lease requires a digital payment platform, keep another way to pay: a tenant can’t be evicted or charged a late fee while both are down (§ 504B.118).

forms.label: Notice of lease violation (the lease sets the terms)
forms.explain: Tells the tenant which lease term they broke and when you’ll end the lease, on the notice the lease itself sets.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term that the lease lets you evict for.
notes: Minnesota sets no notice before an eviction for breach of the lease: your lease decides. Follow any notice, and any chance to fix it, that the lease gives, and set the date to match.

You can evict for a breach only if the lease has a clause giving you the right to evict for that conduct. Describe the lease clause broken, what the tenant did and when: your complaint must identify them, and the eviction clause (Minn. Stat. § 504B.321, subd. 3).
Illegal drugs, prostitution, unlawful firearms or stolen property on the premises end the tenant’s right to possession with no notice (§ 504B.171), and an expedited hearing is available.

You can’t penalize or end a tenancy for the tenant’s conduct away from the premises unless it is a crime of violence against a tenant, guest, landlord or staff, or a conviction for one (§ 504B.171, subd. 2a).

If you serve a notice within 90 days after the tenant used a legal right (a complaint to a government agency, a repair request), you must prove it wasn’t retaliation (Minn. Stat. § 504B.285, subd. 2).

forms.label: Notice to quit (one rental period, month-to-month)
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy at will with written notice of at least the time between rent due dates.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: For monthly rent the notice is one month; for weekly rent, one week; never more than three months (Minn. Stat. § 504B.135).
The statute doesn’t require the date to end a rental period. Older court decisions (NOHM didn’t check them) may; ending it on the day before rent is due is the safest choice.

Under a lease, your notice to quit or not to renew can’t be shorter than the notice the lease asks of the tenant (§ 504B.147, subd. 3). To enforce an automatic renewal clause, remind the tenant in writing 15 to 30 days before their notice is due (§ 504B.145).

Minnesota has no separate demand for possession: a lease that ran out needs no notice, and a tenancy at will ends with this one (§ 504B.285, subd. 1). Attach it to your complaint (§ 504B.321, subd. 3).
No statute says how to serve it; hand delivery is the surest. NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.

If you serve a notice within 90 days after the tenant used a legal right (a complaint to a government agency, a repair request), you must prove it wasn’t retaliation (Minn. Stat. § 504B.285, subd. 2).

forms.label: Eviction action complaint
forms.explain: The eviction filing, with the facts and attachments Minnesota requires, and your verification.
forms.when: The 14-day notice or the notice to quit has run, the lease has ended, or the tenant breached it, and they haven’t left.
notes: File it in the district court of the county where the rental is (Housing Court in Hennepin and Ramsey). The court issues the summons, with the statements on legal help and financial help that the law requires.

Attach the lease and its addenda; for nonpayment, the 14-day notice (without it the court must dismiss the case and expunge it); and any notice to quit (Minn. Stat. § 504B.321, subds. 1(d), 3). The court must dismiss and expunge a case that doesn’t comply (subd. 5).
Never name a tenant’s minor child as a defendant (§ 504B.213).

The appearance is 7 to 14 days after the summons issues. Serve the summons and complaint at least 7 days before it by personal service, or substitute service at the home; mail and post only after two tries on different days, one between 6 and 10 p.m.; file the affidavits of service at least 3 days before. If you usually email or text the tenant, also send them a dated electronic notice of the hearing at least 7 days before (§ 504B.332).
If you win, the writ of recovery issues, usually stayed up to 7 days; the tenant has 15 days to appeal; the officer gives 24 hours to leave (§§ 504B.345, 504B.365, 504B.371).
In a nonpayment case the tenant can pay what’s owed, with interest, costs and a $5 attorney’s fee, until possession is delivered, unless you also claimed a material breach (§ 504B.291).

A management agent or other non-lawyer may bring the case for you, but not try it to a jury or appeal it (§ 481.02, subd. 3). Hennepin and Ramsey ask for a Power of Authority (HOU103), and a company may need a lawyer to sign there (not confirmed by NOHM).
The court’s own form, HOU102 Eviction Action Complaint, covers the same ground; NOHM couldn’t open the court’s site to compare it. Sign the verification in front of a notary.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Minnesota doesn’t require a move-in checklist; it is good practice, and helps if the deposit is disputed.

Minnesota does require you to tell the tenant, at the start of the tenancy or within 14 days after they move in, that they may ask for an initial inspection, and before move-out, that they may ask for a move-out inspection and be there (Minn. Stat. § 504B.182). NOHM has the notice.

Other papers Minnesota requires: the name and address of the manager and of the owner or agent for service, in the lease or in writing before the tenancy starts, and posted (§ 504B.181; NOHM has it); any outstanding inspection or condemnation orders, before the tenant signs or pays (§ 504B.195); a written lease for a building of 12 or more units, and a copy to each signer (§§ 504B.111, 504B.115); on the lease’s first page, the start and end dates, any prorated rent, the total monthly payment and whether utilities are included (§§ 504B.120, 504B.146); with pet fees, that they don’t apply to service or support animals (§ 504B.113); a receipt for cash rent (§ 504B.118); and the federal lead disclosure for homes built before 1978.

forms.label: Notice of the right to an inspection
forms.explain: Tells the tenant they may ask for an inspection at move-in, or at move-out and be there for it.
forms.when: At the start of the tenancy or within 14 days after move-in; again before move-out.
notes: Give the move-in notice at the start of the tenancy, or within 14 days after the tenant moves in; give the move-out notice, in writing, before the tenant moves out (Minn. Stat. § 504B.182).
A move-out inspection is held no earlier than 5 days before the tenant moves out. You and the tenant may agree to dated photos or video instead.
Not giving these notices can cost the amount you withhold from the deposit, plus interest (§ 504B.178, subd. 4).

forms.label: Disclosure of manager and owner
forms.explain: Names who manages the rental and who accepts legal papers for the owner, as Minnesota requires before you can sue for rent or possession.
forms.when: In the lease, or in writing before the tenancy starts; and posted on the premises.
notes: Give it to the tenant in writing, in the lease or before the tenancy starts, and post it in a conspicuous place on the premises. Without it you can’t sue for rent or possession until it is given (Minn. Stat. § 504B.181, subd. 4).
Post a notice too that the Attorney General’s statement of landlord and tenant rights is available (§ 504B.181).
Update it when the manager, owner or agent changes.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ notice, with a time or a window of time, and enter only between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. unless the tenant agrees otherwise (Minn. Stat. § 504B.211). The tenant can’t waive this.

A reasonable business purpose includes showing the unit to prospective tenants (during the notice period), buyers or insurers; maintenance; a code inspection; a disturbance; a reasonable belief of a lease violation in the unit; an unauthorized occupant; or a vacated unit.

Without notice you may enter only to prevent injury or damage, check on someone’s safety, or comply with an ordinance on unlawful activity; if the tenant isn’t home, leave a written note saying you entered. A violation can cost up to $500 each (§ 504B.211, subds. 4–6).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Minnesota sets no general notice for a rent increase. For a month-to-month, give at least what ending the tenancy would take, one rental period (Minn. Stat. § 504B.135); NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date.
Under a lease, change the rent only as the lease allows, and never on shorter notice than the lease asks of the tenant to quit (§ 504B.147, subd. 3).
Minnesota has no statewide cap; a city may control rents only with the voters’ approval (§ 471.9996). St. Paul has rent stabilization: check it if your rental is there.
A rent increase in retaliation is a defense to an eviction (§ 504B.285, subd. 3).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 21 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within three weeks after the tenancy ends and you have the tenant’s mailing address or delivery instructions, return the deposit with 1% simple interest, or give this statement of the specific reasons for keeping any of it. Mailing it first class within that time counts. If the building was condemned, it is 5 days (Minn. Stat. § 504B.178, subd. 3).

You must prove each deduction. Not giving the statement, or not giving the inspection notices (§ 504B.182), costs the amount withheld plus interest, on top of the deposit; keeping it in bad faith can add up to $500 (subds. 4, 7).
A tenant can’t use the deposit as the last month’s rent, except on a month-to-month with no notice served (subd. 8). Minnesota sets no cap on deposits.

forms.label: Notice of sale of abandoned property
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: The tenant abandoned the home and left things behind: at least 14 days before you sell them.
notes: Give it at least 14 days before the sale: in person, or by first class AND certified mail (the 14 days start when you mail it); and post it on the premises at least two weeks before (Minn. Stat. § 504B.271).
The sale can be no sooner than 28 days after you learn of the abandonment, or it reasonably appears the tenant abandoned the home, whichever is later.

If the tenant asks in writing for their property, return it within 24 hours (48 hours, not counting weekends and holidays, if you stored it elsewhere). Withholding it can cost up to twice their actual damages or $1,000.
After an eviction, don’t use this: the officer’s procedure applies (§ 504B.365, subd. 3).

forms.label: 3-day notice to pay rent
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rental agreement ends if the rent isn’t paid within 3 days (weekends and holidays not counted).
forms.when: Rent is due and unpaid (Mississippi has no grace period).
notes: Mississippi sets no grace period before this notice: serve it once rent is due and unpaid.
Email or text counts only if the tenant agreed in writing to be notified that way; NOHM has a consent form. NOHM adds 3 days if you mail it.
Even after a judgment for nonpayment, the tenant can pay everything the judgment awards by the court’s move-out date, and you must accept full payment in good faith (§ 89-8-39(4)).
At the hearing the judge must follow the rental agreement you and the tenant signed (§ 89-8-13(5)(b)).
Since 2022, residential evictions in Mississippi are under Miss. Code Ann. §§ 89-8-31 to 89-8-45. File a copy of this notice with your complaint (§ 89-8-33(b)).

forms.label: 14-day notice of breach
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong: remedy it within 14 days, or the rental agreement ends.
forms.when: The tenant broke the rental agreement or a tenant’s duty under the law (other than rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the law requires the notice to specify it.

If substantially the same breach happens again within 6 months, you can end the agreement on 14 days’ written notice with no chance to cure (§ 89-8-13(3)(b)). For a violation that materially affects health or safety, no notice is required (§ 89-8-19(4)).
You can’t end it for a condition you or your family or guests caused (§ 89-8-13(3)(c)).
Since 2022, residential evictions in Mississippi are under Miss. Code Ann. §§ 89-8-31 to 89-8-45. File a copy of this notice with your complaint (§ 89-8-33(b)).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a date at least 30 days after the notice.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice instead (Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-19(2)). The date doesn’t have to end a rental period.
A lease with a fixed term ends on its own date (§ 89-8-17(1)); for a tenant who stays after it, give the 3-day notice of holding over (§ 89-8-17(2)).
If the tenant stays after the date, you may file to evict (§ 89-8-31(b)).
You may raise the rent after a rental agreement ends, but not mainly to retaliate against the tenant (§ 89-8-17(2)).
Since 2022, residential evictions in Mississippi are under Miss. Code Ann. §§ 89-8-31 to 89-8-45. File a copy of this notice with your complaint (§ 89-8-33(b)).

forms.label: Notice of holding over (3 days)
forms.explain: Tells a tenant who stayed after the lease expired that you will file to evict no earlier than 3 days later.
forms.when: A lease with a fixed term expired and the tenant is still there.
notes: For a lease with a fixed term that has expired: tell the tenant they are holding over, and that you will file no earlier than 3 days after this notice, not counting intermediate weekends and holidays (Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-17(2)). File a copy with your complaint (§ 89-8-33(b)).
A month-to-month ended with the 30-day notice needs no further notice: that notice goes with your complaint.
Unless your lease says otherwise, you may charge double rent for the time a tenant stays after you notified them to leave (§ 89-8-45).
Email or text counts only if the tenant agreed to it in writing.

forms.label: Complaint for residential eviction
forms.explain: The eviction filing, sworn, with the summons in the words the law requires for the clerk to issue.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid, remedied the breach or left.
notes: File in justice court, county court or circuit court in the county where the rental is (Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-7(1)(b)). Justice court has a limit on money claims (§ 9-11-9; NOHM didn’t check the amount). The courts post sample forms only; none is required.

Attach a copy of the written notice you delivered: the notice of breach or to pay rent, the 30-day notice, or the notice of holding over (§ 89-8-33(b)). Swear to the complaint before the clerk or a notary.

The last page is the summons, in the words § 89-8-35 requires since the 2025 amendments, for the clerk to fill in and issue; the courts’ sample summons is older and lacks two sentences. If the clerk uses their own, check it has the same words. It is served under the Mississippi Rules of Court.

One adjournment can’t be longer than 10 days, and the whole case can’t go past 30 days after filing, unless you and the tenant agree (§ 89-8-41). A judgment is signed the same business day (§ 89-8-37).

The judge orders the tenant out in 7 days unless an emergency justifies a shorter or longer time. After that date, ask for a warrant for removal; law enforcement must remove the occupants, not just post the warrant. The tenant then has 72 hours of reasonable access to take their belongings (§ 89-8-39).
In a nonpayment case the tenant can still pay everything the judgment awards by the move-out date, and you must accept full payment in good faith (§ 89-8-39(4)).
NOHM found no rule letting a non-lawyer appear for a company; if your rental is owned by an LLC or corporation, use a lawyer.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Mississippi doesn’t require a move-in checklist; it is good practice, and helps if the deposit is disputed.

Mississippi requires no other written disclosure at move-in, apart from the federal lead disclosure for homes built before 1978. If you want to send notices by email or text, get the tenant’s written consent (NOHM has the form).
A lease can’t include a confession of judgment, or excuse you from liability for your own willful misconduct (Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-5).

forms.label: Consent to notices by email or text
forms.explain: The tenant’s written agreement to be notified by email or text message, which Mississippi requires before a notice counts that way.
forms.when: At lease signing, or any time the tenant agrees.
notes: A notice of breach, a notice to pay rent or a notice of holding over counts by email or text only if the tenant agreed in writing to be notified that way (Miss. Code Ann. §§ 89-8-13, 89-8-17). Have every adult tenant sign.
The 30-day notice to end a month-to-month isn’t on that list: deliver it in writing.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Mississippi has no statute on entry; your lease decides. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours’ notice.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Mississippi sets no notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date. For a month-to-month, the clean way is to end it with the 30-day notice and offer new terms.
During a lease, change the rent only as the lease allows. After it expires you may raise the rent, but not mainly to retaliate against the tenant (Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-17(2)).
Mississippi has no rent cap.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Return what is left no later than 45 days after the tenancy ends, the tenant gives back possession and asks for it (Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-21(3)). Itemize every amount you keep in this written notice.
Keeping any of it wrongly and in bad faith can cost up to $200 on top of the tenant’s actual damages (§ 89-8-21(4)).
Mississippi sets no cap on deposits and requires no interest.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: For the 72 hours after law enforcement executes the warrant for removal, give the tenant reasonable access to take their belongings; after that you may move what is left to the curb, a garbage area or a place you both agree on (Miss. Code Ann. § 89-8-39(3)).
If the tenant moved out by the court’s move-out date and left things, you may dispose of them without further notice (§ 89-8-39(1)).
Without a court case, Mississippi has no statute on property left behind: hold it longer (NOHM suggests 30 days) and change the date.

A federal court in northern Mississippi reportedly found parts of the state’s property-disposal scheme unconstitutional (news reports; NOHM didn’t read the decision). Be cautious, and photograph everything.

forms.label: Demand for rent (no waiting period)
forms.explain: Demands the rent that is due; Missouri needs only the demand before you file for rent and possession.
forms.when: Rent is due and unpaid (wait out any forfeiture time your lease sets).
notes: Missouri requires a demand for the rent, not a notice period: any demand made after rent is due counts (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 535.060). The month-to-month notice isn’t needed first (§ 535.020). Pick a reasonable date to pay.
If your written lease says it is forfeited for nonpayment “for a specified time”, wait until that time has run before you file (§ 535.050).
Hand it to the tenant, or leave it at their home with a family member over 15 (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 1.190). Missouri’s statutes don’t provide for mailing it.
The tenant can stop the case by paying the rent and costs at the hearing, and stop the eviction by paying the judgment and costs before it becomes final (§§ 535.040, 535.160).
A company (LLC or corporation) must appear in court through a lawyer in Missouri (a 2014 Missouri Supreme Court decision, as reported; NOHM didn’t read it).

forms.label: 10-day notice to vacate (lease violation)
forms.explain: Ten days’ notice to leave for breaking the written lease, assigning it without consent, or damaging the property.
forms.when: The tenant violated a condition of the written lease, subleased without your written consent, or committed waste.
notes: This is for a tenant whose term is two years or less, or at will or by sufferance (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.030). The statute gives no chance to cure; your lease may.

§ 441.020 covers gaming devices, a bawdyhouse or brothel, and the illegal possession, sale or distribution of controlled substances on the premises. For drugs you must prove the use in court, but you aren’t liable for relying on a law enforcement agency’s written notice.
You can’t evict a tenant because they are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, except as § 441.920 allows.
If the tenant hasn’t left after the 10 days, serve the written demand for possession, then file for unlawful detainer (§ 534.030).
Hand it to the tenant, or leave it at their home with a family member over 15 (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 1.190). Missouri’s statutes don’t provide for mailing it.

forms.label: 1-month notice to vacate (month-to-month)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a rent-paying date at least one month after the tenant receives it.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: Missouri ends a month-to-month on a rent-paying date at least one month after the tenant receives the notice (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.060.4(1)). NOHM sets the last day before that rent day, so the tenancy ends as the rent day begins.
A year-to-year tenancy needs notice at least 60 days before the year ends (§ 441.050); a lease that ends on a set date needs none (§ 441.070).
If the tenant stays, serve a written demand for possession before you file for unlawful detainer (§ 534.030).
Hand it to the tenant, or leave it at their home with a family member over 15 (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 1.190). Missouri’s statutes don’t provide for mailing it.

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: A tenant who holds over after the tenancy ends, and after a written demand for possession, is guilty of unlawful detainer (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 534.030.1). Serve this demand after the lease, the 10-day notice or the month-to-month notice has ended the tenancy.
Missouri sets no waiting period after the demand; NOHM fills in 3 days. Give more if you like.

Serve it by handing it to the person in possession, or leaving it with someone over 15 who lives there or is in charge; if no one is there, post it on the premises (§ 534.050). Anyone but a sheriff or other officer must swear to the return: sign it before a notary.
You don’t need this demand to file for rent and possession; the demand for rent is enough there.

forms.label: Statement for rent and possession
forms.explain: The filing for unpaid rent: the terms of the rental, the rent due, and your demand for it, verified by affidavit.
forms.when: You demanded the rent and it hasn’t been paid.
notes: File it with the associate circuit judge of the county where the rental is (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 535.020). Sign the affidavit before a notary or the clerk. Missouri has no statewide form; some circuits post their own (Boone County’s, for one).

The court date is within 21 business days after the summons issues, unless you agree in writing to a later one; the summons is served at least 4 days before it. If it is served by posting and mailing (which you may do yourself, at least 10 days before the court date), the court can give possession but no money judgment on a default (§ 535.030).

The tenant can stop the case by paying the rent and costs at the hearing (§ 535.040). After judgment they have 10 days to ask to set it aside or for a new trial; then it is final (§ 535.030.4). The officer delivers possession within 5 days after receiving the execution (§ 535.040.1). A tenant who appeals must post a bond for the rent (§ 535.110).

If the officer hasn’t delivered possession within 7 days of receiving the writ, you may, within 60 days after the judgment and with a law enforcement officer present, change the locks and remove the tenant’s property (§ 441.060.5).
If your written lease is forfeited for nonpayment only after a set time, wait until it runs before you file (§ 535.050).
A company (LLC or corporation) must appear in court through a lawyer in Missouri (a 2014 Missouri Supreme Court decision, as reported; NOHM didn’t read it). Bills to change that weren’t enacted.

forms.label: Complaint for unlawful detainer
forms.explain: The sworn filing to recover possession from a tenant who stayed after the tenancy ended and a written demand.
forms.when: The tenancy ended, you served a written demand for possession, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: File it with the associate circuit judge of the county where the rental is (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 534.060). It must be signed and sworn to: sign the affidavit before a notary or the clerk (§ 534.070.1).

The court date is within 21 business days after the summons issues, and the summons is served at least 4 days before it (§§ 534.070.2, 534.090.1). The execution for possession issues no sooner than 10 days after the judgment (§ 534.350).
Keep copies of the notice that ended the tenancy and of the written demand, with its sworn return.
A company (LLC or corporation) must appear in court through a lawyer in Missouri (a 2014 Missouri Supreme Court decision, as reported; NOHM didn’t read it). Bills to change that weren’t enacted.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Missouri doesn’t require a move-in checklist; it is good practice, and helps if the deposit is disputed.

Papers Missouri requires: a written disclosure if you know the home was used to make methamphetamine (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.236); to charge for carpet cleaning, a lease clause setting the amounts and telling the tenant they may owe actual costs beyond ordinary wear and tear (§ 535.300); written notice of the move-out inspection (NOHM has it); and the federal lead disclosure for homes built before 1978.
The deposit can be no more than two months’ rent, held in a federally insured bank or credit union (§ 535.300).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Missouri has no statute on entry or notice before it; your lease decides. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
Never enter to remove the tenant or their things, or change the locks, without a court order: that is forcible entry and detainer (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.233).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Missouri sets no notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date. For a month-to-month, the clean way is the 1-month notice to vacate, offering a new tenancy at the new rent.
During a lease, change the rent only as the lease allows.
No city or county in Missouri may regulate the amount of rent (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.043.1).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, return the full deposit, or send this list with the balance. Mailing them to the tenant’s last known address is enough (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 535.300).
Carpet cleaning can be deducted only if the lease set the amounts and told the tenant they may owe actual costs beyond ordinary wear and tear; give a receipt for the actual cost within 30 days.
Keeping any of it wrongfully costs twice the amount withheld. Interest on the deposit is yours; a pet deposit isn’t a security deposit; the tenant can’t use the deposit as rent.

forms.label: Notice of belief of abandonment
forms.explain: The notice in the statute’s words when you believe a tenant has abandoned the home: 10 days to answer before you may remove what is left.
forms.when: Rent has been unpaid for 30 days and you believe the tenant has moved out.
notes: Use it only when you reasonably believe the tenant has moved out and doesn’t mean to return, and the rent has been due and unpaid for 30 days (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 441.065).

Post it on the door AND mail it by first class AND certified mail, return receipt requested, to the tenant’s last known address, on the date of the notice. The 10 days run from when you have done both.
If the tenant doesn’t pay the rent or answer in writing within those 10 days, the premises are abandoned and you may remove and dispose of what is left, without liability to the tenant.
This is not for a tenant who is still living there: removing a tenant or their things without a court order is forcible entry and detainer (§ 441.233).

forms.label: Notice of move-out inspection
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll inspect after the tenancy ends, so they can be there.
forms.when: Before you inspect the home after the tenancy ends.
notes: Give the tenant reasonable written notice of the date and time, at their last known address or in person; they may be there (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 535.300.5).

forms.label: 3-day notice to pay rent or quit
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid: pay it within 3 days, or the rental agreement ends and they must move.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Montana has no grace period).
notes: Montana has no grace period: rent is due without demand on the day the rental agreement sets (MCA 70-24-201(3)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it with a certificate of mailing (USPS Form 3817) or by certified mail: mailed, it counts as given 3 days after mailing (MCA 70-24-108(1)(d)). Email works only to an address the tenant gave in the rental agreement, and counts from a read receipt or a reply that isn’t automatic. Montana doesn’t allow taping it to the door or leaving it with someone else.
If the tenant pays in full within the 3 days, the tenancy goes on. Taking the full rent after that waives the nonpayment; taking part of it doesn’t (MCA 70-24-423).
Montana needs no other demand before you file: if the tenant stays after the rental agreement ends, file the complaint for possession (MCA 70-24-429(1)).

forms.label: 14-day notice of noncompliance
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what they did wrong: remedy it within 14 days, or the rental agreement ends.
forms.when: The tenant broke the rental agreement (other than rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the law requires the notice to specify it.

Some breaches have shorter notices (MCA 70-24-422): an unauthorized pet or person living there, or verbal abuse of the landlord, 3 days with the chance to remedy; damage to the premises, or conduct that puts the premises or neighbors at risk (drugs, gang activity, weapons), 3 days to terminate; the same breach again within 6 months of a notice, 5 days. NOHM’s notice is the 14-day one; the courts’ “Notice to Vacate” form letter (courts.mt.gov/Forms/landlord) has a box for each of the others.
A tenant who refuses lawful access or changes a lock without giving you a key gets a 24-hour notice to correct first, then a 3-day notice to terminate (MCA 70-24-424).
Taking rent doesn’t waive a breach other than nonpayment (MCA 70-24-423).
For a month-to-month tenancy you can use the 30-day notice instead, with no reason (MCA 70-24-422(7)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it with a certificate of mailing (USPS Form 3817) or by certified mail: mailed, it counts as given 3 days after mailing (MCA 70-24-108(1)(d)). Email works only to an address the tenant gave in the rental agreement, and counts from a read receipt or a reply that isn’t automatic. Montana doesn’t allow taping it to the door or leaving it with someone else.
Montana needs no other demand before you file: if the tenant stays after the rental agreement ends, file the complaint for possession (MCA 70-24-429(1)).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on any date at least 30 days out, no reason needed.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out.
notes: Any date at least 30 days out works; it needn’t end a rental period (MCA 70-24-441(3)). A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice (MCA 70-24-441(1)).
No reason is needed, but you may not end a tenancy to retaliate for a complaint (MCA 70-24-431).
A tenant who stays on after a lawful 30-day notice can owe up to 3 months’ rent or three times your damages, whichever is more (MCA 70-24-429(3)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it with a certificate of mailing (USPS Form 3817) or by certified mail: mailed, it counts as given 3 days after mailing (MCA 70-24-108(1)(d)). Email works only to an address the tenant gave in the rental agreement, and counts from a read receipt or a reply that isn’t automatic. Montana doesn’t allow taping it to the door or leaving it with someone else.
Montana needs no other demand before you file: if the tenant stays after the rental agreement ends, file the complaint for possession (MCA 70-24-429(1)).

forms.label: Complaint for possession
forms.explain: The eviction filing: asks the court for possession of the rental, the rent owed and costs.
forms.when: The notice ran out, or the lease ended, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: File it with the justice court of the county where the rental is (or a city or district court). Attach the rental agreement if it’s written, and the notice you gave.

Montana’s courts publish an optional complaint in their Action for Possession packet (courts.mt.gov/Forms/landlord); this one asks for the same things. The packet’s instructions about a hearing within 20 days are out of date: the law now says 10 business days.
The clerk issues the summons; the sheriff or another levying officer serves it with the complaint. You can’t hand them to the tenant yourself.

The tenant has 5 business days after service, not counting the day of service, to answer (MCA 70-24-429(4)). The hearing must be held within 10 business days after the tenant appears or the answer date, or 5 business days where you ended the lease for drugs, gang activity, weapons or other dangerous conduct (MCA 70-24-427(2)(a)).

The court rules within 5 days after the hearing. If you win, it issues a writ of possession and a writ of assistance at once, and the sheriff carries out the writ of assistance within 5 business days (MCA 70-24-427(4)).
No bond is required. The winner may be awarded reasonable attorney fees and costs (MCA 70-24-442).
In justice court, a member with a majority interest may represent an LLC (MCA 25-31-601(3), 35-8-301(5)). Otherwise, and in district court, plan on a lawyer for a company.
Never lock the tenant out or shut off utilities to get them out (MCA 70-24-428).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: If you take a security deposit, Montana requires this statement, signed by you or your agent, given to each tenant when the lease is signed or the tenancy starts. Without it you can’t charge the deposit for damage or cleaning unless you prove it by clear and convincing evidence (MCA 70-25-206).
If the tenant asks in writing, give them a copy of the last tenant’s list of damage and cleaning charges for this home (MCA 70-25-206(1)).

At or before the start of the tenancy, also tell the tenant in writing the name and address of the person managing the premises, and of the owner or the person authorized to accept service and notices for the owner (MCA 70-24-301).
Check that the smoke and carbon monoxide detectors work when the tenancy starts (MCA 70-24-303(1)(g)).
To give notices by email, the rental agreement must let the tenant choose email; you can’t make an email address a condition of renting (MCA 70-24-202(4)).
When the lease ends, give the tenant the property-left-behind rules of MCA 70-24-430 in plain language (MCA 70-24-430(9)).
A home built before 1978 also needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ notice and enter only at reasonable times, unless it’s an emergency or notice is impracticable (MCA 70-24-312(3)(a)).
Besides the usual ways of giving notice, you may post this on the main entry door of the unit (MCA 70-24-312(3)(b)).
Don’t use the right of entry to harass the tenant. A tenant who refuses lawful access gets a 24-hour notice to correct, then a 3-day notice to terminate (MCA 70-24-424).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Montana statute sets the notice for a rent increase. A month-to-month tenancy can be ended on 30 days’ written notice (MCA 70-24-441), so NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date.
During a fixed-term lease, the rent changes only as the lease allows.
Montana has no rent cap, and cities and counties can’t control rents (MCA 7-1-111(26)).
You may not raise rent to retaliate for a complaint or a tenants’ union (MCA 70-24-431).

forms.label: Notice of cleaning required
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what cleaning is left undone; they have 24 hours to do it before you charge the deposit for it.
forms.when: Before you deduct cleaning from the deposit.
notes: You can’t deduct cleaning from the deposit until you’ve given this notice; the tenant then has 24 hours to do the cleaning (MCA 70-25-201(3)).

Give it as any notice (in hand, or mail with a certificate of mailing or certified mail: served 3 days after mailing). If the tenant left without notice, you may leave it in a conspicuous place in the unit and tell them by email, phone or text (MCA 70-25-201(3)(c)).
Not needed where the rental agreement was already terminated and your claim is pending in court.
Montana’s courts publish an optional “Letter Additional Cleaning” for the same purpose (courts.mt.gov/Forms/landlord).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends (or the home is surrendered and accepted, if sooner), give the tenant this list with the refund (MCA 70-25-202(1)(a)). If there’s no damage, no cleaning and no unpaid rent, and the tenant shows the utilities are paid, return the whole deposit within 10 days (MCA 70-25-202(1)(b)).
Deduct cleaning only after the 24-hour cleaning notice (MCA 70-25-201(3)), and nothing for any purpose the law doesn’t list (MCA 70-25-201(4)).

Without this list you lose the right to keep any of the deposit for damage or cleaning (MCA 70-25-203). Withholding wrongfully makes you liable for the amount withheld, and you carry the burden of proving the damage (MCA 70-25-204).
Montana has no deposit cap and no interest requirement. A fee for cleaning and damage, whatever it’s called, is a deposit (MCA 70-25-101(4)).
These rules don’t apply where the rental agreement was terminated and your claim is pending in court (MCA 70-25-202(2)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: If the tenancy ended by court order, the property is considered abandoned and you may dispose of it right away (MCA 70-24-430(1)(a)). Otherwise you need clear and convincing evidence the tenant abandoned it, and 48 hours since you got that evidence; then trash and anything hazardous, perishable or valueless can go at once (MCA 70-24-430(1)(b)).

Inventory and store what you reasonably believe is valuable, with reasonable care, and mail this notice with a certificate of mailing or by certified mail to the tenant’s last-known address. The date must be at least 10 days after mailing (MCA 70-24-430(2)–(3)).
Items labeled “rent to own” or “leased” may be disposed of only after the owner confirms its lien (MCA 70-24-430(1)(c)).

After a sale, deduct the reasonable costs of notice, storage, labor and sale and any rent or damages owed, and send the tenant the rest with an itemized accounting; if they can’t be found, deposit it with the county treasurer (MCA 70-24-430(8)).

forms.label: 7-day notice to pay rent or quit
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid: pay it within 7 calendar days, or the rental agreement ends.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Nebraska has no grace period).
notes: Nebraska has no grace period: rent is due without demand when the rental agreement says (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1414(3)).
Accepting rent knowing of the default waives your right to terminate for it (§ 76-1433): taking a late payment after the 7 days generally ends this notice.

The 7 days are calendar days. If the last one falls on a weekend or court holiday, NOHM moves it to the next business day; Nebraska’s time rule (§ 25-2221) may not reach a notice, and later is the safe side.

Hand it to the tenant or mail it; the statute adds no days for mail, NOHM adds 3 for delivery. Email works only if the tenant affirmatively consented after getting the statements § 76-1413(7) lists, and you can’t require it as a condition of renting (§ 76-1413(9)); if you don’t get the receipt the law asks for, mail it (§ 76-1413(11)). Nebraska has no posting on the door.
Nebraska needs no other demand before you file: a tenant who stays after the rental agreement ends is sued for possession (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1437(3)).
A rental the Act doesn’t cover (a hotel, employee housing, a lease of land for 5 years or more) uses a 3-day notice to leave instead (§ 25-21,221).

forms.label: 14-day notice to remedy a breach (30 days to end)
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what they did wrong: remedy it within 14 days, or the rental agreement ends at least 30 days after they got the notice.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the rental agreement (other than rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the notice must specify it.
The same breach again within 6 months of this notice: 14 days’ written notice terminates the agreement, with no chance to remedy (§ 76-1431(1)).

Violent criminal activity, sale of a controlled substance, or another threat to health or safety on the premises: 5 days’ written notice, with no right to cure (§ 76-1431(4)). Not against a tenant who is the victim and sought a protective order or reported it to the police (§ 76-1431(5)). NOHM’s notice is the 14-day one.
A tenant who refuses lawful access can be given this notice (§ 76-1438(1)). A rule is enforceable only if the tenant had notice of it when the lease was signed (§ 76-1422(6)).

Hand it to the tenant or mail it; the statute adds no days for mail, NOHM adds 3 for delivery. Email works only if the tenant affirmatively consented after getting the statements § 76-1413(7) lists, and you can’t require it as a condition of renting (§ 76-1413(9)); if you don’t get the receipt the law asks for, mail it (§ 76-1413(11)). Nebraska has no posting on the door.
Nebraska needs no other demand before you file: a tenant who stays after the rental agreement ends is sued for possession (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1437(3)).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a rental date at least 30 days out, no reason needed.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out.
notes: The date must be a periodic rental date at least 30 days out (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1437(2)). A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice (§ 76-1437(1)).
No reason is needed, but you may not end a tenancy to retaliate for a complaint or tenants’ union activity (§ 76-1439).
A tenant whose holdover is willful and not in good faith can owe up to 3 months’ rent or three times your damages, whichever is more, and your attorney’s fees (§ 76-1437(3)).

Hand it to the tenant or mail it; the statute adds no days for mail, NOHM adds 3 for delivery. Email works only if the tenant affirmatively consented after getting the statements § 76-1413(7) lists, and you can’t require it as a condition of renting (§ 76-1413(9)); if you don’t get the receipt the law asks for, mail it (§ 76-1413(11)). Nebraska has no posting on the door.
Nebraska needs no other demand before you file: a tenant who stays after the rental agreement ends is sued for possession (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1437(3)).

forms.label: Complaint for restitution of premises
forms.explain: The eviction filing: asks the court to restore the rental to you, with the facts and notice the law requires.
forms.when: The notice ran out, or the lease ended, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: File it with the clerk of the county court (or district court) of the county where the rental is. Nebraska has no statewide complaint form (the Judicial Branch says none is available), so NOHM writes it with the four things § 76-1441(1) requires.

The clerk issues the summons with the time and place of trial. It must be served within 3 days of issuance, not counting nonjudicial days, and is returnable within 5 (§ 76-1442). If diligent efforts to serve it fail, it may be posted on the front door and mailed first class, with your affidavit (the next form); then you can’t get a money judgment (§ 76-1442.01, § 76-1446).

Trial is held 10 to 14 days after the summons issues, by the judge without a jury (§ 76-1446). The tenant may answer on or before the appearance day; if they don’t appear, the court tries the case as though they were there (§ 76-1444, § 76-1445).
If you win, ask for the writ of restitution (the praecipe); it directs the sheriff or constable to restore possession on a date not more than 10 days after it issues (§ 76-1446).
Claims for rent or damages are other causes of action: the tenant can ask in writing for them to be answered and tried separately (§ 76-1441(1)).
No bond is needed to file. A tenant who appeals stays the writ only by depositing the judgment and costs or an appeal bond, and paying rent monthly into court (§ 76-1447).
Except in small claims court, a corporation or LLC landlord must be represented by an attorney (Nebraska Judicial Branch).
Never lock the tenant out or cut off utilities (§ 76-1430).

forms.label: Affidavit of diligent efforts and service by posting and mailing
forms.explain: Your sworn statement that the summons couldn’t be served the usual way, so it was posted on the door and mailed.
forms.when: Diligent efforts to serve the summons failed, and it was posted and mailed instead.
notes: Use it only after diligent efforts to serve the summons in the usual ways (§§ 25-505.01 to 25-516.01) failed. Then a copy is posted on the front door of the unit and mailed by first-class mail to the tenant’s last-known address (§ 76-1442.01).
With service this way, the court can give you possession but no money judgment (§ 76-1446).
Sign it in front of a notary, and file it with the court.

forms.label: Praecipe for writ of restitution (CC 3:24)
forms.explain: Asks the clerk to issue the writ that has the sheriff or constable put you back in possession.
forms.when: The court entered judgment for restitution of the premises.
notes: The writ issues at your request after judgment, and restores possession on a date not more than 10 days after it issues (§ 76-1446).

This follows the Nebraska Supreme Court’s form CC 3:24, Praecipe for Writ of Restitution/Execution. If your clerk asks for that form itself, it’s at supremecourt.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/CC-3-24.pdf.
Remove property left on the premises only as the Disposition of Personal Property Landlord and Tenant Act allows (§ 76-1446; the property form).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Nebraska doesn’t require a move-in checklist, but a signed one is the best proof of the home’s condition when you itemize the deposit. Keep it with the lease.

At or before the start of the tenancy, tell the tenant in writing the name and address of the person managing the premises, and of an owner or the person authorized to accept service and notices for the owner (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1417).

Give the tenant instructions for testing the smoke detector, with the battery working at move-in (§ 81-5,144(2)); have a working carbon monoxide alarm on each habitable floor and give the tenant its batteries (§ 76-606).
Give the tenant your rules when the lease is signed: a rule is enforceable only if they had notice of it then (§ 76-1422(6)).

To send notices by email, get the tenant’s affirmative consent after the statements § 76-1413(7) requires (the right to withdraw it, the notices it covers, paper copies, how to update the address); it can’t be a condition of renting.
The deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent, plus a pet deposit of up to a quarter month’s rent (§ 76-1416(1)).
A home built before 1978 also needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ written notice to each unit, with the purpose and a reasonable time window, and enter only at reasonable times, except in an emergency or where it’s impracticable (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-1423(3)).
Don’t use the right of entry to harass the tenant. Abuse of access can cost at least one month’s rent (§ 76-1438(2)).
During an absence of more than 7 days you may enter when reasonably necessary (§ 76-1432(2)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Nebraska statute sets the notice for a rent increase. A month-to-month tenancy can be ended on 30 days’ written notice to a rental date (§ 76-1437(2)), so NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date.
During a fixed-term lease, the rent changes only as the lease allows.
Nebraska has no rent cap, and cities can’t enact rent control (§ 13-331).
You may not raise rent to retaliate for a complaint or tenants’ union activity (§ 76-1439).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 14 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Deliver or mail the balance and the itemization within 14 days after the tenancy ends. With no address from the tenant, mail them first class to the last-known mailing address (§ 76-1416(2)).
If the mail comes back, or the refund goes unclaimed for a year, it’s abandoned property to report to the State Treasurer.
Keeping it wrongfully costs the deposit, court costs and attorney’s fees; if willful and not in good faith, also one month’s rent or twice the deposit, whichever is less (§ 76-1416(3)).
The deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent, plus a pet deposit of up to a quarter month’s rent (§ 76-1416(1)). No interest is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Give this notice within 6 months after the lease expired or you discovered the abandonment, whichever is later (§ 69-2303(2)(d)).

The claim date must be at least 7 days after you hand it to the tenant, or 14 days after you mail it (first class, postage prepaid, to the last-known address, and to any other address where they’re likelier to get it) (§ 69-2303(2)(c), (3)).
Send the same notice to anyone else you believe owns the property (§ 69-2305(2)).
Store the property with reasonable care, on the premises or elsewhere; you may charge reasonable storage costs (§ 69-2306, § 69-2310).

If it isn’t claimed, sell it at a public sale after advertising it once a week for two weeks; if you reasonably believe it’s worth less than $2,000, you may keep or dispose of it. Pay the net proceeds to the State Treasurer within 30 days (§ 69-2308).
If the tenant asks in writing within 14 days of moving out, give them an itemized demand for your removal and storage costs within 5 days; they then have 72 hours to remove the property (§ 69-2311).

forms.label: 7-day notice to pay rent or quit
forms.explain: Tells the tenant to pay the rent or surrender the home within 7 judicial days, and how to contest it in court.
forms.when: Rent is past due (a late fee only 3 days after the due date).
notes: In the notice’s details, enter the justice court for the township where the rental is, with its address (for example, Las Vegas Justice Court and its address). The law requires the notice to identify it (NRS 40.253(3)(a)); left blank, the notice prints a line to write it on.

Clark County’s justice courts don’t count Fridays as judicial days (their forms say so). NOHM counts Monday to Friday, so in Clark County count the judicial days Monday to Thursday yourself and give that later date.

Reno Justice Court expects its own current notice form and may dismiss a case that uses another (Administrative Order 2025-01). For a Washoe County rental, serve the court’s form (washoecounty.gov/rjc/forms).

A sheriff, constable, licensed process server or an attorney’s agent must serve it; you can’t serve it yourself (NRS 40.280(1)). The server signs a statement of the date and manner of service with their badge or license number; an attorney’s agent’s needs the attorney’s declaration (NRS 40.280(5)).
You may serve it any time after rent is due. If the tenant then pays the rent, you can’t refuse it because collection fees, attorney’s fees or other costs are unpaid (NRS 40.253(11)).
Rent paid by the week or less, in a tenancy of 45 days or less, may use a 4-day notice instead (NRS 40.253(1)(b)); NOHM doesn’t draw it.
Keep the notice private: it may not be made available for public inspection (NRS 40.2545(5)). Workers affected by a government shutdown have protections (NRS 40.253(12)).
If the tenant doesn’t pay, leave, or file an answer by the deadline, file your court’s complaint for summary eviction (the eviction filing worksheet).

forms.label: 5-day notice to perform lease condition or quit
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what they did wrong: remedy it within 5 judicial days, or the rental agreement may be terminated.
forms.when: The tenant broke the rental agreement (other than rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the law requires the notice to specify it.
The statute says 5 days; the courts’ own forms count 5 judicial days, and so does NOHM, which is never earlier.

Subletting against the lease, waste, an unlawful business, a nuisance or a drug violation on the premises gets a 3-day notice to quit with no chance to cure (NRS 40.2514). NOHM doesn’t draw it; the courts’ forms do.
Then, if the tenant stays, serve the 5-day notice of unlawful detainer (NRS 40.254), NOHM’s next form.
A lease can’t shorten these notice periods (NRS 40.252).

Clark County’s justice courts don’t count Fridays as judicial days (their forms say so). NOHM counts Monday to Friday, so in Clark County count the judicial days Monday to Thursday yourself and give that later date.

A sheriff, constable, licensed process server or an attorney’s agent must serve it; you can’t serve it yourself (NRS 40.280(1)). The server signs a statement of the date and manner of service with their badge or license number; an attorney’s agent’s needs the attorney’s declaration (NRS 40.280(5)).

forms.label: 30-day no-cause notice to quit
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month (or other periodic) tenancy at least 30 days out, no reason needed.
forms.when: You want a periodic tenant out.
notes: Any date at least 30 calendar days after service works; it needn’t end a rental period. A week-to-week tenancy needs at least 7 days, and the age and disability extension doesn’t apply to it (NRS 40.251(1)(b), (2)).
The notice must tell the tenant about the age, disability and shutdown protections (NRS 40.251(5)); NOHM’s does.
After the date passes, serve the 5-day notice of unlawful detainer (NRS 40.254) to begin a summary eviction.
After a foreclosure, a new owner gives at least 60 days after a notice of change of ownership (NRS 40.255(2)).
