No reason is needed, but you may not end a tenancy to retaliate (NRS 118A.510).

A sheriff, constable, licensed process server or an attorney’s agent must serve it; you can’t serve it yourself (NRS 40.280(1)). The server signs a statement of the date and manner of service with their badge or license number; an attorney’s agent’s needs the attorney’s declaration (NRS 40.280(5)).

forms.label: 5-day notice of unlawful detainer
forms.explain: The notice to surrender that starts a summary eviction for any reason but unpaid rent.
forms.when: A 5-day notice to perform ran out, a no-cause notice or the lease term ended, and the tenant is still there.
notes: This is the second notice of a summary eviction for any reason but unpaid rent: after a 5-day notice to perform that wasn’t complied with, a 3-day notice for nuisance or waste, a 30-day (or 7-day) no-cause notice, or the end of the lease term (NRS 40.254, 40.251).

It must name the court and tell the tenant they may contest it by an affidavit filed before the court’s close of business on the 5th judicial day after service, or ask for a stay of up to 10 days (NRS 40.254); NOHM’s does.
Serve it the way NRS 40.280 requires: by a sheriff, constable, licensed process server or an attorney’s agent. You can’t serve it yourself.
Clark County’s justice courts don’t count Fridays as judicial days (their forms say so). NOHM counts Monday to Friday: in Clark County, count Monday to Thursday yourself and use that later date.
Reno Justice Court expects its own current form and may dismiss a case on another (Administrative Order 2025-01): for a Washoe County rental, use the court’s form.
After the 5 judicial days, if the tenant hasn’t left or filed an answer, file your court’s complaint for summary eviction (the eviction filing worksheet).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (your justice court’s summary eviction forms)
forms.explain: Everything your justice court’s complaint for summary eviction asks for, filled in from the lease, with where to get the form and the steps after.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid, left or answered.
notes: Each Nevada justice court publishes its own summary-eviction forms, and Reno Justice Court may dismiss a case filed on other versions (Administrative Order 2025-01). So NOHM doesn’t write the complaint: copy these values onto your court’s current form.
The complaint is an affidavit or declaration under penalty of perjury; Henderson’s must be typed.
A company landlord may file the complaint through its agent, but plan on a lawyer if the tenant contests it.
Clark County’s justice courts don’t count Fridays as judicial days (their forms say so). NOHM counts Monday to Friday: in Clark County, count Monday to Thursday yourself and use that later date.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Nevada requires every rental agreement to include a signed record of the inventory and condition of the premises in the tenant’s exclusive control (NRS 118A.200(3)(k)). Sign it with the tenant and attach it to the lease.

The agreement must also state, among other things, the rent as a single figure that includes every mandatory fee, the deposits and how they’re refunded, late and dishonored-check charges, who pays which utilities, your inspection rights, and how to report a nuisance or a code violation (NRS 118A.200(3), (6)).

A house or a building of 4 or fewer units whose lease isn’t signed by a licensed property manager needs the disclosure of NRS 118A.200(4) at the top of the first page, in type twice the size of any other.

In writing, at or before the start of the tenancy: the names and addresses of the manager, of a person in Nevada authorized to accept service and notices, and of the owner, and a phone number for emergencies answered by someone within 60 miles (NRS 118A.260). Tell a prospective tenant if the home is in foreclosure (NRS 118A.275).
Rent paid weekly or more often: to use the short 4-day notice later, have the tenant sign at move-in that you told them the short-term eviction rules (NRS 40.253(2)).
A home built before 1978 also needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ notice and enter only at reasonable times during normal business hours, unless it’s an emergency or the tenant expressly agrees to shorter notice or another time for that entry (NRS 118A.330(3)).
Don’t use the right of entry to harass the tenant.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 60 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Serve it at least 60 days before the first increased payment; 30 days for a periodic tenancy shorter than a month (NRS 118A.300).
Serve it the way NRS 40.280 provides (NRS 118A.190(2)).
During a fixed-term lease, the rent changes only as the lease allows. State the rent as one figure that includes every mandatory fee (NRS 118A.200(6)).
Nevada has no rent cap. You may not raise rent to retaliate (NRS 118A.510).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, give the tenant this written accounting and the rest of the deposit, in hand where the rent is paid or by mail (NRS 118A.242(4)).
Keeping it wrongfully costs the whole deposit, plus up to that much again as the court decides (NRS 118A.242(6)).
The deposit (with any surety bond and last month’s rent) can’t be more than 3 months’ rent. Only a reasonable cleaning charge may be nonrefundable (NRS 118A.242(1), (8)). No interest is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Store the property safely for 30 days after the abandonment, eviction or end of the rental period; you’re liable only for negligent or wrongful acts in storing it (NRS 118A.460(1)(a)).

Then you may dispose of it if you made reasonable efforts to find the tenant, mailed them this notice, and 14 days have passed since (NRS 118A.460(1)(b)). Vehicles go through the abandoned-vehicle law (NRS ch. 487).
For 5 days after an eviction or lockout, give the tenant a reasonable chance to retrieve essentials: medication, baby formula, basic clothing, personal care items (NRS 118A.460(3)).

forms.label: Demand for rent and 7-day eviction notice
forms.explain: Demands the back rent and gives 7 days’ notice to leave; the tenant can still pay everything before the hearing to stay.
forms.when: Rent is due and in arrears.
notes: New Hampshire uses two papers, the Demand for Rent (court form NHJB-3040-D) and the Eviction Notice (NHJB-3041-D), which may be served together (RSA 540:4, 540:5, I). NOHM’s notice is both.

Your notice must carry the same information as the court’s Eviction Notice form, NHJB-3041-D (RSA 540:5, II), which the court revised on October 8, 2026. NOHM couldn’t read that revision: compare it at courts.nh.gov before you serve.

The tenant can stop the eviction by paying everything listed in the box before the hearing, up to 3 times in 12 months; you then file the receipt with the court and send the tenant a copy (RSA 540:9). What a tenant paid your utility to prevent a shutoff isn’t unpaid rent (RSA 540:2, VI).

If you take the arrears after you file, tell the tenant in writing that you’ll proceed with the eviction anyway, or the payment can create a new tenancy (RSA 540:13, VII): NOHM’s Notice of intent to proceed.

Anyone may serve it, in hand or by leaving it at the tenant’s last and usual place of abode; no mail. Keep a true attested copy and sign an affidavit of service (it needn’t be sworn): the court needs both (RSA 540:5, I). The days are calendar days; a weekend doesn’t extend them (RSA 21:35).
After the date passes, get the Landlord and Tenant Writ from the circuit court (the eviction filing worksheet). No other demand is needed (RSA 540:12).

forms.label: 30-day eviction notice (lease term broken)
forms.explain: Ends the tenancy in 30 days because the tenant broke a material term of the lease, stated in the notice.
forms.when: The tenant failed to comply with a material term of the lease.
notes: Name the lease term and exactly how it was broken: the notice must state the reason with specificity (RSA 540:3, III).

Substantial damage to the premises, or behavior that harms the health or safety of other tenants or the landlord, needs only 7 days (RSA 540:2, II(b), (d); 540:3, II). NOHM’s notice is the 30-day one; the court’s Eviction Notice form has a box for each.
There’s no chance to cure. For “other good cause” based on what the tenant, family or guests did, first give the written warning (RSA 540:2, III): NOHM’s form.
You can’t evict a tenant solely because they or a household member were a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking (RSA 540:2, VII).

Your notice must carry the same information as the court’s Eviction Notice form, NHJB-3041-D (RSA 540:5, II), which the court revised on October 8, 2026. NOHM couldn’t read that revision: compare it at courts.nh.gov before you serve.

Anyone may serve it, in hand or by leaving it at the tenant’s last and usual place of abode; no mail. Keep a true attested copy and sign an affidavit of service (it needn’t be sworn): the court needs both (RSA 540:5, I). The days are calendar days; a weekend doesn’t extend them (RSA 21:35).
After the date passes, get the Landlord and Tenant Writ from the circuit court (the eviction filing worksheet). No other demand is needed (RSA 540:12).

forms.label: 30-day eviction notice (other good cause)
forms.explain: Ends the tenancy in 30 days for a legitimate business or economic reason, stated in the notice.
forms.when: You need the rental back for a business or economic reason.
citations: N.H. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 540:2, II(e), V
notes: Most rentals are restricted property, ended only for a reason the law lists. A legitimate business or economic reason is good cause, and needn’t be anything the tenant did (RSA 540:2, V). Write the reason in the notice’s details.

Nonrestricted property (a single-family house whose owner owns no more than 3, or a unit in an owner-occupied building of 4 or fewer) can be ended for any reason on 30 days’ notice (RSA 540:1-a, 540:2, I).

Since July 1, 2026, a lease of 12 months or more (or renewed to 12 months) may end at its term if you give written notice at least 60 days before the term ends, and you file within 6 months after it expires (RSA 540:2, II(i)). For that, serve this notice 60 days ahead. It’s a no-fault termination, not an eviction, for tenant screening (RSA 540:2, VIII).
A tenant’s refusal of a rent increase you gave 30 days’ written notice of is good cause (RSA 540:2, IV).
A tenant who complained to a code authority, or used RSA 540-A, may have a retaliation defense (RSA 540:13-a).

Your notice must carry the same information as the court’s Eviction Notice form, NHJB-3041-D (RSA 540:5, II), which the court revised on October 8, 2026. NOHM couldn’t read that revision: compare it at courts.nh.gov before you serve.

Anyone may serve it, in hand or by leaving it at the tenant’s last and usual place of abode; no mail. Keep a true attested copy and sign an affidavit of service (it needn’t be sworn): the court needs both (RSA 540:5, I). The days are calendar days; a weekend doesn’t extend them (RSA 21:35).
After the date passes, get the Landlord and Tenant Writ from the circuit court (the eviction filing worksheet). No other demand is needed (RSA 540:12).

forms.label: Written warning (before an eviction for conduct)
forms.explain: Warns the tenant that if their conduct happens again it will be grounds for eviction.
forms.when: Before an eviction for “other good cause” based on what the tenant, their family or guests did.
notes: Required before an eviction notice for other good cause that rests on the actions or inactions of the tenant, their family or guests (RSA 540:2, III).
Serve it in hand, by leaving it at the tenant’s last and usual place of abode, or by certified mail, and keep a copy.
If the conduct happens again, give the 30-day eviction notice, and say in it that this warning was given.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Landlord and Tenant Writ)
forms.explain: What the court’s Landlord and Tenant Writ asks for, filled in from the lease, with where to get it and every step and deadline after.
forms.when: The eviction notice expired and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: The Landlord and Tenant Writ is the court’s own form, issued by the circuit court’s District Division; NOHM doesn’t write it. Copy these values onto it.
Bring the expired eviction notice (and, for rent, the demand for rent), each with its attested copy and affidavit of service.

The court revised its procedure on October 8, 2026 (answers due 5 days after the return day; judgment 7 days after the notice of judgment). Follow the court’s current filing and service instructions at courts.nh.gov.
A limited liability company, corporation or partnership with 5 or fewer members may appear through a member or employee, with a written authorization for each appearance (RSA 540:30): NOHM’s form.
Never lock the tenant out, remove their property or cut off utilities yourself (RSA 540-A:3).

forms.label: Notice of intent to proceed after accepting payment
forms.explain: Tells the tenant you took their payment while the eviction case is pending, and are still going ahead with it.
forms.when: You accept a payment of the arrears after filing.
notes: While the possessory action is pending, you may accept payment of the arrears without creating a new tenancy only if you tell the tenant in writing that you intend to proceed with the eviction anyway (RSA 540:13, VII). Give this when you take the payment.

In a case for unpaid rent alone, a tenant who pays everything RSA 540:9 lists before the hearing (rent, $15, lawful lease charges, filing and service costs) gets the case dismissed: this notice doesn’t change that.

forms.label: Written authorization to represent a company (RSA 540:30)
forms.explain: Lets a member or employee of a small company landlord appear for it in an eviction case.
forms.when: Before each court appearance, if the landlord is an LLC, corporation or partnership with 5 or fewer members.
notes: A person of good character who isn’t a lawyer, but is a member or employee of an LLC, corporation or partnership with 5 or fewer members, may represent it in the circuit court in a case under RSA 540, with the organization’s written authorization (RSA 540:30).
Each appearance needs a new authorization: make one for every hearing.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in; the tenant has 5 days to return it.
notes: When you take a deposit, you must tell the tenant in writing that conditions needing repair or correction should be listed and given to you within 5 days of occupancy (RSA 540-A:6, I(b)–(c)). This form does it.
Exempt: an owner renting a single-family home who owns no other rental property, or units in an owner-occupied building of 5 units or fewer, unless the tenant is 60 or older (RSA 540-A:5, I).
Also give the signed deposit receipt (the next form) unless the tenant paid by personal, bank or agency check.

Before taking an application fee, disclose its amount in writing and any background or credit check you require (RSA 540-A:3, VIII). Let the tenant pay rent at least one way other than electronically (RSA 540-A:3, X).
Owners of restricted property file with the town or city clerk the name, address and phone of an in-state agent for service of process, within 30 days of becoming the owner (RSA 540:1-b).
A home built before 1978 also needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Security deposit receipt
forms.explain: The signed receipt for the deposit: how much, where it’s held, and the tenant’s 5 days to list repairs.
forms.when: When you receive a security deposit.
notes: Give it at once on receiving a deposit. It isn’t needed when the tenant pays by personal, bank or agency check, but the 5-day notice still is (RSA 540-A:6, I(c)).
The deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent or $100, whichever is greater (RSA 540-A:6, I(a)).

Hold it in trust, not mixed with your own money, in a New Hampshire bank account (or post a bond with the town or city clerk) (RSA 540-A:6, II). After a year it earns interest at the account’s savings rate (RSA 540-A:6, IV).
If you sell the property, turn the deposit over and tell the tenant by registered or certified mail who holds it (RSA 540-A:6, III).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: New Hampshire sets no number of hours: you need the tenant’s consent, after notice adequate under the circumstances (RSA 540-A:3, IV–V). NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
For a bed bug evaluation, give 48 hours’ written notice (RSA 540-A:3, V-b).
Without consent you may enter only to make emergency repairs, or with a court order (RSA 540-A:3, IV, V-d).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Give written notice of the amount and effective date at least 30 days ahead. If the tenant then refuses the increase, that is good cause for eviction (RSA 540:2, IV).
During a fixed-term lease, the rent changes only as the lease allows.
New Hampshire has no rent cap. A rent increase to retaliate for a complaint can be a defense in an eviction (RSA 540:13-a).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, return the deposit with any interest due, less the itemized deductions (RSA 540-A:7, I).

Describe each repair with particularity and enclose your evidence that it was or will be done: receipts, estimates, bills or invoices (RSA 540-A:7, I). Give the period of each rent claim (RSA 540-A:7, II).
A deposit held a year or more earns interest at the bank account’s savings rate (RSA 540-A:6, IV).

Getting it wrong costs twice the deposit plus interest, less what you paid and what’s owed (RSA 540-A:8, I(b)). If the tenant gave no forwarding address, a deposit unclaimed 6 months after the tenancy ends becomes yours (RSA 540-A:8, II).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: After a tenant vacates, voluntarily or by eviction, store their property with reasonable care for 7 days; they may take it without paying rent or storage. After 7 days you may dispose of it without notice (RSA 540-A:3, VII). This notice isn’t required, but it heads off disputes.

If you believe the tenant abandoned the home without saying so, the statute’s own Notice of Property Abandonment (RSA 540-A:4, XII) gives you a presumption of abandonment: leave it at the premises and send it by certified mail. It must be printed in 12-point type, which NOHM’s papers don’t yet print, so NOHM doesn’t draw it.
Never remove a tenant’s property while they still have possession, except through the court (RSA 540-A:3, III).

forms.label: Demand for payment of rent (optional)
forms.explain: Asks for the rent due. New Jersey needs no notice before filing for nonpayment, so this is a courtesy.
forms.when: Rent is past due (5 business days’ grace for some seniors and benefit recipients).
notes: New Jersey requires no notice before you file for nonpayment of rent, unless your lease does: the lease decides (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2). This demand is a courtesy, served the ways the statute allows for a notice to quit.

Seniors on Social Security or a government pension, and tenants on SSDI, SSI or Work First New Jersey, get 5 business days’ grace for rent due on the 1st, with no late fee in that time (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-6.1, 6.3).
Your complaint can claim late fees or attorney’s fees only if the written lease calls them “additional rent”, and never against Section 8 or public-housing tenants (court form CN 11252).

The tenant can end the case by paying the rent and costs any time before trial (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-9), and within 3 business days after a lockout for nonpayment; you must accept it and tell the court in writing within 2 business days (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.16a): NOHM’s form.
Rent a tenant used to keep a utility on, after a shutoff notice for your own nonpayment, isn’t unpaid rent (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)).
No judgment for possession until you’re registered under the Landlord Identity Law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-33).

forms.label: Notice to cease
forms.explain: Tells the tenant, in detail, what conduct to stop: the first step before a notice to quit for conduct or habitual late rent.
forms.when: The tenant is disorderly, breaks your rules or a lease covenant, or habitually pays late.
notes: New Jersey requires a written notice to cease before a notice to quit for disorderly conduct (b), breaking reasonable rules the tenant accepted in writing (d), breaking a reasonable lease covenant with a right of reentry (e), or habitual late rent (j) (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1).
The law sets no period: give a time that is reasonable for the conduct (Truth in Renting). Describe the conduct in detail.
If the tenant keeps it up, serve the notice to quit (NOHM’s form): 3 days for disorderly conduct; one month for rules, covenants or habitual late payment (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).
Willful or grossly negligent damage to the premises needs no notice to cease: serve the 3-day notice to quit directly.
The statute doesn’t say how to serve a notice to cease; NOHM uses the notice-to-quit methods (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).

forms.label: One-month notice to quit (owner-occupied, 2 rental units or fewer)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy in a building you live in with no more than 2 rental units; nowhere else.
forms.when: You live in the building, it has 2 or fewer rental units, and you want a month-to-month tenant out.
notes: Use this only if you live in the building and it has no more than 2 rental units (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1). For every other rental, New Jersey doesn’t let a tenancy end because the lease ran out or you want it back: you need one of the Anti-Eviction Act’s causes, each with its own notice (NOHM’s notice to quit). Ask a lawyer.

A month-to-month tenancy needs 1 month’s notice to quit; year-to-year, 3 months; another term, one term’s notice (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-56). NOHM couldn’t confirm whether the date must end a rental period: the day before a rent due date is the safe choice.
Serve it in person or leave it with a family member over 14 at the tenant’s home: certified mail isn’t listed for this notice (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53(a)).
You may not end or refuse to renew a tenancy in reprisal for a complaint or tenant organizing (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10).

forms.label: Notice to quit (Anti-Eviction Act cause)
forms.explain: The written demand and notice for delivery of possession the Anti-Eviction Act requires before an eviction for any cause but unpaid rent.
forms.when: The tenant kept up the conduct after a notice to cease, damaged the premises, or you’re an owner of 3 units or fewer moving in.
notes: It must specify the cause in detail (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2). Attach it, and the notice to cease, to your complaint.

Periods before you may file: 3 days for disorderly conduct or damage; one month for rules, lease covenants or habitual late payment; two months for an owner of 3 units or fewer moving in, and not before a written lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).

Other causes (drug, assault, theft and trafficking offenses: 3 days; code-violation closings, retirement from residential use, condominium conversion, refused lease changes) have their own conditions and periods: talk to a lawyer.
Serve it in person, leave it at the tenant’s home with a family member over 14, or send it by certified mail, then regular mail if the certified letter isn’t claimed.
You may not serve it in reprisal for a complaint or tenant organizing (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (CN 11252, CN 10822, CN 12770, CN 12842)
forms.explain: What the Judiciary’s mandatory landlord-tenant forms ask for, filled in from the lease, with where to get them and every step after.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid, or a notice to quit ran out, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: New Jersey’s courts require their own forms for a residential eviction: the verified complaint (CN 11252), the summons (CN 10822), the Landlord Case Information Statement (CN 12770) and the certification of lease and registration (CN 12842). NOHM doesn’t write a complaint: copy these values onto those forms.
A corporation or LLC must be represented by a New Jersey attorney in the Landlord/Tenant Section (CN 10289).
Without a current landlord registration, no judgment for possession (N.J.S.A. 46:8-33).

forms.label: Notice to the court of payment after a lockout
forms.explain: Tells the court the tenant paid all the rent due within 3 business days after the warrant was posted or the lockout, so the case is dismissed.
forms.when: Within 2 business days after a tenant paid in full after a lockout for nonpayment.
notes: For 3 business days after a warrant for removal is posted or a lockout is executed for nonpayment, the tenant may pay the rent due; you must accept all of it, with no late fee beyond the one in your application for the warrant (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.16a(a)–(b)).
Within 2 business days after the payment, give the court this written notice, and the tenant a copy. The court then dismisses the case with prejudice.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: New Jersey doesn’t require a move-in checklist, but a signed one is the best proof of the home’s condition when you itemize the deposit.

Truth in Renting: give each new tenant the Department of Community Affairs’ current Truth in Renting statement at or before move-in, and keep a copy posted where all your tenants can see it (N.J.S.A. 46:8-46; nj.gov/dca). It applies unless the building has 2 units or fewer, or 3 or fewer with you living there (N.J.S.A. 46:8-44). Up to $100 a violation.
Give each new tenant a copy of your landlord registration certificate when the tenancy starts (N.J.S.A. 46:8-29).

Before the lease is signed or renewed, tell the tenant in writing whether the home is in a FEMA 100-year or 500-year floodplain and whether you know it has flooded, and put the statute’s flood-insurance sentence in the lease (N.J.S.A. 46:8-50; DCA’s model Flood Risk Notice). Used as a lease rider it must be in 12-point type, which NOHM’s papers don’t yet print, so NOHM doesn’t draw it.
Within 30 days of taking a deposit, give the tenant the deposit’s bank notice (the next form) (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19(c)).

For a home built before 1978, give a new tenant your valid lead-safe certification (N.J.S.A. 52:27D-437.16), and the federal lead-based paint disclosure. Once the state publishes its model statement, a Lead in Drinking Water Disclosure is due before a lease or renewal too.
An application fee can’t be more than $50, indexed each year (N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1).

forms.label: Security deposit bank notice
forms.explain: Tells the tenant where their deposit is held: the bank, the type of account, its interest rate and the amount.
forms.when: Within 30 days of taking the deposit or moving it; with each annual interest payment; within 30 days of a sale.
notes: Give it within 30 days after you receive the deposit, within 30 days after you move it, at each annual interest payment, and within 30 days after the property is sold (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19(c)).

Owners of 10 or more units keep deposits in an insured New Jersey money market fund or a variable-rate account; fewer, in an interest-bearing account at an insured New Jersey bank. The deposit stays the tenant’s money, held in trust (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19).
Without this notice, the tenant may by written notice have the deposit plus 7% interest applied to rent, and owe no further deposit.

The deposit can’t be more than one and a half months’ rent; any increase in a year, no more than 10% of the current deposit (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2). An owner-occupied building of 2 rental units or fewer is exempt unless the tenant gives 30 days’ written notice invoking the law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: No New Jersey statute sets notice for entry. The housing code asks occupants of a multiple dwelling (3 or more units) to allow access on reasonable notice, ordinarily one day, for inspections and repairs; immediately in a safety or structural emergency (N.J.A.C. 5:10-5.1(c)). NOHM asks for a day everywhere.
Otherwise, a landlord generally may not enter without the tenant’s consent or a court judgment (Truth in Renting). Entering while the tenant is out can be an unlawful entry (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-1).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No New Jersey statute sets a rent increase or its notice. To raise a month-to-month rent, end the current term with a notice to quit and offer the tenancy at the new rent: a tenant can be evicted for not paying an increase only after a valid notice to quit and notice of increase, and only if the increase isn’t unconscionable and complies with any rent ordinance (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f); Truth in Renting).
NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date. Courts may expect a full rental period’s notice; NOHM couldn’t confirm how long a “valid” notice is.
About 100 municipalities have rent control ordinances: check yours. During a fixed-term lease, raise the rent only at renewal.
Manufactured home park sites: no more than 3.5% in 12 months (N.J.S.A. 52:27D-287.13).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Within 30 days after the lease ends, return the deposit with its interest, less charges the lease allows, itemized, by personal delivery or registered or certified mail (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

Faster: 5 business days for a tenant displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation; 15 business days after a domestic-violence lease termination. Nothing may be deducted while the tenant stays in possession.
Withholding wrongfully costs double the amount, with court costs and possibly attorney’s fees (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Only after the warrant for removal was executed and possession restored, or the tenant gave written notice of voluntarily giving up possession, and you reasonably believe they left the property with no intent to claim it (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-72).

Mail it certified (return receipt) or first class with a certificate of mailing, to the last known address and any other you know, marked “Please Forward” (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-73). The date must be at least 30 days after delivery or 33 after mailing, whichever comes first: NOHM uses 33 days after mailing. A manufactured or mobile home needs 75 or 78 days, and notice to the Motor Vehicle Commission and lienholders.
If the tenant responds, they get 15 more days; if not, the property is conclusively abandoned (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-76).

After a sale, deduct your costs and rent owed that the deposit didn’t cover, and send the tenant the rest with an itemized accounting; if they can’t be found, deposit it with the Superior Court (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-80). Getting it wrong can cost twice the tenant’s actual damages (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-82).

forms.label: 3-day notice of nonpayment of rent
forms.explain: Tells the resident the rent owed: pay it in full within 3 days, or the owner may end the rental agreement and file to evict.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid when due (New Mexico has no grace period).
notes: Serve it any day after rent is unpaid when due; New Mexico has no grace period (§ 47-8-15(B)).

Under “Payment”, say how you’ll accept it (cash, money order, cashier’s or certified check, or personal check) and where. If the tenant tenders the full amount that way before the 3 days end, you can’t file for nonpayment (§ 47-8-33(D)).
This is the courts’ Form 4-901 NMRA, with its tenant-rights statements. Keep two copies: attach one to the petition.
Write on it the date you hand it over, mail it or post it: that date is the notice’s effective date (§ 47-8-13(D)).

A last day on a weekend or federal holiday moves to the next day that isn’t one (§ 47-8-33(H)). Whether weekends in between also don’t count (NMSA § 12-2A-7(E)) isn’t settled; NOHM counts calendar days. NOHM adds 3 days when you mail it.
If the mail comes back, or the last known address is the unit the tenant left, serve another notice at any other address the tenant gave you (§ 47-8-13(F)).
Late fees: only if the lease provides them, at most 5% of the rent for each period in default, and you must give notice of the fee by the end of the next rental period (§ 47-8-15(D)).
A rent payment can’t be put toward deposits or damages unless you both agreed in writing (§ 47-8-15(G)).

forms.label: 7-day notice of noncompliance
forms.explain: Describes the breach with its dates and facts: fix it within 7 days, or the rental agreement ends.
forms.when: The resident broke the rental agreement (not rent), within the last 30 days or since you learned of it.
notes: For the first material breach of the lease (other than rent), or a breach of the tenant’s duties under § 47-8-22 that materially affects health and safety.
Describe what happened, with the dates and specific facts: the court can grant relief only on the grounds in the notice (§ 47-8-33(G)).
Serve it within 30 days of the breach, or of when you learned of it, or it isn’t effective (§ 47-8-33(C)).

A second material breach within 6 months of the first gets a 7-day notice with no chance to fix it (§ 47-8-33(B); Form 4-902’s “Second notice”). A substantial violation (drugs, a deadly weapon, serious harm, sexual assault, a break-in, robbery, or over $1,000 of damage, on or within 300 feet of the premises) gets a 3-day notice with no cure (§ 47-8-33(I); Form 4-901A). NOHM’s notice is the first-breach notice; ask a lawyer for the others.
A posted notice must also be mailed first class or handed over (§ 47-8-13(D)). NOHM adds 3 days when you mail it.

forms.label: 30-day notice to terminate a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month residency at least 30 days before the rental date named in it.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month resident out, no fault needed.
notes: A week-to-week residency needs 7 days’ written notice before the termination date instead (§ 47-8-37(A)).
A fixed-term lease ends on its end date; the statute requires no notice for it. Check your lease.
New Mexico requires no separate demand for possession: if the tenant stays after the date, you may file a petition for restitution (§ 47-8-37(C)).
You can’t end a tenancy, or threaten to, in retaliation within 6 months after the tenant’s protected acts (§ 47-8-39).
NOHM adds 3 days when you mail it.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (Forms 4-904, 4-905, 4-909, 4-913 NMRA)
forms.explain: The court’s own petition for restitution and the papers after it, each with where to get it, the values from your lease to copy onto it, and the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The notice ran out (or the term ended) and the resident hasn’t left.
notes: New Mexico’s Supreme Court has its own landlord-tenant forms. Clerks expect them, so NOHM fills in this worksheet for you to copy from, not a petition of its own. The worksheet isn’t filed.

Some courts use the Eviction Prevention and Diversion Program’s forms (4-904B petition, 4-905B summons) in nonpayment cases, and the 4-904B petition asks for a sworn affirmation and the court’s Resource Information Sheet. NOHM couldn’t confirm the program still runs in every district in 2026: ask the clerk which petition to use.

A company owner: in magistrate and metropolitan court, a closely held corporation or LLC may appear through an officer, member or manager it authorizes on Form 4-403 NMRA, sworn before a notary; in district court, it generally needs a lawyer. NOHM read the form, not the court rules themselves (Rules 2-107 and 3-107), so check with the clerk.
Never lock the resident out, shut off utilities or remove their things without a court order: the penalty is twice the monthly rent, and more (§ 47-8-36, § 47-8-48(C)).
Bring the rental agreement, every notice with proof of how and when you served it, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: New Mexico doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It’s good practice: a signed record of the home’s condition settles deposit disputes.
Give the resident a written rental agreement before the residency begins (§ 47-8-20(G)), and a copy of any rules when they sign it, or the rules can’t be enforced (§ 47-8-23(F)).
Disclose in writing, at or before the start, who manages the home and who receives notices and legal papers for the owner (§ 47-8-19(A)): NOHM has that disclosure.
Listings must show the base rent and every fee (§ 47-8-19.1); a screening fee is capped at $50, with the applicant’s written agreement and a receipt (§ 47-8-19.2).
Homes built before 1978: give the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Disclosure of owner and manager
forms.explain: Tells the resident, in writing, who manages the home and who receives notices and legal papers for the owner.
forms.when: At or before the start of the residency, and again when either changes.
notes: Required in writing at or before the residency begins (§ 47-8-19(A)), and kept current (§ 47-8-19(B)).
Without it, the resident is relieved of the duty to give you the notices the Act otherwise requires (§ 47-8-19(D)).
A property manager may sign for the owner.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give 24 hours’ written notice of your intent to enter, its purpose, and its date and estimated time frame, unless you and the resident agreed otherwise (§ 47-8-24(A)(1)).

No notice is needed to make repairs the resident asked for within 7 days of the request, or when you’re with a public inspector or a utility or cable representative (§ 47-8-24(A)(2)); or in an emergency (§ 47-8-24(B)).
If the resident offers another reasonable time, try to accommodate it (§ 47-8-24(A)(3)). Don’t use entry to harass (§ 47-8-24(C)).
A resident who refuses lawful access can be ordered to allow it, or the rental agreement ended (§ 47-8-24(E)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Month-to-month: at least 30 days before the rental date the new rent starts (§ 47-8-15(F)). A fixed term: at least 30 days before the term ends. A residency shorter than a month: one rental period ahead.
Raising a fee in the rental agreement (not the rent) needs 60 days’ written notice (§ 47-8-19.4).
New Mexico has no rent cap. You can’t raise the rent to retaliate (§ 47-8-39(A)); an increase made uniformly is allowed (§ 47-8-39(C)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the agreement ends or the resident leaves, whichever is later.
notes: Within 30 days after the rental agreement ends or the resident leaves, whichever is later, give an itemized list of the deductions and the balance. Mailing it, and any payment, to the resident’s last known address counts (§ 47-8-18(C)).
Nothing may be kept for normal wear and tear; uncleanliness isn’t normal wear and tear (§ 47-8-3(K)).

Miss the 30 days and you lose the right to keep any of it, to counterclaim for it, and to sue for damage to the home, and you owe the resident’s court costs and attorney’s fees (§ 47-8-18(D)). Keeping it in bad faith adds a $250 penalty (§ 47-8-18(E)).

Interest: on a one-year agreement with a deposit over one month’s rent, pay the resident interest yearly at the passbook rate (§ 47-8-18(A)(1)). For a shorter agreement the deposit can’t exceed one month’s rent (§ 47-8-18(A)(2)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: This notice is for property left after the resident abandoned the unit: absent more than 7 days in a row without telling you, after the rent is delinquent (§ 47-8-3(A)).

Store the property at least 30 days, and give this notice in person or by first-class mail to the last known address. If it comes back, or that address is the vacated unit, also send one to any other address the resident gave you: work, family or emergency contact (§ 47-8-34.1(A)(3)).
The notice must give a telephone number and an address where the resident can reach you to get the property back (§ 47-8-34.1(A)(2)).

A resident who surrendered the unit: store their property at least 14 days, with reasonable access; no notice is required (§ 47-8-34.1(B)). After a writ of restitution is executed: no duty to store it past 3 days (§ 47-8-34.1(C)).

Property worth $100 or less may be disposed of any way. Over $100: sell it, or keep it at fair market value, and mail any surplus with an itemized statement within 15 days (§ 47-8-34.1(D)–(E)). You may ask for reasonable storage and moving costs before releasing it, but can’t hold it for other debts (§ 47-8-34.1(G)–(H)).

forms.label: 14-day rent demand
forms.explain: Demands the rent owed, or the home back, within 14 days, with the Good Cause Eviction Law notice attached.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid; if it’s 5 days late, send the late-rent notice by certified mail first.
notes: First, if rent isn’t received within 5 days of the due date, send the tenant a written notice of nonpayment by certified mail (Real Prop. Law § 235-e(d)); NOHM has it as the 5-day late-rent notice. Without it, the tenant has a defense to the case.

You can’t serve it yourself: someone 18 or older who isn’t a party to the case must (UCS Landlord’s Guide). Leave it with someone, or post it, only after a reasonable try at handing it over; the courts’ guide reads that as two tries at different times.

Attach the Good Cause Eviction Law notice, filled in to say whether the premises are covered and, if exempt, why (Real Prop. Law § 231-c). Get it from the courts’ Landlord’s Guide or New York State Homes and Community Renewal.
When service by leaving it with someone or posting it is complete isn’t settled for a rent demand; NOHM adds 3 days when you serve it that way.
If the tenant pays all the rent due before the hearing, you must accept it and the case ends (RPAPL § 731(4)).
Late fees: only after rent is 5 days late, and at most $50 or 5% of the monthly rent, whichever is less (Real Prop. Law § 238-a(2)). They can’t go in this demand.
Where the Good Cause Eviction Law applies, unpaid rent is good cause only if it didn’t come from an unreasonable rent increase (Real Prop. Law § 216(1)(a)).
New York City’s Housing Court, and rent-stabilized units, have rules of their own; use a lawyer there.

forms.label: Notice to cure a lease violation
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what to stop or fix, and by when; New York leaves the period to the lease.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term (10 days to cure where the Good Cause Eviction Law applies).
notes: Follow your lease: its notice to cure and its notice ending the tenancy, in its periods. NOHM’s 30 days is longer than most leases ask.

Where the Good Cause Eviction Law applies (New York City and the localities that opted in), the tenant must have failed to stop after written notice that the violation cease within 10 days of receipt (Real Prop. Law § 216(1)(b)).
After a judgment for a lease breach, the court must stay the warrant 30 days so the tenant can fix it (RPAPL § 753(4)).
Serve it as a rent demand is served (RPAPL § 735), the safest way.

forms.label: 30, 60 or 90-day notice of non-renewal
forms.explain: Tells the tenant you won’t renew, or ends a month-to-month, with the notice the time they’ve lived there calls for.
forms.when: You won’t renew the lease, or want to end a month-to-month tenancy.
notes: Real Prop. Law § 226-c(2) sets the notice by the longer of how long the tenant has lived there and the lease’s term: under a year, 30 days; one to two years, 60; two years or more, 90. NOHM counts from the lease and ends the tenancy on the last day of a rental period, to be safe.
Given late, the tenancy goes on under its existing terms until the notice period has run from the day you gave it (§ 226-c(1)(a)).

Where the Good Cause Eviction Law applies (New York City and the cities, towns and villages that opted in), a covered tenancy can end only for a reason in Real Prop. Law § 216; say which on the attached notice. Check whether your locality opted in.

In New York City, the notice must be served the way a notice of petition is (Real Prop. Law § 232-a); NOHM’s ways of serving are those (RPAPL § 735), and NOHM adds 3 days when you leave it with someone or post it.
A fixed-term lease ends on its date with no notice to terminate, but this non-renewal notice is still required (§ 226-c).
Taking rent after the date can create a new tenancy, and a judge may dismiss your case (UCS Landlord’s Guide).
New York requires no separate demand for possession: if the tenant stays after the date, you may bring a holdover proceeding (RPAPL § 711(1)).

forms.label: 5-day late-rent notice (certified mail)
forms.explain: The written notice the law requires when rent isn’t received within 5 days of its due date, sent by certified mail.
forms.when: Rent wasn’t received within 5 days of the due date: send it before the 14-day rent demand.
notes: Send it by certified mail, and keep a copy and the certified-mail receipt: the courts’ nonpayment petition asks you to attach both.
Without it, the tenant can use the missing notice as an affirmative defense to a nonpayment case (Real Prop. Law § 235-e(d)).
It starts no period. Serve the 14-day rent demand next.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (UCS-LTN1, UCS-LTN2, UCS-LTH1, UCS-LTH2)
forms.explain: The courts’ notice of petition and petition for your case, where to get them, the values from your lease to copy onto them, and the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The rent demand ran out, or the tenancy ended, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: The courts publish their own notice of petition and petition for eviction cases outside New York City; the courts’ forms page says they’re required in City, District, Town and Village Courts from September 3, 2024 (NOHM saw that in a search result; the page wouldn’t open). NOHM fills in this worksheet for you to copy from, not a petition of its own. The worksheet isn’t filed.

A company landlord: in City and District Court, a corporation or voluntary association must appear with a lawyer; in Town or Village Court, a corporation may appear with a lawyer or an authorized officer, director or employee (UCS Landlord’s Guides). The guides don’t name LLCs: NOHM couldn’t confirm their rule, so ask the clerk or a lawyer.
New York City’s Housing Court has its own forms and rules, and many units there are rent-stabilized: use a lawyer.
Newburgh, Syracuse and Schenectady also ask the petition to show the rental is registered (RPAPL § 741(7)–(9)); NOHM read those items only in summary.
The courts’ do-it-yourself forms program isn’t open to corporations, owners of 3 or more units, or New York City property.
Bring the lease, the 5-day notice and its certified-mail receipt, the 14-day demand or the termination notice with the affidavit of service, the Good Cause notice, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition agreement
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: After the lease is signed, before move-in, if the tenant asks for the inspection.
notes: After the lease is signed and before the tenant moves in, offer to inspect the home together. If the tenant asks for the inspection, you both sign this agreement before they move in (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-108(1-a)(c)).
You can’t keep any of the deposit for a condition noted here.

Every lease and renewal carries the Good Cause Eviction Law notice (Real Prop. Law § 231-c(1)), the flood disclosure (§ 231-b) and the sprinkler notice (§ 231-a): NOHM has the flood and sprinkler forms.
When you deposit the security in a bank, tell the tenant in writing where (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-103(2)): NOHM has that notice. The deposit can’t exceed one month’s rent (§ 7-108(1-a)(a)).

Give a written receipt for rent paid in cash or by anything but the tenant’s own check (Real Prop. Law § 235-e). Application fees: only the actual cost of a background or credit check, at most $20 (§ 238-a(1)).
Homes built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure. New York City adds its own (bedbug history, lead, window guards); NOHM hasn’t confirmed those.

forms.label: Flood history and risk disclosure
forms.explain: The four flood questions every New York residential lease must answer, and the statute’s notice about flood insurance.
forms.when: With every residential lease: attach it when the lease is signed or renewed.
notes: Every residential lease must disclose these four things and carry the flood insurance notice (Real Prop. Law § 231-b).
Check the premises against FEMA’s current Flood Insurance Rate Maps. Disclose any prior flood damage you know of, or reasonably should know of, and what it was.
Attach it to the lease, and have every tenant sign.

forms.label: Sprinkler system notice
forms.explain: The bold-face notice every New York residential lease must give of whether the premises have a working sprinkler system.
forms.when: With every residential lease: attach it when the lease is signed or renewed.
notes: Every residential lease must give conspicuous notice, in bold face type, of whether the leased premises have a maintained and operative sprinkler system, and if they do, the last date it was maintained and inspected (Real Prop. Law § 231-a).

forms.label: Notice of where the deposit is held
forms.explain: Tells the tenant, in writing, the bank where you deposited their security and how much.
forms.when: When you deposit the security in a bank.
notes: The deposit stays the tenant’s money, held in trust, never mixed with yours (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-103(1)).
When you put it in a bank, tell each tenant who paid it, in writing, the bank’s name and address and the amount (§ 7-103(2)). The bank must have a place of business in New York.

A building with 6 or more units: the deposit must be in an interest-bearing account at the prevailing rate (§ 7-103(2-a)). In an interest-bearing account, you may keep one percent a year on the deposit for administration.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No New York statute sets notice for entry. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours; your lease may say more. The Attorney General’s tenants’ guide advises reasonable notice (NOHM didn’t re-read it).
New York City’s housing rules set their own notice for inspections and repairs; NOHM hasn’t confirmed them.
Where the Good Cause Eviction Law applies, a tenant who unreasonably refuses access for repairs, or to show the unit to a buyer or lender, gives you good cause (Real Prop. Law § 216(1)(f)).
A move-out inspection the tenant asked for needs at least 48 hours’ written notice (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-108(1-a)(d)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the higher rent you’ll renew at, with the 30, 60 or 90 days’ notice the law sets.
forms.when: At least 30, 60 or 90 days before the new rent starts, by how long the tenant has lived there or the lease’s term.
notes: An offer to renew with a rent increase of 5% or more needs written notice: 30 days if the tenant has lived there under a year and has a lease under a year; 60 days for one to two years, or a lease of one to two years; 90 days for two years or more, or a lease of two years or more (Real Prop. Law § 226-c(2)). NOHM uses it for any increase.
Given late, the tenancy goes on under its existing terms from the day you gave notice until the notice period runs (§ 226-c(1)(a)).

Attach the Good Cause Eviction Law notice (§ 231-c(1)). In a covered unit, an increase above the local rent standard (the lower of 5% plus the regional consumer price index change, or 10%) needs a justification on it, and unpaid rent from an unreasonable increase isn’t good cause to evict (§ 216(1)(a)).
New York has no statewide rent cap. Rent-stabilized and rent-controlled units have their own rules.
During a lease, change the rent only as the lease allows.

forms.label: Notice of the right to a move-out inspection
forms.explain: Tells the tenant they may ask for an inspection before moving out, and be there for it.
forms.when: Soon after you or the tenant gives notice to end the tenancy.
notes: Within a reasonable time after either of you gives notice to end the tenancy, tell the tenant in writing of their right to ask for an inspection before moving out, and to be there (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-108(1-a)(d)). Not needed if the tenant gave less than two weeks’ notice.

If they ask, inspect no earlier than two weeks and no later than one week before the end, on at least 48 hours’ written notice; then give them an itemized statement of the repairs or cleaning you’d deduct for, and let them fix it before they leave.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 14 days after the tenant moves out.
notes: Within 14 days after the tenant moves out, give an itemized statement of the basis for anything you keep, and return the rest. Miss it and you forfeit any right to keep any of the deposit (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-108(1-a)(e)).
You must prove what you keep is reasonable (§ 7-108(1-a)(f)). A willful violation can cost punitive damages up to twice the deposit (§ 7-108(1-a)(g)).
Nothing for ordinary wear and tear, a prior tenant’s damage, or a condition noted in the move-in agreement.
Interest: a deposit in an interest-bearing account earns it for the tenant, less the 1% a year you may keep (§ 7-103(2)). Rent-stabilized units have their own rules.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: No New York statute sets a notice, a storage period or a sale for a tenant’s belongings. NOHM fills in 30 days to hold them; ask a lawyer before you dispose of anything of value.

Use it only after the tenant has moved out, or the officer executed the warrant: never while they still have possession. When an officer executes a warrant, the officer removes the tenant’s possessions (UCS Landlord’s Guide).
You may charge the reasonable, itemized cost of moving and storing them to the deposit (Gen. Oblig. Law § 7-108(1-a)(b)).

forms.label: 10-day demand for rent
forms.explain: Demands all past-due rent: if it isn’t paid within 10 days, the lease term is forfeited.
forms.when: Rent is past due and your lease has no clause ending it for nonpayment.
notes: G.S. 42-3 fills a gap: use it when your lease has no clause ending the tenancy for unpaid rent (so the courts’ complaint form instructions and the UNC School of Government read it). If your lease has one, you proceed under the lease, and must still demand possession before you file (G.S. 42-26(a)).
Make the demand clear: pay all past-due rent, and say you intend to use the statute’s forfeiture (Snipes v. Snipes). A lease line saying a demand is always in effect doesn’t count.
No rule sets how the 10 days are counted. NOHM counts 10 full days after the day of the demand, so file on the 11th day or later; it adds 3 days when you mail it.
Until judgment, the tenant can stop the case by paying the rent due and the court costs (G.S. 42-33).
Late fees: only if the lease provides them, after rent is 5 days late, at most $15 or 5% of the monthly rent, whichever is greater (G.S. 42-46(a)).
No statute sets how to deliver it. Hand it over or mail it, and keep a dated record.

forms.label: Notice of lease violation
forms.explain: Tells the tenant about a breach; North Carolina leaves the rest to the lease.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease condition that the lease says ends the tenancy.
notes: Your lease decides: it must say the tenancy ends on that breach (G.S. 42-26(a)(2)). Then demand possession before you file (G.S. 42-26(a)).

For a breach of the tenant’s duties in G.S. 42-43(a) (keeping it clean and safe, the plumbing, the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, damage), notify the tenant in writing, except in an emergency (G.S. 42-43(b)).
The lease may say that taking partial rent doesn’t waive the breach (G.S. 42-26(c)).
Criminal activity is its own expedited case, with no notice first (G.S. 42-59 to 42-68); ask a lawyer.

forms.label: 7-day notice to quit (month-to-month)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at the end of a rental period, with at least 7 days’ notice.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy needs 2 days’ notice, a year-to-year one a month before the end of the year, and a manufactured home space 60 days before the end of the period (G.S. 42-14).
If the tenant stays after the date, demand possession in writing before you file (G.S. 42-26(a)): NOHM has the demand for possession.
A subsidized or federally covered tenancy (VAWA, Section 8, public housing) may need more.
No statute sets how to deliver it. NOHM adds 3 days when you mail it.

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Every summary ejectment needs a demand that the tenant surrender the premises before you file (G.S. 42-26(a)); the complaint says you made it. The statute sets no waiting period: NOHM fills in 3 days.
Use it after the lease ran out, after your notice to quit ended a periodic tenancy, after the 10-day rent demand ran, or when the tenant broke a lease condition that ends the tenancy.
No statute says how to deliver it. Hand it over or mail it, and keep a dated record.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (AOC-CVM-201)
forms.explain: The courts’ Complaint in Summary Ejectment and the papers after it, where to get them, the values from your lease to copy onto them, and the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The 10-day demand, the lease or the notice to quit ran out, and the tenant hasn’t left after your demand for possession.
notes: The Administrative Office of the Courts’ Complaint in Summary Ejectment (AOC-CVM-201) is what clerks and magistrates expect. The law allows a complaint in any clear form (G.S. 7A-216), but NOHM fills in this worksheet for you to copy onto the court’s form. The worksheet isn’t filed.
Don’t change an AOC form in a way that keeps its official look; if you change it, mark it as changed and say what changed (G.S. 7A-232).
NOHM read the complaint form’s 2012 revision (the courts’ site wouldn’t open); a search result shows a July 2024 revision NOHM couldn’t read. Check the boxes against the current form.
Name the owner as the plaintiff, not the managing agent (the UNC School of Government, citing Rule 17(a)). An agent with actual knowledge of the facts may sign.

The writ forms (AOC-CV-401, Writ of Possession; AOC-CV-412, for a judgment more than 30 days old) and when clerks issue the writ (in practice, after the 10-day appeal period) come from search results NOHM couldn’t open: ask the clerk.

Fees you may recover (G.S. 42-46): a complaint-filing fee if the tenant cures before judgment, a court-appearance fee if you win, and court costs; attorney’s fees only under a written lease and only if you prevail.
Bring the lease, the demands and your record of them, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: North Carolina doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It’s good practice: a signed record of the home’s condition settles deposit disputes.
Within 30 days after the lease begins, tell the tenant where the deposit is held (G.S. 42-50): NOHM has that notice.

Smoke alarms, and carbon monoxide alarms where there’s a fossil-fuel heater, appliance or fireplace or an attached garage, must work at the start of each tenancy, with new batteries (G.S. 42-42(a)(5), (7)).
If you bill for water and know it exceeds a maximum contaminant level, say so (G.S. 42-42(a)(6)). If you require renter’s insurance, you can’t name the insurer (G.S. 42-46(l)).
Homes built before 1978: give the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of where the deposit is held
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the bank where their deposit is held in trust, or the insurer that bonds it.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the lease term begins.
notes: Keep the deposit in a trust account with a licensed and federally insured depository institution or trust institution in North Carolina, or furnish a bond from a North Carolina-licensed insurer (G.S. 42-50).
Tell the tenant within 30 days after the lease term begins (G.S. 42-50). Willfully failing to can void your right to keep any of the deposit (G.S. 42-55).
The deposit can’t exceed two weeks’ rent for a week-to-week tenancy, one and a half months’ rent for month-to-month, or two months’ rent for longer terms (G.S. 42-51(b)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No North Carolina statute sets notice for entry; your lease decides. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
In an emergency you may need to go in right away; tell the tenant as soon as you can.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No North Carolina statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date; for a month-to-month, that is more than the 7-day notice to quit (G.S. 42-14).
During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Cities and counties can’t regulate rents (G.S. 42-14.1). An eviction substantially in response to a tenant’s protected act within the last 12 months can be defended as retaliation (G.S. 42-37.1).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get possession back.
notes: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get possession back, itemize any damage in writing and mail or deliver it, with the rest of the deposit (G.S. 42-52).
If you can’t work out the full claim in 30 days, send an interim accounting within 30 days and a final one within 60 (G.S. 42-52).
If you don’t know the tenant’s address, apply the deposit after 30 days and hold the balance at least six months for them to collect (G.S. 42-52).
Willfully failing to follow the deposit, bond or notice rules voids your right to keep any of it, and can cost damages and attorney’s fees (G.S. 42-55).

The deposit act covers anyone in the business of renting or managing homes, except single rooms (G.S. 42-56); transient occupancies and vacation rentals are outside the chapter (G.S. 42-14.6, 42-39(a1)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: For property left after the sheriff executed a writ of possession. Hold it 7 days; release it if the tenant asks during that time (G.S. 42-25.9(g)).

To sell it, mail the tenant written notice by first-class mail to the last known address at least 7 days before the sale, with its date, time and place, and that any surplus after unpaid rent, damages, storage fees and sale costs goes to the tenant on request within 7 days, then to the county (G.S. 42-25.9(g)). Fill in the sale below and NOHM adds that notice.

Property worth less than $500 in all is abandoned 5 days after the writ is executed (G.S. 42-25.9(h)). Property worth $750 or less may go to a nonprofit that stores it 30 days, with the notice G.S. 42-25.9(d) requires.
A tenant who left without a writ: property is abandoned 10 or more days after you post a notice of suspected abandonment inside and outside the home and get no response (G.S. 42-25.9(e)).

forms.label: 3-day notice of intention to evict (rent unpaid)
forms.explain: The written notice North Dakota requires before you file to evict for unpaid rent: 3 days, then you may file.
forms.when: Rent is still unpaid 3 days after it was due.
notes: Rent must be unpaid 3 days after it was due before you serve it (§ 47-32-01(4)).

You can’t serve it yourself. The sheriff, or another adult who isn’t a party to or interested in the case, serves it as a summons is served and signs a declaration of service. Only if the tenant can’t be found (try at least once between 6 and 10 p.m.) may the sheriff or a process server post it on the premises (§ 47-32-02).

Counting (the courts’ instructions): start with the day after service and count 3 calendar days; if the third day is a Saturday, Sunday or North Dakota holiday, go to the next day that isn’t one. File after that.
The statute gives the tenant no right to pay and stay; the courts’ self-help form offers the choice to pay the total due or move out. If you accept full payment, don’t file.

forms.label: 3-day notice of intention to evict (lease violation)
forms.explain: The written notice North Dakota requires before you file to evict for breaking a material term of a written lease.
forms.when: The tenant violated a material term of the written lease.
notes: Only for a material term of a written lease (§ 47-32-01(8)). The statute gives no chance to fix it.
A tenant who unreasonably disturbs other tenants’ peaceful enjoyment can be taken to court with no notice first (§ 47-32-01(7)), and the court can’t stay that eviction (§ 47-32-04).

You can’t serve it yourself. The sheriff, or another adult who isn’t a party to or interested in the case, serves it as a summons is served and signs a declaration of service. Only if the tenant can’t be found (try at least once between 6 and 10 p.m.) may the sheriff or a process server post it on the premises (§ 47-32-02).

Counting (the courts’ instructions): start with the day after service and count 3 calendar days; if the third day is a Saturday, Sunday or North Dakota holiday, go to the next day that isn’t one. File after that.

forms.label: One-month notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy with at least one calendar month’s written notice.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A lease that turned month-to-month when its term ran out (§ 47-16-06 or § 47-16-06.1) can end only on the last day of a month (§ 47-16-15(5)), so NOHM ends every one on the last day of a rental period. If rent isn’t due on the 1st, pick the last day of a calendar month.
The lease may ask for longer notice in writing (§ 47-16-15(2)). A week-to-week tenancy needs a week’s notice before the end of the week (§ 47-16-15(1)).
If the tenant stays after the date, serve the 3-day notice of intention to evict before you file (§ 47-32-02): NOHM has it, for a tenant holding over.
The statute names no way to deliver it. NOHM adds 3 days when you mail it.

forms.label: 3-day notice of intention to evict (holding over)
forms.explain: The written notice North Dakota requires before you file against a tenant who stayed after the lease, or your notice, ended it.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: A tenant who holds over after the lease ended, or after your termination notice ran, gets this 3-day notice before you file (§ 47-32-01(4), § 47-32-02).

You can’t serve it yourself. The sheriff, or another adult who isn’t a party to or interested in the case, serves it as a summons is served and signs the proof of service. Only if the tenant can’t be found (try at least once between 6 and 10 p.m.) may the sheriff or a process server post it on the premises.

Counting (the courts’ instructions): start the day after service and count 3 calendar days; if the third day is a Saturday, Sunday or North Dakota holiday, go to the next day that isn’t one. NOHM fills in that day.

forms.label: Complaint for eviction
forms.explain: The eviction filing for the district court: the facts the statute asks for, the notice you served, and what you ask the court for.
forms.when: The 3-day notice of intention to evict ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: North Dakota has no mandatory eviction forms: the courts’ self-help packet isn’t official, and courts needn’t accept it. NOHM writes the complaint from the statute and the packet’s outline.
File it with a summons in the district court of the county where the rental is. The filing fee is $160 (the courts’ instructions, June 2026).

The summons sets the hearing 3 to 15 days after it’s issued. Serve it at least 3 days before the hearing if it’s handed to the tenant in the county, otherwise at least 7 (§ 47-32-02). The sheriff or another adult who isn’t a party serves it.

Posting the summons on the door is allowed only if the tenant can’t be found after at least one try between 6 and 10 p.m., with your affidavit saying so, and a copy mailed to the tenant’s last known address (§ 47-32-02).
A judicial referee may hear the case; either side may ask in writing for a judge within 7 days of getting the notice of hearing. The tenant answers at the hearing.
Judgment is for immediate restitution of the premises; for hardship the court may stay it up to 5 days, but not for a disturbance of the peace (§ 47-32-04). The sheriff carries out the writ.
Only a lawyer licensed in North Dakota can file for a company (an LLC or a corporation); papers a non-lawyer signs for one are void (the courts’ eviction page).
Only rent and profits, or damages from the tenant’s possession, may be joined with the eviction; the tenant may counterclaim only as a setoff (§ 47-32-04).
No verification is required. Attach the lease and the notice of intention to evict with its proof of service.

forms.label: Statement of condition of premises
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: When you enter the rental agreement: both of you sign it.
notes: North Dakota requires it: give the tenant a statement of the condition of the premises when you enter the rental agreement, and both of you sign it (§ 47-16-07.2).

The deposit goes in a federally insured, interest-bearing account for the tenant, and can’t exceed one month’s rent (two in limited cases); a pet deposit is capped at the greater of $2,500 or two months’ rent, and none for an assistance animal (§ 47-16-07.1).
A lease that asks the tenant to give more than a month’s notice must say so with a space the tenant initials (§ 47-16-15(4)).
An automatic renewal clause in a lease of two months or more needs a written reminder at least 30 days before the lease ends (§ 47-16-06.1): NOHM has it.
Homes built before 1978: give the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: North Dakota sets no number of hours: notify the tenant and get their consent to a time certain, unless that’s impractical (§ 47-16-07.3(2)). NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.

If the tenant doesn’t object after notice of a time certain, consent is presumed. Give the notice in person, by posting it in a conspicuous place in or about the unit for a reasonable time, or any other way that actually reaches the tenant.
In an emergency, or if you reasonably believe the tenant abandoned the unit or is in substantial violation of the lease, you may enter at any time (§ 47-16-07.3(1)). Don’t use access to harass.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the end of the month before the new rent starts.
notes: In a month-to-month lease, give written notice at least 30 days before the month ends; the new rent starts when the month ends (§ 47-16-07). NOHM counts 31 days to the new rent’s due date, so the notice is always in time.
Any reasonable way that actually tells the tenant counts (§ 47-16-07).
After a change of terms, the tenant may end the tenancy at the end of a month on 25 days’ notice (§ 47-16-15(3)).
North Dakota has no rent cap, and cities can’t control rents (§ 47-16-02.1).

forms.label: Automatic renewal reminder
forms.explain: The written reminder of the lease’s automatic renewal clause, without which the clause can’t be enforced.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the lease expires, if it renews automatically.
notes: In a lease of two months or more, an automatic renewal clause is enforceable only if you remind the tenant of it in writing, delivered personally or by first-class mail, at least 30 days before the lease expires (§ 47-16-06.1).
Without the reminder, the lease expires and turns into a month-to-month tenancy on its latest terms.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the lease ends and the tenant gives back possession.
notes: Within 30 days after the lease ends and the tenant gives back possession, deliver or mail the itemized list, the amount due and a written notice of any amount still due you or the refund due them, to the last address the tenant gave you (§ 47-16-07.1(3)).
Pay the deposit’s interest with it, unless the tenant lived there less than 9 months.
Withholding any of it without reasonable justification costs treble damages (§ 47-16-07.1(4)).
Money the tenant doesn’t claim within a year is reported as unclaimed property (§ 47-30.2-04).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: North Dakota requires no notice: property worth $2,500 or less in all may be kept and disposed of 28 or more days after you learn, or it reasonably appears, that the tenant left (§ 47-16-30.1). Giving notice heads off disputes. NOHM counts the 28 days from this notice, the safe way.

You keep what a sale brings, and may take storage and moving costs beyond it from the deposit. After an eviction and the special execution, you have a lien on what you moved for reasonable storage and moving costs.
Property worth more than $2,500: no statute; ask a lawyer.

forms.label: 3-day notice to leave (rent unpaid)
forms.explain: The notice to leave the premises Ohio requires before an eviction for unpaid rent, with the statute’s warning.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Ohio’s statute has no grace period).
notes: This is a notice to leave, not to pay. Taking rent after you serve it may waive it; some courts ask you to say in the complaint that you haven’t (Lakewood Municipal Court’s form does). NOHM couldn’t confirm that as a statewide rule.

Counting (Ohio Rev. Code § 1.14): the day you deliver it doesn’t count. File no earlier than the fourth day after delivery; if the third day is a Sunday or legal holiday, wait a day more. NOHM adds 3 days when you send it by certified mail.
Ohio has no grace period in the statute: serve it any time after a default.
A written lease: unpaid rent is a breach of the lease (§ 1923.02(A)(9)). An oral tenancy: unpaid rent forfeits the right of occupancy, and this notice ends the tenancy (§ 1923.02(B)).

forms.label: 30-day notice to remedy (health and safety)
forms.explain: Names the tenant’s breach of a duty that affects health and safety: fix it in 30 days, or the agreement ends.
forms.when: The tenant’s breach of a § 5321.05 duty materially affects health and safety.
notes: Only for a breach of the tenant’s duties under § 5321.05(A) that materially affects health and safety: safe and sanitary premises, garbage, plumbing, fixtures and appliances, no damage, not disturbing neighbors (not the drug duty, (A)(9)).
If it isn’t fixed and the agreement ends, you must still serve the 3-day notice to leave the premises before you file (§ 1923.04): NOHM has it.
Another breach of a written lease needs only the 3-day notice to leave (§ 1923.02(A)(9), § 1923.04).
Drug activity the police told you about has its own 3-day termination notice (§ 5321.17(C)); ask a lawyer.
The statute names no way to deliver this notice and runs it from receipt: NOHM uses § 1923.04’s ways and adds 3 days for certified mail.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at least 30 days before a rental date.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ notice before the date (§ 5321.17(A)).
If the tenant stays after the date, you must still serve the 3-day notice to leave the premises before you file (§ 1923.04): NOHM has it.
You can’t end a tenancy to retaliate for a complaint to a code agency, a complaint about your duties, or joining a tenants’ union (§ 5321.02).
