The statute names no way to deliver it: NOHM uses § 1923.04’s ways and adds 3 days for certified mail.

forms.label: 3-day notice to leave (lease ended or broken)
forms.explain: The notice to leave the premises Ohio requires before any eviction other than for rent, with the statute’s warning.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Ohio requires this notice before every eviction (§ 1923.04(A)): after the lease ran out, after your 30-day notice ended a month-to-month, after a 30-day notice to remedy wasn’t met, or for a breach of a written lease. For unpaid rent, use the 3-day notice to leave for rent.
Counting (Ohio Rev. Code § 1.14): the day you deliver it doesn’t count. File no earlier than the day after the date in it; NOHM moves a third day on a weekend or holiday to the next business day.
For a breach of a written lease, write what the tenant did under “Anything to add”, and choose “Another reason”.

forms.label: Complaint in forcible entry and detainer
forms.explain: The eviction filing: the complaint for possession (and for rent and damages), with the summons in the words the statute requires, for the clerk.
forms.when: The 3-day notice to leave ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Ohio has no statewide eviction court forms; courts publish their own. NOHM writes the complaint from the statute. Check your court’s local rules and forms: some ask more (Lakewood’s asks whether the tenant gets federal housing assistance, and that you haven’t taken rent since the notice).

File it with the clerk of the municipal or county court for the rental’s address, with copies for each defendant and the 3-day notice. The clerk issues the summons (the last page has the words the statute requires) and serves it by ordinary mail and as you ask: by bailiff, sheriff or certified mail (§ 1923.06).

The summons is served at least 7 days before the hearing, and the hearing on possession is no sooner than the 7th day after service is complete (§ 1923.06(A), (H)(1)). The answer day for rent and damages is 28 days after service (§ 1923.06(H)(2)).
Any defense may be raised at trial (§ 1923.061); either side may ask for a jury. A continuance is 8 days at most, unless you agree or the tenant posts a bond for the rent (§ 1923.08).
Only the owner or a licensed lawyer may sign and file. A property manager can’t, and a company owner needs a lawyer (Cleveland Bar Assn. v. Picklo, 2002, as courts’ notices to landlords say).
Taking rent after the notice to leave may waive it. NOHM couldn’t confirm that as statewide law, but some courts ask you to say you haven’t; ask a lawyer before you accept any.
Never lock the tenant out, shut off utilities or take their things to get them out (§ 5321.15).

forms.label: Request for writ of execution
forms.explain: Asks the court for the writ that has the bailiff or sheriff restore the premises to you, with the writ in the statute’s form for the judge.
forms.when: The court entered judgment for restitution of the premises and the tenant is still there.
notes: After a judgment for restitution, the court issues the writ at your request, in the statute’s form (§ 1923.13(A)). The officer executes it within 10 days of receiving it (§ 1923.14(A)).
Local rules set when you may ask: in Lakewood Municipal Court, no sooner than 10 days after the judgment and no later than 30. Check your court’s rule.
An appeal with a stay and any bond the court requires stops the writ (§ 1923.14(A)).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Ohio doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It’s good practice: a signed record of the home’s condition settles deposit disputes.
Every written rental agreement must name the owner and the owner’s agent, with their addresses (§ 5321.18(A)); for an oral one, give that notice in writing at the start: NOHM has it.
If you rent 3 or fewer units, say so in the written agreement (or in writing at move-in for an oral one) and the tenant’s rent-escrow remedy doesn’t apply (§ 5321.07(C)).
Ask the tenant to give you a forwarding address in writing when they leave (§ 5321.16(B)).

In counties over 200,000 people, owners file their information with the county auditor (§ 5323.02; NOHM hasn’t re-read the 2025 change). Homes built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of owner and agent (oral lease)
forms.explain: Tells a tenant with no written lease the name and address of the owner and the owner’s agent.
forms.when: At the start of an oral tenancy (a written lease must include it).
notes: A written rental agreement must contain the owner’s and the agent’s names and addresses (§ 5321.18(A)); with an oral one, give this written notice when the tenancy begins (§ 5321.18(B)).
For a company, give its principal place of business in the county (or else in Ohio) and the name of the person in charge.
Without it, the tenant is excused from the notices §§ 5321.07(A) and 5321.08(A) otherwise require (§ 5321.18(C)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give reasonable notice and enter only at reasonable times; 24 hours is presumed reasonable (§ 5321.04(A)(8)). The statute names no way to give it.
In an emergency, or where notice is impracticable, you may enter without it. Don’t abuse the right of access (§ 5321.04(A)(7)); a tenant can recover damages for improper entry (§ 5321.04(B)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Ohio statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date, the notice a month-to-month needs to end (§ 5321.17(B)).
During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Ohio has no rent control; cities can’t impose it (§ 5321.19). You can’t raise rent to retaliate for a complaint (§ 5321.02); increases for improvements or higher costs are allowed.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the agreement ends and you get possession back.
notes: Within 30 days after the agreement ends and you get possession back, deliver a written notice itemizing every deduction, with the amount due, to the forwarding address the tenant gave you in writing (§ 5321.16(B)).
A tenant who didn’t give a forwarding address in writing can’t get damages or attorney’s fees for a late notice.
Interest: on any deposit over $50 or one month’s rent, whichever is greater, pay 5% a year on the excess, yearly, if the tenant stayed 6 months or more (§ 5321.16(A)).
Wrongful withholding costs the amount withheld again as damages, plus attorney’s fees (§ 5321.16(C)). Ohio has no deposit cap.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: No Ohio statute sets a notice, a storage period or a sale for a residential tenant’s belongings. NOHM fills in 30 days to hold them; ask a lawyer before disposing of anything of value.
Use it only after the tenant has moved out, or the writ was executed: never while they still have possession, and never to collect rent (§ 5321.15).
Manufactured homes in a park have their own rules (§§ 1923.12 to 1923.14).

forms.label: 5-day demand for rent
forms.explain: Demands the past-due rent: if it isn’t paid in 5 days the rental agreement can be terminated. It is also the demand for possession.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Oklahoma has no grace period).
notes: Oklahoma sets no grace period: you may serve this as soon as rent is unpaid when due (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 131(A)–(B)), and before or after you file a suit for the rent.
The five days start the day after service. If the fifth day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the period runs to the next day that isn’t (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 61).

Serve it on the tenant personally. Only if the tenant can’t be located may you give it to a family member over 12 who lives with them; only if neither can be served may you post it on the unit and mail a copy certified (or by the Post Office’s Firm Mailing Book for Accountable Mail) (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(E)).
When it is posted and mailed, the statute doesn’t say when service is complete; NOHM adds 3 days for the mail.

The demand for rent is itself the demand for possession (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 131(B)): if the rent isn’t paid, you can file the eviction affidavit without another notice. That’s why NOHM has no separate demand form for Oklahoma.
Oklahoma’s definition of rent (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 102(11)) can reach other lease payments, but NOHM demands rent only. Claim late fees and damages in the eviction affidavit.

forms.label: 10-day notice to remedy a breach
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong: fix it in 10 days, or the rental agreement ends no sooner than 15 days after they get it.
forms.when: The tenant broke the lease or a tenant’s duty under the law (not rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or failed to do: the statute requires the notice to specify it.
The ten days run from when the tenant receives it. NOHM adds 3 days when it is posted and mailed.

Serve it on the tenant personally. Only if the tenant can’t be located may you give it to a family member over 12 who lives with them; only if neither can be served may you post it on the unit and mail a copy certified (or by the Post Office’s Firm Mailing Book for Accountable Mail) (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(E)).

A breach you can fix by a repair, a replacement or cleaning: after 10 days’ written notice you may do the work yourself and bill it as rent on the next due date, but then you can’t end the lease for that breach (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 132(A)).
Any later breach after this notice lets you end the lease on written notice, without another chance to fix it (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 132(B)).

Imminent, irremediable harm to the premises or a person: you may file the eviction at once (§ 132(C)). Criminal activity that threatens other tenants, or drug-related criminal activity on or near the premises: immediate termination (§ 132(D)). Ask a lawyer before you rely on either.

Oklahoma needs no separate demand for possession: a tenant who stays after the tenancy ends or is terminated can be sued for possession right away (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(D)). So NOHM has no separate demand form for Oklahoma.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a date at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out; no reason is needed.
notes: Any day at least 30 days after service works: Oklahoma doesn’t require it to end a rental period (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(A)).
A tenancy of less than a month (week to week) needs 7 days’ written notice instead (§ 111(B)). A lease for a definite term ends on its last day without notice (§ 111(C)).

Serve it on the tenant personally. Only if the tenant can’t be located may you give it to a family member over 12 who lives with them; only if neither can be served may you post it on the unit and mail a copy certified (or by the Post Office’s Firm Mailing Book for Accountable Mail) (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(E)).

Oklahoma has no just-cause rule, but you can’t refuse to renew or end a tenancy because a tenant or household member is a victim of domestic violence, sexual violence or stalking (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 113.3).

A tenant who stays willfully and not in good faith can owe up to twice the average monthly rent, prorated daily, for each month they stay (§ 111(D)). If you agree to them staying, a new month-to-month tenancy begins.

Oklahoma needs no separate demand for possession: a tenant who stays after the tenancy ends or is terminated can be sued for possession right away (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(D)). So NOHM has no separate demand form for Oklahoma.

forms.label: Eviction affidavit (forcible entry and detainer)
forms.explain: The sworn statement that starts the eviction in district court: the premises, the tenants, why, the notice served, and what they owe.
forms.when: The notice ran out, or the lease ended, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: File it with the clerk of the district court in the county where the rental is (Okla. Stat. tit. 12, §§ 1148.1, 1148.15). Sign it in front of a notary or the court clerk.
Many clerks hand out the Oklahoma Bar Association’s plain-language affidavit (oscn.net, evictions-affidavit.pdf). If yours asks for it, copy these facts onto it.

The clerk issues the summons. The hearing is set 5 to 10 days after it issues (§§ 1148.4, 1148.16), and it must be served at least 3 days before: by the sheriff or a process server, by leaving it with someone over 15 living there, or, failing both, by certified mail (§ 1148.5). Posting with certified mail at least 5 days before gives you possession only, no money judgment unless the tenant appears (§ 1148.5A).
The tenant needn’t file an answer before the hearing (§ 1148.6(C)), and possession is never tried to a jury (§ 1148.7).
If you win, ask the clerk for the writ, then give the 48-hour notice before it is executed (NOHM’s next form).

If the money you claim is $10,000 or less, the case can go on the small-claims docket; there an LLC or corporation can appear through an officer, member, manager or full-time employee (§§ 1148.14, 1751).
The court awards the winner a reasonable attorney fee (§ 1148.9).
Bring the lease, the notice and how you served it, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: 48-hour notice before the writ is executed
forms.explain: Tells the tenant you, your agent or an officer will return in at least 48 hours to restore you to possession under the writ.
forms.when: You won, the clerk issued the writ, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Ask for the writ after judgment (Okla. Stat. tit. 12, § 1148.10). A motion for a new trial (only within 3 days) doesn’t stop it.
Give this notice to the tenant in person, or post it in a conspicuous place at the premises (§ 1148.10A(A), (C)). Come back no sooner than 48 hours after, at the date and time in it.
You may call the sheriff or the city police to help (§ 1148.10A(E)). Never remove the tenant or their things by force yourself.

Within 2 days of the judgment (up to 7 if the court allows) the tenant may post a supersedeas bond and appeal; they must then pay rent into the court clerk’s office while the appeal runs (§ 1148.10A(F)).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Oklahoma doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: walk through with the tenant, both sign it, and keep a copy for the deposit.

Required in writing at or before move-in: who manages the premises, who owns them (or their agent for service of process and notices), and, in the lease itself, prominently, who is entitled to accept service and notices (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 116(A)). Keep them current.
If the premises flooded within the past 5 years and you know it, say so prominently in the written lease (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 113a(A)).
If you know or have reason to know it was used to make methamphetamine, disclose it before the lease starts, unless it tested at or below 0.1 µg per 100 cm² (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 118(C)).
An agreement for the tenant to do repairs must be in a conspicuous writing separate from the lease (§ 118(B)); give the tenant your rules at signing (§ 126(A)(6)).
Built before 1978: give the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least one day’s notice and enter only at reasonable times, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 128(C)).
In an emergency you may enter without consent (§ 128(B)). Don’t use entry to harass the tenant.
If a tenant refuses lawful entry you may seek an injunction or end the agreement (§ 128(E)); entering unlawfully lets the tenant recover damages (§ 124).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Oklahoma statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days, the notice that ends a month-to-month tenancy (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 111(A)), and starts the new rent on a due date.
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Oklahoma has no rent cap, and cities can’t regulate rents (Okla. Stat. tit. 11, § 14-101.1).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Return the balance, with this itemized statement, within 45 days after the tenancy ends, you get possession back, and the tenant asks for the deposit in writing (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 115(B)). If they don’t ask in writing within 6 months, it reverts to you.
Send it by return-receipt mail, signed for by someone of service age at the address, or hand it to the tenant if you can reasonably find them.
Keep the deposit in an escrow account at a federally insured bank in Oklahoma; misappropriating it is a crime (§ 115(A)). No interest is owed.
If you don’t follow § 115, the tenant can recover the deposit and any prepaid rent, and the winner gets attorney’s fees (§§ 115(E), 105(B)).
Oklahoma doesn’t cap deposits. If you sell, transfer the deposits and tell the tenants in writing who holds them (§ 115(C)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Send it by certified mail to the tenant’s last-known address for property that has an ascertainable or apparent value (Okla. Stat. tit. 41, § 130(B)). Property with no ascertainable value, and perishables, you may dispose of without notice (§ 130(A)).
The statute lets you specify the time; NOHM fills in 30 days, when property left with you is conclusively abandoned.
Store it safely and with reasonable care. Storage in the unit can’t cost more than its fair rental value; a commercial storage company’s actual charges can be passed on (§ 130(C)).
Use it only after the tenant abandoned or surrendered the unit, or was lawfully removed by eviction.
If a sole tenant died, follow § 130.1 instead (the person they designated, 30 days from the notice’s postmark).

forms.label: 13-day notice of nonpayment of rent
forms.explain: Gives the tenant 13 days to pay the rent owed, or the rental agreement ends. Goes with the court’s rental-assistance notice.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid on the 5th day of the rental period (counting the due date).
notes: Serve it no sooner than the 5th day of the rental period, counting the day rent is due: rent due on the 1st, serve on the 5th or later (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.394(2)(b)). Oregon also has a 10-day notice from the 8th day; NOHM uses the 13-day notice.
Attach the Oregon Judicial Department’s rental-assistance notice (FED-Notice.pdf, all its languages) to every copy. Without it the court must dismiss the eviction (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.395(3)).

The notice must give the amount and a date and time to pay: NOHM gives 11:59 p.m. on the last day, when Oregon’s day ends (Or. Rev. Stat. §§ 90.160(1), 90.394(3)). Weekends and holidays aren’t skipped.

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it first class (not certified: Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.100(18)) and NOHM adds the 3 days the law adds. Mail-and-attach works only if your written lease allows it for notices from the tenant to you too; mail-and-email only with the statutory email addendum signed after move-in (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.155(1)(c)–(d), (5)). Neither adds days.

A payment the tenant mails within the period is on time, unless you served this in person, by mail-and-attach or by mail-and-email AND both your lease and this notice name a place to pay (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.394(4)).
You must accept a check or another commercially reasonable payment and may not insist on electronic payment; refusing an allowed payment bars this notice (Or. Laws 2026, ch. 23, § 3).
Taking partial rent after this notice waives it unless you and the tenant signed a non-waiver agreement (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.417(4)).
A week-to-week tenancy uses a 72-hour notice instead (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.394(1)); ask a lawyer.
If the rent isn’t paid, file the eviction: Oregon needs no separate demand for possession, so NOHM has none.

forms.label: 30-day notice with stated cause (14 days to cure)
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong and how to fix it: cure in 14 days, or the rental agreement ends in 30.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease or a tenant’s duty (not rent alone).
notes: In the description, say exactly what the tenant did or failed to do, AND at least one way they can fix it: the statute requires both (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.392(3)).

Causes: a material violation of the lease (including not paying a late charge or a utility or service charge), a material violation of the tenant’s duties under Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.325, or failure to pay rent (§ 90.392(2)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it first class (not certified: Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.100(18)) and NOHM adds the 3 days the law adds. Mail-and-attach works only if your written lease allows it for notices from the tenant to you too; mail-and-email only with the statutory email addendum signed after move-in (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.155(1)(c)–(d), (5)). Neither adds days.

The same violation again within 6 months of this notice: a 10-day notice with no right to cure (§ 90.392(5)). Week to week: 7 days, 4 to cure (§ 90.392(6)). NOHM’s notice is the first one; ask a lawyer for the others.
Serious acts (threats or injury, reckless endangerment, intentional damage, an act “outrageous in the extreme”) allow a 24-hour notice (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.396). Ask a lawyer.
This is a “tenant cause” notice, so you may use it after the first year of a tenancy (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.427(3)(c)(A)).
If the tenancy ends and the tenant stays, file the eviction: no separate demand for possession is needed (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.427(11)).

forms.label: Notice ending a month-to-month (30 or 90 days)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month: 30 days in the first year, no reason needed; after it, 90 days for a qualifying landlord reason.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out and the law allows it.
notes: First year of occupancy (any tenant has lived there a year or less): 30 days, no reason needed (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.427(3)(b)). NOHM uses 30 days in the first year of the lease and 90 after it.

After the first year you may end a month-to-month tenancy only for tenant cause (use the nonpayment or violation notice) or for a qualifying landlord reason, with 90 days’ notice that states the reason and its supporting facts: you will demolish it or convert it to non-residential use; you will repair or renovate and it is, or will be, unsafe or unfit to live in; you or an immediate family member will live there and you own no comparable unit in the building that is free; or you accepted an offer from a buyer who will live there, with written evidence of the offer attached (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.427(5)–(6)). Write the reason and facts in the notice’s Reason box.
With that 90-day notice, pay the tenant one month’s rent when you deliver it, unless you own 4 or fewer units (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.427(6)).
Breaking these rules costs three months’ rent plus actual damages, and is a defense to the eviction (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.427(9)).

Shorter periods that NOHM doesn’t use: 60 days for an accepted owner-occupant purchase offer plus an extra month’s rent (§ 90.427(5)(b)); 60 days without cause in an owner-occupied building of 2 units or fewer (§ 90.427(8)). A week-to-week tenancy needs 10 days (§ 90.427(2)).

A fixed-term lease can’t be ended early without cause. One that ends in the first year: 30 days before its end date. One that ends after the first year becomes month to month unless one of the § 90.427(4) exceptions applies.
The tenancy ends on the date given, whatever the rental period (§ 90.427(10)). If you end a tenancy in its first year, the next tenant’s rent is capped (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.323(4)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it first class (not certified: Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.100(18)) and NOHM adds the 3 days the law adds. Mail-and-attach works only if your written lease allows it for notices from the tenant to you too; mail-and-email only with the statutory email addendum signed after move-in (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.155(1)(c)–(d), (5)). Neither adds days.
Portland and some other cities add relocation payments and longer notice; NOHM hasn’t confirmed them. Check your city.
If the tenant stays after the date, file the eviction: Oregon needs no separate demand for possession (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.427(11)).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (OJD Residential Eviction Complaint and Summons)
forms.explain: What to copy onto the Oregon Judicial Department’s eviction forms, where to get them, and each step and deadline after you file.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Oregon’s courts use statewide eviction forms. Clerks expect them, so NOHM doesn’t write the complaint: copy these values onto the OJD forms (or use the court’s iForms at courts.oregon.gov/iforms).
Attach a copy of the notice you relied on to the complaint (Or. Rev. Stat. § 105.124(3)).
An agent or employee can appear for you, without a lawyer (§ 105.130(4)).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Oregon doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: walk through with the tenant, both sign it, and keep a copy for the deposit accounting.
In writing at or before move-in: who manages the premises, and an owner or the owner’s agent for service of process and notices (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.305(1)). Keep it current.
Before the lease is signed, for a building of 4 or fewer units: any notice of default or trustee’s sale, pending foreclosure, forfeiture or tax-lien foreclosure (§ 90.310).
In the rental agreement: that the unit is in a 100-year flood plain, if it is (§ 90.228); the smoking policy (§ 90.220(4)); the deposit and any fees (§§ 90.300(3), 90.302).
At move-in: carbon monoxide alarm testing instructions (§§ 90.316, 90.317), a receipt for the deposit (§ 90.300(2)), and a copy of the signed rental agreement (§ 90.220(3)).
Built before 1978: give the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ actual notice and enter only at reasonable times, unless you and the tenant agree otherwise for a specific entry (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.322(1)(f)). If the tenant says no after getting it, you may not enter.
In an emergency you may enter without notice; if the tenant wasn’t there, give actual notice within 24 hours after, with the date and time, the emergency and who entered (§ 90.322(1)(b)).
A tenant’s written repair request lets you enter for that repair for 7 days (§ 90.322(1)(c)).
An unlawful entry can cost at least one month’s rent (§ 90.322(8)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 90 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Oregon caps rent increases: for 2027 the maximum is 10% (it was 9.5% for 2026). The Department of Administrative Services publishes each year’s by September 30 (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.324(1)(b)).
No increase in the first year of a tenancy, none more than once in 12 months, and at least 90 days’ written notice (§ 90.323(2)). Week to week: 7 days (§ 90.323(1)).
The notice states the amount of the increase, the new rent and the date it takes effect (§ 90.323(3)). NOHM’s paper does.

A building whose first certificate of occupancy is under 15 years old, and some regulated affordable housing, are exempt from the cap; the notice must then state the facts of the exemption (§ 90.323(5)). NOHM’s form doesn’t; ask a lawyer.
Breaking these rules costs three months’ rent plus actual damages (§ 90.323(6)). A fixed-term lease’s rent can’t be changed unless it allows it.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 31 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Give the written accounting, and the balance, within 31 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant gives back possession (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.300(12)–(13)).
Deliver it in person or by first-class mail; by email only under a signed email-notice addendum (§ 90.300(14)).

Deduct only what is reasonably necessary for the tenant’s defaults (including unpaid rent) and for damage they caused beyond ordinary wear and tear; labor at a reasonable hourly rate. Carpet cleaning only if it was machine-cleaned, cleaned before move-in, and your written lease allows the deduction (§ 90.300(7)).
A last month’s rent deposit is a security deposit; apply it to the last month after any termination notice other than a nonpayment one (§ 90.300(9)).
Withholding without a written accounting, or in bad faith, costs twice the amount withheld (§ 90.300(16)).
Oregon doesn’t cap deposits or require interest.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Use it once the tenancy has ended and you reasonably believe the tenant left the property with no intent to claim it, after the tenant was absent 7 days following an unexecuted termination order, or after the sheriff restored possession to you (Or. Rev. Stat. § 90.425(2)).
Hand it to the tenant, or mail it first class to the premises, any post-office box you know of, and any forwarding address (§ 90.425(3)).
The date to contact you must be at least 5 days after personal delivery or 8 days after mailing (§ 90.425(6)); NOHM requires 8.
Store the property safely, with reasonable care. After the tenant contacts you, make it available for 15 days by appointment (§ 90.425(7)–(8)).

Unclaimed, you may sell it, or dispose of it if it is worth $1,000 or less or less than the cost of storage and sale. From a sale’s proceeds deduct your costs and unpaid rent and remit the rest with an itemized accounting (§ 90.425(10), (13)).
Not for a manufactured dwelling, floating home or recreational vehicle: those have longer periods and lienholder notices.
Breaking these rules can cost twice actual damages (§ 90.425(15), (17)).

forms.label: 10-day notice to quit (rent unpaid)
forms.explain: Demands the rent due and tells the tenant to move out within 10 days of service.
forms.when: Rent is due and unpaid (Pennsylvania has no grace period).
notes: This is a notice to quit, not to pay: the law gives no right to stay by paying within the 10 days. But in a case only for unpaid rent, the tenant can stop the eviction any time before the order for possession is carried out by paying the rent in arrears and the costs (68 P.S. § 250.503(c); Pa.R.Civ.P.M.D.J. 518).
Ten days from service, not counting the day of service. If the tenth day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, it runs to the next day that isn’t (1 Pa.C.S. § 1908).
Serve it personally, leave it at the principal building on the premises, or post it conspicuously on the leased premises (68 P.S. § 250.501(f)). Pennsylvania’s statute has no mail method.
Check your lease: it may shorten this notice or waive it, which the law allows (68 P.S. § 250.501(e)). The court’s complaint asks whether notice was given or wasn’t required by the lease.
NOHM demands rent only. Whether lease fees called “additional rent” can be demanded isn’t settled; claim them in the complaint instead.
You can’t evict for rent being paid into escrow under the City Rent Withholding Act (Pa.R.Civ.P.M.D.J. 582).
Philadelphia evictions go to Municipal Court and have their own good-cause and diversion rules; NOHM hasn’t confirmed them.
This notice to quit is the only notice before filing: Pennsylvania needs no separate demand for possession, so NOHM has none.

forms.label: Notice to quit for a lease breach (15 or 30 days)
forms.explain: Ends the lease for breach of its conditions: 15 days to move out, or 30 for a lease of more than a year.
forms.when: The tenant broke a condition of the lease.
notes: The statute gives no right to cure; whether the tenant can is up to your lease. Describe the breach exactly.

Drug-related grounds under 68 P.S. § 250.505-A (a conviction for selling, making or distributing drugs on the premises, a second drug violation there, or a police seizure of illegal drugs there) need only 10 days (§ 250.501(d)). Ask a lawyer.
You can’t end or refuse to renew a lease because a tenant joined a tenants’ association (68 P.S. § 250.205).
Serve it personally, leave it at the principal building on the premises, or post it conspicuously on the leased premises (68 P.S. § 250.501(f)). Pennsylvania’s statute has no mail method.
Check your lease: it may shorten this notice or waive it, which the law allows (68 P.S. § 250.501(e)). The court’s complaint asks whether notice was given or wasn’t required by the lease.
Philadelphia evictions go to Municipal Court and have their own good-cause and diversion rules; NOHM hasn’t confirmed them.
This notice to quit is the only notice before filing: Pennsylvania needs no separate demand for possession, so NOHM has none.

forms.label: Notice to quit at the end of the term (15 or 30 days)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month, or a lease at its end: 15 days, or 30 for a lease of more than a year.
forms.when: You want the tenant out at the end of the term; no reason is needed.
notes: Month to month, or a lease of a year or less: 15 days. A lease of more than a year: 30 days (68 P.S. § 250.501(b)).
The statute doesn’t require the date to end a rental period. Ending it the day before rent is due is the cleanest choice.
Pennsylvania has no statewide just-cause rule, but you can’t end or refuse to renew a lease because a tenant joined a tenants’ association (68 P.S. § 250.205).
The notice-to-quit process doesn’t apply to someone who never was a tenant (68 P.S. § 250.501(g)).
Serve it personally, leave it at the principal building on the premises, or post it conspicuously on the leased premises (68 P.S. § 250.501(f)). Pennsylvania’s statute has no mail method.
Check your lease: it may shorten this notice or waive it, which the law allows (68 P.S. § 250.501(e)). The court’s complaint asks whether notice was given or wasn’t required by the lease.
Philadelphia evictions go to Municipal Court and have their own good-cause and diversion rules; NOHM hasn’t confirmed them.
This notice to quit is the only notice before filing: Pennsylvania needs no separate demand for possession, so NOHM has none.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (AOPC 310A, SCRA affidavit, AOPC 311A)
forms.explain: What to copy onto Pennsylvania’s Landlord/Tenant Complaint and its companion forms, where to get them, and each step and deadline after you file.
forms.when: The notice to quit ran out (or your lease waives it) and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: The complaint must be on the state’s form (Pa.R.Civ.P.M.D.J. 503A), and courts refuse altered ones, so NOHM doesn’t write it: copy these values onto AOPC 310A.
For each tenant who is a person, attach the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act affidavit (Rule 503D).
An LLC or corporation may appear through an officer, or an employee or agent with personal knowledge and an officer’s written authorization filed for this case (Rule 207).
Philadelphia evictions go to Municipal Court, with their own rules; this worksheet is for the magisterial district courts.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Pennsylvania doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: walk through with the tenant, both sign it, and keep a copy for the list of damages at move-out.
When you put a deposit over $100 in escrow, tell the tenant in writing the bank’s name and address and the amount: use NOHM’s Notice of deposit escrow account (68 P.S. § 250.511b(a)).

From about December 21, 2026 (Act 64 of 2026), your lease must say whether parking is provided and, if so, whether there is a fee and how much; you can’t add or change a parking fee during the lease unless parking availability or a third party’s pass-through fee changes.
From the same date (Act 67 of 2026), any application fee must be reasonably related to your actual administrative costs.
Built before 1978: give the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet. Philadelphia and other cities add their own disclosures; NOHM hasn’t confirmed them.

forms.label: Notice of deposit escrow account
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the name and address of the bank holding their deposit, and the amount.
forms.when: When you deposit a security deposit over $100 in escrow.
notes: Deposits over $100 go in an escrow account at a bank regulated by the Federal Reserve, the Comptroller of the Currency or the Pennsylvania Department of Banking, and you must then tell each tenant in writing the bank’s name and address and the amount (68 P.S. § 250.511b(a)).

From the second anniversary of the deposit it must earn interest; you may keep 1% a year as an administrative fee and pay the rest of the interest to the tenant each year on the lease’s anniversary (§ 250.511b(b)–(c)). A bond can take the escrow’s place (§ 250.511c).
Cap: two months’ rent in the first year of the lease, one month’s from the second year on, and after five years a rent increase can’t raise the deposit (§ 250.511a).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No Pennsylvania statute sets notice for entry; your lease governs. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours, except in an emergency.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Pennsylvania statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days, which covers the 15 or 30 days a notice to quit would need (68 P.S. § 250.501(b)), and starts the new rent on a due date.
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Pennsylvania has no statewide rent cap. After a lease’s fifth year, a rent increase can’t raise the deposit (68 P.S. § 250.511a(d)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Give the written list of damages, with the balance (including any unpaid interest), within 30 days after the lease ends or you accept the tenant’s surrender, whichever is first (68 P.S. § 250.512(a)).

No list within 30 days: you lose the right to withhold any of the deposit and to sue for damage to the premises. Not paying the difference: liability for double the amount wrongly kept (§ 250.512(b)–(c)). You bear the burden of proof.
If the tenant didn’t give you a new address in writing, you aren’t liable under this section (§ 250.512(e)); send it to the last known address anyway.
Interest: if you held the deposit more than two years, add the interest owed, less your 1% a year (§ 250.511b).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Property is abandoned only if: the tenant left after a written lease ended; an eviction order or order for possession was entered and the tenant left and removed substantially everything; such an order was executed; the tenant gave a forwarding address in writing and left with substantially everything; or the tenant left without saying they’d return, rent is more than 15 days late, and you posted notice of their rights (68 P.S. § 250.505a(b)).

Before you remove or dispose of anything, mail this notice first class to the premises and every forwarding address, emergency ones included (§ 250.505a(d)–(e)). The tenant has 10 days from the postmark to retrieve it or ask you to store it, for up to 30 days from the notice, at their cost.

Never on premises someone still lives in without permission, and hold 30 days if you know of a protection-from-abuse order (§ 250.505a(f), (h)). A deceased tenant’s property goes by the decedents’ estates law instead (§ 250.505a(c)).
Breaking these rules: treble damages, attorney’s fees and costs (§ 250.505a(i)).

forms.label: Five-day demand notice for nonpayment of rent
forms.explain: The statute’s own demand, mailed: pay all rent in arrears within 5 days of mailing, or an eviction may be filed.
forms.when: Rent is 15 days in arrears.
notes: Send it only once rent is 15 days in arrears (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-35(a)): rent due on the 1st, mail it on the 16th or later.
Mail it first class and fill in the certificate of mailing; the five days run from the date of mailing. File no earlier than the 6th day after mailing (§ 34-18-35(b)).
Rhode Island’s statute counts from the date of mailing and doesn’t say whether a weekend or holiday extends the period; NOHM moves a last day that falls on one to the next business day.

The tenant can cure by paying all the rent in arrears before you file. If they had no demand notice in the 6 months before you file, they can also cure at the hearing by paying the arrears and court costs (§ 34-18-35(e)).
To file a nonpayment eviction you must be registered in the statewide rental registry, and show the court proof when you file (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-58(g)).
This is the statute’s own form (§ 34-18-56(a)); the Judiciary’s DC-55 has the same words.
If the rent isn’t paid, file the complaint: Rhode Island needs no separate demand for possession, so NOHM has none.

forms.label: Notice of noncompliance (20 days to remedy)
forms.explain: The statute’s own notice, mailed: remedy the breach within 20 days, or the rental agreement ends at least 21 days after mailing.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease or a tenant’s duty under § 34-18-24.
notes: Describe the breach in the notice’s details: they fill the line after “because you:”. Then, by hand on the printed notice, write what the tenant must do to remedy it (the acts, repairs or payment of damages) and the termination date NOHM shows, at least 21 days after mailing (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-36(a)).
Mail it first class and fill in the certificate of mailing; the twenty days run from the date of mailing.
Rhode Island’s statute counts from the date of mailing and doesn’t say whether a weekend or holiday extends the period; NOHM moves a last day that falls on one to the next business day.
If the tenant remedies it before the date, the agreement goes on. If not, file no earlier than the day after the termination date (§ 34-18-36(b)).
The same breach again within 6 months of a good-faith notice: you may end the agreement on at least 20 days’ written notice, with no time to remedy (§ 34-18-36(e)).
No notice is needed for drug or violent-crime breaches of § 34-18-24(8)–(10), or for some seasonal tenants: you may file at once (§ 34-18-36(f)). Ask a lawyer.
This is the statute’s own form (§ 34-18-56(b)); the Judiciary’s DC-62 has the same words.

forms.label: 30-day notice of termination of tenancy
forms.explain: The statute’s own notice ending a month-to-month tenancy at least 30 days out, the day after a rental period ends.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out; no reason is needed.
notes: Deliver it at least 30 days before the date in it (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-37(b)). The statute’s form names “the first day after the end of your current rental period”: set the date to a rent due date at least 30 days out (rent due on the 1st, the 1st of a month).
A week-to-week tenancy needs 10 days; a year-to-year tenancy, 3 months before the end of the occupation year (§ 34-18-37(a), (c)).
Mail it first class and fill in the certificate of mailing, or hand it to the tenant (§ 34-18-14(b)).

If the tenant stays, you may file the day after the tenancy ends: no separate demand for possession is needed, so NOHM has none (§ 34-18-38(a)). A willful holdover can owe up to three months’ rent or three times actual damages, whichever is greater, plus attorney’s fees (§ 34-18-38(c)).
When a tenant dies, an adult resident or live-in caregiver may continue the agreement for up to 3 months or the rest of the term (§ 34-18-38(d)).
This is the statute’s own form (§ 34-18-56(c)); the Judiciary’s DC-63 has the same words.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (DC-54, DC-38)
forms.explain: What to copy onto the Judiciary’s eviction complaint, where to get it, and each step and deadline after you file.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Rhode Island’s statute sets the eviction complaints’ form (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-56(d)–(e)) and the Judiciary’s DC-54 and DC-38 follow it, so NOHM doesn’t write the complaint: copy these values onto the Judiciary’s form.
For a nonpayment case, bring proof you are registered in the statewide rental registry (and lead-compliant where required): without it the case can’t proceed (§ 34-18-58(g)).
Attach the notice you mailed, with its certificate of mailing.
NOHM hasn’t confirmed whether an LLC or corporation may file without a lawyer in District Court; ask the clerk.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Rhode Island doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: walk through with the tenant, both sign it, and keep a copy for the deposit.

In writing at or before move-in: the name, address and number of the person managing the premises, and of an owner or the owner’s agent for service of process and notices (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-20(a)). Keep it current.

In the lease: every fee beyond rent, next to the rent, with a statement that additional fees may apply; which utilities the rent includes and which the tenant pays; any renter’s-insurance requirement (§ 34-18-15(a), since January 1, 2025).
Before signing: any outstanding minimum housing code violations (§ 34-18-22.1).

Register the unit in the statewide rental registry within 30 days of renting it, and re-register by October 1 each year; pre-1978 units need a lead certificate of conformance or exemption (§ 34-18-58).
No application fee beyond the actual cost of a background or credit check (§ 34-18-59). A nonresident landlord designates an agent (§ 34-18-22.3).
A 2026 law adds a shoreline-access disclosure for shoreline property (S 2734); NOHM hasn’t confirmed its enactment. Built before 1978: the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: Give at least 2 days’ notice and enter only at reasonable times, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-26(c)).
Without consent you may enter in an emergency, or during an absence of more than 7 days if reasonably necessary to protect the property (§ 34-18-26(b)). Don’t use entry to harass the tenant.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 60 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Give written notice at least 60 days before a rent increase takes effect (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-16.1(a)).
A month-to-month tenant over 62 needs at least 120 days: set the date that far out (§ 34-18-16.1(b)).

Rhode Island has no rent cap. An increase within 6 months of a tenant’s complaint can be presumed retaliatory (§ 34-18-46). A fee change in an unwritten tenancy needs 30 days’ written notice (§ 34-18-15(a)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 20 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Deliver this itemized notice and the balance within 20 days after the latest of: the tenancy ending, the tenant giving back possession, or the tenant giving you a forwarding address for the deposit (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-19(b)). First-class mail counts as delivery (§ 34-18-14(b)).
Deduct only unpaid rent, reasonable cleaning and trash removal, and physical damage beyond ordinary wear and tear.
Failing to comply: the amount due, plus twice the amount wrongly withheld, plus attorney’s fees (§ 34-18-19(c)). The lease can’t waive it.
The deposit can’t exceed one month’s rent (a separate furniture deposit of up to a month’s rent is allowed for furniture worth $5,000 or more). No interest or separate account is required.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Rhode Island’s landlord-tenant act sets no procedure for property a tenant leaves behind. NOHM fills in 14 days to hold it, its own choice, not the law’s; giving notice heads off disputes.
After an eviction, the sheriff or constable removes the property and the tenant pays moving and storage before it is released (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-50).
If the tenant may have abandoned the unit, send NOHM’s 7-day notice of abandonment first (§ 34-18-40).
Photograph the property before you move or dispose of it. Never remove a tenant’s things while they still have possession (§ 34-18-44).

forms.label: Notice of abandonment (7 days to reply)
forms.explain: The certified letter the law requires when a tenant seems to have abandoned the unit: reply within 7 days, or you will re-rent it.
forms.when: The tenant left without notice, rent is more than 15 days unpaid, and their things are gone.
notes: A unit is abandoned when the tenant has vacated without notice and doesn’t intend to return, as shown by rent unpaid for more than 15 days and substantially all their possessions removed (R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-11(1)).

Send it by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the tenant’s last known address (§ 34-18-40). If it comes back undeliverable, or the tenant doesn’t contact you within 7 days, make reasonable efforts to re-rent the unit at a fair rental.
NOHM fills in a reply date 10 days out, to allow for the certified mail; the statute’s period is 7 days.

forms.label: 5-day notice of nonpayment of rent
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid and that the rental agreement ends if it isn’t paid in 5 days.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid when due (once per lease term; not needed if your lease has the statute’s clause).
notes: You may end the agreement once rent is unpaid 5 days after it was due (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-710(B)). NOHM gives the tenant 5 days after this notice, the safer reading of the statute.

You need give this notice only once per lease term, and not at all if your written lease has the statute’s “IF YOU DO NOT PAY YOUR RENT ON TIME” clause in conspicuous language; that clause covers a month-to-month tenancy after the term too (§ 27-40-710(B)). NOHM’s move-in forms include it.
Five days, not counting weekends and holidays; a last day on one moves on (SCRCP 6(a)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it registered or certified to the address they gave for notices (or their last known residence); proof of mailing is notice (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-240(B)(3)). Court rules add 5 days for some papers served by mail (SCRCP 6(e)); it isn’t settled that this applies here, so NOHM adds them.
The same 5-day notice applies when a tenant conducts or permits illegal activity in the unit or uses it other than as a home (§§ 27-40-540, 27-40-710(B)).
Attorney’s fees for a nonpayment not in good faith are available only if a lawyer represents you (§ 27-40-710(C)).

South Carolina needs no separate demand for possession: after the tenancy ends you may apply for ejectment (S.C. Code Ann. §§ 27-37-10(A), 27-40-770(c)). So NOHM has no separate demand form for South Carolina.

forms.label: 14-day notice to remedy a breach
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong: remedy it in 14 days, or the rental agreement ends.
forms.when: The tenant broke the lease, or a duty affecting health and safety (not rent).
notes: Describe exactly what the tenant did or failed to do: the statute requires the notice to specify it (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-710(A)).
A breach of the tenant’s health-and-safety duties (§ 27-40-510) you can fix by repair, replacement or cleaning: after 14 days’ written notice you may do the work and bill the tenant (§ 27-40-720).
Illegal activity, or using the unit other than as a home, uses the 5-day notice instead (§§ 27-40-540, 27-40-710(B)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it registered or certified to the address they gave for notices (or their last known residence); proof of mailing is notice (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-240(B)(3)). Court rules add 5 days for some papers served by mail (SCRCP 6(e)); it isn’t settled that this applies here, so NOHM adds them.
South Carolina has no shorter notice for a repeated breach.
Attorney’s fees for a wilful breach are available only if a lawyer represents you (§ 27-40-710(C)).

South Carolina needs no separate demand for possession: after the tenancy ends you may apply for ejectment (S.C. Code Ann. §§ 27-37-10(A), 27-40-770(c)). So NOHM has no separate demand form for South Carolina.

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy on a date at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out; no reason is needed.
notes: Any day at least 30 days out works: South Carolina doesn’t require it to end a rental period, and rent is apportioned day to day unless the lease says otherwise (S.C. Code Ann. §§ 27-40-770(b), 27-40-310(c)).
A week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days’ written notice instead (§ 27-40-770(a)).

Hand it to the tenant, or mail it registered or certified to the address they gave for notices (or their last known residence); proof of mailing is notice (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-240(B)(3)). Court rules add 5 days for some papers served by mail (SCRCP 6(e)); it isn’t settled that this applies here, so NOHM adds them.
No just-cause rule, but a notice found to be retaliation bars recovering possession for 75 days (§ 27-40-910). A victim of documented domestic abuse may end the lease early (§ 27-40-350).
A holdover not in good faith can owe your attorney’s fees; a wilful one up to three months’ rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater (§ 27-40-770(c)).

South Carolina needs no separate demand for possession: after the tenancy ends you may apply for ejectment (S.C. Code Ann. §§ 27-37-10(A), 27-40-770(c)). So NOHM has no separate demand form for South Carolina.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (SCCA 732, 733A, 734)
forms.explain: What to copy onto the magistrate’s Application for Ejectment, where to get it and the forms that follow, and each step and deadline.
forms.when: The notice ran out, or the rent is 5 days late and your lease has the statute’s clause, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: South Carolina’s magistrates use the Judicial Branch’s statewide forms, so NOHM doesn’t write the application: copy these values onto SCCA 732 and swear to it before a notary.

A business can be represented by a non-lawyer officer, agent or employee with written authorization from its president, owner or chief executive (Magistrate Court Rule 21). A licensed broker-in-charge or property manager may complete the form for you (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-710(C)).
Attach the lease or other written proof that the tenant rents from you.

forms.label: Lease addendum: notice for late rent
forms.explain: The statute’s “IF YOU DO NOT PAY YOUR RENT ON TIME” clause, signed with the lease, so no separate 5-day notice is needed.
forms.when: At signing, or added to a running lease.
notes: With this clause in the written lease, in conspicuous language, you needn’t send a separate 5-day notice before applying for ejectment for nonpayment, during the term or a month-to-month after it (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-710(B)).
It also makes nonpayment within 5 days of the due date legal notice that you may begin ejectment (§ 27-37-10(B)). The paper prints it in bold, boxed.
Have every tenant sign it, and keep it with the lease.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: South Carolina doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: walk through with the tenant, both sign it, and keep a copy for the deposit.
In writing at or before move-in: the name and address of an owner, or of the owner’s agent for service of process and notices (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-420(a)). Keep it current.
Put the “IF YOU DO NOT PAY YOUR RENT ON TIME” clause in your lease (NOHM’s lease addendum) to skip the 5-day notice (§ 27-40-710(B)).
More than 4 adjoining units with different deposit standards for different tenants: post the standards or give each prospective tenant a statement of them (§ 27-40-410(c)).
To enter for regularly scheduled services without notice, put that right conspicuously in the lease (§ 27-40-530(b)(2)).
Built before 1978: give the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ notice and enter only at reasonable times (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-530(c)).

Without notice you may enter in an emergency (a coming storm can count); between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. for regularly scheduled services your lease conspicuously provides for, announcing yourself first; or between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. for services the tenant asked for, announcing yourself first (§ 27-40-530(b)).
Don’t use entry to harass the tenant.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No South Carolina statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days, the notice that ends a month-to-month tenancy (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-770(b)), and starts the new rent on a due date.
During a fixed-term lease you can change the rent only if the lease allows it.
South Carolina has no rent cap, and counties and cities can’t regulate rents (§ 27-39-60). An increase in retaliation, above fair market rent, is barred (§ 27-40-910(a)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Itemize deductions in writing and send the amount due within 30 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant gives back possession, or after the tenant demands it, whichever is later (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-410(a)).
If the tenant gave no forwarding address in writing and you didn’t know where they were, mailing it to their last known address protects you from damages.
Wrongful withholding: three times the amount wrongly kept, plus attorney’s fees (§ 27-40-410(b)).
South Carolina doesn’t cap deposits or require interest or a separate account.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Only for property worth $500 or less in all, after the unit was abandoned or the lease ended and the tenant took most of their things or shut off their utilities (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-730(d)). Abandoned means 15 days’ unexplained absence after rent went unpaid, or at once if they ended their utilities (§ 27-40-730(a)–(b)).
South Carolina requires no notice for it. NOHM fills in 7 days to hold the property, its own choice, to head off disputes.
Worth more than $500: you may remove it only through ejectment (§ 27-40-730(e); SCCA 737, Affidavit of Abandonment).
After an ejectment, property put on the street is removed after 48 hours, not counting weekends and holidays (§ 27-40-710(D)).

forms.label: Demand for payment of rent (no notice required)
forms.explain: An optional written demand for the rent. South Dakota requires no notice before you file.
forms.when: Rent is past due; you can file once it is unpaid 3 days after the due date.
notes: South Dakota repealed its 3-day notice to quit in 2024 (SL 2024, ch 75): no notice is required before you file. You can file once the rent is unpaid for 3 days after it was due (S.D. Codified Laws § 21-16-1(4)).

Counting the 3 days: the due date doesn’t count (S.D. Codified Laws § 2-14-14). NOHM also skips Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, as the court rule for periods under 11 days does (§ 15-6-6(a)), and waits until the third day has passed: the safe reading.
This demand is optional: a courtesy, or the notice your lease promises. Letting the tenant pay by a date is your choice, not a right the statute gives; give the time your lease sets, if it sets one.
South Dakota’s law sets no way to serve it. Put it in writing, hand it to the tenant or mail it, and keep proof; NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed.

forms.label: Notice of lease violation and termination
forms.explain: Ends the lease for a use or act it forbids. The lease sets any notice period or chance to fix it.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term (other than rent).
notes: South Dakota sets no notice period and no chance to fix a lease violation: your lease decides. Give the notice and any chance to cure your lease promises; NOHM leaves the date to you.
For repairs the tenant is bound to make, you must first ask for them and allow a reasonable time before you end the lease (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-18(2)).

You can’t evict a tenant because they called the police or emergency help about domestic abuse, unlawful sexual behavior or stalking, or because they or someone in their household was the victim (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-18.1).

A notice not based on a breach of the lease, given within 180 days after a tenant’s good-faith code complaint, written repair notice or tenant-union activity, can be retaliation (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-27).
A false disability or service-animal claim lets you evict and claim a damage fee of up to $1,000 (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-36).
South Dakota’s law sets no way to serve it. Put it in writing, hand it to the tenant or mail it, and keep proof; NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed.

forms.label: 1-month notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at the end of a rental month, on at least a month’s notice.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: The notice must be at least as long as the rental period, up to one month, and end at the end of a period (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-15). A week-to-week tenancy needs one week’s notice, ending at the end of a week.
If the tenant stays after the date and you accept rent, the tenancy renews on the same terms (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-14). Don’t take rent for any time after the date.

A fixed-term lease ends on its own date. Once the tenant holds over you may file; no notice or demand is required (S.D. Codified Laws § 21-16-1(4)). A written notice to quit and demand for possession lets you claim double damages for willful holding over (§ 21-3-8): NOHM’s demand for possession is that paper.
A mobile home lot that is being put to another use needs 90 days’ notice to vacate (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-31).
South Dakota’s law sets no way to serve it. Put it in writing, hand it to the tenant or mail it, and keep proof; NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed.

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: Not required before you file: since 2024 you may sue once a tenant holds over after the lease ends (S.D. Codified Laws § 21-16-1(4)). Give it anyway if you want double damages: they need notice to quit and a demand of possession (§ 21-3-8), and the complaint must claim them (§ 21-16-10).
South Dakota sets no period for it. NOHM fills in 3 days; give more if you like.
Don’t accept rent for time after the lease ended: accepting it renews the tenancy on the same terms, for up to a year (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-14).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (UJS-232, UJS-111, UJS-112)
forms.explain: Everything the Unified Judicial System’s eviction forms ask for, filled in from the lease, with where to get each form and the steps after filing.
forms.when: Rent is 3 days late, the lease ended, or the tenant broke it, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: South Dakota’s courts use the Unified Judicial System’s eviction forms. File those, filled in from this worksheet: a clerk can turn away a homemade complaint.
Get them one by one, or all in the landlord’s “Print All” packet, from the UJS self-help page.
A corporation or LLC must file through an attorney (the UJS forms’ instructions; S.D. Codified Laws § 15-39-47).
Bring the lease, any notice you gave and how, and the rent ledger to the hearing.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: South Dakota doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: the deposit can only be kept to restore the home to its condition at the start of the tenancy, ordinary wear and tear excepted (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-24), and this form records that condition.

Written disclosures: if you know the home was ever used to manufacture methamphetamine, you must tell the tenant before they rent it (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-30). A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.
A lease for more than one year must be in writing and signed (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-5).
A security deposit can’t be more than one month’s rent, unless special conditions pose a danger to the premises and you both agree to more (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-6.1).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give it in writing at least 24 hours ahead, unless your lease sets another way or time (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-32).

The law requires the notice to give the date, a time window during normal business hours, the purpose, and a way for the tenant to ask to reschedule. Pick a window between about 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.; the notice tells the tenant to contact you to reschedule.
In an emergency, or where notice is impracticable, you may enter without it.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: A month-to-month’s rent or terms change on written notice given at least 30 days before the end of the month, taking effect when the month ends (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-13). Start the new rent on a rent due date.
The tenant may end the tenancy on the first of the next month by telling you within 15 days of getting the notice.
During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it.
South Dakota has no rent cap. A rent increase above fair market value after a tenant’s complaint or repair request can be retaliation (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-27).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 21 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant gives you a mailing address or delivery instructions.
notes: Return the deposit, or send this statement of the specific reasons for keeping any of it, within 21 days after the tenancy ends and you receive the tenant’s mailing address or delivery instructions (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-24, as amended effective July 1, 2026; it was two weeks).
Keep only what is reasonably needed for unpaid rent and other money due under an agreement, and to restore the home to its condition at move-in, ordinary wear and tear excepted.
If the tenant asks, give an itemized accounting of what you withheld within 45 days after the tenancy ends.
Missing these steps forfeits your right to keep any of the deposit; bad faith can add punitive damages of up to $200.
No interest or separate account is required. The deposit cap is one month’s rent (§ 43-32-6.1).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: South Dakota doesn’t require this notice. Giving one heads off disputes.

Property worth $500 or less in all may be disposed of 10 days after the tenant has quit the home (S.D. Codified Laws § 43-32-25). Worth more: store it at least 30 days; you have a lien for handling and storage (§ 43-32-26). NOHM fills in 30 days, which works for both.
Use it only after the tenant has quit the home, never while they still have possession. Photograph the property before you move it.

forms.label: 14-day notice to pay rent, or the lease ends
forms.explain: Demands the rent due: if it isn’t paid within 14 days after the tenant gets the notice, the rental agreement ends.
forms.when: Rent is past due (a late fee only after the 5-day grace period).
notes: Tennessee has two sets of rules. The Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (URLTA) applies in Anderson, Blount, Bradley, Davidson, Hamilton, Knox, Madison, Maury, Montgomery, Rutherford, Sevier, Shelby, Sullivan, Sumner, Washington, Williamson and Wilson counties (those over 75,000 people at the 2010 census, Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-102(a); the list follows from the census, not from the statute's text, so ask the county clerk if unsure). Every other county follows § 66-7-109.

Both sets give 14 days to pay: in URLTA counties from when the tenant receives the notice (§ 66-28-505(a)(2)); elsewhere, notice of 14 days for rent in arrears upon demand (§ 66-7-109(a)(1)(A)). This notice meets both.
If the same breach happens again within 6 months, the next notice can be shorter: 7 days in URLTA counties (§ 66-28-505(a)(2)(B)); elsewhere 14 days, with no chance to cure (§ 66-7-109(a)(2)).

In URLTA counties a lease can waive this notice, if the waiver is in 12-point bold type or larger; the 5-day grace period still applies (§ 66-28-505(b)). Outside them, this notice doesn’t apply to a rental period under 14 days (§ 66-7-109(c)).
Accepting rent without reservation, knowing of the default, can waive the termination (§ 66-28-508).

Written notice goes to the tenant’s last known address or the one in the lease (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-106(b)); in URLTA counties, to the email the tenant gave in the lease, if they gave one (§ 66-28-108). The period runs from receipt: NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed. A last day on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next day (§ 1-3-102).

forms.label: 30-day notice to remedy a breach, or the lease ends
forms.explain: Says what the tenant did wrong: remedy it within 30 days, or the rental agreement ends. Good in every county.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term (other than rent).
notes: Tennessee has two sets of rules. The Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (URLTA) applies in Anderson, Blount, Bradley, Davidson, Hamilton, Knox, Madison, Maury, Montgomery, Rutherford, Sevier, Shelby, Sullivan, Sumner, Washington, Williamson and Wilson counties (those over 75,000 people at the 2010 census, Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-102(a); the list follows from the census, not from the statute's text, so ask the county clerk if unsure). Every other county follows § 66-7-109.

NOHM gives 30 days, with a chance to remedy, so the notice is good in every county. URLTA counties allow 14 days after receipt, to remedy or, for a breach that can’t be remedied, to end the agreement (§ 66-28-505(a)(2)–(3)); other counties allow 14 days to remedy damage beyond normal wear and tear, and require 30 days for every other default (§ 66-7-109(a)(1)(B), (b)).

Shorter notices exist for serious cases; ask a lawyer before using them: 7 days for the same breach again within 6 months (URLTA, § 66-28-505(a)(2)(B)); 3 days for a violent act, a real and present danger, a hazardous condition, or an unauthorized occupant who won’t leave (URLTA, § 66-28-517, from the day the tenant receives it); 3 days outside URLTA counties for a violent act, drug-related criminal activity or a real danger by a tenant who is not disabled (§ 66-7-109(d)), or an unauthorized occupant (§ 66-7-109(f)).
Describe exactly what the tenant did or didn’t do: the law requires the notice to specify it.
If the tenant must make repairs to remedy it, the notice must say they need your written authorization first; this one does.

Written notice goes to the tenant’s last known address or the one in the lease (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-106(b)); in URLTA counties, to the email the tenant gave in the lease, if they gave one (§ 66-28-108). The period runs from receipt: NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed. A last day on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next day (§ 1-3-102).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at the end of a rental period, at least 30 days out.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: Tennessee has two sets of rules. The Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (URLTA) applies in Anderson, Blount, Bradley, Davidson, Hamilton, Knox, Madison, Maury, Montgomery, Rutherford, Sevier, Shelby, Sullivan, Sumner, Washington, Williamson and Wilson counties (those over 75,000 people at the 2010 census, Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-102(a); the list follows from the census, not from the statute's text, so ask the county clerk if unsure). Every other county follows § 66-7-109.

In URLTA counties a month-to-month ends on written notice given at least 30 days before the rent date it names (§ 66-28-512(b)); a week-to-week, 10 days (§ 66-28-512(a)). Other counties have no statute: the common law’s rule is one full rental period, ending at the end of a period (not confirmed from a statute). NOHM’s 30 days, ending a rental period, meets both.

No notice to quit or demand for possession is needed before you file, other than the detainer warrant itself (Tenn. Code Ann. § 29-18-113). This notice, or the end of a lease’s term, is the only notice the law uses, so NOHM has no separate demand.
If the tenant stays without your consent, you may sue for possession, back rent and reasonable attorney’s fees, and more if the holdover is willful (§ 66-28-512(c)).
A tenant 55 or older, current on rent, in a qualifying federally assisted senior facility being redeveloped, needs 60 days (§ 66-28-523; § 66-7-109(i)).

Written notice goes to the tenant’s last known address or the one in the lease (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-106(b)); in URLTA counties, to the email the tenant gave in the lease, if they gave one (§ 66-28-108). The period runs from receipt: NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed. A last day on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next day (§ 1-3-102).

forms.label: Detainer warrant and complaint for unlawful detainer
forms.explain: The eviction filing: your complaint, and the detainer warrant in the words Tennessee’s statute sets, for the General Sessions clerk to issue.
forms.when: The rental agreement ended (by a notice, or its term ran out) and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: File in the General Sessions Court of the county where the rental is (Tenn. Code Ann. § 29-18-107). Tennessee has no statewide eviction form: most clerks issue the detainer warrant on their own form. Ask yours; copy these facts onto it, or file this complaint with it if the clerk accepts it.

You must give a bond, with good security, for the costs and damages of a wrongful suit before the warrant issues (§ 29-18-111); the clerk collects the costs (in Sevier County, for example, $250.50 plus $52 for each added defendant).

A sheriff, deputy, constable or private process server serves it. After three tries on different dates, it may be posted on the door and mailed first class at least 6 days before the trial date, but then only for possession, not money (§ 29-18-115(e)). The trial is at least 6 days after service (§ 29-18-117); a postponement is 7 days at most unless the parties agree (§ 29-18-118, Pub. Ch. 755 (2024)).
No written answer is needed in General Sessions; the judge hears it without a jury, decides possession, and works out the rent, interest and damages owed (§§ 29-18-119, 29-18-125).

No writ of possession issues until 10 days after the judgment (§ 29-18-126). The tenant may appeal to circuit court within 10 days, but only by posting a bond, cash or letter of credit, or two good sureties, for a year’s rent (§ 29-18-130(b)(2)(A), Pub. Ch. 755 (2024)).

No statute requires the complaint to be sworn; county clerks’ forms vary, so sign it as your clerk asks. County clerks say an LLC or corporation must file through an attorney (not confirmed as a statewide rule).
Bring the lease, the notice and how you gave it, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Tennessee doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: it records the home’s condition for the damage listing at move-out.

In URLTA counties, give the tenant in writing, at or before move-in: who manages the home and who accepts legal notices, with their addresses, and a maintenance phone, email or online portal (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-302(a), Pub.
