Ch. 907, for agreements from January 1, 2025); that you don’t provide insurance for the tenant’s belongings (§ 66-28-201(a)); and where the deposit account is (§ 66-28-301(h)). NOHM’s landlord disclosures form has all three.

A lease clause waiving the 14-day rent notice must be in 12-point bold type or larger (§ 66-28-505(b)); a clause making a no-show tenant waive objections to the move-out inspection must be in the lease (§ 66-28-301(b)(1)(A)).
Davidson County landlords register each rental with the codes department (§ 66-28-107). A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.
From January 1, 2027, a lease entered, amended or renewed generally can’t ban a tenant’s lawful firearms (Pub. Ch. 606 (2026); its exact text wasn’t read).

forms.label: Landlord disclosures (URLTA counties)
forms.explain: The written disclosures the URLTA requires at the start of a tenancy: the manager, the owner or agent for notices, maintenance contact, insurance, and the deposit account.
forms.when: At or before the start of the tenancy, with the lease.
notes: Required in URLTA counties; harmless anywhere. Give it at or before the start of the tenancy, and keep it current (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-302(b)).
The manager and maintenance disclosure applies to agreements entered, amended or renewed from January 1, 2025 (Pub. Ch. 907 (2024)).
Name the bank and where it is; the account number isn’t required (§ 66-28-301(h)). A deposit not kept in its own account, with no damage listing at move-out, can’t be kept at all (§ 66-28-301(c)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: Tennessee sets no notice period for most entries. To show the home to new tenants in the last 30 days of the lease, the lease must allow it and you must give at least 24 hours’ notice (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-403(e)(5)). NOHM suggests 24 hours every time.

In an emergency you may enter without consent (§ 66-28-403(b)); also during a tenant’s absence of more than 7 days, at times reasonably necessary (§ 66-28-507(b)). Don’t use entry to harass (§ 66-28-403(d)).
Outside URLTA counties no statute governs entry; your lease does.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Tennessee statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date; in URLTA counties a month-to-month ends on 30 days’ notice before a rent date (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-512(b)), so give at least that.
During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Tennessee has no rent cap, and cities and counties can’t control rents (§ 66-35-102(a)).
In URLTA counties you can’t raise rent to retaliate for a complaint or a tenant’s use of their remedies (§ 66-28-514).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: After the tenant moves out: list the damage at the move-out inspection, and send the refund notice.
notes: This is the URLTA’s procedure; outside URLTA counties no deposit statute was found, and itemizing is still the safe practice.

Within 5 days after the tenant’s written notice to vacate you may tell them of their right to be at the move-out inspection; inspect the day they leave or within 4 days after. Together you list the damage and its estimated cost and both sign; a tenant who disagrees says in writing which items (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-301(b)(1)).

If the tenant left without notice, abandoned the home, was evicted, or didn’t come, list the damage yourself, and send them a copy by certificate of mailing if they ask in writing (§ 66-28-301(b)(2)).
Damage found later counts only if found before the earlier of 30 days after they vacate or 7 days after a new tenant moves in (§ 66-28-301(g)).

Tennessee sets no deadline to return the deposit. NOHM suggests sending this within 30 days. Send the refund notice to the last known or reasonably determinable address; after 60 days with no response you may keep the deposit (§ 66-28-301(f)).
A deposit not kept in its own account at a regulated bank, with no damage listing, can’t be kept at all (§ 66-28-301(a), (c)). No cap; no interest.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: In URLTA counties, store a tenant’s belongings at least 30 days after you take possession of them; then you may sell or dispose of them, apply the proceeds to what’s owed, and hold any balance for 6 months (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-405(c)). Before you re-enter an abandoned home, post and mail the notice of abandonment.
After a writ of possession is executed, the tenant’s property is set out on the premises; don’t disturb it for 48 hours, then it may be discarded (Tenn. Code Ann. § 29-18-127(b)).
Outside URLTA counties no statute on property left behind was found; this notice is a courtesy that heads off disputes.
Photograph the property before you move it.

forms.label: Notice of abandonment (URLTA counties)
forms.explain: The notice the URLTA requires before you re-enter a home you believe the tenant abandoned: 10 days to contact you.
forms.when: Rent is 15 days past due and the tenant appears to have moved out.
notes: Rent unpaid 15 days past the due date, with other facts showing the tenant has moved out for good, is evidence of abandonment; so is an unexplained absence of 30 days without paying rent (Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-28-405(a)–(b)).

Post it at the home and send it by regular mail, postage prepaid, to the tenant at the home’s address, the same day. It must give a phone number and a mailing address where you can be reached (§ 66-28-405(b)(2)–(3)).
If the tenant doesn’t contact you within 10 days, you may re-enter. If they tell you they intend to stay, you must go to court instead (§ 66-28-405(b)(4)).
Store their belongings at least 30 days after you take them (§ 66-28-405(c)).

forms.label: 3-day notice to pay rent or vacate
forms.explain: Demands the rent, or the home back, at least 3 days after it’s delivered: the notice before an eviction suit.
forms.when: Rent is past due (a late fee only once it’s two full days late).
notes: A written lease can set a shorter or longer notice period (Tex. Prop. Code § 24.005(a)); follow it.
A tenant who was never late before the month of this notice must get a notice to pay rent or vacate, as this one is. A tenant who was late before may get either it or a plain notice to vacate.
Days are calendar days, not counting the day it’s delivered; if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or state or federal holiday, the period runs to the next day that isn’t (Tex. Prop. Code § 24.0042).

Deliver it one of the ways § 24.005(f-3) allows: by mail (first class, registered, certified, or a delivery service); inside the home in a conspicuous place; by hand to a tenant 16 or older; or electronically if you both agreed in writing. Posting on the outside of the door no longer counts (since January 1, 2026). NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed, for delivery.

If federal law requires a longer notice (the CARES Act’s 30 days for a property with a federally backed mortgage or subsidy), you may still file after this notice, but the writ of possession can’t be served until the federal period has run (§ 24.005(c-1)).

forms.label: 3-day notice to vacate (lease default)
forms.explain: Demands the home back at least 3 days after it’s delivered, for a default under the lease.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term (other than rent).
notes: Texas gives no right to cure a lease default and sets no list of breaches: the lease decides. If it promises a chance to cure or a longer notice, follow it (Tex. Prop. Code § 24.005(a)).

Within 6 months after a tenant’s good-faith repair request or complaint, an eviction can be retaliation unless it rests on a ground § 92.332 allows (delinquent rent, intentional damage, threats and others).
A conviction for public indecency on the premises lets you end the lease by written notice within 6 months; possession returns on the 10th day after the notice (§ 91.003).
Days are calendar days, not counting the day it’s delivered; if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or state or federal holiday, the period runs to the next day that isn’t (Tex. Prop. Code § 24.0042).

Deliver it one of the ways § 24.005(f-3) allows: by mail (first class, registered, certified, or a delivery service); inside the home in a conspicuous place; by hand to a tenant 16 or older; or electronically if you both agreed in writing. Posting on the outside of the door no longer counts (since January 1, 2026). NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed, for delivery.

forms.label: 1-month notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy one month after the notice, or on a later date it names.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A month-to-month ends one month after the notice, or on a later date it names; it needn’t end a rental period (Tex. Prop. Code § 91.001(b), (d)). A week-to-week ends after as many days as the rent period (§ 91.001(c)).
A lease signed by both of you can set a different notice, or none (§ 91.001(e)); NOHM uses the lease’s if it’s longer.
If the tenant stays after the date, you must still give a written 3-day notice to vacate before filing (§ 24.005(a)): NOHM’s demand for possession is that notice.
A buyer at foreclosure gives a tenant who is current on rent at least 30 days’ written notice to vacate (§ 24.005(b)).
Section 91.001 sets no way to serve it; NOHM uses the ways § 24.005(f-3) allows for the 3-day notice.

forms.label: Demand for possession
forms.explain: A written demand to hand the home back, the step before filing to evict.
forms.when: The lease ended, or a notice ended it, and the tenant is still there.
notes: A tenant who holds over after the lease’s term ends must get at least 3 days’ written notice to vacate before you file (Tex. Prop. Code § 24.005(a)), unless the lease sets a shorter or longer period. The demand for possession must be in writing (§ 24.002(b)).
For a month-to-month, end the tenancy first with the one-month notice (§ 91.001); this notice then follows if the tenant stays.
Days are calendar days, not counting the day it’s delivered; a last day on a weekend or a state or federal holiday moves to the next day (§ 24.0042). Deliver it one of the ways § 24.005(f-3) allows.

forms.label: Demand to vacate for attorney’s fees (10 days before filing)
forms.explain: The written demand that lets you recover attorney’s fees in an eviction suit when your lease doesn’t provide for them.
forms.when: At least 10 days before you file, if your written lease has no attorney’s-fee clause.
notes: Optional. You need it to recover attorney’s fees only if your written lease doesn’t entitle you to them (Tex. Prop. Code § 24.006(a)–(b)).
Send it by registered mail, or by certified mail, return receipt requested, at least 10 days before you file the suit.
It doesn’t replace the 3-day notice to vacate (§ 24.005); give that too.

forms.label: Sworn petition for eviction
forms.explain: The eviction filing for the justice court: the sworn petition with everything Rule 510.6 requires, and the military status statement.
forms.when: The 3-day notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid or left.
notes: File it in the justice court for the precinct where the rental is (Tex. Prop. Code § 24.0041). No statewide form is required: many courts hand out the Texas Justice Court Training Center’s “Petition: Eviction Case”, and a court can’t require more than the rules do (§ 24.00506). This petition has what Rule 510.6 asks for; check the court’s current requirements, since the rewritten Rule 510 was read from the Supreme Court’s amended order and its final approval wasn’t found.
It must be sworn: sign it before a notary, or sign the statement that it is true and correct under penalty of perjury (Rule 510.2), as the verification here does.
Name every tenant on the written lease who lives there (Rule 510.6(d)), and list every home and work address you know of for them in the county: the court needs them to allow alternative service.
Only a sheriff or constable serves it (Rule 510.8). The trial is 10 to 21 days after you file, and at least 4 days after service (§ 24.0051(g)).
You, your agent or your property manager may represent you, and so may an owner, officer or employee of an LLC or corporation: no lawyer is needed in justice court (§ 24.011; Rule 510.3(b)).
Rent claims are capped at $20,000 (Rule 510.6(e)). The writ of possession can’t issue before the 6th day after judgment (§ 24.0061(b)); the tenant has 5 days to appeal (§ 24.005107).
The filing fee is set by the county; ask the court. File the military status statement too; the court can’t give a default judgment without it.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Texas doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: no deduction may be made for normal wear and tear (Tex. Prop. Code § 92.104(b)), and this form records the home’s condition.
Give the flood disclosure at or before signing (§ 92.0135): NOHM has it. Give the tenant a copy of the lease within 3 business days after signing (§ 92.024).

Put these in the lease in underlined or bold print where you use them: the repair remedies (§ 92.056(g)), a surrender-notice condition on the deposit refund (§ 92.103(b)), a rekeying charge (§ 92.156(e)), the landlord’s lien (§ 54.043), and the early-termination statements on family violence, military deployment, and sexual offenses or stalking (§§ 92.016(f), 92.017(g), 92.0161(g)).

Rekey the locks within 7 days after each tenant moves out (§ 92.156(a)); test the smoke alarms at the start of the tenancy (§§ 92.255, 92.258). Disclose the owner and any off-site manager on request (§ 92.201), and give a 24-hour emergency number (§ 92.020).
Give your tenant selection criteria at application (§ 92.3515). A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Flood disclosure notice
forms.explain: The notice Texas requires with every lease: whether you know the home is in a 100-year floodplain, and whether it has flooded in the last five years.
forms.when: At or before signing the lease; you and the tenant both sign it.
notes: Give it with the lease, as a lease paragraph, an addendum, or this separate paper, at or before the lease is signed; you and the tenant must both sign it (Tex. Prop. Code § 92.0135(e)).
Leases under 30 days don’t need it (§ 92.0135(a-1)).
If you don’t give it and the tenant suffers a substantial flood loss, the tenant may end the lease (§ 92.0135(f)).
Check FEMA’s flood map for the address before you answer.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No Texas statute sets notice or hours for entry; your lease does. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours.
In an emergency you may need to go in right away; tell the tenant as soon as you can.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Texas statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date; for a month-to-month, a change in effect ends the old tenancy, which takes a month’s notice (Tex. Prop. Code § 91.001), so give at least a month (NOHM’s reading, not a rule the statute states).
During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Texas has no rent cap; a city can control rents only in a housing emergency from a disaster, with the governor’s approval (Tex. Loc. Gov’t Code § 214.902).
You can’t raise rent within 6 months after a tenant’s good-faith repair request or complaint in retaliation (Tex. Prop. Code § 92.331).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenant surrenders the home, once you have their forwarding address in writing.
notes: Refund the deposit with a written description and itemized list of all deductions on or before the 30th day after the tenant surrenders the home (Tex. Prop. Code §§ 92.103(a), 92.104(c)). You don’t have to until the tenant gives you a forwarding address in writing (§ 92.107).
No deduction for normal wear and tear (§ 92.104(b)). If the tenant owes rent and doesn’t dispute it, the itemized list isn’t required, but it is still the safe practice.
Mail postmarked by the 30th day is on time (§ 92.1041). You may send it by e-mail if you and the tenant have e-mailed each other before (§ 92.113).

Keeping a deposit in bad faith costs $100, three times what was wrongfully withheld, and attorney’s fees; not itemizing in bad faith forfeits your right to keep any of it. Missing the 30 days is presumed bad faith (§ 92.109).
No cap, interest or separate account. Keep accurate records (§ 92.106).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Texas has no general statute on property left behind: your lease’s terms on abandoned property govern. NOHM fills in 30 days to hold it, as a courtesy.

Seizing a tenant’s property for unpaid rent (the landlord’s lien) has its own rules: an underlined or bold lease clause, items you may not take, a notice left in the home, and a sale notice mailed 30 days ahead by first class and certified mail (Tex. Prop. Code §§ 54.041–54.045). Ask a lawyer before you do it.
If a sole tenant dies, follow § 92.014(c) for their property. After a writ of possession, the officer handles the tenant’s property (§ 24.0062).

forms.label: 3-business-day notice to pay or vacate
forms.explain: Demands the rent and other amounts due, or the home back, within 3 business days after service.
forms.when: Rent is past due (any day after it’s due).
notes: You may serve it any time after the rent is due (Utah Code § 78B-6-802(1)(c)); Utah has no grace period by statute.
Business days: start counting with the business day after service; weekends and legal holidays (Utah’s include Pioneer Day, July 24, and Good Friday) don’t count.
The courts’ own form is 1001EV, “Three Day Notice to Pay or to Vacate”.

Serve it as Utah Code § 78B-6-805(1) allows: in person; by registered or certified mail (or an equivalent) to the tenant’s home; with a person of suitable age and discretion there if the tenant is out; or, if no one is there, posted in a conspicuous place on the property. The statute doesn’t require mailing a second copy after leaving or posting it, but the court’s return of service form asks about one; mailing one too is good practice. NOHM adds 3 days when you send it by mail.
For a property covered by the CARES Act, its 30-day notice to vacate applies before removal, but the tenant still gets only three business days to pay (§ 78B-6-802(5)).

forms.label: 3-day notice to comply with lease or vacate
forms.explain: Says what lease term the tenant broke: comply within 3 calendar days, or leave.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term (other than rent).
notes: Serve it on the tenant and on any subtenant living there (Utah Code § 78B-6-802(1)(h)). The courts’ form is 1005EV.

Some breaches get a 3-calendar-day notice to quit with no chance to comply: assigning or subletting against the lease, or waste (§ 78B-6-802(1)(d), forms 1020EV, 1025EV); an unlawful business (1030EV); a nuisance (1015EV, 1015.5EV); a criminal act on the premises (1040EV); and a violation that can’t be brought into compliance (§ 78B-6-802(2), 1035EV). Ask a lawyer before using one; since H.B. 591 (May 6, 2026), abating a nuisance by eviction has its own action (§ 78B-6a-303).

Serve it as Utah Code § 78B-6-805(1) allows: in person; by registered or certified mail (or an equivalent) to the tenant’s home; with a person of suitable age and discretion there if the tenant is out; or, if no one is there, posted in a conspicuous place on the property. The statute doesn’t require mailing a second copy after leaving or posting it, but the court’s return of service form asks about one; mailing one too is good practice. NOHM adds 3 days when you send it by mail.

forms.label: 15-day notice to vacate (month-to-month)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month (or other periodic) tenancy at the end of a rental period, served at least 15 calendar days before.
forms.when: You want a month-to-month tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: A month-to-month, a week-to-week, or any tenancy with periodic rent ends at the end of a period on 15 calendar days’ notice (Utah Code § 78B-6-802(1)(b)(i)). The courts’ form is 1045EV.
A tenancy at will ends on 5 calendar days’ notice (§ 78B-6-802(1)(b)(ii), form 1050EV).

A fixed-term lease ends at the end of its term without notice (§ 78B-6-802(1)(a)): you may file once the tenant holds over. For a periodic tenancy this notice is the only notice the law uses, so NOHM has no separate demand for possession.
Utah has no just-cause rule, and cities can’t control rents or fees (§ 57-20-1).

Serve it as Utah Code § 78B-6-805(1) allows: in person; by registered or certified mail (or an equivalent) to the tenant’s home; with a person of suitable age and discretion there if the tenant is out; or, if no one is there, posted in a conspicuous place on the property. The statute doesn’t require mailing a second copy after leaving or posting it, but the court’s return of service form asks about one; mailing one too is good practice. NOHM adds 3 days when you send it by mail.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (1100EV, 1105EV, 1044XX)
forms.explain: Everything the Utah State Courts’ eviction forms ask for, filled in from the lease, with the forms and the steps after filing.
forms.when: The notice ran out, or the lease ended, and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Utah’s district courts use the courts’ approved eviction forms (the Online Court Assistance Program). File those, filled in from this worksheet; the worksheet isn’t filed.
The courts say their self-help pages haven’t been updated for H.B. 591 (May 6, 2026); check the form versions before you file.
Bring the lease, every notice and its return of service, and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Before signing the lease, Utah requires one of three things: a written inventory of the unit’s condition (normal wear and tear excepted), a form like this one for the tenant to complete and return within a reasonable time after moving in, or a walkthrough inspection (Utah Code § 57-22-4(6)).

Before taking an application fee, give a written good-faith estimate of the rent and each fixed non-rent cost, the type of each usage-based cost, the date the unit is available, your screening criteria, and how an applicant gets money back if the terms differ (§ 57-22-4(3)).

At or before move-in, give in writing the owner’s name, address and phone (or the manager’s, or an agent for notices), a signed copy of the lease, and the rules (§ 57-22-4(7)). Any non-refundable part of the deposit must be stated in writing when the deposit is taken (§ 57-17-2).
A home built before 1978 needs the federal lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 24 hours before you enter.
notes: Give at least 24 hours’ notice, unless the lease says otherwise (Utah Code § 57-22-4(2)).
A renter may not unreasonably deny you entry to make repairs (§ 57-22-5(2)(c)). Utah sets no hours or emergency rule; come at reasonable times.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No Utah statute sets notice for a rent increase. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date; a month-to-month can be ended on 15 days’ notice before a period ends (Utah Code § 78B-6-802(1)(b)), so 30 days is more than that.
Adding a new fee to a month-to-month takes 15 days’ notice (§ 57-22-4(5)(b)). During a fixed-term lease, change the rent only if the lease allows it.
Utah has no rent cap, and cities and counties can’t control rents or fees (§ 57-20-1).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: No later than 30 days after the tenant vacates and returns possession, mail or deliver to their last known address (or send electronically by a means they gave you) the deposit’s balance, the balance of any prepaid rent, and this itemized notice (Utah Code § 57-17-3(2)).

Deduct only rent, damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, other costs and fees the lease provides for, and cleaning (§ 57-17-3(1)). A non-refundable part must have been stated in writing when the deposit was taken (§ 57-17-2).

If the tenant serves the statutory “Tenant’s Notice to Provide Deposit Disposition”, you have 5 business days to comply (§ 57-17-3(3), (5)); after that, failing to costs the full deposit and prepaid rent, a $100 penalty, and attorney fees for bad faith (§ 57-17-5).
No cap, interest or separate account.

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Post a copy in a conspicuous place and send one by first class mail to the tenant’s last known address (Utah Code § 78B-6-816(2)(b)). The tenant may get it back within 15 calendar days by paying the costs of inventory, moving and storage.

After 15 calendar days in storage with no reasonable effort to recover it, you may sell it at a public sale (mail notice of the sale at least 5 calendar days before) or donate it if that is commercially reasonable; pay any surplus to the tenant or as unclaimed property (§ 78B-6-816(9), (11)).
Up to 15 more days for documented domestic violence, hospitalization or death (§ 78B-6-816(7)). Hazardous items, pets, garbage and perishables needn’t be stored; vehicles have their own rules.
Property left after an order of restitution is handled the same way (§ 78B-6-812(4)(d)).

forms.label: Declaration of abandonment
forms.explain: The statutory declaration that lets you retake a home the tenant appears to have abandoned, unless they dispute it in writing within 24 hours.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid and the tenant seems to have left for good.
notes: A home is presumed abandoned when the tenant gave no notice of an absence, rent is 15 days past due, and nothing shows anyone living there but their belongings; or when rent is unpaid and their belongings are gone (Utah Code § 78B-6-815(1)).
Serve it the way the eviction notices are served (§ 78B-6-805). The 24 hours don’t count Saturdays, Sundays or holidays the courts are closed.
If the tenant doesn’t dispute it in writing at your contact address within the 24 hours, you may retake possession. Then handle what they left with the notice of abandoned property (§ 78B-6-816).

forms.label: 14-day notice of termination for nonpayment
forms.explain: Ends the tenancy for unpaid rent at least 14 days after the tenant gets it, unless they pay the rent due first.
forms.when: Rent is past due (Vermont has no grace period).
notes: The tenant can stop the termination by paying, or offering, the rent due through the end of the rental period in which they pay, before the termination date (9 V.S.A. § 4467(a)). After you file, they can stop the case once in 12 months by paying all rent due, interest and costs into court before the writ is executed (12 V.S.A. § 4773).
Taking part of the rent doesn’t waive the termination (§ 4467(a)); taking rent after the termination doesn’t dismiss the case (§ 4467(j)).

The days run from “actual notice”: hand delivery, or mail to the last known address, which is presumed received three days after mailing by first-class or certified mail (9 V.S.A. § 4451(1)). NOHM adds those 3 days when it’s mailed. Vermont law has no e-mail service for these notices.

Start the eviction within 60 days after the termination date, or the notice won’t support a judgment (9 V.S.A. § 4467(k)). Several valid notices on different grounds can all support the case (§ 4467(i)).
For a nonpayment case the complaint must include the Declaration of Compliance with the CARES Act (court form 100-00031): for a covered property, a 30-day notice is needed.

forms.label: 30-day notice of termination for breach
forms.explain: Ends the tenancy at least 30 days after the tenant gets it, for breaking a material term of the lease.
forms.when: The tenant broke a material lease term (other than rent).
notes: Vermont gives no right to cure a breach: the tenancy ends on the date stated.
For criminal activity, illegal drug activity or acts of violence that threaten other residents’ health or safety, 14 days’ notice is enough (9 V.S.A. § 4467(b)(2)); ask a lawyer before using it.
A termination for something other than rent within 90 days after a government notice that the home doesn’t meet health or safety rules is presumed retaliation (§ 4465).

The days run from “actual notice”: hand delivery, or mail to the last known address, which is presumed received three days after mailing by first-class or certified mail (9 V.S.A. § 4451(1)). NOHM adds those 3 days when it’s mailed. Vermont law has no e-mail service for these notices.

Start the eviction within 60 days after the termination date, or the notice won’t support a judgment (9 V.S.A. § 4467(k)). Several valid notices on different grounds can all support the case (§ 4467(i)).

forms.label: 60- or 90-day notice of termination for no cause
forms.explain: Ends a monthly tenancy for no cause: 60 days’ notice, or 90 after two years.
forms.when: You want a monthly tenant out, no fault needed.
notes: With no written rental agreement and rent paid monthly: 60 days, or 90 days for a tenant who has lived there more than two years (9 V.S.A. § 4467(c)(1)). NOHM gives 90 days from 24 full months on, so it is never short.

With a written lease, the notice ends it at the end of its term: at least 30 days before the term ends, or 60 days after two years (§ 4467(e)). NOHM uses the longer no-written-lease notice, which is never shorter; set the lease’s end date if it is later.

Weekly rent: 21 days with no written agreement (§ 4467(c)(2)), 7 days with a written week-to-week agreement (§ 4467(e)). Sale of the building (no written agreement): 30 days (§ 4467(d)). Sharing the landlord’s own home: 15 days monthly, 7 weekly (§ 4467(h)).
No separate demand for possession: once the tenancy ends, a tenant who stays without your express consent can be sued for possession (§ 4468).

The days run from “actual notice”: hand delivery, or mail to the last known address, which is presumed received three days after mailing by first-class or certified mail (9 V.S.A. § 4451(1)). NOHM adds those 3 days when it’s mailed. Vermont law has no e-mail service for these notices.

Start the eviction within 60 days after the termination date, or the notice won’t support a judgment (9 V.S.A. § 4467(k)). Several valid notices on different grounds can all support the case (§ 4467(i)).

forms.label: Complaint for ejectment
forms.explain: The eviction filing for the Superior Court: that the tenant holds the home unlawfully after the tenancy ended, with the rental agreement and the notice attached.
forms.when: The termination date in your notice has passed and the tenant hasn’t left (file within 60 days).
notes: File it in the Superior Court, Civil Division, for the county (unit) where the rental is. Attach a copy of the rental agreement, if any, and of the notice that ended the tenancy (12 V.S.A. § 4852).

Use the Judiciary’s Summons and Notice of Appearance (form 100-00268); a sheriff serves it, and you file the Sheriff’s Return of Service (100-00261). The tenant has 21 days to answer. The Judiciary also has a general complaint form (100-00050), which you may use instead of this one.
For a case based in whole or part on unpaid rent, file the Declaration of Compliance with the CARES Act (form 100-00031) with the complaint: the form says it is required.

You may ask the court to order rent paid into court while the case goes on (12 V.S.A. § 4853a), by motion with an affidavit (Civil Division Motion, 100-00053); it is heard on 14 days’ notice, and failing to pay as ordered leads to judgment for immediate possession.

If you win, the writ of possession issues the day judgment is entered, and the sheriff puts you in possession no sooner than 14 days after serving it (§ 4854). Attorney’s fees only where a written rental agreement provides for them.
Start the case within 60 days after the termination date in the notice, or the notice can’t support a judgment (9 V.S.A. § 4467(k)). Whether an LLC needs a lawyer wasn’t confirmed; ask the court.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: Vermont doesn’t require a move-in checklist. It is good practice: only damage beyond normal wear and tear can come out of the deposit (9 V.S.A. § 4461(b)), and this form records the home’s condition.
Before the lease is signed, give the flood hazard disclosure in a separate written document (9 V.S.A. § 4466): NOHM has it.

For a home built before 1978, give the Health Department’s approved lead materials and a copy of your most recent lead-safe maintenance (RRPM) compliance statement before the lease (18 V.S.A. § 1759(d)(1)), plus the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

You may not charge an application fee, and may not require a Social Security number; accept a government ID or an ITIN (9 V.S.A. § 4456a). A lease may not ban possessing cannabis or its non-smoked use in the unit (§ 4468b).

forms.label: Flood hazard disclosure (FEMA flood area)
forms.explain: The separate written disclosure Vermont requires before a lease: whether any part of the rental is in a FEMA mapped special flood hazard area.
forms.when: At or before the lease is signed, as its own document.
notes: Required since June 17, 2024 (Act 181): disclose before entering the lease whether any part of the premises is in a FEMA mapped special flood hazard area, in a separate written document given at or before signing, substantially in the form the Department of Housing and Community Development prescribes (9 V.S.A. § 4466(a)).

This form follows the Department’s model form (Rev. 9/2024): the map number and date, the answer, your certification that you checked the map yourself, and the signatures. The Department’s form also has its own notice to tenants about flood insurance; NOHM’s follows it in substance. You may use the Department’s form instead.
Look the address up on FEMA’s Flood Map Service Center (msc.fema.gov) before you answer.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter.
notes: Give at least 48 hours’ notice, and enter only between 9 A.M. and 9 P.M. (9 V.S.A. § 4460(b)). Pick a window inside those hours.

Entry on notice is only to inspect, make repairs, alterations or improvements, supply agreed services, or show the unit. Any other time needs the tenant’s consent, which they may not unreasonably withhold (§ 4460(a)).
Without consent or notice only when you reasonably believe there is imminent danger to a person or property (§ 4460(c)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 60 days before the new rent starts.
notes: A rent increase takes effect on the first day of a rental period at least 60 days after the tenant gets actual notice (9 V.S.A. § 4455(b)). Mailed notice is presumed received 3 days after mailing (§ 4451(1)): if you mail it, allow 63 days.

In age-restricted housing, give the Department of Housing and Community Development’s form to the Department and every affected resident at least 60 days ahead, or the increase can’t be enforced (§ 4468a).
Vermont has no rent cap. You can’t change the terms of a tenancy to retaliate (§ 4465(a)).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 14 days after the tenant vacates (or you discover they have).
notes: Return the deposit with this written statement within 14 days after the tenant vacated, if they told you the date, or after you discover they vacated or abandoned the home (9 V.S.A. § 4461(c)). For a seasonal rental that isn’t a primary residence, 60 days.
Hand-deliver it, or mail it to the tenant’s last known address (§ 4461(d)).
Miss the 14 days and you forfeit the right to keep any of it; if that is willful, you owe double what was wrongfully withheld, plus attorney’s fees and costs (§ 4461(e)).

Vermont sets no cap or interest, but a town may (Burlington, Brattleboro and Winooski have deposit rules; § 4461(g)). On a sale, transfer the deposit and give the tenant the new landlord’s name and address (§ 4461(f)).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Use it when a tenant abandoned the home: you reasonably believe they no longer live there full time, rent isn’t current, and you made reasonable efforts to learn their intentions (9 V.S.A. § 4462(a)). Mail it to their last known address (§ 4462(c)(1)).
Keep the property in a safe, dry, secured place; trash, garbage and refuse may be thrown out. Unclaimed after 60 days, it becomes yours (§ 4462(c)(2)).
No notice is needed if the tenant gave you actual notice that they were leaving, or left at the end of the rental agreement (§ 4462(d)).
After an eviction, property may be disposed of without notice 15 days after the writ is served or you are restored to possession, whichever is later (12 V.S.A. § 4854a).

forms.label: 14-day notice of nonpayment (pay or quit)
forms.explain: Tells the tenant the rent is unpaid and that the lease ends if it isn’t paid within 14 days.
forms.when: Rent is unpaid when due (Virginia sets no grace period; with no written lease, rent is late after the 5th).
notes: The notice is 14 days since July 1, 2026 (it was 5). Serve it any time after rent is unpaid when due; the statute sets no grace period. With no written lease, rent is due on the 1st and late after the 5th (Va. Code § 55.1-1204(C)(4)).

Serve it by hand, by regular mail to the tenant’s last known residence, electronically if the lease provides for it, or by the sheriff, and keep the certificate of service: the Act’s definition of notice requires one. NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed; the Act adds none.

The notice includes the acceptance-with-reservation language of Va. Code § 55.1-1250(A), so you can take a partial payment and still evict. If you file, give the court a copy of this notice to serve with the summons.

The tenant can still redeem by paying everything owed at or before the first court date, and after judgment up to 48 hours before the eviction (Va. Code § 55.1-1250). A landlord of 4 or fewer units can limit that to once per lease period by telling the tenant in writing.

For a tenant with a Housing Choice Voucher or other tenant-based rental assistance, the notice works only if the statewide legal aid number and website are on its first page, in type as large as the rest (Va. Code § 55.1-1202(D)). NOHM prints them in the statements; check they fall on page 1.

If a check bounced or a funds transfer was rejected, the notice must demand payment by cash, cashier’s check, certified check or a completed electronic funds transfer (Va. Code § 55.1-1245(F)). Say so in the notice.
To claim attorney’s fees or civil recovery later, the notice of Va. Code § 55.1-1202 may be included in this notice.
The 14th day can fall on a weekend or holiday; Virginia’s time rule (Va. Code § 1-210) doesn’t clearly move it. Give a later date if you want to be safe.

From July 1, 2027, the notice must include a statement of charges and payments over the tenancy or the past 12 months (Va. Code § 55.1-1202(E)), and a landlord of more than 4 units must offer a payment plan when the rent owed is one month’s rent plus late charges or less (Va. Code § 55.1-1245(G)). This notice doesn’t have them yet: don’t use it on or after that date without them.
The court won’t order possession unless a copy of a proper termination notice is in evidence (Va. Code § 8.01-126(D)). Keep this one and its certificate of service.

forms.label: 21/30-day notice of material noncompliance
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what breaks the lease: remedy it in 21 days, or the lease ends in 30.
forms.when: The tenant materially broke the lease, or a health and safety duty.
notes: Specify the acts and omissions that are the breach: the statute requires it.
You can’t file a lease-violation case until you’ve given the tenant the Statement of Tenant Rights and Responsibilities (Va. Code § 55.1-1204(H)).

This is the notice for a breach the tenant can remedy. For one that can’t be remedied, or a repeat of a like breach after a prior notice, the notice is 30 days with no chance to remedy, and must say so (and, for a repeat, refer to the prior breach) (Va. Code § 55.1-1245(C), (E)). A criminal or willful act that threatens health or safety lets you terminate immediately (Va. Code § 55.1-1245(C)). Ask a lawyer for those.
A lease doesn’t terminate solely because of an act of family abuse against the tenant (Va. Code § 55.1-1245(D)).

A breach that repair, replacement or cleaning can fix: you may instead give written notice that you’ll enter and do the work, and bill the tenant, the bill due as rent on the next due date (Va. Code § 55.1-1248).

forms.label: 30-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy, served at least 30 days before the next rent due date.
forms.when: You want to end a month-to-month tenancy.
notes: The rental agreement can set a different notice period (Va. Code § 55.1-1253(A)). A week-to-week tenancy takes 7 days before the next rent due date.
An owner of multifamily premises who doesn’t renew 20 or more month-to-month tenancies, or half of them, within 30 days must give each tenant 60 days’ written notice (Va. Code § 55.1-1253(B)).

A landlord of more than 4 units must give written notice of nonrenewal at least 60 days before a fixed-term lease ends (Va. Code § 55.1-1204(K)). A lease that simply ends still needs a written notice: the court won’t order possession without a termination notice in evidence (Va. Code § 8.01-126(D)).

Virginia has no separate demand for possession: if the tenant stays after the date, file the Summons for Unlawful Detainer (Va. Code § 55.1-1253(C)). The lease may set holdover damages of up to 150% of the daily rent.
Virginia has no just-cause rule, but a notice in retaliation is barred (Va. Code § 55.1-1258).

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (DC-421, DC-413, DC-418, DC-422, DC-469)
forms.explain: Everything to copy onto the court’s Summons for Unlawful Detainer and the forms after it, with the steps and deadlines.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid, remedied or left.
notes: Virginia’s general district courts use the Supreme Court of Virginia’s forms, so NOHM doesn’t write the summons: copy these values onto DC-421 and file it. The clerk or magistrate has the forms too.
Ask for “all amounts due as of the hearing date” on DC-421 to have rent that comes due before the hearing included (Va. Code § 8.01-126(F)(1)).
For a lease violation, the tenant must have had the Statement of Tenant Rights and Responsibilities before you file (Va. Code § 55.1-1204(H)).

forms.label: Move-in inspection report
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Within 5 days after the tenant moves in; they have 5 days after they get it to object in writing.
notes: Give the tenant this report within 5 days after they move in (Va. Code § 55.1-1214). It is deemed correct unless they object in writing within 5 days after receiving it. Your written policy may let the tenant prepare it, or both of you together, and both sign it.

Fill in the mold row: the report must disclose whether there is visible evidence of mold. If there is, the tenant may end the lease, or you remediate it within 5 business days and give a new report (Va. Code § 55.1-1215).

Also at the start of a tenancy: offer a written lease and give the Statement of Tenant Rights and Responsibilities with it, both of you signing the Department of Housing and Community Development’s acknowledgment form, and give a signed copy of both within 10 business days (Va. Code § 55.1-1204(B), (H)).

The lease must have the fee disclosure statement on its first page (Va. Code § 55.1-1204.1), and you must give the names and addresses of the manager and of an owner or someone authorized to act for the owner (Va. Code § 55.1-1216(A)).

Give the renter’s insurance notice before signing if the lease doesn’t require renter’s insurance (NOHM’s form, Va. Code § 55.1-1206(D)), and a certificate that all smoke alarms are present, inspected and working (Va. Code § 55.1-1220(A)(8)).

Where they apply: the military air installation (Va. Code § 55.1-1217), defective drywall (§ 55.1-1218) and methamphetamine (§ 55.1-1219) disclosures, and the federal lead-based paint disclosure for homes built before 1978.

forms.label: Renter’s insurance and flood notice
forms.explain: The written notice that your insurance doesn’t cover the tenant’s belongings, and that renter’s insurance doesn’t cover floods.
forms.when: Before the lease is signed, when the lease doesn’t require renter’s insurance.
notes: Required before the tenant signs a lease that doesn’t require renter’s insurance (Va. Code § 55.1-1206(D)). Keep the tenant’s signed copy.
If you provide damage or renter’s insurance yourself, the tenant must also get notice of their right to their own policy and a summary of yours before signing (Va. Code § 55.1-1206(A)–(B)).

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter; at least 72 hours before routine maintenance the tenant didn’t ask for.
notes: Virginia asks for notice of your intent to enter and entry at reasonable times, except in an emergency or where notice is impractical (Va. Code § 55.1-1229(A)(4)). The statute sets no hours except for routine maintenance the tenant didn’t ask for: at least 72 hours, done within 14 days, and the notice must give the last date it may be done.

You may enter to inspect, make necessary or agreed repairs, decorations, alterations or improvements, supply services, or show the unit to purchasers, mortgagees, tenants, workmen or contractors (Va. Code § 55.1-1229(A)(1)).

Applying an insecticide or pesticide in the unit takes at least 48 hours’ written notice (Va. Code § 55.1-1223). A temporary relocation for a nonemergency repair takes 30 days’ written notice (Va. Code § 55.1-1229(B)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: For a month-to-month tenancy (or a tenant holding over), a new rent takes effect only on the next rent due date coming 30 days after written notice (Va. Code § 55.1-1253(D)).
During a lease, rent changes only if both of you agree in writing (Va. Code § 55.1-1204(I)).

A landlord of more than 4 units must give written notice of a rent increase for a renewal term at least 60 days before the lease ends (Va. Code § 55.1-1204(K)); from July 1, 2027, 90 days, with a deadline at least 30 days out for the tenant to say whether they’ll renew.
Virginia has no rent cap, and localities can’t adopt their own landlord-tenant rules (Va. Code § 55.1-1201(E)). A retaliatory increase is barred (Va. Code § 55.1-1258).

forms.label: Notice of the right to be at the move-out inspection
forms.explain: Tells the tenant they may be present when you inspect the home for the deposit.
forms.when: When you ask the tenant to vacate, or within 5 days after the tenant tells you they’re leaving.
notes: Give it when you ask the tenant to vacate, or within 5 days after you get the tenant’s notice that they intend to vacate (Va. Code § 55.1-1226(G)).

If the tenant asks to be present, inspect within 72 hours after they deliver possession. Afterward, give them the written security deposit disposition statement with its itemized list of damages (NOHM’s deposit form).

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 45 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Itemize the deposit and every deduction in a written notice, with any refund, within 45 days after the tenancy ends or the tenant vacates, whichever is later (Va. Code § 55.1-1226).

If damages exceed the deposit and need a third-party contractor, tell the tenant in writing within the 45 days; you then have 15 more days to itemize the damages and the cost of repair (Va. Code § 55.1-1226(E)).

With several tenants, one check payable to all of them goes to the forwarding address one of them gave. With no forwarding address, hold it; after a year it may go to the State Treasurer as unclaimed property (Va. Code § 55.1-1226(B)).

You may hold back enough for the final water, sewer or utility bill only if the tenant was told so in writing at least 15 days before; refund the rest within 10 days after the bill is paid (Va. Code § 55.1-1226(C)).
The deposit can’t be more than two months’ rent (Va. Code § 55.1-1226(A)). No interest is owed. Keep records of deductions for 2 years (§ 55.1-1226(F)).
Willfully failing to comply means returning the deposit with actual damages and attorney’s fees, unless the tenant owes rent (Va. Code § 55.1-1226(E)).

forms.label: 7-day notice of suspected abandonment
forms.explain: Asks a tenant who seems to have left to say in writing, within 7 days, that they intend to stay.
forms.when: You can’t tell whether the tenant has abandoned the home.
notes: Use it when you can’t determine whether the tenant has abandoned the premises (Va. Code § 55.1-1249). If they don’t answer in writing within 7 days, the premises are presumed abandoned and the rental agreement is deemed to end that day.
It includes the statement Va. Code § 55.1-1254 asks for, so property left may be disposed of within 24 hours after the 7 days end.
While the tenant is absent more than 7 days, you may enter at times reasonably necessary to protect your property (Va. Code § 55.1-1249).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: After the tenancy ended and the tenant left things behind.
notes: Use it after the tenancy has ended and possession is back with you. You may dispose of the property within 24 hours after 10 days from the date of this notice (Va. Code § 55.1-1254).
The same statement may instead go in the termination notice (disposal within 24 hours after termination) or in the 7-day abandonment notice (NOHM’s form).
Sale proceeds go to the tenant’s account, against what they owe and the costs; the rest is treated as a security deposit (Va. Code § 55.1-1254).

After a writ of eviction is executed, this section doesn’t apply: Va. Code § 55.1-1255 does. For a sole tenant who died, give the emergency contact at least 10 days’ written notice instead (Va. Code § 55.1-1256).

forms.label: 14-day notice to pay rent or vacate
forms.explain: The statute’s own form: pay the rent due in 14 days, or move out.
forms.when: Rent is past due (any time after it’s due).
notes: Washington requires this notice in substantially the form RCW 59.18.057 sets; NOHM prints its words. The Attorney General has it in other languages at www.atg.wa.gov/landlord-tenant (RCW 59.18.058).
Serve it any time after the rent is due (RCW 59.12.030(3)). Fill in where to pay: the form names the landlord and the address.

When any copy is mailed, five more days are allowed before you can file, so NOHM’s date is 19 days out. Mail it from within Washington. Certified mail isn’t required for notices served on or after June 11, 2026.
Prove service with a declaration or affidavit of the person who served it.

Payments go to rent first (RCW 59.18.283). A late fee can’t be charged for rent paid within 5 days of its due date (RCW 59.18.170(2)), and a judgment can include no more than $75 in late fees (RCW 59.18.410(1)).
A tenant whose main income is monthly government assistance that arrives after the due date can ask to move the due date up to 5 days later (RCW 59.18.170(3)).
Some cities (Seattle, Tacoma and others) and King County add their own rules; NOHM hasn’t covered them.

forms.label: 10-day notice to comply or vacate
forms.explain: States the breach and its facts: fix it within 10 days, or move out.
forms.when: The tenant broke a material lease term or a duty the law sets (not one for money).
notes: The breach must be of a material term of the lease, a material program requirement of subsidized housing, or a tenant obligation the law imposes, and not an obligation for money damages (RCW 59.18.650(2)(b)).
State the facts in detail: the notice must let the tenant respond and prepare a defense (RCW 59.18.650(6)). A subtenant in possession must be served too (RCW 59.12.030(4)).

Waste, nuisance, unlawful activity, or substantial or repeated and unreasonable interference allows a 3-day notice to quit with no chance to cure (RCW 59.18.650(2)(c)). Four or more violations in 12 months, each with a written warning notice, allow a 60-day notice to end the tenancy at the end of the term (RCW 59.18.650(2)(n)). Ask a lawyer for those.
When a copy is mailed, NOHM adds the five days RCW 59.12.040 allows.

forms.label: 90-day notice to end a tenancy for cause
forms.explain: Ends a tenancy for a cause the law allows, with its facts, at least 90 days out.
forms.when: The initial or fixed term is ending, you or family will move in, you’re selling, or another cause RCW 59.18.650 lists.
notes: Washington has no no-cause ending: a landlord may end a periodic tenancy or refuse to continue one only for a cause RCW 59.18.650 lists (RCW 59.18.650(1)(a)). Write the cause and its facts in the reason.

NOHM gives 90 days, which covers the causes that need 60 or 90: the end of an initial lease of 6 to 12 months that rolls into month-to-month, or of a fixed term of 12 months or more that doesn’t roll over (60 days, RCW 59.18.650(1)(b)–(c)); the owner or family moving in, or the owner selling a single-family home (90 days, RCW 59.18.650(2)(d)–(e)); another legitimate business reason (60 days before the end of the period, RCW 59.18.650(2)(m)).
Demolition, substantial rehabilitation, a change of use or a condominium conversion needs 120 days (RCW 59.18.200(2)); don’t use this notice for them.
A fixed term can’t be ended early for the owner moving in, a sale or demolition unless you and the tenant agree in writing and the tenant has at least 60 days to leave (RCW 59.18.650(5)).
Washington has no separate demand for possession: this notice is the demand. If the tenant stays after the date, file for unlawful detainer.

Ending a tenancy without a lawful cause costs the greater of the tenant’s damages or three months’ rent (RCW 59.18.650(4)). Local just-cause and relocation rules (Seattle, Tacoma, Burien and others) can be stricter; NOHM hasn’t covered them.

forms.label: Eviction summons and complaint for unlawful detainer
forms.explain: The statute’s Eviction Summons (Residential) and your complaint, for the superior court.
forms.when: The notice ran out and the tenant hasn’t paid, complied or left.
notes: Washington has no statewide court form for an eviction. The summons is in the words RCW 59.18.365(3) sets; the complaint states the facts, describes the premises and, for unpaid rent, the amount (RCW 59.12.070). File in the superior court of the county where the rental is (RCW 59.12.050).

Set the response date at least 7 and no more than 30 days after the summons is served (RCW 59.12.070). Have the summons and complaint served by someone other than you, after the notice has run out; you may serve before filing (say so on the summons).

If the tenant responds, ask the court for an order to show cause; the hearing is 7 to 30 days after it is served (RCW 59.18.370), and the court may order the writ of restitution there (RCW 59.18.380). The sheriff serves the writ and waits 3 days to execute it (RCW 59.18.390); in a rent case, not until 5 court days after judgment (RCW 59.18.410(2)).

You need a bond only for a writ before final judgment (RCW 59.18.380). Give the sheriff the statutory Request for Storage of Personal Property form to serve with the writ (RCW 59.18.312(6)); NOHM doesn’t draw it.

A judgment can include rent, damages, late fees due under the lease up to $75 in all, costs and attorney’s fees (RCW 59.18.410(1)); no attorney’s fees on a default, or when the rent awarded is no more than the greater of two months’ rent or $1,200 (RCW 59.18.290(3)). Low-income tenants have a right to an appointed lawyer (RCW 59.18.640).
A company (an LLC or a corporation) needs a lawyer in superior court (Dutch Village Mall v. Pelletti, 2011). NOHM read only summaries of that case; ask the clerk or a lawyer.
Attach the notice, the proof you served it, and the rental agreement.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: You may not collect a deposit unless the rental agreement is in writing and you give the tenant this checklist at the start of the tenancy, signed and dated by both of you, with a copy for the tenant; without it, you are liable to the tenant for the amount of the deposit (RCW 59.18.260). Describe condition and cleanliness on every row.
Deductions can’t be taken for anything whose condition wasn’t documented here (RCW 59.18.280(1)(c)).

Put the deposit in a trust account in Washington, give a written receipt, and tell the tenant in writing the name, address and location of the depository (RCW 59.18.270). On the tenant’s written request, deposits, fees and last month’s rent can be paid in installments (RCW 59.18.610).

Also at signing: the fire safety and smoke detection notice, signed by both of you (RCW 59.18.060(12)); the Department of Health’s mold information (RCW 59.18.060(14)); the landlord’s name and address (RCW 59.18.060(16)); for leases entered into after December 31, 2026, the flood disclosure (NOHM’s form, RCW 59.18.060(13)); and the federal lead-based paint disclosure for homes built before 1978.

forms.label: Flood disclosure
forms.explain: The three things the law says to tell a tenant about flood risk and insurance.
forms.when: At lease signing, for leases entered into after December 31, 2026.
notes: Required for leases entered into after December 31, 2026 (RCW 59.18.060(13)(b)). Give it with the lease, and keep the tenant’s signed copy.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 2 days before you enter (1 day to show the unit).
notes: Give at least two days’ written notice (one day to show the unit to prospective or actual purchasers or tenants), and enter only at reasonable times (RCW 59.18.150(6)). The window you give is the earliest and latest possible times of entry.
The notice must give a phone number the tenant can call to object or reschedule: put it in your address and phone.

You may enter to inspect, make necessary or agreed repairs, alterations or improvements, supply services, or show the unit to purchasers, mortgagees, tenants, workers or contractors (RCW 59.18.150(1)). No notice is needed in an emergency or after abandonment (RCW 59.18.150(5)).

forms.label: Rent and fee increase notice
forms.explain: The statute’s notice of a rent increase: the new total, and that it’s within the state limit or which exemption you claim.
forms.when: At least 90 days before the new rent starts.
notes: Give at least 90 days’ written notice, and the increase can’t take effect before the rental agreement’s term ends (RCW 59.18.140(3)(a)); 30 days for a subsidized tenancy whose rent is based on income (RCW 59.18.140(3)(b)). Serve it as RCW 59.12.040 says.
Washington requires this notice in substantially the form RCW 59.18.720(3) sets; NOHM prints its words. It counts rent and every other recurring or periodic charge together.

No increase in the first 12 months of a tenancy, and in any 12 months no more than 7% plus inflation or 10%, whichever is less (RCW 59.18.700(1)). The Department of Commerce publishes the figure each year (reported as 9.683% for 2026 and 10% for 2027; NOHM couldn’t confirm either from the statute). NOHM stops anything over 10%.
An exemption must be one RCW 59.18.710 lists, with its facts stated or documents attached. Owner-occupancy exemptions don’t apply to a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member.

A tenant can demand the excess be fixed, or end the tenancy with 20 days’ notice before the increase; overcharging can cost up to three months of the excess and penalties from the Attorney General (RCW 59.18.700). Seattle and other cities may require more notice.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and you get the home back.
notes: Give it, with any refund and the documentation, within 30 days after the rental agreement ends and the tenant vacates; if the tenant abandoned the home, within 30 days after you learn of it (RCW 59.18.280(1)).

You can’t deduct for ordinary wear and tear, for carpet cleaning unless documented wear beyond ordinary, for anything the move-in checklist didn’t document, or more than the cost of repairing the damaged part (RCW 59.18.280(1)(c)).

Late, or without the checklist, you owe the whole deposit; an intentional refusal can cost up to twice the deposit (RCW 59.18.280(2), 59.18.260). Sue for damages beyond the deposit within 3 years (RCW 59.18.280(3)(c)).
Nonrefundable fees count as a deposit unless the written lease says they’re nonrefundable (RCW 59.18.285).

forms.label: Notice of property left behind
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: A tenant who owed rent abandoned the home and left property.
notes: This is for a tenant who defaulted in rent and, by words or actions, showed they won’t resume the tenancy (RCW 59.18.310(1)). Mail it first class to the last known address and any other address you know (RCW 59.18.310(2)).

The sale or disposal can be no sooner than 45 days after the notice is mailed or delivered; 7 days if everything left is worth $250 or less, except personal papers, family pictures and keepsakes (RCW 59.18.310(2)). Hold any excess from a sale for a year.
After a writ of restitution, RCW 59.18.312 governs instead (storage on the tenant’s request; 30 days’ notice of sale). For a sole tenant who died, RCW 59.18.595.

forms.label: Demand for payment of rent (no notice required)
forms.explain: A written demand for the rent owed. West Virginia doesn’t require one before filing.
forms.when: Rent is past due, and any grace period or notice in the lease has passed.
notes: West Virginia requires no notice before filing: the court case itself is the demand (W. Va. Code § 37-6-19). Once rent is in arrears you can file the Petition for Summary Relief (W. Va. Code § 55-3A-1(a)(3)).
The lease decides: if it sets a notice or grace period, or a time before reentry, give it first and wait it out (W. Va. Code § 37-6-19). Put that date in the notice.
NOHM adds 3 days when it’s mailed, for delivery.

forms.label: Notice of lease violation (optional)
forms.explain: Tells the tenant what breaks the lease, with any time the lease gives to fix it.
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease covenant or damaged the property.
notes: West Virginia law doesn’t require this notice: you may petition for summary relief when the tenant has breached a warranty or covenant of the lease, or damaged the property (W. Va. Code § 55-3A-1(a)(3)).
The lease decides: if it gives the tenant time to cure, or sets a time before reentry, use that date and wait it out (W. Va. Code § 37-6-19).

forms.label: Notice to end a periodic tenancy (one full rental period)
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month (or other periodic) tenancy at the end of a full rental period.
forms.when: You want to end a month-to-month, week-to-week or year-to-year tenancy.
notes: The notice may be served on the tenant or on anyone holding the premises under them (W. Va. Code § 37-6-5).
The lease can set a different notice period, or none (W. Va. Code § 37-6-5). A lease whose term ends on a set date needs no notice at all.
A week-to-week tenancy takes one full week’s notice; a year-to-year tenancy takes 3 months’ notice before the end of a year.
West Virginia has no separate demand for possession: if the tenant stays after the date, file the Petition for Summary Relief.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (MLTPTWR, MLTSMWO)
forms.explain: Everything to copy onto the court’s Petition for Summary Relief, with the steps and deadlines after it.
forms.when: Rent is in arrears, or the tenant broke a covenant or damaged the property, or a notice ended the tenancy.
notes: West Virginia’s magistrate courts use the Judiciary’s own forms, so NOHM doesn’t write the petition: copy these values onto MLTPTWR, sign it before a notary, and file it. The clerk has the forms too.
No notice is required before filing, but if the lease sets a notice, grace period or time before reentry, it must run out first (W. Va. Code § 37-6-19).
A tenant who stays after a fixed term ends, or after a § 37-6-5 notice runs out, can also be sued for unlawful detainer (W. Va. Code § 55-3-1); the summary petition is the usual route.

In circuit court a company generally needs a lawyer (a 2014 Attorney General opinion and a 2012 Supreme Court of Appeals case; NOHM read only summaries). In magistrate court it may appear by an agent (W. Va. Code § 50-4-4a).

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Give it at move-in, and keep the signed copy.
notes: No West Virginia statute requires a move-in checklist. It’s good practice: it shows the home’s condition when deposit deductions come up later.

West Virginia requires no other move-in disclosures for an ordinary residential lease. If a pet fee or application fee is nonrefundable, agree on that in writing, or it counts as part of the deposit (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-1(14)). The federal lead-based paint disclosure applies to homes built before 1978.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: Before you enter for an inspection, a repair or a showing.
notes: No West Virginia statute sets notice for a landlord’s entry: follow your lease. NOHM suggests at least 24 hours, at a reasonable time.

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: No West Virginia statute sets notice for a rent increase, or caps rent. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date: that is NOHM’s practice, not the law.

For a month-to-month tenant, a change takes the notice that ends the tenancy: one full rental period (W. Va. Code § 37-6-5). NOHM’s date is the first due date at least 30 days out, which leaves a full period; pick another date only if a full period still passes.
During a lease, the rent changes only as the lease allows.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 60 days after the tenancy ends, or 45 days after a new tenant moves in, whichever is sooner.
notes: Deliver the deposit, less deductions, with a written itemization within 60 days after the tenancy ends, or within 45 days after a new tenant occupies the home, whichever is sooner (W. Va. Code §§ 37-6A-1(7), 37-6A-2(a)). NOHM warns at 60; if a new tenant moved in, your deadline is earlier.

If damages exceed the deposit and need a third-party contractor, give written notice within that time; you then have 15 more days to itemize the damages and the cost of repair (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-2(c)).

If it comes back undeliverable, hold it 6 months and hand it over at your place of business within 72 hours of a written request (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-2(g)). Keep records of deductions for a year (§ 37-6A-3).

No cap, no interest and no separate account are required. Withholding in bad faith costs the deposit plus one and a half times the amount wrongfully withheld (W. Va. Code § 37-6A-5(a)). A lease can’t waive these rules (§ 37-6A-4).

forms.label: Posted notice to pay rent within one month (home abandoned)
forms.explain: Posted on a home the tenant left owing rent: pay within a month, or the tenancy ends and you take possession.
forms.when: A tenant who owes rent has abandoned the home.
notes: Post it in writing in a conspicuous part of the property (W. Va. Code § 37-6-6(a)). If the rent isn’t paid within a month, you are entitled to possession and may enter, and the tenant’s right to the property ends.
Then, for anything left behind, use the notice of abandoned property (W. Va. Code § 37-6-6(c)–(d)).

forms.label: Notice of abandoned property
forms.explain: Lists what the tenant left, and how long you’ll hold it before you dispose of it.
forms.when: The tenant abandoned the home and left property behind.
notes: Post it on the property AND mail it first class with a certificate of mailing, in an envelope marked “Please Forward”, to the leased property, any post office box of the tenant you know of, and the latest forwarding address (W. Va. Code § 37-6-6(c)).
The date to remove it must be at least 30 days after you mail the notice, or 60 if the tenant told you they’re on active duty in the Armed Forces (W. Va. Code § 37-6-6(d)).
Property worth more than $300: if the tenant or a secured party says they’ll remove it and pays reasonable storage and removal costs, store it up to 30 more days (W. Va. Code § 37-6-6(e)).
After a court order of possession, W. Va. Code § 55-3A-3(h)–(i) governs property left instead.

forms.label: 5-day notice to pay rent or vacate
forms.explain: Pay the rent due within 5 days or move out (30 days for a lease of more than a year).
forms.when: Rent is past due.
notes: NOHM counts the 5 days without Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, the longer reading, and gives 30 (counted the same way) for a lease of more than one year.

The agency guide says a month-to-month tenant can instead get a 14-day notice to vacate with no chance to pay, and a tenant on a lease of a year or less who is late again within 12 months after a cured 5-day notice can get a 14-day notice with no chance to pay. NOHM doesn’t draw those.
No fee or penalty may be charged for not paying a late fee (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.09(8)(c)).
The ways of serving are the ones Wis. Stat. § 704.21 is understood to allow; NOHM couldn’t confirm them from the statute, or whether mailing adds days.

forms.label: 5-day notice to remedy or vacate
forms.explain: Fix the breach within 5 days or move out (30 days for a lease of more than a year).
forms.when: The tenant broke a lease term or damaged the property.
notes: NOHM counts the 5 days without Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, the longer reading, and gives 30 for a lease of more than one year.

The agency guide says a repeat breach within a year allows a 14-day notice with no chance to cure, and criminal or drug-related activity a 5-day notice to vacate with required contents (Wis. Stat. § 704.17(3m)). NOHM doesn’t draw those.
A lease can’t let you end a tenancy because the tenant, or someone living with them, was the victim of a crime there (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.08(9)).
The ways of serving are the ones Wis. Stat. § 704.21 is understood to allow; NOHM couldn’t confirm them from the statute, or whether mailing adds days.

forms.label: 28-day notice to end a month-to-month
forms.explain: Ends a month-to-month tenancy at the end of a rental period, at least 28 days out.
forms.when: You want to end a month-to-month tenancy.
notes: A week-to-week tenancy is understood to take 7 days (Wis. Stat. § 704.19); NOHM couldn’t confirm it.
No separate demand for possession is needed once the notice runs out: file the eviction (Summons and Complaint, SC-500).
You can’t end or refuse to renew a tenancy in retaliation for reporting code violations, organizing, or asserting legal rights (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.09(5)).

An automatic renewal clause can be enforced only if the tenant got a separate written reminder 15 to 30 days before it takes effect (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.09(3)): use NOHM’s automatic renewal notice.
The ways of serving are the ones Wis. Stat. § 704.21 is understood to allow; NOHM couldn’t confirm them from the statute, or whether mailing adds days.

forms.label: Eviction filing worksheet (SC-500, SC-5100V, SC-512)
forms.explain: Everything to copy onto the court’s Summons and Complaint for an eviction, with the steps after it.
forms.when: Your notice ended the tenancy and the tenant hasn’t left.
notes: Wisconsin evictions use the statewide Summons and Complaint (SC-500), which may not be modified, so NOHM doesn’t write one: copy these values onto it and file it with the clerk of circuit court.

NOHM couldn’t read Wis. Stat. ch. 799 from the official site. Not confirmed, so not on the paper: the return date is understood to be 5 to 25 days after the summons issues (§ 799.05(3)(b)); the court may stay a writ up to 30 days for hardship (§ 799.44(3)); a tenant who wrongfully stays may owe double rent, prorated daily (§ 704.27).
NOHM couldn’t find whether a company may appear without a lawyer in small claims (believed to be Wis. Stat. § 799.06). Ask the clerk before an employee appears for an LLC.
Bring the notice you served, your proof of serving it, the lease and the rent ledger.

forms.label: Move-in condition checklist
forms.explain: The written record of the home’s condition when the tenant moves in, signed by both of you.
forms.when: Before you accept a security deposit; the tenant has until a date at least 7 days after the tenancy starts.
notes: Before you accept a security deposit, you must tell the tenant in writing that they may, by a date at least 7 days after the tenancy starts, inspect the unit and report preexisting damages or defects, and ask for the list of damages charged to the previous tenant’s deposit (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.06(1)(a)). This form does that, with a checklist to note them.
If asked, give that list within 30 days after the request, or within 7 days after you notify the previous tenant of their deductions, whichever is later (ATCP 134.06(1)(b)).
Wis. Stat. § 704.08 is understood to require a check-in sheet with 7 days to complete it; NOHM couldn’t confirm its words.

Before signing or taking a deposit: copies of the lease and rules (ATCP 134.03(1)); a written receipt for any deposit (ATCP 134.03(2)); the names and addresses of the landlord, manager and owner or agent (ATCP 134.04(1)); known uncorrected code violations and habitability problems (ATCP 134.04(2)); and utility charges not in the rent, with how they’re split (ATCP 134.04(3)).

Extra deposit deductions, entry terms or a lien on property need a separate signed document titled “NONSTANDARD RENTAL PROVISIONS” (ATCP 134.06(3)(b), 134.09(2)(c), 134.09(4)(b)). A lease that lets you end a tenancy for a crime must include the Notice of Domestic Abuse Protections of Wis. Stat. § 704.14, or it is void (ATCP 134.08(10)); NOHM couldn’t confirm its text. Homes built before 1978 need the federal lead-based paint disclosure.

forms.label: Notice of entry
forms.explain: Tells the tenant when you’ll come in, and why.
forms.when: At least 12 hours before you enter.
notes: Enter only to inspect, make repairs, or show the unit to prospective tenants or purchasers, with at least 12 hours’ advance notice and at reasonable times (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.09(2)).

No notice is needed if the tenant asks you to come in or agrees ahead of time knowing when, in a health or safety emergency, or when the tenant is absent and entry is reasonably needed to protect the premises (ATCP 134.09(2)(b)).
Announce yourself before entering, and say who you are if asked (ATCP 134.09(2)(d)). Other entry terms need a signed “NONSTANDARD RENTAL PROVISIONS” document (ATCP 134.09(2)(c)).

forms.label: Notice of rent change
forms.explain: Changes a month-to-month tenant’s rent from a rent due date.
forms.when: At least 30 days before the new rent starts.
notes: NOHM found no Wisconsin rule on notice of a rent increase, and no cap. NOHM asks for 30 days and starts the new rent on a due date: that is NOHM’s practice, not the law.

For a month-to-month tenant, a change is understood to take the 28-day notice that ends the tenancy (Wis. Stat. § 704.19); NOHM couldn’t confirm it. During a lease, the rent changes only as the lease allows.

Cities and counties can’t control rents (Wis. Stat. § 66.1015, not confirmed). A lease clause allowing an increase because the tenant called the police, health or safety services is void (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.08(1)).

forms.label: Notice of automatic renewal
forms.explain: The separate written reminder a tenant must get before a lease’s automatic renewal can be enforced.
forms.when: 15 to 30 days before the lease renews or extends itself.
notes: You can enforce an automatic renewal or extension clause only if the tenant got a separate written notice of it at least 15 days, but no more than 30 days, before its stated effective date (Wis. Admin. Code § ATCP 134.09(3)).
Wis. Stat. § 704.15 may require more; NOHM couldn’t read it.

forms.label: Security deposit: itemized deductions
forms.explain: The written list of what you kept from the deposit, and why, with the refund.
forms.when: Within 21 days after the tenancy ends (or the tenant leaves, as the rule sets).
